text_en: The parables of Solomon , the son of David , king of Israel ,
text_la: Parabolæ Salomonis, filii David, regis Israël,
text_pt: Provérbios de Salomão, filho de Davi, rei de Israel;
text_el: παροιμίαι Σαλωμῶντος υἱοῦ Δαυιδ ὃς ἐβασίλευσεν ἐν Ισραηλ

text_en: to know wisdom, and instruction:
text_la: ad sciendam sapientiam et disciplinam;
text_pt: Para se conhecer a sabedoria e a instrução; para se entenderem, as palavras da prudência.
text_el: γνῶναι σοφίαν καὶ παιδείαν νοῆσαί τε λόγους φρονήσεως

text_en: To understand the words of prudence : and to receive the instruction of doctrine, justice , and judgment, and equity:
text_la: ad intelligenda verba prudentiæ, et suscipiendam eruditionem doctrinæ, justitiam, et judicium, et æquitatem :
text_pt: Para se receber a instrução do entendimento, a justiça, o juízo e a eqüidade;
text_el: δέξασθαί τε στροφὰς λόγων νοῆσαί τε δικαιοσύνην ἀληθῆ καὶ κρίμα κατευθύνειν

text_en: To give subtilty to little ones, to the young man knowledge and understanding.
text_la: ut detur parvulis astutia, adolescenti scientia et intellectus.
text_pt: Para dar aos simples, prudência, e aos moços, conhecimento e bom siso;
text_el: ἵνα δῷ ἀκάκοις πανουργίαν παιδὶ δὲ νέῳ αἴσθησίν τε καὶ ἔννοιαν

text_en: A wise man shall hear, and shall be wiser: and he that understands shall possess governments.
text_la: Audiens sapiens, sapientior erit, et intelligens gubernacula possidebit.
text_pt: O sábio ouvirá e crescerá em conhecimento, e o entendido adquirirá sábios conselhos;
text_el: τῶνδε γὰρ ἀκούσας σοφὸς σοφώτερος ἔσται ὁ δὲ νοήμων κυβέρνησιν κτήσεται

text_en: He shall understand a parable and the interpretation, the words of the wise, and their mysterious sayings.
text_la: Animadvertet parabolam et interpretationem, verba sapientum et ænigmata eorum.
text_pt: Para entender os provérbios e sua interpretação; as palavras dos sábios e as suas proposições.
text_el: νοήσει τε παραβολὴν καὶ σκοτεινὸν λόγον ῥήσεις τε σοφῶν καὶ αἰνίγματα

text_en: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. Fools despise wisdom and instruction.
text_la: Timor Domini principium sapientiæ; sapientiam atque doctrinam stulti despiciunt.
text_pt: O temor do Senhor é o princípio do conhecimento; os loucos desprezam a sabedoria e a instrução.
text_el: ἀρχὴ σοφίας φόβος θεοῦ σύνεσις δὲ ἀγαθὴ πᾶσι τοῖς ποιοῦσιν αὐτήν εὐσέβεια δὲ εἰς θεὸν ἀρχὴ αἰσθήσεως σοφίαν δὲ καὶ παιδείαν ἀσεβεῖς ἐξουθενήσουσιν

text_en: My son, hear the instruction of your father, and forsake not the law of your mother:
text_la: Audi, fili mi, disciplinam patris tui, et ne dimittas legem matris tuæ :
text_pt: Filho meu, ouve a instrução de teu pai, e não deixes o ensinamento de tua mãe,
text_el: ἄκουε υἱέ παιδείαν πατρός σου καὶ μὴ ἀπώσῃ θεσμοὺς μητρός σου

text_en: That grace may be added to your head, and a chain of gold to your neck.
text_la: ut addatur gratia capiti tuo, et torques collo tuo.
text_pt: Porque serão como diadema gracioso em tua cabeça, e colares ao teu pescoço.
text_el: στέφανον γὰρ χαρίτων δέξῃ σῇ κορυφῇ καὶ κλοιὸν χρύσεον περὶ σῷ τραχήλῳ

text_en: My son, if sinners shall entice you, consent not to them.
text_la: Fili mi, si te lactaverint peccatores, ne acquiescas eis.
text_pt: Filho meu, se os pecadores procuram te atrair com agrados, não aceites.
text_el: υἱέ μή σε πλανήσωσιν ἄνδρες ἀσεβεῖς μηδὲ βουληθῇς ἐὰν παρακαλέσωσί σε λέγοντες

text_en: If they shall say: Come with us, let us lie in wait for blood, let us hide snares for the innocent without cause:
text_la: Si dixerint : Veni nobiscum, insidiemur sanguini; abscondamus tendiculas contra insontem frustra;
text_pt: Se disserem: Vem conosco a tocaias de sangue; embosquemos o inocente sem motivo;
text_el: ἐλθὲ μεθ' ἡμῶν κοινώνησον αἵματος κρύψωμεν δὲ εἰς γῆν ἄνδρα δίκαιον ἀδίκως

text_en: Let us swallow him up alive like hell, and whole as one that goes down into the pit.
text_la: deglutiamus eum sicut infernus viventem, et integrum quasi descendentem in lacum;
text_pt: Traguemo-los vivos, como a sepultura; e inteiros, como os que descem à cova;
text_el: καταπίωμεν δὲ αὐτὸν ὥσπερ ᾅδης ζῶντα καὶ ἄρωμεν αὐτοῦ τὴν μνήμην ἐκ γῆς

text_en: We shall find all precious substance, we shall fill our houses with spoils.
text_la: omnem pretiosam substantiam reperiemus; implebimus domos nostras spoliis :
text_pt: Acharemos toda sorte de bens preciosos; encheremos as nossas casas de despojos;
text_el: τὴν κτῆσιν αὐτοῦ τὴν πολυτελῆ καταλαβώμεθα πλήσωμεν δὲ οἴκους ἡμετέρους σκύλων

text_en: Cast in your lot with us, let us all have one purse.
text_la: sortem mitte nobiscum, marsupium unum sit omnium nostrum :
text_pt: Lança a tua sorte conosco; teremos todos uma só bolsa!
text_el: τὸν δὲ σὸν κλῆρον βάλε ἐν ἡμῖν κοινὸν δὲ βαλλάντιον κτησώμεθα πάντες καὶ μαρσίππιον ἓν γενηθήτω ἡμῖν

text_en: My son, walk not with them, restrain your foot from their paths.
text_la: fili mi, ne ambules cum eis; prohibe pedem tuum a semitis eorum :
text_pt: Filho meu, não te ponhas a caminho com eles; desvia o teu pé das suas veredas;
text_el: μὴ πορευθῇς ἐν ὁδῷ μετ' αὐτῶν ἔκκλινον δὲ τὸν πόδα σου ἐκ τῶν τρίβων αὐτῶν

text_en: For their feet run to evil , and make haste to shed blood.
text_la: pedes enim illorum ad malum currunt, et festinant ut effundant sanguinem.
text_pt: Porque os seus pés correm para o mal, e se apressam a derramar sangue.
text_el: οἱ γὰρ πόδες αὐτῶν εἰς κακίαν τρέχουσιν καὶ ταχινοὶ τοῦ ἐκχέαι αἷμα

text_en: But a net is spread in vain before the eyes of them that have wings.
text_la: Frustra autem jacitur rete ante oculos pennatorum.
text_pt: Na verdade é inútil estender-se a rede ante os olhos de qualquer ave.
text_el: οὐ γὰρ ἀδίκως ἐκτείνεται δίκτυα πτερωτοῖς

text_en: And they themselves lie in wait for their own blood, and practise deceits against their own souls .
text_la: Ipsi quoque contra sanguinem suum insidiantur, et moliuntur fraudes contra animas suas.
text_pt: No entanto estes armam ciladas contra o seu próprio sangue; e espreitam suas próprias vidas.
text_el: αὐτοὶ γὰρ οἱ φόνου μετέχοντες θησαυρίζουσιν ἑαυτοῖς κακά ἡ δὲ καταστροφὴ ἀνδρῶν παρανόμων κακή

text_en: So the ways of every covetous man destroy the souls of the possessors.
text_la: Sic semitæ omnis avari : animas possidentium rapiunt.
text_pt: São assim as veredas de todo aquele que usa de cobiça: ela põe a perder a alma dos que a possuem.
text_el: αὗται αἱ ὁδοί εἰσιν πάντων τῶν συντελούντων τὰ ἄνομα τῇ γὰρ ἀσεβείᾳ τὴν ἑαυτῶν ψυχὴν ἀφαιροῦνται

text_en: Wisdom preaches abroad, she utters her voice in the streets:
text_la: Sapientia foris prædicat; in plateis dat vocem suam :
text_pt: A sabedoria clama lá fora; pelas ruas levanta a sua voz.
text_el: σοφία ἐν ἐξόδοις ὑμνεῖται ἐν δὲ πλατείαις παρρησίαν ἄγει

text_en: At the head of multitudes she cries out, in the entrance of the gates of the city she utters her words, saying:
text_la: in capite turbarum clamitat; in foribus portarum urbis profert verba sua, dicens :
text_pt: Nas esquinas movimentadas ela brada; nas entradas das portas e nas cidades profere as suas palavras:
text_el: ἐπ' ἄκρων δὲ τειχέων κηρύσσεται ἐπὶ δὲ πύλαις δυναστῶν παρεδρεύει ἐπὶ δὲ πύλαις πόλεως θαρροῦσα λέγει

text_en: O children, how long will you love childishness, and fools covet those things which are hurtful to themselves, and the unwise hate knowledge ?
text_la: Usquequo, parvuli, diligitis infantiam, et stulti ea quæ sibi sunt noxia cupient, et imprudentes odibunt scientiam?
text_pt: Até quando, ó simples, amareis a simplicidade? E vós escarnecedores, desejareis o escárnio? E vós insensatos, odiareis o conhecimento?
text_el: ὅσον ἂν χρόνον ἄκακοι ἔχωνται τῆς δικαιοσύνης οὐκ αἰσχυνθήσονται οἱ δὲ ἄφρονες τῆς ὕβρεως ὄντες ἐπιθυμηταί ἀσεβεῖς γενόμενοι ἐμίσησαν αἴσθησιν

text_en: Turn at my reproof: behold I will utter my spirit to you, and will show you my words.
text_la: convertimini ad correptionem meam. En proferam vobis spiritum meum, et ostendam vobis verba mea.
text_pt: Atentai para a minha repreensão; pois eis que vos derramarei abundantemente do meu espírito e vos farei saber as minhas palavras.
text_el: καὶ ὑπεύθυνοι ἐγένοντο ἐλέγχοις ἰδοὺ προήσομαι ὑμῖν ἐμῆς πνοῆς ῥῆσιν διδάξω δὲ ὑμᾶς τὸν ἐμὸν λόγον

text_en: Because I called, and you refused: I stretched out my hand, and there was none that regarded.
text_la: Quia vocavi, et renuistis; extendi manum meam, et non fuit qui aspiceret :
text_pt: Entretanto, porque eu clamei e recusastes; e estendi a minha mão e não houve quem desse atenção,
text_el: ἐπειδὴ ἐκάλουν καὶ οὐχ ὑπηκούσατε καὶ ἐξέτεινον λόγους καὶ οὐ προσείχετε

text_en: You have despised all my counsel, and have neglected my reprehensions.
text_la: despexistis omne consilium meum, et increpationes meas neglexistis.
text_pt: Antes rejeitastes todo o meu conselho, e não quisestes a minha repreensão,
text_el: ἀλλὰ ἀκύρους ἐποιεῖτε ἐμὰς βουλάς τοῖς δὲ ἐμοῖς ἐλέγχοις ἠπειθήσατε

text_en: I also will laugh in your destruction, and will mock when that shall come to you which you feared.
text_la: Ego quoque in interitu vestro ridebo, et subsannabo cum vobis id quod timebatis advenerit.
text_pt: Também de minha parte eu me rirei na vossa perdição e zombarei, em vindo o vosso temor.
text_el: τοιγαροῦν κἀγὼ τῇ ὑμετέρᾳ ἀπωλείᾳ ἐπιγελάσομαι καταχαροῦμαι δέ ἡνίκα ἂν ἔρχηται ὑμῖν ὄλεθρος

text_en: When sudden calamity shall fall on you, and destruction, as a tempest, shall be at hand: when tribulation and distress shall come upon you:
text_la: Cum irruerit repentina calamitas, et interitus quasi tempestas ingruerit; quando venerit super vos tribulatio et angustia :
text_pt: Vindo o vosso temor como a assolação, e vindo a vossa perdição como uma tormenta, sobrevirá a vós aperto e angústia.
text_el: καὶ ὡς ἂν ἀφίκηται ὑμῖν ἄφνω θόρυβος ἡ δὲ καταστροφὴ ὁμοίως καταιγίδι παρῇ καὶ ὅταν ἔρχηται ὑμῖν θλῖψις καὶ πολιορκία ἢ ὅταν ἔρχηται ὑμῖν ὄλεθρος

text_en: Then shall they call upon me, and I will not hear: they shall rise in the morning, and shall not find me:
text_la: tunc invocabunt me, et non exaudiam; mane consurgent, et non invenient me :
text_pt: Então clamarão a mim, mas eu não responderei; de madrugada me buscarão, porém não me acharão.
text_el: ἔσται γὰρ ὅταν ἐπικαλέσησθέ με ἐγὼ δὲ οὐκ εἰσακούσομαι ὑμῶν ζητήσουσίν με κακοὶ καὶ οὐχ εὑρήσουσιν

text_en: Because they have hated instruction, and received not the fear of the Lord ,
text_la: eo quod exosam habuerint disciplinam, et timorem Domini non susceperint,
text_pt: Porquanto odiaram o conhecimento; e não preferiram o temor do Senhor:
text_el: ἐμίσησαν γὰρ σοφίαν τὸν δὲ φόβον τοῦ κυρίου οὐ προείλαντο

text_en: nor consented to my counsel, but despised all my reproof.
text_la: nec acquieverint consilio meo, et detraxerint universæ correptioni meæ.
text_pt: Não aceitaram o meu conselho, e desprezaram toda a minha repreensão.
text_el: οὐδὲ ἤθελον ἐμαῖς προσέχειν βουλαῖς ἐμυκτήριζον δὲ ἐμοὺς ἐλέγχους

text_en: Therefore they shall eat the fruit of their own way, and shall be filled with their own devices.
text_la: Comedent igitur fructus viæ suæ, suisque consiliis saturabuntur.
text_pt: Portanto comerão do fruto do seu caminho, e fartar-se-ão dos seus próprios conselhos.
text_el: τοιγαροῦν ἔδονται τῆς ἑαυτῶν ὁδοῦ τοὺς καρποὺς καὶ τῆς ἑαυτῶν ἀσεβείας πλησθήσονται

text_en: The turning away of little ones shall kill them, and the prosperity of fools shall destroy them.
text_la: Aversio parvulorum interficiet eos, et prosperitas stultorum perdet illos.
text_pt: Porque o erro dos simples os matará, e o desvario dos insensatos os destruirá.
text_el: ἀνθ' ὧν γὰρ ἠδίκουν νηπίους φονευθήσονται καὶ ἐξετασμὸς ἀσεβεῖς ὀλεῖ

text_en: But he that shall hear me, shall rest without terror, and shall enjoy abundance, without fear of evils .
text_la: Qui autem me audierit, absque terrore requiescet, et abundantia perfruetur, timore malorum sublato.
text_pt: Mas o que me der ouvidos habitará em segurança, e estará livre do temor do mal.
text_el: ὁ δὲ ἐμοῦ ἀκούων κατασκηνώσει ἐπ' ἐλπίδι καὶ ἡσυχάσει ἀφόβως ἀπὸ παντὸς κακοῦ

text_en: My son, if you will receive my words, and will hide my commandments with you,
text_la: Fili mi, si susceperis sermones meos, et mandata mea absconderis penes te :
text_pt: Filho meu, se aceitares as minhas palavras, e esconderes contigo os meus mandamentos,
text_el: υἱέ ἐὰν δεξάμενος ῥῆσιν ἐμῆς ἐντολῆς κρύψῃς παρὰ σεαυτῷ

text_en: that your ear may hearken to wisdom: incline your heart to know prudence .
text_la: ut audiat sapientiam auris tua, inclina cor tuum ad cognoscendam prudentiam.
text_pt: Para fazeres o teu ouvido atento à sabedoria; e inclinares o teu coração ao entendimento;
text_el: ὑπακούσεται σοφίας τὸ οὖς σου καὶ παραβαλεῖς καρδίαν σου εἰς σύνεσιν παραβαλεῖς δὲ αὐτὴν ἐπὶ νουθέτησιν τῷ υἱῷ σου

text_en: For if you shall call for wisdom, and incline your heart to prudence :
text_la: Si enim sapientiam invocaveris, et inclinaveris cor tuum prudentiæ;
text_pt: Se clamares por conhecimento, e por inteligência alçares a tua voz,
text_el: ἐὰν γὰρ τὴν σοφίαν ἐπικαλέσῃ καὶ τῇ συνέσει δῷς φωνήν σου τὴν δὲ αἴσθησιν ζητήσῃς μεγάλῃ τῇ φωνῇ

text_en: If you shall seek her as money, and shall dig for her as for a treasure:
text_la: si quæsieris eam quasi pecuniam, et sicut thesauros effoderis illam :
text_pt: Se como a prata a buscares e como a tesouros escondidos a procurares,
text_el: καὶ ἐὰν ζητήσῃς αὐτὴν ὡς ἀργύριον καὶ ὡς θησαυροὺς ἐξερευνήσῃς αὐτήν

text_en: Then shall you understand the fear of the Lord , and shall find the knowledge of God :
text_la: tunc intelliges timorem Domini, et scientiam Dei invenies,
text_pt: Então entenderás o temor do Senhor, e acharás o conhecimento de Deus.
text_el: τότε συνήσεις φόβον κυρίου καὶ ἐπίγνωσιν θεοῦ εὑρήσεις

text_en: Because the Lord gives wisdom: and out of his mouth comes prudence and knowledge .
text_la: quia Dominus dat sapientiam, et ex ore ejus prudentia et scientia.
text_pt: Porque o Senhor dá a sabedoria; da sua boca é que vem o conhecimento e o entendimento.
text_el: ὅτι κύριος δίδωσιν σοφίαν καὶ ἀπὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ γνῶσις καὶ σύνεσις

text_en: He will keep the salvation of the righteous, and protect them that walk in simplicity,
text_la: Custodiet rectorum salutem, et proteget gradientes simpliciter,
text_pt: Ele reserva a verdadeira sabedoria para os retos. Escudo é para os que caminham na sinceridade,
text_el: καὶ θησαυρίζει τοῖς κατορθοῦσι σωτηρίαν ὑπερασπιεῖ τὴν πορείαν αὐτῶν

text_en: keeping the paths of justice , and guarding the ways of saints .
text_la: servans semitas justitiæ, et vias sanctorum custodiens.
text_pt: Para que guardem as veredas do juízo. Ele preservará o caminho dos seus santos.
text_el: τοῦ φυλάξαι ὁδοὺς δικαιωμάτων καὶ ὁδὸν εὐλαβουμένων αὐτὸν διαφυλάξει

text_en: Then shall you understand justice , and judgment, and equity, and every good path.
text_la: Tunc intelliges justitiam, et judicium, et æquitatem, et omnem semitam bonam.
text_pt: Então entenderás a justiça, o juízo, a eqüidade e todas as boas veredas.
text_el: τότε συνήσεις δικαιοσύνην καὶ κρίμα καὶ κατορθώσεις πάντας ἄξονας ἀγαθούς

text_en: If wisdom shall enter into your heart, and knowledge please your soul :
text_la: Si intraverit sapientia cor tuum, et scientia animæ tuæ placuerit,
text_pt: Pois quando a sabedoria entrar no teu coração, e o conhecimento for agradável à tua alma,
text_el: ἐὰν γὰρ ἔλθῃ ἡ σοφία εἰς σὴν διάνοιαν ἡ δὲ αἴσθησις τῇ σῇ ψυχῇ καλὴ εἶναι δόξῃ

text_en: Counsel shall keep you, and prudence shall preserve you,
text_la: consilium custodiet te, et prudentia servabit te :
text_pt: O bom siso te guardará e a inteligência te conservará;
text_el: βουλὴ καλὴ φυλάξει σε ἔννοια δὲ ὁσία τηρήσει σε

text_en: that you may be delivered from the evil way, and from the man that speaks perverse things:
text_la: ut eruaris a via mala, et ab homine qui perversa loquitur;
text_pt: Para te afastar do mau caminho, e do homem que fala coisas perversas;
text_el: ἵνα ῥύσηταί σε ἀπὸ ὁδοῦ κακῆς καὶ ἀπὸ ἀνδρὸς λαλοῦντος μηδὲν πιστόν

text_en: Who leave the right way, and walk by dark ways:
text_la: qui relinquunt iter rectum, et ambulant per vias tenebrosas;
text_pt: Dos que deixam as veredas da retidão, para andarem pelos caminhos escusos;
text_el: ὦ οἱ ἐγκαταλείποντες ὁδοὺς εὐθείας τοῦ πορεύεσθαι ἐν ὁδοῖς σκότους

text_en: Who are glad when they have done evil , and rejoice in the most wicked things:
text_la: qui lætantur cum malefecerint, et exsultant in rebus pessimis;
text_pt: Que se alegram de fazer mal, e folgam com as perversidades dos maus,
text_el: οἱ εὐφραινόμενοι ἐπὶ κακοῖς καὶ χαίροντες ἐπὶ διαστροφῇ κακῇ

text_en: Whose ways are perverse, and their steps infamous.
text_la: quorum viæ perversæ sunt, et infames gressus eorum.
text_pt: Cujas veredas são tortuosas e que se desviam nos seus caminhos;
text_el: ὧν αἱ τρίβοι σκολιαὶ καὶ καμπύλαι αἱ τροχιαὶ αὐτῶν

text_en: That you may be delivered from the strange woman , and from the stranger, who softens her words;
text_la: Ut eruaris a muliere aliena, et ab extranea quæ mollit sermones suos,
text_pt: Para te afastar da mulher estranha, sim da estranha que lisonjeia com suas palavras;
text_el: τοῦ μακράν σε ποιῆσαι ἀπὸ ὁδοῦ εὐθείας καὶ ἀλλότριον τῆς δικαίας γνώμης

text_en: and forsakes the guide of her youth,
text_la: et relinquit ducem pubertatis suæ,
text_pt: Que deixa o guia da sua mocidade e se esquece da aliança do seu Deus;
text_el: υἱέ μή σε καταλάβῃ κακὴ βουλὴ ἡ ἀπολείπουσα διδασκαλίαν νεότητος καὶ διαθήκην θείαν ἐπιλελησμένη

text_en: and has forgotten the covenant of her God : for her house inclines unto death, and her paths to hell.
text_la: et pacti Dei sui oblita est. Inclinata est enim ad mortem domus ejus, et ad inferos semitæ ipsius.
text_pt: Porque a sua casa se inclina para a morte, e as suas veredas para os mortos.
text_el: ἔθετο γὰρ παρὰ τῷ θανάτῳ τὸν οἶκον αὐτῆς καὶ παρὰ τῷ ᾅδῃ μετὰ τῶν γηγενῶν τοὺς ἄξονας αὐτῆς

text_en: None that go in unto her, shall return again, neither shall they take hold of the paths of life.
text_la: Omnes qui ingrediuntur ad eam non revertentur, nec apprehendent semitas vitæ.
text_pt: Todos os que se dirigem a ela não voltarão e não atinarão com as veredas da vida.
text_el: πάντες οἱ πορευόμενοι ἐν αὐτῇ οὐκ ἀναστρέψουσιν οὐδὲ μὴ καταλάβωσιν τρίβους εὐθείας οὐ γὰρ καταλαμβάνονται ὑπὸ ἐνιαυτῶν ζωῆς

text_en: That you may walk in a good way: and may keep the paths of the just .
text_la: Ut ambules in via bona, et calles justorum custodias :
text_pt: Para andares pelos caminhos dos bons, e te conservares nas veredas dos justos.
text_el: εἰ γὰρ ἐπορεύοντο τρίβους ἀγαθάς εὕροσαν ἂν τρίβους δικαιοσύνης λείους

text_en: For they that are upright, shall dwell in the earth; and the simple shall continue in it.
text_la: qui enim recti sunt habitabunt in terra, et simplices permanebunt in ea;
text_pt: Porque os retos habitarão a terra, e os íntegros permanecerão nela.
text_el: χρηστοὶ ἔσονται οἰκήτορες γῆς ἄκακοι δὲ ὑπολειφθήσονται ἐν αὐτῇ ὅτι εὐθεῖς κατασκηνώσουσι γῆν καὶ ὅσιοι ὑπολειφθήσονται ἐν αὐτῇ

text_en: But the wicked shall be destroyed from the earth: and they that do unjustly , shall be taken away from it.
text_la: impii vero de terra perdentur, et qui inique agunt auferentur ex ea.
text_pt: Mas os ímpios serão arrancados da terra, e os aleivosos serão dela exterminados.
text_el: ὁδοὶ ἀσεβῶν ἐκ γῆς ὀλοῦνται οἱ δὲ παράνομοι ἐξωσθήσονται ἀπ' αὐτῆς

text_en: My son, forget not my law, and let your heart keep my commandments.
text_la: Fili mi, ne obliviscaris legis meæ, et præcepta mea cor tuum custodiat :
text_pt: Filho meu, não te esqueças da minha lei, e o teu coração guarde os meus mandamentos.
text_el: υἱέ ἐμῶν νομίμων μὴ ἐπιλανθάνου τὰ δὲ ῥήματά μου τηρείτω σὴ καρδία

text_en: For they shall add to you length of days, and years of life, and peace.
text_la: longitudinem enim dierum, et annos vitæ, et pacem, apponent tibi.
text_pt: Porque eles aumentarão os teus dias e te acrescentarão anos de vida e paz.
text_el: μῆκος γὰρ βίου καὶ ἔτη ζωῆς καὶ εἰρήνην προσθήσουσίν σοι

text_en: Let not mercy and truth leave you, put them about your neck, and write them in the tables of your heart.
text_la: Misericordia et veritas te non deserant; circumda eas gutturi tuo, et describe in tabulis cordis tui :
text_pt: Não te desamparem a benignidade e a fidelidade; ata-as ao teu pescoço; escreve-as na tábua do teu coração.
text_el: ἐλεημοσύναι καὶ πίστεις μὴ ἐκλιπέτωσάν σε ἄφαψαι δὲ αὐτὰς ἐπὶ σῷ τραχήλῳ καὶ εὑρήσεις χάριν

text_en: And you shall find grace , and good understanding before God and men .
text_la: et invenies gratiam, et disciplinam bonam, coram Deo et hominibus.
text_pt: E acharás graça e bom entendimento aos olhos de Deus e do homem.
text_el: καὶ προνοοῦ καλὰ ἐνώπιον κυρίου καὶ ἀνθρώπων

text_en: Have confidence in the Lord with all your heart, and lean not upon your own prudence .
text_la: Habe fiduciam in Domino ex toto corde tuo, et ne innitaris prudentiæ tuæ.
text_pt: Confia no Senhor de todo o teu coração, e não te estribes no teu próprio entendimento.
text_el: ἴσθι πεποιθὼς ἐν ὅλῃ καρδίᾳ ἐπὶ θεῷ ἐπὶ δὲ σῇ σοφίᾳ μὴ ἐπαίρου

text_en: In all your ways think on him, and he will direct your steps.
text_la: In omnibus viis tuis cogita illum, et ipse diriget gressus tuos.
text_pt: Reconhece-o em todos os teus caminhos, e ele endireitará as tuas veredas.
text_el: ἐν πάσαις ὁδοῖς σου γνώριζε αὐτήν ἵνα ὀρθοτομῇ τὰς ὁδούς σου ὁ δὲ πούς σου οὐ μὴ προσκόπτῃ

text_en: Be not wise in your own conceit: fear God , and depart from evil :
text_la: Ne sis sapiens apud temetipsum; time Deum, et recede a malo :
text_pt: Não sejas sábio a teus próprios olhos; teme ao Senhor e aparta-te do mal.
text_el: μὴ ἴσθι φρόνιμος παρὰ σεαυτῷ φοβοῦ δὲ τὸν θεὸν καὶ ἔκκλινε ἀπὸ παντὸς κακοῦ

text_en: For it shall be health to your navel, and moistening to your bones.
text_la: sanitas quippe erit umbilico tuo, et irrigatio ossium tuorum.
text_pt: Isto será saúde para o teu âmago, e medula para os teus ossos.
text_el: τότε ἴασις ἔσται τῷ σώματί σου καὶ ἐπιμέλεια τοῖς ὀστέοις σου

text_en: Honour the Lord with your substance, and give him of the first of all your fruits ;
text_la: Honora Dominum de tua substantia, et de primitiis omnium frugum tuarum da ei :
text_pt: Honra ao Senhor com os teus bens, e com a primeira parte de todos os teus ganhos;
text_el: τίμα τὸν κύριον ἀπὸ σῶν δικαίων πόνων καὶ ἀπάρχου αὐτῷ ἀπὸ σῶν καρπῶν δικαιοσύνης

text_en: and your barns shall be filled with abundance, and your presses shall run over with wine.
text_la: et implebuntur horrea tua saturitate, et vino torcularia tua redundabunt.
text_pt: E se encherão os teus celeiros, e transbordarão de vinho os teus lagares.
text_el: ἵνα πίμπληται τὰ ταμίειά σου πλησμονῆς σίτου οἴνῳ δὲ αἱ ληνοί σου ἐκβλύζωσιν

text_en: My son, reject not the correction of the Lord : and do not faint when you are chastised by him:
text_la: Disciplinam Domini, fili mi, ne abjicias, nec deficias cum ab eo corriperis :
text_pt: Filho meu, não rejeites a correção do Senhor, nem te enojes da sua repreensão.
text_el: υἱέ μὴ ὀλιγώρει παιδείας κυρίου μηδὲ ἐκλύου ὑπ' αὐτοῦ ἐλεγχόμενος

text_en: For whom the Lord loves , he chastises: and as a father in the son he pleases himself.
text_la: quem enim diligit Dominus, corripit, et quasi pater in filio complacet sibi.
text_pt: Porque o Senhor repreende aquele a quem ama, assim como o pai ao filho a quem quer bem.
text_el: ὃν γὰρ ἀγαπᾷ κύριος παιδεύει μαστιγοῖ δὲ πάντα υἱὸν ὃν παραδέχεται

text_en: Blessed is the man that finds wisdom, and is rich in prudence :
text_la: Beatus homo qui invenit sapientiam, et qui affluit prudentia.
text_pt: Bem-aventurado o homem que acha sabedoria, e o homem que adquire conhecimento;
text_el: μακάριος ἄνθρωπος ὃς εὗρεν σοφίαν καὶ θνητὸς ὃς εἶδεν φρόνησιν

text_en: The purchasing thereof is better than the merchandise of silver, and her fruit than the chief and purest gold:
text_la: Melior est acquisitio ejus negotiatione argenti, et auri primi et purissimi fructus ejus.
text_pt: Porque é melhor a sua mercadoria do que artigos de prata, e maior o seu lucro que o ouro mais fino.
text_el: κρεῖττον γὰρ αὐτὴν ἐμπορεύεσθαι ἢ χρυσίου καὶ ἀργυρίου θησαυρούς

text_en: She is more precious than all riches: and all the things that are desired, are not to be compared to her.
text_la: Pretiosior est cunctis opibus, et omnia quæ desiderantur huic non valent comparari.
text_pt: Mais preciosa é do que os rubis, e tudo o que mais possas desejar não se pode comparar a ela.
text_el: τιμιωτέρα δέ ἐστιν λίθων πολυτελῶν οὐκ ἀντιτάξεται αὐτῇ οὐδὲν πονηρόν εὔγνωστός ἐστιν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐγγίζουσιν αὐτῇ πᾶν δὲ τίμιον οὐκ ἄξιον αὐτῆς ἐστιν

text_en: Length of days is in her right hand, and in her left hand riches and glory .
text_la: Longitudo dierum in dextera ejus, et in sinistra illius divitiæ et gloria.
text_pt: Vida longa de dias está na sua mão direita; e na esquerda, riquezas e honra.
text_el: μῆκος γὰρ βίου καὶ ἔτη ζωῆς ἐν τῇ δεξιᾷ αὐτῆς ἐν δὲ τῇ ἀριστερᾷ αὐτῆς πλοῦτος καὶ δόξα

text_en: Her ways are beautiful ways, and all her paths are peaceable.
text_la: Viæ ejus viæ pulchræ, et omnes semitæ illius pacificæ.
text_pt: Os seus caminhos são caminhos de delícias, e todas as suas veredas de paz.
text_el: αἱ ὁδοὶ αὐτῆς ὁδοὶ καλαί καὶ πάντες οἱ τρίβοι αὐτῆς ἐν εἰρήνῃ

text_en: She is a tree of life to them that lay hold on her: and he that shall retain her is blessed .
text_la: Lignum vitæ est his qui apprehenderint eam, et qui tenuerit eam beatus.
text_pt: É árvore de vida para os que dela tomam, e são bem-aventurados todos os que a retêm.
text_el: ξύλον ζωῆς ἐστι πᾶσι τοῖς ἀντεχομένοις αὐτῆς καὶ τοῖς ἐπερειδομένοις ἐπ' αὐτὴν ὡς ἐπὶ κύριον ἀσφαλής

text_en: The Lord by wisdom has founded the earth, has established the heavens by prudence .
text_la: Dominus sapientia fundavit terram; stabilivit cælos prudentia.
text_pt: O Senhor, com sabedoria fundou a terra; com entendimento preparou os céus.
text_el: ὁ θεὸς τῇ σοφίᾳ ἐθεμελίωσεν τὴν γῆν ἡτοίμασεν δὲ οὐρανοὺς ἐν φρονήσει

text_en: By his wisdom the depths have broken out, and the clouds grow thick with dew.
text_la: Sapientia illius eruperunt abyssi, et nubes rore concrescunt.
text_pt: Pelo seu conhecimento se fenderam os abismos, e as nuvens destilam o orvalho.
text_el: ἐν αἰσθήσει ἄβυσσοι ἐρράγησαν νέφη δὲ ἐρρύησαν δρόσους

text_en: My son, let not these things depart from your eyes: keep the law and counsel:
text_la: Fili mi, ne effluant hæc ab oculis tuis. Custodi legem atque consilium,
text_pt: Filho meu, não se apartem estas coisas dos teus olhos: guarda a verdadeira sabedoria e o bom siso;
text_el: υἱέ μὴ παραρρυῇς τήρησον δὲ ἐμὴν βουλὴν καὶ ἔννοιαν

text_en: And there shall be life to your soul , and grace to your mouth.
text_la: et erit vita animæ tuæ, et gratia faucibus tuis.
text_pt: Porque serão vida para a tua alma, e adorno ao teu pescoço.
text_el: ἵνα ζήσῃ ἡ ψυχή σου καὶ χάρις ᾖ περὶ σῷ τραχήλῳ

text_en: Then shall you walk confidently in your way, and your foot shall not stumble:
text_la: Tunc ambulabis fiducialiter in via tua, et pes tuus non impinget.
text_pt: Então andarás confiante pelo teu caminho, e o teu pé não tropeçará.
text_el: ἵνα πορεύῃ πεποιθὼς ἐν εἰρήνῃ πάσας τὰς ὁδούς σου ὁ δὲ πούς σου οὐ μὴ προσκόψῃ

text_en: If you sleep, you shall not fear: you shall rest, and your sleep shall be sweet.
text_la: Si dormieris, non timebis; quiesces, et suavis erit somnus tuus.
text_pt: Quando te deitares, não temerás; ao contrário, o teu sono será suave ao te deitares.
text_el: ἐὰν γὰρ κάθῃ ἄφοβος ἔσῃ ἐὰν δὲ καθεύδῃς ἡδέως ὑπνώσεις

text_en: Be not afraid of sudden fear, nor of the power of the wicked falling upon you.
text_la: Ne paveas repentino terrore, et irruentes tibi potentias impiorum.
text_pt: Não temas o pavor repentino, nem a investida dos perversos quando vier.
text_el: καὶ οὐ φοβηθήσῃ πτόησιν ἐπελθοῦσαν οὐδὲ ὁρμὰς ἀσεβῶν ἐπερχομένας

text_en: For the Lord will be at your side, and will keep your foot that you be not taken.
text_la: Dominus enim erit in latere tuo, et custodiet pedem tuum, ne capiaris.
text_pt: Porque o Senhor será a tua esperança; guardará os teus pés de serem capturados.
text_el: ὁ γὰρ κύριος ἔσται ἐπὶ πασῶν ὁδῶν σου καὶ ἐρείσει σὸν πόδα ἵνα μὴ σαλευθῇς

text_en: Do not withhold him from doing good , who is able: if you are able, do good yourself also.
text_la: Noli prohibere benefacere eum qui potest : si vales, et ipse benefac.
text_pt: Não deixes de fazer bem a quem o merece, estando em tuas mãos a capacidade de fazê-lo.
text_el: μὴ ἀπόσχῃ εὖ ποιεῖν ἐνδεῆ ἡνίκα ἂν ἔχῃ ἡ χείρ σου βοηθεῖν

text_en: Say not to your friend: Go, and come again: and tomorrow I will give to you: when you can give at present.
text_la: Ne dicas amico tuo : Vade, et revertere : cras dabo tibi : cum statim possis dare.
text_pt: Não digas ao teu próximo: Vai, e volta amanhã que to darei, se já o tens contigo.
text_el: μὴ εἴπης ἐπανελθὼν ἐπάνηκε καὶ αὔριον δώσω δυνατοῦ σου ὄντος εὖ ποιεῖν οὐ γὰρ οἶδας τί τέξεται ἡ ἐπιοῦσα

text_en: Practise not evil against your friend, when he has confidence in you.
text_la: Ne moliaris amico tuo malum, cum ille in te habeat fiduciam.
text_pt: Não maquines o mal contra o teu próximo, pois que habita contigo confiadamente.
text_el: μὴ τεκτήνῃ ἐπὶ σὸν φίλον κακὰ παροικοῦντα καὶ πεποιθότα ἐπὶ σοί

text_en: Strive not against a man without cause, when he has done you no evil .
text_la: Ne contendas adversus hominem frustra, cum ipse tibi nihil mali fecerit.
text_pt: Não contendas com alguém sem causa, se não te fez nenhum mal.
text_el: μὴ φιλεχθρήσῃς πρὸς ἄνθρωπον μάτην μή τι εἰς σὲ ἐργάσηται κακόν

text_en: Envy not the unjust man , and do not follow his ways.
text_la: Ne æmuleris hominem injustum, nec imiteris vias ejus :
text_pt: Não tenhas inveja do homem violento, nem escolhas nenhum dos seus caminhos.
text_el: μὴ κτήσῃ κακῶν ἀνδρῶν ὀνείδη μηδὲ ζηλώσῃς τὰς ὁδοὺς αὐτῶν

text_en: For every mocker is an abomination to the Lord , and his communication is with the simple.
text_la: quia abominatio Domini est omnis illusor, et cum simplicibus sermocinatio ejus.
text_pt: Porque o perverso é abominável ao Senhor, mas com os sinceros ele tem intimidade.
text_el: ἀκάθαρτος γὰρ ἔναντι κυρίου πᾶς παράνομος ἐν δὲ δικαίοις οὐ συνεδριάζει

text_en: Want is from the Lord in the house of the wicked : but the habitations of the just shall be blessed .
text_la: Egestas a Domino in domo impii; habitacula autem justorum benedicentur.
text_pt: A maldição do Senhor habita na casa do ímpio, mas a habitação dos justos abençoará.
text_el: κατάρα θεοῦ ἐν οἴκοις ἀσεβῶν ἐπαύλεις δὲ δικαίων εὐλογοῦνται

text_en: He shall scorn the scorners, and to the meek he will give grace .
text_la: Ipse deludet illusores, et mansuetis dabit gratiam.
text_pt: Certamente ele escarnecerá dos escarnecedores, mas dará graça aos mansos.
text_el: κύριος ὑπερηφάνοις ἀντιτάσσεται ταπεινοῖς δὲ δίδωσιν χάριν

text_en: The wise shall possess glory : the promotion of fools is disgrace.
text_la: Gloriam sapientes possidebunt; stultorum exaltatio ignominia.
text_pt: Os sábios herdarão honra, mas os loucos tomam sobre si vergonha.
text_el: δόξαν σοφοὶ κληρονομήσουσιν οἱ δὲ ἀσεβεῖς ὕψωσαν ἀτιμίαν

text_en: Hear, you children, the instruction of a father, and attend, that you may know prudence .
text_la: Audite, filii, disciplinam patris, et attendite ut sciatis prudentiam.
text_pt: Ouvi, filhos, a instrução do pai, e estai atentos para conhecerdes a prudência.
text_el: ἀκούσατε παῖδες παιδείαν πατρὸς καὶ προσέχετε γνῶναι ἔννοιαν

text_en: I will give you a good gift, forsake not my law.
text_la: Donum bonum tribuam vobis : legem meam ne derelinquatis.
text_pt: Pois dou-vos boa doutrina; não deixeis a minha lei.
text_el: δῶρον γὰρ ἀγαθὸν δωροῦμαι ὑμῖν τὸν ἐμὸν νόμον μὴ ἐγκαταλίπητε

text_en: For I also was my father's son, tender, and as an only son in the sight of my mother:
text_la: Nam et ego filius fui patris mei, tenellus et unigenitus coram matre mea.
text_pt: Porque eu era filho tenro na companhia de meu pai, e único diante de minha mãe.
text_el: υἱὸς γὰρ ἐγενόμην κἀγὼ πατρὶ ὑπήκοος καὶ ἀγαπώμενος ἐν προσώπῳ μητρός

text_en: And he taught me, and said: Let your heart receive my words, keep my commandments, and you shall live.
text_la: Et docebat me, atque dicebat : Suscipiat verba mea cor tuum; custodi præcepta mea, et vives.
text_pt: E ele me ensinava e me dizia: Retenha o teu coração as minhas palavras; guarda os meus mandamentos, e vive.
text_el: οἳ ἔλεγον καὶ ἐδίδασκόν με ἐρειδέτω ὁ ἡμέτερος λόγος εἰς σὴν καρδίαν

text_en: Get wisdom, get prudence : forget not, neither decline from the words of my mouth.
text_la: Posside sapientiam, posside prudentiam : ne obliviscaris, neque declines a verbis oris mei.
text_pt: Adquire sabedoria, adquire inteligência, e não te esqueças nem te apartes das palavras da minha boca.
text_el: φύλασσε ἐντολάς μὴ ἐπιλάθῃ μηδὲ παρίδῃς ῥῆσιν ἐμοῦ στόματος

text_en: Forsake her not, and she shall keep you: love her, and she shall preserve you.
text_la: Ne dimittas eam, et custodiet te : dilige eam, et conservabit te.
text_pt: Não a abandones e ela te guardará; ama-a, e ela te protegerá.
text_el: μηδὲ ἐγκαταλίπῃς αὐτήν καὶ ἀνθέξεταί σου ἐράσθητι αὐτῆς καὶ τηρήσει σε

text_en: The beginning of wisdom, get wisdom, and with all your possession purchase prudence .
text_la: Principium sapientiæ : posside sapientiam, et in omni possessione tua acquire prudentiam.
text_pt: A sabedoria é a coisa principal; adquire pois a sabedoria, emprega tudo o que possuis na aquisição de entendimento.

text_en: Take hold on her, and she shall exalt you: you shall be glorified by her, when you shall embrace her.
text_la: Arripe illam, et exaltabit te; glorificaberis ab ea cum eam fueris amplexatus.
text_pt: Exalta-a, e ela te exaltará; e, abraçando-a tu, ela te honrará.
text_el: περιχαράκωσον αὐτήν καὶ ὑψώσει σε τίμησον αὐτήν ἵνα σε περιλάβῃ

text_en: She shall give to your head increase of graces , and protect you with a noble crown.
text_la: Dabit capiti tuo augmenta gratiarum, et corona inclyta proteget te.
text_pt: Dará à tua cabeça um diadema de graça e uma coroa de glória te entregará.
text_el: ἵνα δῷ τῇ σῇ κεφαλῇ στέφανον χαρίτων στεφάνῳ δὲ τρυφῆς ὑπερασπίσῃ σου

text_en: Hear, O my son, and receive my words, that years of life may be multiplied to you.
text_la: Audi, fili mi, et suscipe verba mea, ut multiplicentur tibi anni vitæ.
text_pt: Ouve, filho meu, e aceita as minhas palavras, e se multiplicarão os anos da tua vida.
text_el: ἄκουε υἱέ καὶ δέξαι ἐμοὺς λόγους καὶ πληθυνθήσεται ἔτη ζωῆς σου ἵνα σοι γένωνται πολλαὶ ὁδοὶ βίου

text_en: I will show you the way of wisdom, I will lead you by the paths of equity:
text_la: Viam sapientiæ monstrabo tibi; ducam te per semitas æquitatis :
text_pt: No caminho da sabedoria te ensinei, e por veredas de retidão te fiz andar.
text_el: ὁδοὺς γὰρ σοφίας διδάσκω σε ἐμβιβάζω δέ σε τροχιαῖς ὀρθαῖς

text_en: Which when you shall have entered, your steps shall not be straitened, and when you run, you shall not meet a stumbling block.
text_la: quas cum ingressus fueris, non arctabuntur gressus tui, et currens non habebis offendiculum.
text_pt: Por elas andando, não se embaraçarão os teus passos; e se correres não tropeçarás.
text_el: ἐὰν γὰρ πορεύῃ οὐ συγκλεισθήσεταί σου τὰ διαβήματα ἐὰν δὲ τρέχῃς οὐ κοπιάσεις

text_en: Take hold on instruction, leave it not: keep it, because it is your life.
text_la: Tene disciplinam, ne dimittas eam; custodi illam, quia ipsa est vita tua.
text_pt: Apega-te à instrução e não a largues; guarda-a, porque ela é a tua vida.
text_el: ἐπιλαβοῦ ἐμῆς παιδείας μὴ ἀφῇς ἀλλὰ φύλαξον αὐτὴν σεαυτῷ εἰς ζωήν σου

text_en: Be not delighted in the paths of the wicked , neither let the way of evil men please you.
text_la: Ne delecteris in semitis impiorum, nec tibi placeat malorum via.
text_pt: Não entres pela vereda dos ímpios, nem andes no caminho dos maus.
text_el: ὁδοὺς ἀσεβῶν μὴ ἐπέλθῃς μηδὲ ζηλώσῃς ὁδοὺς παρανόμων

text_en: Flee from it, pass not by it: go aside, and forsake it.
text_la: Fuge ab ea, nec transeas per illam; declina, et desere eam.
text_pt: Evita-o; não passes por ele; desvia-te dele e passa de largo.
text_el: ἐν ᾧ ἂν τόπῳ στρατοπεδεύσωσιν μὴ ἐπέλθῃς ἐκεῖ ἔκκλινον δὲ ἀπ' αὐτῶν καὶ παράλλαξον

text_en: For they sleep not, except they have done evil : and their sleep is taken away unless they have made some to fall.
text_la: Non enim dormiunt nisi malefecerint, et rapitur somnus ab eis nisi supplantaverint.
text_pt: Pois não dormem, se não fizerem mal, e foge deles o sono se não fizerem alguém tropeçar.
text_el: οὐ γὰρ μὴ ὑπνώσωσιν ἐὰν μὴ κακοποιήσωσιν ἀφῄρηται ὁ ὕπνος αὐτῶν καὶ οὐ κοιμῶνται

text_en: They eat the bread of wickedness , and drink the wine of iniquity .
text_la: Comedunt panem impietatis, et vinum iniquitatis bibunt.
text_pt: Porque comem o pão da impiedade, e bebem o vinho da violência.
text_el: οἵδε γὰρ σιτοῦνται σῖτα ἀσεβείας οἴνῳ δὲ παρανόμῳ μεθύσκονται

text_en: But the path of the just , as a shining light, goes forwards, and increases even to perfect day.
text_la: Justorum autem semita quasi lux splendens procedit, et crescit usque ad perfectam diem.
text_pt: Mas a vereda dos justos é como a luz da aurora, que vai brilhando mais e mais até ser dia perfeito.
text_el: αἱ δὲ ὁδοὶ τῶν δικαίων ὁμοίως φωτὶ λάμπουσιν προπορεύονται καὶ φωτίζουσιν ἕως κατορθώσῃ ἡ ἡμέρα

text_en: The way of the wicked is darksome: they know not where they fall.
text_la: Via impiorum tenebrosa; nesciunt ubi corruant.
text_pt: O caminho dos ímpios é como a escuridão; nem sabem em que tropeçam.
text_el: αἱ δὲ ὁδοὶ τῶν ἀσεβῶν σκοτειναί οὐκ οἴδασιν πῶς προσκόπτουσιν

text_en: My son, hearken to my words, and incline your ear to my sayings.
text_la: Fili mi, ausculta sermones meos, et ad eloquia mea inclina aurem tuam.
text_pt: Filho meu, atenta para as minhas palavras; às minhas razões inclina o teu ouvido.
text_el: υἱέ ἐμῇ ῥήσει πρόσεχε τοῖς δὲ ἐμοῖς λόγοις παράβαλε σὸν οὖς

text_en: Let them not depart from your eyes, keep them in the midst of your heart:
text_la: Ne recedant ab oculis tuis : custodi ea in medio cordis tui :
text_pt: Não as deixes apartar-se dos teus olhos; guarda-as no íntimo do teu coração.
text_el: ὅπως μὴ ἐκλίπωσίν σε αἱ πηγαί σου φύλασσε αὐτὰς ἐν σῇ καρδίᾳ

text_en: For they are life to those that find them, and health to all flesh.
text_la: vita enim sunt invenientibus ea, et universæ carni sanitas.
text_pt: Porque são vida para os que as acham, e saúde para todo o seu corpo.
text_el: ζωὴ γάρ ἐστιν τοῖς εὑρίσκουσιν αὐτὰς καὶ πάσῃ σαρκὶ ἴασις

text_en: With all watchfulness keep your heart, because life issues out from it.
text_la: Omni custodia serva cor tuum, quia ex ipso vita procedit.
text_pt: Sobre tudo o que se deve guardar, guarda o teu coração, porque dele procedem as fontes da vida.
text_el: πάσῃ φυλακῇ τήρει σὴν καρδίαν ἐκ γὰρ τούτων ἔξοδοι ζωῆς

text_en: Remove from you a froward mouth, and let detracting lips be far from you.
text_la: Remove a te os pravum, et detrahentia labia sint procul a te.
text_pt: Desvia de ti a falsidade da boca, e afasta de ti a perversidade dos lábios.
text_el: περίελε σεαυτοῦ σκολιὸν στόμα καὶ ἄδικα χείλη μακρὰν ἀπὸ σοῦ ἄπωσαι

text_en: Let your eyes look straight on, and let your eyelids go before your steps.
text_la: Oculi tui recta videant, et palpebræ tuæ præcedant gressus tuos.
text_pt: Os teus olhos olhem para a frente, e as tuas pálpebras olhem direto diante de ti.
text_el: οἱ ὀφθαλμοί σου ὀρθὰ βλεπέτωσαν τὰ δὲ βλέφαρά σου νευέτω δίκαια

text_en: Make straight the path for your feet, and all your ways shall be established.
text_la: Dirige semitam pedibus tuis, et omnes viæ tuæ stabilientur.
text_pt: Pondera a vereda de teus pés, e todos os teus caminhos sejam bem ordenados!
text_el: ὀρθὰς τροχιὰς ποίει σοῖς ποσὶν καὶ τὰς ὁδούς σου κατεύθυνε

text_en: Decline not to the right hand, nor to the left: turn away your foot from evil . For the Lord knows the ways that are on the right hand: but those are perverse which are on the left hand. But he will make your courses straight, he will bring forward your ways in peace.
text_la: Ne declines ad dexteram neque ad sinistram; averte pedem tuum a malo : vias enim quæ a dextris sunt novit Dominus : perversæ vero sunt quæ a sinistris sunt. Ipse autem rectos faciet cursus tuos, itinera autem tua in pace producet.
text_pt: Não declines nem para a direita nem para a esquerda; retira o teu pé do mal.
text_el: μὴ ἐκκλίνῃς εἰς τὰ δεξιὰ μηδὲ εἰς τὰ ἀριστερά ἀπόστρεψον δὲ σὸν πόδα ἀπὸ ὁδοῦ κακῆς

text_en: My son, attend to my wisdom, and incline your ear to my prudence ,
text_la: Fili mi, attende ad sapientiam meam, et prudentiæ meæ inclina aurem tuam :
text_pt: Filho meu, atende à minha sabedoria; à minha inteligência inclina o teu ouvido;
text_el: υἱέ ἐμῇ σοφίᾳ πρόσεχε ἐμοῖς δὲ λόγοις παράβαλλε σὸν οὖς

text_en: that you may keep thoughts, and your lips may preserve instruction. Mind not the deceit of a woman .
text_la: ut custodias cogitationes, et disciplinam labia tua conservent. Ne attendas fallaciæ mulieris;
text_pt: Para que guardes os meus conselhos e os teus lábios observem o conhecimento.
text_el: ἵνα φυλάξῃς ἔννοιαν ἀγαθήν αἴσθησιν δὲ ἐμῶν χειλέων ἐντέλλομαί σοι

text_en: For the lips of a harlot are like a honeycomb dropping, and her throat is smoother than oil.
text_la: favus enim distillans labia meretricis, et nitidius oleo guttur ejus :
text_pt: Porque os lábios da mulher estranha destilam favos de mel, e o seu paladar é mais suave do que o azeite.
text_el: μὴ πρόσεχε φαύλῃ γυναικί μέλι γὰρ ἀποστάζει ἀπὸ χειλέων γυναικὸς πόρνης ἣ πρὸς καιρὸν λιπαίνει σὸν φάρυγγα

text_en: But her end is bitter as wormwood , and sharp as a two-edged sword.
text_la: novissima autem illius amara quasi absinthium, et acuta quasi gladius biceps.
text_pt: Mas o seu fim é amargoso como o absinto, agudo como a espada de dois gumes.
text_el: ὕστερον μέντοι πικρότερον χολῆς εὑρήσεις καὶ ἠκονημένον μᾶλλον μαχαίρας διστόμου

text_en: Her feet go down into death, and her steps go in as far as hell.
text_la: Pedes ejus descendunt in mortem, et ad inferos gressus illius penetrant.
text_pt: Os seus pés descem para a morte; os seus passos estão impregnados do inferno.
text_el: τῆς γὰρ ἀφροσύνης οἱ πόδες κατάγουσιν τοὺς χρωμένους αὐτῇ μετὰ θανάτου εἰς τὸν ᾅδην τὰ δὲ ἴχνη αὐτῆς οὐκ ἐρείδεται

text_en: They walk not by the path of life, her steps are wandering, and unaccountable.
text_la: Per semitam vitæ non ambulant; vagi sunt gressus ejus et investigabiles.
text_pt: Para que não ponderes os caminhos da vida, as suas andanças são errantes: jamais os conhecerás.
text_el: ὁδοὺς γὰρ ζωῆς οὐκ ἐπέρχεται σφαλεραὶ δὲ αἱ τροχιαὶ αὐτῆς καὶ οὐκ εὔγνωστοι

text_en: Now, therefore, my son, hear me, and depart not from the words of my mouth.
text_la: Nunc ergo fili mi, audi me, et ne recedas a verbis oris mei.
text_pt: Agora, pois, filhos, dai-me ouvidos, e não vos desvieis das palavras da minha boca.
text_el: νῦν οὖν υἱέ ἄκουέ μου καὶ μὴ ἀκύρους ποιήσῃς ἐμοὺς λόγους

text_en: Remove your way far from her, and come not near the doors of her house.
text_la: Longe fac ab ea viam tuam, et ne appropinques foribus domus ejus.
text_pt: Longe dela seja o teu caminho, e não te chegues à porta da sua casa;
text_el: μακρὰν ποίησον ἀπ' αὐτῆς σὴν ὁδόν μὴ ἐγγίσῃς πρὸς θύραις οἴκων αὐτῆς

text_en: Give not your honour to strangers, and your years to the cruel.
text_la: Ne des alienis honorem tuum, et annos tuos crudeli :
text_pt: Para que não dês a outrem a tua honra, e não entregues a cruéis os teus anos de vida;
text_el: ἵνα μὴ πρόῃ ἄλλοις ζωήν σου καὶ σὸν βίον ἀνελεήμοσιν

text_en: Lest strangers be filled with your strength, and your labours be in another man's house,
text_la: ne forte implentur extranei viribus tuis, et labores tui sint in domo aliena,
text_pt: Para que não farte a estranhos o teu esforço, e todo o fruto do teu trabalho vá parar em casa alheia;
text_el: ἵνα μὴ πλησθῶσιν ἀλλότριοι σῆς ἰσχύος οἱ δὲ σοὶ πόνοι εἰς οἴκους ἀλλοτρίων εἰσέλθωσιν

text_en: and you mourn at the last, when you shall have spent your flesh and your body, and say,
text_la: et gemas in novissimis, quando consumpseris carnes tuas et corpus tuum, et dicas :
text_pt: E no fim venhas a gemer, no consumir-se da tua carne e do teu corpo.
text_el: καὶ μεταμεληθήσῃ ἐπ' ἐσχάτων ἡνίκα ἂν κατατριβῶσιν σάρκες σώματός σου

text_en: Why have I hated instruction, and my heart consented not to reproof,
text_la: Cur detestatus sum disciplinam, et increpationibus non acquievit cor meum,
text_pt: E então digas: Como odiei a correção! e o meu coração desprezou a repreensão!
text_el: καὶ ἐρεῖς πῶς ἐμίσησα παιδείαν καὶ ἐλέγχους ἐξέκλινεν ἡ καρδία μου

text_en: and have not heard the voice of them that taught me, and have not inclined my ear to masters?
text_la: nec audivi vocem docentium me, et magistris non inclinavi aurem meam?
text_pt: E não escutei a voz dos que me ensinavam, nem aos meus mestres inclinei o meu ouvido!
text_el: οὐκ ἤκουον φωνὴν παιδεύοντός με καὶ διδάσκοντός με οὐδὲ παρέβαλλον τὸ οὖς μου

text_en: I have almost been in all evil , in the midst of the church and of the congregation.
text_la: pene fui in omni malo, in medio ecclesiæ et synagogæ.
text_pt: No meio da congregação e da assembléia foi que eu me achei em quase todo o mal.
text_el: παρ' ὀλίγον ἐγενόμην ἐν παντὶ κακῷ ἐν μέσῳ ἐκκλησίας καὶ συναγωγῆς

text_en: Drink water out of your own cistern , and the streams of your own well :
text_la: Bibe aquam de cisterna tua, et fluenta putei tui;
text_pt: Bebe água da tua fonte, e das correntes do teu poço.
text_el: πῖνε ὕδατα ἀπὸ σῶν ἀγγείων καὶ ἀπὸ σῶν φρεάτων πηγῆς

text_en: Let your fountains be conveyed abroad, and in the streets divide your waters.
text_la: deriventur fontes tui foras, et in plateis aquas tuas divide.
text_pt: Derramar-se-iam as tuas fontes por fora, e pelas ruas os ribeiros de águas?
text_el: μὴ ὑπερεκχείσθω σοι τὰ ὕδατα ἐκ τῆς σῆς πηγῆς εἰς δὲ σὰς πλατείας διαπορευέσθω τὰ σὰ ὕδατα

text_en: Keep them to yourself alone, neither let strangers be partakers with you.
text_la: Habeto eas solus, nec sint alieni participes tui.
text_pt: Sejam para ti só, e não para os estranhos contigo.
text_el: ἔστω σοι μόνῳ ὑπάρχοντα καὶ μηδεὶς ἀλλότριος μετασχέτω σοι

text_en: Let your vein be blessed , and rejoice with the wife of your youth:
text_la: Sit vena tua benedicta, et lætare cum muliere adolescentiæ tuæ.
text_pt: Seja bendito o teu manancial, e alegra-te com a mulher da tua mocidade.
text_el: ἡ πηγή σου τοῦ ὕδατος ἔστω σοι ἰδία καὶ συνευφραίνου μετὰ γυναικὸς τῆς ἐκ νεότητός σου

text_en: Let her be your dearest hind, and most agreeable fawn: let her breasts inebriate you at all times: be delighted continually with her love .
text_la: Cerva carissima, et gratissimus hinnulus : ubera ejus inebrient te in omni tempore; in amore ejus delectare jugiter.
text_pt: Como cerva amorosa, e gazela graciosa, os seus seios te saciem todo o tempo; e pelo seu amor sejas atraído perpetuamente.
text_el: ἔλαφος φιλίας καὶ πῶλος σῶν χαρίτων ὁμιλείτω σοι ἡ δὲ ἰδία ἡγείσθω σου καὶ συνέστω σοι ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ ἐν γὰρ τῇ ταύτης φιλίᾳ συμπεριφερόμενος πολλοστὸς ἔσῃ

text_en: Why are you seduced , my son, by a strange woman , and are cherished in the bosom of another?
text_la: Quare seduceris, fili mi, ab aliena, et foveris in sinu alterius?
text_pt: E porque, filho meu, te deixarias atrair por outra mulher, e te abraçarias ao peito de uma estranha?
text_el: μὴ πολὺς ἴσθι πρὸς ἀλλοτρίαν μηδὲ συνέχου ἀγκάλαις τῆς μὴ ἰδίας

text_en: The Lord beholds the ways of man , and considers all his steps.
text_la: Respicit Dominus vias hominis, et omnes gressus ejus considerat.
text_pt: Eis que os caminhos do homem estão perante os olhos do Senhor, e ele pesa todas as suas veredas.
text_el: ἐνώπιον γάρ εἰσιν τῶν τοῦ θεοῦ ὀφθαλμῶν ὁδοὶ ἀνδρός εἰς δὲ πάσας τὰς τροχιὰς αὐτοῦ σκοπεύει

text_en: His own iniquities catch the wicked , and he is fast bound with the ropes of his own sins .
text_la: Iniquitates suas capiunt impium, et funibus peccatorum suorum constringitur.
text_pt: Quanto ao ímpio, as suas iniqüidades o prenderão, e com as cordas do seu pecado será detido.
text_el: παρανομίαι ἄνδρα ἀγρεύουσιν σειραῖς δὲ τῶν ἑαυτοῦ ἁμαρτιῶν ἕκαστος σφίγγεται

text_en: He shall die, because he has not received instruction, and in the multitude of his folly he shall be deceived.
text_la: Ipse morietur, quia non habuit disciplinam, et in multitudine stultitiæ suæ decipietur.
text_pt: Ele morrerá, porque desavisadamente andou, e pelo excesso da sua loucura se perderá.
text_el: οὗτος τελευτᾷ μετὰ ἀπαιδεύτων ἐκ δὲ πλήθους τῆς ἑαυτοῦ βιότητος ἐξερρίφη καὶ ἀπώλετο δι' ἀφροσύνην

text_en: My son, if you be surety for your friend, you have engaged fast your hand to a stranger,
text_la: Fili mi, si spoponderis pro amico tuo, defixisti apud extraneum manum tuam :
text_pt: Filho meu, se ficaste por fiador do teu companheiro, se deste a tua mão ao estranho,
text_el: υἱέ ἐὰν ἐγγυήσῃ σὸν φίλον παραδώσεις σὴν χεῖρα ἐχθρῷ

text_en: you are ensnared with the words of your mouth, and caught with your own words.
text_la: illaqueatus es verbis oris tui, et captus propriis sermonibus.
text_pt: E te deixaste enredar pelas próprias palavras; e te prendeste nas palavras da tua boca;
text_el: παγὶς γὰρ ἰσχυρὰ ἀνδρὶ τὰ ἴδια χείλη καὶ ἁλίσκεται χείλεσιν ἰδίου στόματος

text_en: Do, therefore, my son, what I say, and deliver yourself: because you are fallen into the hand of your neighbour. Run about, make haste, stir up your friend:
text_la: Fac ergo quod dico, fili mi, et temetipsum libera, quia incidisti in manum proximi tui. Discurre, festina, suscita amicum tuum.
text_pt: Faze pois isto agora, filho meu, e livra-te, já que caíste nas mãos do teu companheiro: vai, humilha-te, e importuna o teu companheiro.
text_el: ποίει υἱέ ἃ ἐγώ σοι ἐντέλλομαι καὶ σῴζου ἥκεις γὰρ εἰς χεῖρας κακῶν διὰ σὸν φίλον ἴθι μὴ ἐκλυόμενος παρόξυνε δὲ καὶ τὸν φίλον σου ὃν ἐνεγυήσω

text_en: Give not sleep to your eyes, neither let your eyelids slumber.
text_la: Ne dederis somnum oculis tuis, nec dormitent palpebræ tuæ.
text_pt: Não dês sono aos teus olhos, nem deixes adormecer as tuas pálpebras.
text_el: μὴ δῷς ὕπνον σοῖς ὄμμασιν μηδὲ ἐπινυστάξῃς σοῖς βλεφάροις

text_en: Deliver yourself as a doe from the hand, and as a bird from the hand of the fowler.
text_la: Eruere quasi damula de manu, et quasi avis de manu aucupis.
text_pt: Livra-te, como a gazela da mão do caçador, e como a ave da mão do passarinheiro.
text_el: ἵνα σῴζῃ ὥσπερ δορκὰς ἐκ βρόχων καὶ ὥσπερ ὄρνεον ἐκ παγίδος

text_en: Go to the ant, O sluggard, and consider her ways, and learn wisdom:
text_la: Vade ad formicam, o piger, et considera vias ejus, et disce sapientiam.
text_pt: Vai ter com a formiga, ó preguiçoso; olha para os seus caminhos, e sê sábio.
text_el: ἴθι πρὸς τὸν μύρμηκα ὦ ὀκνηρέ καὶ ζήλωσον ἰδὼν τὰς ὁδοὺς αὐτοῦ καὶ γενοῦ ἐκείνου σοφώτερος

text_en: Which, although she has no guide, nor master, nor captain ,
text_la: Quæ cum non habeat ducem, nec præceptorem, nec principem,
text_pt: Pois ela, não tendo chefe, nem guarda, nem dominador,
text_el: ἐκείνῳ γὰρ γεωργίου μὴ ὑπάρχοντος μηδὲ τὸν ἀναγκάζοντα ἔχων μηδὲ ὑπὸ δεσπότην ὢν

text_en: provides her meat for herself in the summer, and gathers her food in the harvest.
text_la: parat in æstate cibum sibi, et congregat in messe quod comedat.
text_pt: Prepara no verão o seu pão; na sega ajunta o seu mantimento.
text_el: ἑτοιμάζεται θέρους τὴν τροφὴν πολλήν τε ἐν τῷ ἀμήτῳ ποιεῖται τὴν παράθεσιν

text_en: How long will you sleep, O sluggard? When will you arise out of your sleep?
text_la: Usquequo, piger, dormies? quando consurges e somno tuo?
text_pt: Ó preguiçoso, até quando ficarás deitado? Quando te levantarás do teu sono?
text_el: ἕως τίνος ὀκνηρέ κατάκεισαι πότε δὲ ἐξ ὕπνου ἐγερθήσῃ

text_en: You will sleep a little, you will slumber a little, you will fold your hands a little to sleep:
text_la: Paululum dormies, paululum dormitabis, paululum conseres manus ut dormias;
text_pt: Um pouco a dormir, um pouco a tosquenejar; um pouco a repousar de braços cruzados;
text_el: ὀλίγον μὲν ὑπνοῖς ὀλίγον δὲ κάθησαι μικρὸν δὲ νυστάζεις ὀλίγον δὲ ἐναγκαλίζῃ χερσὶν στήθη

text_en: And want shall come upon you, as a traveller, and poverty as a man armed. But if you be diligent, your harvest shall come as a fountain, and want shall flee far from you.
text_la: et veniet tibi quasi viator egestas, et pauperies quasi vir armatus. Si vero impiger fueris, veniet ut fons messis tua, et egestas longe fugiet a te.
text_pt: Assim sobrevirá a tua pobreza como o meliante, e a tua necessidade como um homem armado.
text_el: εἶτ' ἐμπαραγίνεταί σοι ὥσπερ κακὸς ὁδοιπόρος ἡ πενία καὶ ἡ ἔνδεια ὥσπερ ἀγαθὸς δρομεύς

text_en: A man that is an apostate, an unprofitable man , walks with a perverse mouth,
text_la: Homo apostata, vir inutilis, graditur ore perverso;
text_pt: O homem mau, o homem iníquo tem a boca pervertida.
text_el: ἀνὴρ ἄφρων καὶ παράνομος πορεύεται ὁδοὺς οὐκ ἀγαθάς

text_en: he winks with the eyes, presses with the foot, speaks with the finger.
text_la: annuit oculis, terit pede, digito loquitur,
text_pt: Acena com os olhos, fala com os pés e faz sinais com os dedos.
text_el: ὁ δ' αὐτὸς ἐννεύει ὀφθαλμῷ σημαίνει δὲ ποδί διδάσκει δὲ ἐννεύμασιν δακτύλων

text_en: With a wicked heart he devises evil , and at all times he sows discord.
text_la: pravo corde machinatur malum, et omni tempore jurgia seminat.
text_pt: Há no seu coração perversidade, todo o tempo maquina mal; anda semeando contendas.
text_el: διεστραμμένῃ δὲ καρδίᾳ τεκταίνεται κακὰ ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ ὁ τοιοῦτος ταραχὰς συνίστησιν πόλει

text_en: To such a one his destruction shall presently come, and he shall suddenly be destroyed, and shall no longer have any remedy.
text_la: Huic extemplo veniet perditio sua, et subito conteretur, nec habebit ultra medicinam.
text_pt: Por isso a sua destruição virá repentinamente; subitamente será quebrantado, sem que haja cura.
text_el: διὰ τοῦτο ἐξαπίνης ἔρχεται ἡ ἀπώλεια αὐτοῦ διακοπὴ καὶ συντριβὴ ἀνίατος

text_en: Six things there are, which the Lord hates , and the seventh his soul detests:
text_la: Sex sunt quæ odit Dominus, et septimum detestatur anima ejus :
text_pt: Estas seis coisas o Senhor odeia, e a sétima a sua alma abomina:
text_el: ὅτι χαίρει πᾶσιν οἷς μισεῖ ὁ κύριος συντρίβεται δὲ δι' ἀκαθαρσίαν ψυχῆς

text_en: Haughty eyes, a lying tongue, hands that shed innocent blood,
text_la: oculos sublimes, linguam mendacem, manus effundentes innoxium sanguinem,
text_pt: Olhos altivos, língua mentirosa, mãos que derramam sangue inocente,
text_el: ὀφθαλμὸς ὑβριστοῦ γλῶσσα ἄδικος χεῖρες ἐκχέουσαι αἷμα δικαίου

text_en: a heart that devises wicked plots, feet that are swift to run into mischief,
text_la: cor machinans cogitationes pessimas, pedes veloces ad currendum in malum,
text_pt: O coração que maquina pensamentos perversos, pés que se apressam a correr para o mal,
text_el: καὶ καρδία τεκταινομένη λογισμοὺς κακοὺς καὶ πόδες ἐπισπεύδοντες κακοποιεῖν

text_en: a deceitful witness that utters lies, and him that sows discord among brethren.
text_la: proferentem mendacia testem fallacem, et eum qui seminat inter fratres discordias.
text_pt: A testemunha falsa que profere mentiras, e o que semeia contendas entre irmãos.
text_el: ἐκκαίει ψεύδη μάρτυς ἄδικος καὶ ἐπιπέμπει κρίσεις ἀνὰ μέσον ἀδελφῶν

text_en: My son, keep the commandments of your father, and forsake not the law of your mother.
text_la: Conserva, fili mi, præcepta patris tui, et ne dimittas legem matris tuæ.
text_pt: Filho meu, guarda o mandamento de teu pai, e não deixes a lei da tua mãe;
text_el: υἱέ φύλασσε νόμους πατρός σου καὶ μὴ ἀπώσῃ θεσμοὺς μητρός σου

text_en: Bind them in your heart continually, and put them about your neck.
text_la: Liga ea in corde tuo jugiter, et circumda gutturi tuo.
text_pt: Ata-os perpetuamente ao teu coração, e pendura-os ao teu pescoço.
text_el: ἄφαψαι δὲ αὐτοὺς ἐπὶ σῇ ψυχῇ διὰ παντὸς καὶ ἐγκλοίωσαι ἐπὶ σῷ τραχήλῳ

text_en: When you walk, let them go with you: when you sleep, let them keep you, and when you awaken, talk with them.
text_la: Cum ambulaveris, gradiantur tecum; cum dormieris, custodiant te : et evigilans loquere cum eis.
text_pt: Quando caminhares, te guiará; quando te deitares, te guardará; quando acordares, falará contigo.
text_el: ἡνίκα ἂν περιπατῇς ἐπάγου αὐτήν καὶ μετὰ σοῦ ἔστω ὡς δ' ἂν καθεύδῃς φυλασσέτω σε ἵνα ἐγειρομένῳ συλλαλῇ σοι

text_en: Because the commandment is a lamp, and the law a light, and reproofs of instruction are the way of life:
text_la: Quia mandatum lucerna est, et lex lux, et via vitæ increpatio disciplinæ :
text_pt: Porque o mandamento é lâmpada, e a lei é luz; e as repreensões da correção são o caminho da vida,
text_el: ὅτι λύχνος ἐντολὴ νόμου καὶ φῶς καὶ ὁδὸς ζωῆς ἔλεγχος καὶ παιδεία

text_en: That they may keep you from the evil woman , and from the flattering tongue of the stranger.
text_la: ut custodiant te a muliere mala, et a blanda lingua extraneæ.
text_pt: Para te guardarem da mulher vil, e das lisonjas da estranha.
text_el: τοῦ διαφυλάσσειν σε ἀπὸ γυναικὸς ὑπάνδρου καὶ ἀπὸ διαβολῆς γλώσσης ἀλλοτρίας

text_en: Let not your heart covet her beauty, be not caught with her winks:
text_la: Non concupiscat pulchritudinem ejus cor tuum, nec capiaris nutibus illius :
text_pt: Não cobices no teu coração a sua formosura, nem te prendas aos seus olhos.
text_el: μή σε νικήσῃ κάλλους ἐπιθυμία μηδὲ ἀγρευθῇς σοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς μηδὲ συναρπασθῇς ἀπὸ τῶν αὐτῆς βλεφάρων

text_en: For the price of a harlot is scarce one loaf: but the woman catches the precious soul of a man .
text_la: pretium enim scorti vix est unius panis, mulier autem viri pretiosam animam capit.
text_pt: Porque por causa duma prostituta se chega a pedir um bocado de pão; e a adúltera anda à caça da alma preciosa.
text_el: τιμὴ γὰρ πόρνης ὅση καὶ ἑνὸς ἄρτου γυνὴ δὲ ἀνδρῶν τιμίας ψυχὰς ἀγρεύει

text_en: Can a man hide fire in his bosom, and his garments not burn?
text_la: Numquid potest homo abscondere ignem in sinu suo, ut vestimenta illius non ardeant?
text_pt: Porventura tomará alguém fogo no seu seio, sem que suas vestes se queimem?
text_el: ἀποδήσει τις πῦρ ἐν κόλπῳ τὰ δὲ ἱμάτια οὐ κατακαύσει

text_en: Or can he walk upon hot coals, and his feet not be burnt?
text_la: aut ambulare super prunas, ut non comburantur plantæ ejus?
text_pt: Ou andará alguém sobre brasas, sem que se queimem os seus pés?
text_el: ἢ περιπατήσει τις ἐπ' ἀνθράκων πυρός τοὺς δὲ πόδας οὐ κατακαύσει

text_en: So he that goes in to his neighbour's wife, shall not be clean when he shall touch her.
text_la: sic qui ingreditur ad mulierem proximi sui, non erit mundus cum tetigerit eam.
text_pt: Assim ficará o que entrar à mulher do seu próximo; não será inocente todo aquele que a tocar.
text_el: οὕτως ὁ εἰσελθὼν πρὸς γυναῖκα ὕπανδρον οὐκ ἀθῳωθήσεται οὐδὲ πᾶς ὁ ἁπτόμενος αὐτῆς

text_en: The fault is not so great when a man has stolen: for he steals to fill his hungry soul :
text_la: Non grandis est culpa cum quis furatus fuerit : furatur enim ut esurientem impleat animam;
text_pt: Não se injuria o ladrão, quando furta para saciar-se, tendo fome;
text_el: οὐ θαυμαστὸν ἐὰν ἁλῷ τις κλέπτων κλέπτει γὰρ ἵνα ἐμπλήσῃ τὴν ψυχὴν πεινῶν

text_en: And if he be taken, he shall restore sevenfold, and shall give up all the substance of his house.
text_la: deprehensus quoque reddet septuplum, et omnem substantiam domus suæ tradet.
text_pt: E se for achado pagará o tanto sete vezes; terá de dar todos os bens da sua casa.
text_el: ἐὰν δὲ ἁλῷ ἀποτείσει ἑπταπλάσια καὶ πάντα τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ δοὺς ῥύσεται ἑαυτόν

text_en: But he that is an adulterer, for the folly of his heart shall destroy his own soul :
text_la: Qui autem adulter est, propter cordis inopiam perdet animam suam;
text_pt: Assim, o que adultera com uma mulher é falto de entendimento; aquele que faz isso destrói a sua alma.
text_el: ὁ δὲ μοιχὸς δι' ἔνδειαν φρενῶν ἀπώλειαν τῇ ψυχῇ αὐτοῦ περιποιεῖται

text_en: He gathers to himself shame and dishonour, and his reproach shall not be blotted out:
text_la: turpitudinem et ignominiam congregat sibi, et opprobrium illius non delebitur :
text_pt: Achará castigo e vilipêndio, e o seu opróbrio nunca se apagará.
text_el: ὀδύνας τε καὶ ἀτιμίας ὑποφέρει τὸ δὲ ὄνειδος αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἐξαλειφθήσεται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα

text_en: Because the jealousy and rage of the husband will not spare in the day of revenge,
text_la: quia zelus et furor viri non parcet in die vindictæ,
text_pt: Porque os ciúmes enfurecerão o marido; de maneira nenhuma perdoará no dia da vingança.
text_el: μεστὸς γὰρ ζήλου θυμὸς ἀνδρὸς αὐτῆς οὐ φείσεται ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως

text_en: nor will he yield to any man's prayers , nor will he accept for satisfaction ever so many gifts.
text_la: nec acquiescet cujusquam precibus, nec suscipiet pro redemptione dona plurima.
text_pt: Não aceitará nenhum resgate, nem se conformará por mais que aumentes os presentes.
text_el: οὐκ ἀνταλλάξεται οὐδενὸς λύτρου τὴν ἔχθραν οὐδὲ μὴ διαλυθῇ πολλῶν δώρων

text_en: My son, keep my words, and lay up my precepts with you. Son,
text_la: Fili mi, custodi sermones meos, et præcepta mea reconde tibi. Fili,
text_pt: Filho meu, guarda as minhas palavras, e esconde dentro de ti os meus mandamentos.
text_el: υἱέ φύλασσε ἐμοὺς λόγους τὰς δὲ ἐμὰς ἐντολὰς κρύψον παρὰ σεαυτῷ

text_en: Keep my commandments, and you shall live: and my law as the apple of your eye:
text_la: serva mandata mea, et vives; et legem meam quasi pupillam oculi tui :
text_pt: Guarda os meus mandamentos e vive; e a minha lei, como a menina dos teus olhos.
text_el: φύλαξον ἐμὰς ἐντολάς καὶ βιώσεις τοὺς δὲ ἐμοὺς λόγους ὥσπερ κόρας ὀμμάτων

text_en: Bind it upon your fingers, write it upon the tables of your heart.
text_la: liga eam in digitis tuis, scribe illam in tabulis cordis tui.
text_pt: Ata-os aos teus dedos, escreve-os na tábua do teu coração.
text_el: περίθου δὲ αὐτοὺς σοῖς δακτύλοις ἐπίγραψον δὲ ἐπὶ τὸ πλάτος τῆς καρδίας σου

text_en: Say to wisdom: You are my sister: and call prudence your friend,
text_la: Dic sapientiæ : Soror mea es, et prudentiam voca amicam tuam :
text_pt: Dize à sabedoria: Tu és minha irmã; e à prudência chama de tua parenta,
text_el: εἶπον τὴν σοφίαν σὴν ἀδελφὴν εἶναι τὴν δὲ φρόνησιν γνώριμον περιποίησαι σεαυτῷ

text_en: that she may keep you from the woman that is not yours, and from the stranger who sweetens her words.
text_la: ut custodiant te a muliere extranea, et ab aliena quæ verba sua dulcia facit.
text_pt: Para que elas te guardem da mulher alheia, da estranha que lisonjeia com as suas palavras.
text_el: ἵνα σε τηρήσῃ ἀπὸ γυναικὸς ἀλλοτρίας καὶ πονηρᾶς ἐάν σε λόγοις τοῖς πρὸς χάριν ἐμβάληται

text_en: For I looked out of the window of my house through the lattice,
text_la: De fenestra enim domus meæ per cancellos prospexi,
text_pt: Porque da janela da minha casa, olhando eu por minhas frestas,
text_el: ἀπὸ γὰρ θυρίδος ἐκ τοῦ οἴκου αὐτῆς εἰς τὰς πλατείας παρακύπτουσα

text_en: and I see little ones, I behold a foolish young man,
text_la: et video parvulos; considero vecordem juvenem,
text_pt: Vi entre os simples, descobri entre os moços, um moço falto de juízo,
text_el: ὃν ἂν ἴδῃ τῶν ἀφρόνων τέκνων νεανίαν ἐνδεῆ φρενῶν

text_en: who passes through the street by the corner, and goes near the way of her house,
text_la: qui transit per plateam juxta angulum et prope viam domus illius graditur:
text_pt: Que passava pela rua junto à sua esquina, e seguia o caminho da sua casa;
text_el: παραπορευόμενον παρὰ γωνίαν ἐν διόδοις οἴκων αὐτῆς

text_en: in the dark when it grows late, in the darkness and obscurity of the night.
text_la: in obscuro, advesperascente die, in noctis tenebris et caligine.
text_pt: No crepúsculo, à tarde do dia, na tenebrosa noite e na escuridão.
text_el: καὶ λαλοῦντα ἐν σκότει ἑσπερινῷ ἡνίκα ἂν ἡσυχία νυκτερινὴ ᾖ καὶ γνοφώδης

text_en: And behold a woman meets him in harlot's attire, prepared to deceive souls : talkative and wandering,
text_la: Et ecce occurrit illi mulier ornatu meretricio, præparata ad capiendas animas : garrula et vaga,
text_pt: E eis que uma mulher lhe saiu ao encontro com enfeites de prostituta, e astúcia de coração.
text_el: ἡ δὲ γυνὴ συναντᾷ αὐτῷ εἶδος ἔχουσα πορνικόν ἣ ποιεῖ νέων ἐξίπτασθαι καρδίας

text_en: not bearing to be quiet, not able to abide still at home,
text_la: quietis impatiens, nec valens in domo consistere pedibus suis;
text_pt: Estava alvoroçada e irrequieta; não paravam em sua casa os seus pés.
text_el: ἀνεπτερωμένη δέ ἐστιν καὶ ἄσωτος ἐν οἴκῳ δὲ οὐχ ἡσυχάζουσιν οἱ πόδες αὐτῆς

text_en: now abroad, now in the streets, now lying in wait near the corners.
text_la: nunc foris, nunc in plateis, nunc juxta angulos insidians.
text_pt: Foi para fora, depois pelas ruas, e ia espreitando por todos os cantos;
text_el: χρόνον γάρ τινα ἔξω ῥέμβεται χρόνον δὲ ἐν πλατείαις παρὰ πᾶσαν γωνίαν ἐνεδρεύει

text_en: And catching the young man, she kisses him, and with an impudent face, flatters, saying:
text_la: Apprehensumque deosculatur juvenem, et procaci vultu blanditur, dicens :
text_pt: E chegou-se para ele e o beijou. Com face impudente lhe disse:
text_el: εἶτα ἐπιλαβομένη ἐφίλησεν αὐτόν ἀναιδεῖ δὲ προσώπῳ προσεῖπεν αὐτῷ

text_en: I vowed victims for prosperity, this day I have paid my vows .
text_la: Victimas pro salute vovi; hodie reddidi vota mea :
text_pt: Sacrifícios pacíficos tenho comigo; hoje paguei os meus votos.
text_el: θυσία εἰρηνική μοί ἐστιν σήμερον ἀποδίδωμι τὰς εὐχάς μου

text_en: Therefore I have come out to meet you, desirous to see you, and I have found you.
text_la: idcirco egressa sum in occursum tuum, desiderans te videre, et reperi.
text_pt: Por isto saí ao teu encontro a buscar diligentemente a tua face, e te achei.
text_el: ἕνεκα τούτου ἐξῆλθον εἰς συνάντησίν σοι ποθοῦσα τὸ σὸν πρόσωπον εὕρηκά σε

text_en: I have woven my bed with cords, I have covered it with painted tapestry , brought from Egypt .
text_la: Intexui funibus lectulum meum; stravi tapetibus pictis ex Ægypto :
text_pt: Já cobri a minha cama com cobertas de tapeçaria, com obras lavradas, com linho fino do Egito.
text_el: κειρίαις τέτακα τὴν κλίνην μου ἀμφιτάποις δὲ ἔστρωκα τοῖς ἀπ' Αἰγύπτου

text_en: I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.
text_la: aspersi cubile meum myrrha, et aloë, et cinnamomo.
text_pt: Já perfumei o meu leito com mirra, aloés e canela.
text_el: διέρραγκα τὴν κοίτην μου κρόκῳ τὸν δὲ οἶκόν μου κινναμώμῳ

text_en: Come, let us be inebriated with the breasts, and let us enjoy the desired embraces, till the day appear.
text_la: Veni, inebriemur uberibus, et fruamur cupitis amplexibus donec illucescat dies.
text_pt: Vem, saciemo-nos de amores até à manhã; alegremo-nos com amores.
text_el: ἐλθὲ καὶ ἀπολαύσωμεν φιλίας ἕως ὄρθρου δεῦρο καὶ ἐγκυλισθῶμεν ἔρωτι

text_en: For my husband is not at home, he has gone a very long journey.
text_la: Non est enim vir in domo sua : abiit via longissima :
text_pt: Porque o marido não está em casa; foi fazer uma longa viagem;
text_el: οὐ γὰρ πάρεστιν ὁ ἀνήρ μου ἐν οἴκῳ πεπόρευται δὲ ὁδὸν μακρὰν

text_en: He took with him a bag of money: he will return home the day of the full moon.
text_la: sacculum pecuniæ secum tulit; in die plenæ lunæ reversurus est in domum suam.
text_pt: Levou na sua mão um saquitel de dinheiro; voltará para casa só no dia marcado.
text_el: ἔνδεσμον ἀργυρίου λαβὼν ἐν χειρὶ αὐτοῦ δι' ἡμερῶν πολλῶν ἐπανήξει εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ

text_en: She entangled him with many words, and drew him away with the flattery of her lips.
text_la: Irretivit eum multis sermonibus, et blanditiis labiorum protraxit illum.
text_pt: Assim, o seduziu com palavras muito suaves e o persuadiu com as lisonjas dos seus lábios.
text_el: ἀπεπλάνησεν δὲ αὐτὸν πολλῇ ὁμιλίᾳ βρόχοις τε τοῖς ἀπὸ χειλέων ἐξώκειλεν αὐτόν

text_en: Immediately he follows her as an ox led to be a victim, and as a lamb playing the wanton, and not knowing that he is drawn like a fool to bonds,
text_la: Statim eam sequitur quasi bos ductus ad victimam, et quasi agnus lasciviens, et ignorans quod ad vincula stultus trahatur :
text_pt: E ele logo a segue, como o boi que vai para o matadouro, e como vai o insensato para o castigo das prisões;
text_el: ὁ δὲ ἐπηκολούθησεν αὐτῇ κεπφωθείς ὥσπερ δὲ βοῦς ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἄγεται καὶ ὥσπερ κύων ἐπὶ δεσμοὺς

text_en: till the arrow pierce his liver: as if a bird should make haste to the snare, and knows not that his life is in danger.
text_la: donec transfigat sagitta jecur ejus, velut si avis festinet ad laqueum, et nescit quod de periculo animæ illius agitur.
text_pt: Até que a flecha lhe atravesse o fígado; ou como a ave que se apressa para o laço, e não sabe que está armado contra a sua vida.
text_el: ἢ ὡς ἔλαφος τοξεύματι πεπληγὼς εἰς τὸ ἧπαρ σπεύδει δὲ ὥσπερ ὄρνεον εἰς παγίδα οὐκ εἰδὼς ὅτι περὶ ψυχῆς τρέχει

text_en: Now, therefore, my son, hear me, and attend to the words of my mouth.
text_la: Nunc ergo, fili mi, audi me, et attende verbis oris mei.
text_pt: Agora pois, filhos, dai-me ouvidos, e estai atentos às palavras da minha boca.
text_el: νῦν οὖν υἱέ ἄκουέ μου καὶ πρόσεχε ῥήμασιν στόματός μου

text_en: Let not your mind be drawn away in her ways: neither be deceived with her paths.
text_la: Ne abstrahatur in viis illius mens tua, neque decipiaris semitis ejus;
text_pt: Não se desvie para os caminhos dela o teu coração, e não te deixes perder nas suas veredas.
text_el: μὴ ἐκκλινάτω εἰς τὰς ὁδοὺς αὐτῆς ἡ καρδία σου

text_en: For she has cast down many wounded, and the strongest have been slain by her.
text_la: multos enim vulneratos dejecit, et fortissimi quique interfecti sunt ab ea.
text_pt: Porque a muitos feridos derrubou; e são muitíssimos os que por causa dela foram mortos.
text_el: πολλοὺς γὰρ τρώσασα καταβέβληκεν καὶ ἀναρίθμητοί εἰσιν οὓς πεφόνευκεν

text_en: Her house is the way to hell, reaching even to the inner chambers of death.
text_la: Viæ inferi domus ejus, penetrantes in interiora mortis.
text_pt: A sua casa é caminho do inferno que desce para as câmaras da morte.
text_el: ὁδοὶ ᾅδου ὁ οἶκος αὐτῆς κατάγουσαι εἰς τὰ ταμίεια τοῦ θανάτου

text_en: Does not wisdom cry aloud, and prudence put forth her voice?
text_la: Numquid non sapientia clamitat, et prudentia dat vocem suam?
text_pt: Não clama porventura a sabedoria, e a inteligência não faz ouvir a sua voz?
text_el: σὺ τὴν σοφίαν κηρύξεις ἵνα φρόνησίς σοι ὑπακούσῃ

text_en: Standing in the top of the highest places by the way, in the midst of the paths,
text_la: In summis excelsisque verticibus supra viam, in mediis semitis stans,
text_pt: No cume das alturas, junto ao caminho, nas encruzilhadas das veredas se posta.
text_el: ἐπὶ γὰρ τῶν ὑψηλῶν ἄκρων ἐστίν ἀνὰ μέσον δὲ τῶν τρίβων ἕστηκεν

text_en: beside the gates of the city, in the very doors she speaks, saying:
text_la: juxta portas civitatis, in ipsis foribus loquitur, dicens :
text_pt: Do lado das portas da cidade, à entrada da cidade, e à entrada das portas está gritando:
text_el: παρὰ γὰρ πύλαις δυναστῶν παρεδρεύει ἐν δὲ εἰσόδοις ὑμνεῖται

text_en: O you men , to you I call, and my voice is to the sons of men .
text_la: O viri, ad vos clamito, et vox mea ad filios hominum.
text_pt: A vós, ó homens, clamo; e a minha voz se dirige aos filhos dos homens.
text_el: ὑμᾶς ὦ ἄνθρωποι παρακαλῶ καὶ προΐεμαι ἐμὴν φωνὴν υἱοῖς ἀνθρώπων

text_en: O little ones understand subtlety, and you unwise, take notice.
text_la: Intelligite, parvuli, astutiam, et insipientes, animadvertite.
text_pt: Entendei, ó simples, a prudência; e vós, insensatos, entendei de coração.
text_el: νοήσατε ἄκακοι πανουργίαν οἱ δὲ ἀπαίδευτοι ἔνθεσθε καρδίαν

text_en: Hear, for I will speak of great things: and my lips shall be opened to preach right things.
text_la: Audite, quoniam de rebus magnis locutura sum, et aperientur labia mea ut recta prædicent.
text_pt: Ouvi, porque falarei coisas excelentes; os meus lábios se abrirão para a eqüidade.
text_el: εἰσακούσατέ μου σεμνὰ γὰρ ἐρῶ καὶ ἀνοίσω ἀπὸ χειλέων ὀρθά

text_en: My mouth shall meditate truth , and my lips shall hate wickedness .
text_la: Veritatem meditabitur guttur meum, et labia mea detestabuntur impium.
text_pt: Porque a minha boca proferirá a verdade, e os meus lábios abominam a impiedade.
text_el: ὅτι ἀλήθειαν μελετήσει ὁ φάρυγξ μου ἐβδελυγμένα δὲ ἐναντίον ἐμοῦ χείλη ψευδῆ

text_en: All my words are just , there is nothing wicked , nor perverse in them.
text_la: Justi sunt omnes sermones mei : non est in eis pravum quid, neque perversum;
text_pt: São justas todas as palavras da minha boca: não há nelas nenhuma coisa tortuosa nem pervertida.
text_el: μετὰ δικαιοσύνης πάντα τὰ ῥήματα τοῦ στόματός μου οὐδὲν ἐν αὐτοῖς σκολιὸν οὐδὲ στραγγαλῶδες

text_en: They are right to them that understand, and just to them that find knowledge .
text_la: recti sunt intelligentibus, et æqui invenientibus scientiam.
text_pt: Todas elas são retas para aquele que as entende bem, e justas para os que acham o conhecimento.
text_el: πάντα ἐνώπια τοῖς συνιοῦσιν καὶ ὀρθὰ τοῖς εὑρίσκουσι γνῶσιν

text_en: Receive my instruction, and not money: choose knowledge rather than gold.
text_la: Accipite disciplinam meam, et non pecuniam; doctrinam magis quam aurum eligite :
text_pt: Aceitai a minha correção, e não a prata; e o conhecimento, mais do que o ouro fino escolhido.
text_el: λάβετε παιδείαν καὶ μὴ ἀργύριον καὶ γνῶσιν ὑπὲρ χρυσίον δεδοκιμασμένον ἀνθαιρεῖσθε δὲ αἴσθησιν χρυσίου καθαροῦ

text_en: For wisdom is better than all the most precious things: and whatsoever may be desired cannot be compared to it.
text_la: melior est enim sapientia cunctis pretiosissimis, et omne desiderabile ei non potest comparari.
text_pt: Porque melhor é a sabedoria do que os rubis; e tudo o que mais se deseja não se pode comparar com ela.
text_el: κρείσσων γὰρ σοφία λίθων πολυτελῶν πᾶν δὲ τίμιον οὐκ ἄξιον αὐτῆς ἐστιν

text_en: I, wisdom, dwell in counsel, and am present in learned thoughts.
text_la: Ego sapientia, habito in consilio, et eruditis intersum cogitationibus.
text_pt: Eu, a sabedoria, habito com a prudência, e acho o conhecimento dos conselhos.
text_el: ἐγὼ ἡ σοφία κατεσκήνωσα βουλήν καὶ γνῶσιν καὶ ἔννοιαν ἐγὼ ἐπεκαλεσάμην

text_en: The fear of the Lord hates evil ; I hate arrogance, and pride , and every wicked way, and a mouth with a double tongue.
text_la: Timor Domini odit malum : arrogantiam, et superbiam, et viam pravam, et os bilingue, detestor.
text_pt: O temor do Senhor é odiar o mal; a soberba e a arrogância, o mau caminho e a boca perversa, eu odeio.
text_el: φόβος κυρίου μισεῖ ἀδικίαν ὕβριν τε καὶ ὑπερηφανίαν καὶ ὁδοὺς πονηρῶν μεμίσηκα δὲ ἐγὼ διεστραμμένας ὁδοὺς κακῶν

text_en: Counsel and equity is mine, prudence is mine, strength is mine.
text_la: Meum est consilium et æquitas; mea est prudentia, mea est fortitudo.
text_pt: Meu é o conselho e a verdadeira sabedoria; eu sou o entendimento; minha é a fortaleza.
text_el: ἐμὴ βουλὴ καὶ ἀσφάλεια ἐμὴ φρόνησις ἐμὴ δὲ ἰσχύς

text_en: By me kings reign, and lawgivers decree just things.
text_la: Per me reges regnant, et legum conditores justa decernunt;
text_pt: Por mim reinam os reis e os príncipes decretam justiça.
text_el: δι' ἐμοῦ βασιλεῖς βασιλεύουσιν καὶ οἱ δυνάσται γράφουσιν δικαιοσύνην

text_en: By me princes rule, and the mighty decree justice .
text_la: per me principes imperant, et potentes decernunt justitiam.
text_pt: Por mim governam príncipes e nobres; sim, todos os juízes da terra.
text_el: δι' ἐμοῦ μεγιστᾶνες μεγαλύνονται καὶ τύραννοι δι' ἐμοῦ κρατοῦσι γῆς

text_en: I love them that love me: and they that in the morning early watch for me, shall find me.
text_la: Ego diligentes me diligo, et qui mane vigilant ad me, invenient me.
text_pt: Eu amo aos que me amam, e os que cedo me buscarem, me acharão.
text_el: ἐγὼ τοὺς ἐμὲ φιλοῦντας ἀγαπῶ οἱ δὲ ἐμὲ ζητοῦντες εὑρήσουσιν

text_en: With me are riches and glory , glorious riches and justice .
text_la: Mecum sunt divitiæ et gloria, opes superbæ et justitia.
text_pt: Riquezas e honra estão comigo; assim como os bens duráveis e a justiça.
text_el: πλοῦτος καὶ δόξα ἐμοὶ ὑπάρχει καὶ κτῆσις πολλῶν καὶ δικαιοσύνη

text_en: For my fruit is better than gold and the precious stone , and my blossoms than choice silver.
text_la: Melior est enim fructus meus auro et lapide pretioso, et genimina me argento electo.
text_pt: Melhor é o meu fruto do que o ouro, do que o ouro refinado, e os meus ganhos mais do que a prata escolhida.
text_el: βέλτιον ἐμὲ καρπίζεσθαι ὑπὲρ χρυσίον καὶ λίθον τίμιον τὰ δὲ ἐμὰ γενήματα κρείσσω ἀργυρίου ἐκλεκτοῦ

text_en: I walk in the way of justice , in the midst of the paths of judgment,
text_la: In viis justitiæ ambulo, in medio semitarum judicii :
text_pt: Faço andar pelo caminho da justiça, no meio das veredas do juízo.
text_el: ἐν ὁδοῖς δικαιοσύνης περιπατῶ καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον τρίβων δικαιώματος ἀναστρέφομαι

text_en: that I may enrich them that love me, and may fill their treasures.
text_la: ut ditem diligentes me, et thesauros eorum repleam.
text_pt: Para que faça herdar bens permanentes aos que me amam, e eu encha os seus tesouros.
text_el: ἵνα μερίσω τοῖς ἐμὲ ἀγαπῶσιν ὕπαρξιν καὶ τοὺς θησαυροὺς αὐτῶν ἐμπλήσω ἀγαθῶν

text_en: The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his ways, before he made anything from the beginning.
text_la: Dominus possedit me in initio viarum suarum antequam quidquam faceret a principio.
text_pt: O Senhor me possuiu no princípio de seus caminhos, desde então, e antes de suas obras.
text_el: κύριος ἔκτισέν με ἀρχὴν ὁδῶν αὐτοῦ εἰς ἔργα αὐτοῦ

text_en: I was set up from eternity , and of old, before the earth was made.
text_la: Ab æterno ordinata sum, et ex antiquis antequam terra fieret.
text_pt: Desde a eternidade fui ungida, desde o princípio, antes do começo da terra.
text_el: πρὸ τοῦ αἰῶνος ἐθεμελίωσέν με ἐν ἀρχῇ

text_en: The depths were not as yet, and I was already conceived, neither had the fountains of waters as yet sprung out.
text_la: Nondum erant abyssi, et ego jam concepta eram : necdum fontes aquarum eruperant,
text_pt: Quando ainda não havia abismos, fui gerada, quando ainda não havia fontes carregadas de águas.
text_el: πρὸ τοῦ τὴν γῆν ποιῆσαι καὶ πρὸ τοῦ τὰς ἀβύσσους ποιῆσαι πρὸ τοῦ προελθεῖν τὰς πηγὰς τῶν ὑδάτων

text_en: The mountains, with their huge bulk, had not as yet been established: before the hills, I was brought forth:
text_la: necdum montes gravi mole constiterant : ante colles ego parturiebar.
text_pt: Antes que os montes se houvessem assentado, antes dos outeiros, eu fui gerada.
text_el: πρὸ τοῦ ὄρη ἑδρασθῆναι πρὸ δὲ πάντων βουνῶν γεννᾷ με

text_en: He had not yet made the earth, nor the rivers, nor the poles of the world.
text_la: Adhuc terram non fecerat, et flumina, et cardines orbis terræ.
text_pt: Ainda ele não tinha feito a terra, nem os campos, nem o princípio do pó do mundo.
text_el: κύριος ἐποίησεν χώρας καὶ ἀοικήτους καὶ ἄκρα οἰκούμενα τῆς ὑπ' οὐρανόν

text_en: When he prepared the heavens , I was present: when with a certain law, and compass, he enclosed the depths :
text_la: Quando præparabat cælos, aderam; quando certa lege et gyro vallabat abyssos;
text_pt: Quando ele preparava os céus, aí estava eu, quando traçava o horizonte sobre a face do abismo;
text_el: ἡνίκα ἡτοίμαζεν τὸν οὐρανόν συμπαρήμην αὐτῷ καὶ ὅτε ἀφώριζεν τὸν ἑαυτοῦ θρόνον ἐπ' ἀνέμων

text_en: When he established the sky above, and poised the fountains of waters:
text_la: quando æthera firmabat sursum, et librabat fontes aquarum;
text_pt: Quando firmava as nuvens acima, quando fortificava as fontes do abismo,
text_el: ἡνίκα ἰσχυρὰ ἐποίει τὰ ἄνω νέφη καὶ ὡς ἀσφαλεῖς ἐτίθει πηγὰς τῆς ὑπ' οὐρανὸν

text_en: When he compassed the sea with its bounds, and set a law to the waters that they should not pass their limits: when he balanced the foundations of the earth;
text_la: quando circumdabat mari terminum suum, et legem ponebat aquis, ne transirent fines suos; quando appendebat fundamenta terræ :
text_pt: Quando fixava ao mar o seu termo, para que as águas não traspassassem o seu mando, quando compunha os fundamentos da terra.
