text_el: καὶ ἰσχυρὰ ἐποίει τὰ θεμέλια τῆς γῆς

text_en: I was with him forming all things: and was delighted every day, playing before him at all times;
text_la: cum eo eram, cuncta componens. Et delectabar per singulos dies, ludens coram eo omni tempore,
text_pt: Então eu estava com ele, e era seu arquiteto; era cada dia as suas delícias, alegrando-me perante ele em todo o tempo;
text_el: ἤμην παρ' αὐτῷ ἁρμόζουσα ἐγὼ ἤμην ᾗ προσέχαιρεν καθ' ἡμέραν δὲ εὐφραινόμην ἐν προσώπῳ αὐτοῦ ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ

text_en: playing in the world: and my delights were to be with the children of men .
text_la: ludens in orbe terrarum; et deliciæ meæ esse cum filiis hominum.
text_pt: Regozijando-me no seu mundo habitável e enchendo-me de prazer com os filhos dos homens.
text_el: ὅτε εὐφραίνετο τὴν οἰκουμένην συντελέσας καὶ ἐνευφραίνετο ἐν υἱοῖς ἀνθρώπων

text_en: Now, therefore, you children, hear me: blessed are they that keep my ways.
text_la: Nunc ergo, filii, audite me : beati qui custodiunt vias meas.
text_pt: Agora, pois, filhos, ouvi-me, porque bem-aventurados serão os que guardarem os meus caminhos.
text_el: νῦν οὖν υἱέ ἄκουέ μου

text_en: Hear instruction, and be wise, and refuse it not.
text_la: Audite disciplinam, et estote sapientes, et nolite abjicere eam.
text_pt: Ouvi a instrução, e sede sábios, não a rejeiteis.

text_en: Blessed is the man that hears me, and that watches daily at my gates, and waits at the posts of my doors.
text_la: Beatus homo qui audit me, et qui vigilat ad fores meas quotidie, et observat ad postes ostii mei.
text_pt: Bem-aventurado o homem que me dá ouvidos, velando às minhas portas cada dia, esperando às ombreiras da minha entrada.
text_el: μακάριος ἀνήρ ὃς εἰσακούσεταί μου καὶ ἄνθρωπος ὃς τὰς ἐμὰς ὁδοὺς φυλάξει ἀγρυπνῶν ἐπ' ἐμαῖς θύραις καθ' ἡμέραν τηρῶν σταθμοὺς ἐμῶν εἰσόδων

text_en: He that shall find me, shall find life, and shall have salvation from the Lord .
text_la: Qui me invenerit, inveniet vitam, et hauriet salutem a Domino.
text_pt: Porque o que me achar, achará a vida, e alcançará o favor do Senhor.
text_el: αἱ γὰρ ἔξοδοί μου ἔξοδοι ζωῆς καὶ ἑτοιμάζεται θέλησις παρὰ κυρίου

text_en: But he that shall sin against me shall hurt his own soul . All that hate me love death.
text_la: Qui autem in me peccaverit, lædet animam suam; omnes qui me oderunt diligunt mortem.
text_pt: Mas o que pecar contra mim violentará a sua própria alma; todos os que me odeiam amam a morte.
text_el: οἱ δὲ εἰς ἐμὲ ἁμαρτάνοντες ἀσεβοῦσιν τὰς ἑαυτῶν ψυχάς καὶ οἱ μισοῦντές με ἀγαπῶσιν θάνατον

text_en: Wisdom has built herself a house, she has hewn her out seven pillars.
text_la: Sapientia ædificavit sibi domum : excidit columnas septem.
text_pt: A sabedoria já edificou a sua casa, já lavrou as suas sete colunas.
text_el: ἡ σοφία ᾠκοδόμησεν ἑαυτῇ οἶκον καὶ ὑπήρεισεν στύλους ἑπτά

text_en: She has slain her victims, mingled her wine, and set forth her table.
text_la: Immolavit victimas suas, miscuit vinum, et proposuit mensam suam.
text_pt: Já abateu os seus animais e misturou o seu vinho, e já preparou a sua mesa.
text_el: ἔσφαξεν τὰ ἑαυτῆς θύματα ἐκέρασεν εἰς κρατῆρα τὸν ἑαυτῆς οἶνον καὶ ἡτοιμάσατο τὴν ἑαυτῆς τράπεζαν

text_en: She has sent her maids to invite to the tower, and to the walls of the city:
text_la: Misit ancillas suas ut vocarent ad arcem et ad mœnia civitatis.
text_pt: Já ordenou às suas criadas, e está convidando desde as alturas da cidade, dizendo:
text_el: ἀπέστειλεν τοὺς ἑαυτῆς δούλους συγκαλούσα μετὰ ὑψηλοῦ κηρύγματος ἐπὶ κρατῆρα λέγουσα

text_en: Whosoever is a little one, let him come to me. And to the unwise she said:
text_la: Si quis est parvulus, veniat ad me. Et insipientibus locuta est :
text_pt: Quem é simples, volte-se para cá. Aos faltos de senso diz:
text_el: ὅς ἐστιν ἄφρων ἐκκλινάτω πρός με καὶ τοῖς ἐνδεέσι φρενῶν εἶπεν

text_en: Come, eat my bread, and drink the wine which I have mingled for you.
text_la: Venite, comedite panem meum, et bibite vinum quod miscui vobis.
text_pt: Vinde, comei do meu pão, e bebei do vinho que tenho misturado.
text_el: ἔλθατε φάγετε τῶν ἐμῶν ἄρτων καὶ πίετε οἶνον ὃν ἐκέρασα ὑμῖν

text_en: Forsake childishness, and live, and walk by the ways of prudence .
text_la: Relinquite infantiam, et vivite, et ambulate per vias prudentiæ.
text_pt: Deixai os insensatos e vivei; e andai pelo caminho do entendimento.
text_el: ἀπολείπετε ἀφροσύνην καὶ ζήσεσθε καὶ ζητήσατε φρόνησιν ἵνα βιώσητε καὶ κατορθώσατε ἐν γνώσει σύνεσιν

text_en: He that teaches a scorner, does an injury to himself; and he that rebukes a wicked man , gets himself a blot.
text_la: Qui erudit derisorem, ipse injuriam sibi facit, et qui arguit impium, sibi maculam generat.
text_pt: O que repreende o escarnecedor, toma afronta para si; e o que censura o ímpio recebe a sua mancha.
text_el: ὁ παιδεύων κακοὺς λήμψεται ἑαυτῷ ἀτιμίαν ἐλέγχων δὲ τὸν ἀσεβῆ μωμήσεται ἑαυτόν

text_en: Rebuke not a scorner, lest he hate you. Rebuke a wise man , and he will love you.
text_la: Noli arguere derisorem, ne oderit te : argue sapientem, et diliget te.
text_pt: Não repreendas o escarnecedor, para que não te odeie; repreende o sábio, e ele te amará.
text_el: μὴ ἔλεγχε κακούς ἵνα μὴ μισῶσίν σε ἔλεγχε σοφόν καὶ ἀγαπήσει σε

text_en: Give an occasion to a wise man , and wisdom shall be added to him. Teach a just man , and he shall make haste to receive it.
text_la: Da sapienti occasionem, et addetur ei sapientia; doce justum, et festinabit accipere.
text_pt: Dá instrução ao sábio, e ele se fará mais sábio; ensina o justo e ele aumentará em entendimento.
text_el: δίδου σοφῷ ἀφορμήν καὶ σοφώτερος ἔσται γνώριζε δικαίῳ καὶ προσθήσει τοῦ δέχεσθαι

text_en: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is prudence .
text_la: Principium sapientiæ timor Domini, et scientia sanctorum prudentia.
text_pt: O temor do Senhor é o princípio da sabedoria, e o conhecimento do Santo a prudência.
text_el: ἀρχὴ σοφίας φόβος κυρίου καὶ βουλὴ ἁγίων σύνεσις

text_en: For by me shall your days be multiplied, and years of life shall be added to you.
text_la: Per me enim multiplicabuntur dies tui, et addentur tibi anni vitæ.
text_pt: Porque por meu intermédio se multiplicam os teus dias, e anos de vida se te aumentarão.
text_el: τούτῳ γὰρ τῷ τρόπῳ πολὺν ζήσεις χρόνον καὶ προστεθήσεταί σοι ἔτη ζωῆς σου

text_en: If you be wise, you shall be so to yourself: and if a scorner, you alone shall bear the evil .
text_la: Si sapiens fueris, tibimetipsi eris; si autem illusor, solus portabis malum.
text_pt: Se fores sábio, para ti serás sábio; e, se fores escarnecedor, só tu o suportarás.
text_el: υἱέ ἐὰν σοφὸς γένῃ σεαυτῷ σοφὸς ἔσῃ καὶ τοῖς πλησίον ἐὰν δὲ κακὸς ἀποβῇς μόνος ἀναντλήσεις κακά

text_en: A foolish woman and clamorous, and full of allurements, and knowing nothing at all,
text_la: Mulier stulta et clamosa, plenaque illecebris, et nihil omnino sciens,
text_pt: A mulher louca é alvoroçadora; é simples e nada sabe.
text_el: γυνὴ ἄφρων καὶ θρασεῖα ἐνδεὴς ψωμοῦ γίνεται ἣ οὐκ ἐπίσταται αἰσχύνην

text_en: sat at the door of her house, upon a seat, in a high place of the city,
text_la: sedit in foribus domus suæ, super sellam in excelso urbis loco,
text_pt: Assenta-se à porta da sua casa numa cadeira, nas alturas da cidade,
text_el: ἐκάθισεν ἐπὶ θύραις τοῦ ἑαυτῆς οἴκου ἐπὶ δίφρου ἐμφανῶς ἐν πλατείαις

text_en: to call them that pass by the way, and go on their journey:
text_la: ut vocaret transeuntes per viam, et pergentes itinere suo :
text_pt: E põe-se a chamar aos que vão pelo caminho, e que passam reto pelas veredas, dizendo:
text_el: προσκαλουμένη τοὺς παριόντας καὶ κατευθύνοντας ἐν ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτῶν

text_en: He that is a little one, let him turn to me. And to the fool she said:
text_la: Qui est parvulus declinet ad me. Et vecordi locuta est :
text_pt: Quem é simples, volte-se para cá. E aos faltos de entendimento ela diz:
text_el: ὅς ἐστιν ὑμῶν ἀφρονέστατος ἐκκλινάτω πρός με ἐνδεέσι δὲ φρονήσεως παρακελεύομαι λέγουσα

text_en: Stolen waters are sweeter, and hidden bread is more pleasant.
text_la: Aquæ furtivæ dulciores sunt, et panis absconditus suavior.
text_pt: As águas roubadas são doces, e o pão tomado às escondidas é agradável.
text_el: ἄρτων κρυφίων ἡδέως ἅψασθε καὶ ὕδατος κλοπῆς γλυκεροῦ

text_en: And he did not know that giants are there, and that her guests are in the depths of hell.
text_la: Et ignoravit quod ibi sint gigantes, et in profundis inferni convivæ ejus.
text_pt: Mas não sabem que ali estão os mortos; os seus convidados estão nas profundezas do inferno.
text_el: ὁ δὲ οὐκ οἶδεν ὅτι γηγενεῖς παρ' αὐτῇ ὄλλυνται καὶ ἐπὶ πέτευρον ᾅδου συναντᾷ

text_en: A wise son makes the father glad: but a foolish son is the sorrow of his mother.
text_la: Filius sapiens lætificat patrem, filius vero stultus mœstitia est matris suæ.
text_pt: Provérbios de Salomão: O filho sábio alegra a seu pai, mas o filho insensato é a tristeza de sua mãe.
text_el: υἱὸς σοφὸς εὐφραίνει πατέρα υἱὸς δὲ ἄφρων λύπη τῇ μητρί

text_en: Treasures of wickedness shall profit nothing: but justice shall deliver from death.
text_la: Nil proderunt thesauri impietatis, justitia vero liberabit a morte.
text_pt: Os tesouros da impiedade de nada aproveitam; mas a justiça livra da morte.
text_el: οὐκ ὠφελήσουσιν θησαυροὶ ἀνόμους δικαιοσύνη δὲ ῥύσεται ἐκ θανάτου

text_en: The Lord will not afflict the soul of the just with famine, and he will disappoint the deceitful practices of the wicked .
text_la: Non affliget Dominus fame animam justi, et insidias impiorum subvertet.
text_pt: O Senhor não deixa o justo passar fome, mas rechaça a aspiração dos perversos.
text_el: οὐ λιμοκτονήσει κύριος ψυχὴν δικαίαν ζωὴν δὲ ἀσεβῶν ἀνατρέψει

text_en: The slothful hand has wrought poverty: but the hand of the industrious gets riches. He that trusts to lies feeds the winds: and the same runs after birds, that fly away.
text_la: Egestatem operata est manus remissa; manus autem fortium divitias parat. Qui nititur mendaciis, hic pascit ventos; idem autem ipse sequitur aves volantes.
text_pt: O que trabalha com mão displicente empobrece, mas a mão dos diligentes enriquece.
text_el: πενία ἄνδρα ταπεινοῖ χεῖρες δὲ ἀνδρείων πλουτίζουσιν

text_en: He that gathers in the harvest, is a wise son: but he that snorts in the summer, is the son of confusion.
text_la: Qui congregat in messe, filius sapiens est; qui autem stertit æstate, filius confusionis.
text_pt: O que ajunta no verão é filho ajuizado, mas o que dorme na sega é filho que envergonha.
text_el: διεσώθη ἀπὸ καύματος υἱὸς νοήμων ἀνεμόφθορος δὲ γίνεται ἐν ἀμήτῳ υἱὸς παράνομος

text_en: The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of the just : but iniquity covers the mouth of the wicked .
text_la: Benedictio Domini super caput justi; os autem impiorum operit iniquitas.
text_pt: Bênçãos há sobre a cabeça do justo, mas a violência cobre a boca dos perversos.
text_el: εὐλογία κυρίου ἐπὶ κεφαλὴν δικαίου στόμα δὲ ἀσεβῶν καλύψει πένθος ἄωρον

text_en: The memory of the just is with praises: and the name of the wicked shall rot.
text_la: Memoria justi cum laudibus, et nomen impiorum putrescet.
text_pt: A memória do justo é abençoada, mas o nome dos perversos apodrecerá.
text_el: μνήμη δικαίων μετ' ἐγκωμίων ὄνομα δὲ ἀσεβοῦς σβέννυται

text_en: The wise of heart receives precepts : a fool is beaten with lips.
text_la: Sapiens corde præcepta suscipit; stultus cæditur labiis.
text_pt: O sábio de coração aceita os mandamentos, mas o insensato de lábios ficará transtornado.
text_el: σοφὸς καρδίᾳ δέξεται ἐντολάς ὁ δὲ ἄστεγος χείλεσιν σκολιάζων ὑποσκελισθήσεται

text_en: He that walks sincerely, walks confidently: but he that perverts his ways, shall be manifest.
text_la: Qui ambulat simpliciter ambulat confidenter; qui autem depravat vias suas manifestus erit.
text_pt: Quem anda em sinceridade, anda seguro; mas o que perverte os seus caminhos ficará conhecido.
text_el: ὃς πορεύεται ἁπλῶς πορεύεται πεποιθώς ὁ δὲ διαστρέφων τὰς ὁδοὺς αὐτοῦ γνωσθήσεται

text_en: He that winks with the eye, shall cause sorrow: and the foolish in lips shall be beaten.
text_la: Qui annuit oculo dabit dolorem; et stultus labiis verberabitur.
text_pt: O que acena com os olhos causa dores, e o tolo de lábios ficará transtornado.
text_el: ὁ ἐννεύων ὀφθαλμοῖς μετὰ δόλου συνάγει ἀνδράσι λύπας ὁ δὲ ἐλέγχων μετὰ παρρησίας εἰρηνοποιεῖ

text_en: The mouth of the just is a vein of life: and the mouth of the wicked covers iniquity .
text_la: Vena vitæ os justi, et os impiorum operit iniquitatem.
text_pt: A boca do justo é fonte de vida, mas a violência cobre a boca dos perversos.
text_el: πηγὴ ζωῆς ἐν χειρὶ δικαίου στόμα δὲ ἀσεβοῦς καλύψει ἀπώλεια

text_en: Hatred stirs up strifes: and charity covers all sins .
text_la: Odium suscitat rixas, et universa delicta operit caritas.
text_pt: O ódio excita contendas, mas o amor cobre todos os pecados.
text_el: μῖσος ἐγείρει νεῖκος πάντας δὲ τοὺς μὴ φιλονεικοῦντας καλύπτει φιλία

text_en: In the lips of the wise is wisdom found: and a rod on the back of him that wants sense.
text_la: In labiis sapientis invenitur sapientia, et virga in dorso ejus qui indiget corde.
text_pt: Nos lábios do entendido se acha a sabedoria, mas a vara é para as costas do falto de entendimento.
text_el: ὃς ἐκ χειλέων προφέρει σοφίαν ῥάβδῳ τύπτει ἄνδρα ἀκάρδιον

text_en: Wise men lay up knowledge : but the mouth of the fool is next to confusion.
text_la: Sapientes abscondunt scientiam; os autem stulti confusioni proximum est.
text_pt: Os sábios entesouram a sabedoria; mas a boca do tolo o aproxima da ruína.
text_el: σοφοὶ κρύψουσιν αἴσθησιν στόμα δὲ προπετοῦς ἐγγίζει συντριβῇ

text_en: The substance of a rich man is the city of his strength: the fear of the poor is their poverty.
text_la: Substantia divitis, urbs fortitudinis ejus; pavor pauperum egestas eorum.
text_pt: Os bens do rico são a sua cidade forte, a pobreza dos pobres a sua ruína.
text_el: κτῆσις πλουσίων πόλις ὀχυρά συντριβὴ δὲ ἀσεβῶν πενία

text_en: The work of the just is unto life: but the fruit of the wicked unto sin .
text_la: Opus justi ad vitam, fructus autem impii ad peccatum.
text_pt: A obra do justo conduz à vida, o fruto do perverso, ao pecado.
text_el: ἔργα δικαίων ζωὴν ποιεῖ καρποὶ δὲ ἀσεβῶν ἁμαρτίας

text_en: The way of life, to him that observes correction: but he that forsakes reproofs, goes astray.
text_la: Via vitæ custodienti disciplinam; qui autem increpationes relinquit, errat.
text_pt: O caminho para a vida é daquele que guarda a instrução, mas o que deixa a repreensão comete erro.
text_el: ὁδοὺς δικαίας ζωῆς φυλάσσει παιδεία παιδεία δὲ ἀνεξέλεγκτος πλανᾶται

text_en: Lying lips hide hatred : he that utters reproach, is foolish.
text_la: Abscondunt odium labia mendacia; qui profert contumeliam, insipiens est.
text_pt: O que encobre o ódio tem lábios falsos, e o que divulga má fama é um insensato.
text_el: καλύπτουσιν ἔχθραν χείλη δίκαια οἱ δὲ ἐκφέροντες λοιδορίας ἀφρονέστατοί εἰσιν

text_en: In the multitude of words there shall not want sin : but he that refrains his lips, is most wise.
text_la: In multiloquio non deerit peccatum, qui autem moderatur labia sua prudentissimus est.
text_pt: Na multidão de palavras não falta pecado, mas o que modera os seus lábios é sábio.
text_el: ἐκ πολυλογίας οὐκ ἐκφεύξῃ ἁμαρτίαν φειδόμενος δὲ χειλέων νοήμων ἔσῃ

text_en: The tongue of the just is as choice silver: but the heart of the wicked is nothing worth.
text_la: Argentum electum lingua justi; cor autem impiorum pro nihilo.
text_pt: Prata escolhida é a língua do justo; o coração dos perversos é de nenhum valor.
text_el: ἄργυρος πεπυρωμένος γλῶσσα δικαίου καρδία δὲ ἀσεβοῦς ἐκλείψει

text_en: The lips of the just teach many: but they that are ignorant , shall die in the want of understanding.
text_la: Labia justi erudiunt plurimos; qui autem indocti sunt in cordis egestate morientur.
text_pt: Os lábios do justo apascentam a muitos, mas os tolos morrem por falta de entendimento.
text_el: χείλη δικαίων ἐπίσταται ὑψηλά οἱ δὲ ἄφρονες ἐν ἐνδείᾳ τελευτῶσιν

text_en: The blessing of the Lord makes men rich: neither shall affliction be joined to them.
text_la: Benedictio Domini divites facit, nec sociabitur eis afflictio.
text_pt: A bênção do Senhor é que enriquece; e não traz consigo dores.
text_el: εὐλογία κυρίου ἐπὶ κεφαλὴν δικαίου αὕτη πλουτίζει καὶ οὐ μὴ προστεθῇ αὐτῇ λύπη ἐν καρδίᾳ

text_en: A fool works mischief as it were for sport: but wisdom is prudence to a man .
text_la: Quasi per risum stultus operatur scelus, sapientia autem est viro prudentia.
text_pt: Para o tolo, o cometer desordem é divertimento; mas para o homem entendido é o ter sabedoria.
text_el: ἐν γέλωτι ἄφρων πράσσει κακά ἡ δὲ σοφία ἀνδρὶ τίκτει φρόνησιν

text_en: That which the wicked fears, shall come upon him: to the just their desire shall be given.
text_la: Quod timet impius veniet super eum; desiderium suum justus dabitur.
text_pt: Aquilo que o perverso teme sobrevirá a ele, mas o desejo dos justos será concedido.
text_el: ἐν ἀπωλείᾳ ἀσεβὴς περιφέρεται ἐπιθυμία δὲ δικαίου δεκτή

text_en: As a tempest that passes, so the wicked shall be no more: but the just is as an everlasting foundation.
text_la: Quasi tempestas transiens non erit impius; justus autem quasi fundamentum sempiternum.
text_pt: Como passa a tempestade, assim desaparece o perverso, mas o justo tem fundamento perpétuo.
text_el: παραπορευομένης καταιγίδος ἀφανίζεται ἀσεβής δίκαιος δὲ ἐκκλίνας σῴζεται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα

text_en: As vinegar to the teeth, and smoke to the eyes, so is the sluggard to them that sent him.
text_la: Sicut acetum dentibus, et fumus oculis, sic piger his qui miserunt eum.
text_pt: Como vinagre para os dentes, como fumaça para os olhos, assim é o preguiçoso para aqueles que o mandam.
text_el: ὥσπερ ὄμφαξ ὀδοῦσι βλαβερὸν καὶ καπνὸς ὄμμασιν οὕτως παρανομία τοῖς χρωμένοις αὐτήν

text_en: The fear of the Lord shall prolong days: and the years of the wicked shall be shortened.
text_la: Timor Domini apponet dies, et anni impiorum breviabuntur.
text_pt: O temor do Senhor aumenta os dias, mas os perversos terão os anos da vida abreviados.
text_el: φόβος κυρίου προστίθησιν ἡμέρας ἔτη δὲ ἀσεβῶν ὀλιγωθήσεται

text_en: The expectation of the just is joy : but the hope of the wicked shall perish.
text_la: Exspectatio justorum lætitia, spes autem impiorum peribit.
text_pt: A esperança dos justos é alegria, mas a expectação dos perversos perecerá.
text_el: ἐγχρονίζει δικαίοις εὐφροσύνη ἐλπὶς δὲ ἀσεβῶν ὄλλυται

text_en: The strength of the upright is the way of the Lord : and fear to them that work evil .
text_la: Fortitudo simplicis via Domini, et pavor his qui operantur malum.
text_pt: O caminho do Senhor é fortaleza para os retos, mas ruína para os que praticam a iniqüidade.
text_el: ὀχύρωμα ὁσίου φόβος κυρίου συντριβὴ δὲ τοῖς ἐργαζομένοις κακά

text_en: The just shall never be moved: but the wicked shall not dwell on the earth.
text_la: Justus in æternum non commovebitur, impii autem non habitabunt super terram.
text_pt: O justo nunca jamais será abalado, mas os perversos não habitarão a terra.
text_el: δίκαιος τὸν αἰῶνα οὐκ ἐνδώσει ἀσεβεῖς δὲ οὐκ οἰκήσουσιν γῆν

text_en: The mouth of the just shall bring forth wisdom: the tongue of the perverse shall perish.
text_la: Os justi parturiet sapientiam; lingua pravorum peribit.
text_pt: A boca do justo jorra sabedoria, mas a língua da perversidade será cortada.
text_el: στόμα δικαίου ἀποστάζει σοφίαν γλῶσσα δὲ ἀδίκου ἐξολεῖται

text_en: The lips of the just consider what is acceptable: and the mouth of the wicked utters perverse things.
text_la: Labia justi considerant placita, et os impiorum perversa.
text_pt: Os lábios do justo sabem o que agrada, mas a boca dos perversos, só perversidades.
text_el: χείλη ἀνδρῶν δικαίων ἀποστάζει χάριτας στόμα δὲ ἀσεβῶν ἀποστρέφεται

text_en: A deceitful balance is an abomination before the Lord: and a just weight is his will.
text_la: Statera dolosa abominatio est apud Dominum, et pondus æquum voluntas ejus.
text_pt: Balança enganosa é abominação para o SENHOR, mas o peso justo é o seu prazer.
text_el: ζυγοὶ δόλιοι βδέλυγμα ἐνώπιον κυρίου στάθμιον δὲ δίκαιον δεκτὸν αὐτῷ

text_en: Where pride is, there also shall be reproach: but where humility is, there also is wisdom.
text_la: Ubi fuerit superbia, ibi erit et contumelia; ubi autem est humilitas, ibi et sapientia.
text_pt: Em vindo a soberba, virá também a afronta; mas com os humildes está a sabedoria.
text_el: οὗ ἐὰν εἰσέλθῃ ὕβρις ἐκεῖ καὶ ἀτιμία στόμα δὲ ταπεινῶν μελετᾷ σοφίαν

text_en: The simplicity of the just shall guide them: and the deceitfulness of the wicked shall destroy them.
text_la: Simplicitas justorum diriget eos, et supplantatio perversorum vastabit illos.
text_pt: A sinceridade dos íntegros os guiará, mas a perversidade dos aleivosos os destruirá.
text_el: ἀποθανὼν δίκαιος ἔλιπεν μετάμελον πρόχειρος δὲ γίνεται καὶ ἐπίχαρτος ἀσεβῶν ἀπώλεια

text_en: Riches shall not profit in the day of revenge: but justice shall deliver from death.
text_la: Non proderunt divitiæ in die ultionis; justitia autem liberabit a morte.
text_pt: De nada aproveitam as riquezas no dia da ira, mas a justiça livra da morte.

text_en: The justice of the upright shall make his way prosperous: and the wicked man shall fall by his own wickedness .
text_la: Justitia simplicis diriget viam ejus, et in impietate sua corruet impius.
text_pt: A justiça do sincero endireitará o seu caminho, mas o perverso pela sua falsidade cairá.
text_el: δικαιοσύνη ἀμώμους ὀρθοτομεῖ ὁδούς ἀσέβεια δὲ περιπίπτει ἀδικίᾳ

text_en: The justice of the righteous shall deliver them: and the unjust shall be caught in their own snares.
text_la: Justitia rectorum liberabit eos, et in insidiis suis capientur iniqui.
text_pt: A justiça dos virtuosos os livrará, mas na sua perversidade serão apanhados os iníquos.
text_el: δικαιοσύνη ἀνδρῶν ὀρθῶν ῥύεται αὐτούς τῇ δὲ ἀπωλείᾳ αὐτῶν ἁλίσκονται παράνομοι

text_en: When the wicked man is dead, there shall be no hope any more: and the expectation of the solicitous shall perish.
text_la: Mortuo homine impio, nulla erit ultra spes, et exspectatio sollicitorum peribit.
text_pt: Morrendo o homem perverso perece sua esperança, e acaba-se a expectação de riquezas.
text_el: τελευτήσαντος ἀνδρὸς δικαίου οὐκ ὄλλυται ἐλπίς τὸ δὲ καύχημα τῶν ἀσεβῶν ὄλλυται

text_en: The just is delivered out of distress: and the wicked shall be given up for him.
text_la: Justus de angustia liberatus est, et tradetur impius pro eo.
text_pt: O justo é libertado da angústia, e vem o ímpio para o seu lugar.
text_el: δίκαιος ἐκ θήρας ἐκδύνει ἀντ' αὐτοῦ δὲ παραδίδοται ὁ ἀσεβής

text_en: The dissembler with his mouth deceives his friend: but the just shall be delivered by knowledge .
text_la: Simulator ore decipit amicum suum; justi autem liberabuntur scientia.
text_pt: O hipócrita com a boca destrói o seu próximo, mas os justos se libertam pelo conhecimento.
text_el: ἐν στόματι ἀσεβῶν παγὶς πολίταις αἴσθησις δὲ δικαίων εὔοδος

text_en: When it goes well with the just , the city shall rejoice: and when the wicked perish, there shall be praise.
text_la: In bonis justorum exsultabit civitas, et in perditione impiorum erit laudatio.
text_pt: No bem dos justos exulta a cidade; e perecendo os ímpios, há júbilo.
text_el: ἐν ἀγαθοῖς δικαίων κατώρθωσεν πόλις

text_en: By the blessing of the just the city shall be exalted: and by the mouth of the wicked it shall be overthrown.
text_la: Benedictione justorum exaltabitur civitas, et ore impiorum subvertetur.
text_pt: Pela bênção dos homens de bem a cidade se exalta, mas pela boca dos perversos é derrubada.
text_el: στόμασιν δὲ ἀσεβῶν κατεσκάφη

text_en: He that despises his friend, is mean of heart: but the wise man will hold his peace.
text_la: Qui despicit amicum suum indigens corde est; vir autem prudens tacebit.
text_pt: O que despreza o seu próximo carece de entendimento, mas o homem entendido se mantém calado.
text_el: μυκτηρίζει πολίτας ἐνδεὴς φρενῶν ἀνὴρ δὲ φρόνιμος ἡσυχίαν ἄγει

text_en: He that walks deceitfully, reveals secrets: but he that is faithful , conceals the thing committed to him by his friend.
text_la: Qui ambulat fraudulenter, revelat arcana; qui autem fidelis est animi, celat amici commissum.
text_pt: O mexeriqueiro revela o segredo, mas o fiel de espírito o mantém em oculto.
text_el: ἀνὴρ δίγλωσσος ἀποκαλύπτει βουλὰς ἐν συνεδρίῳ πιστὸς δὲ πνοῇ κρύπτει πράγματα

text_en: Where there is no governor, the people shall fall: but there is safety where there is much counsel.
text_la: Ubi non est gubernator, populus corruet; salus autem, ubi multa consilia.
text_pt: Não havendo sábios conselhos, o povo cai, mas na multidão de conselhos há segurança.
text_el: οἷς μὴ ὑπάρχει κυβέρνησις πίπτουσιν ὥσπερ φύλλα σωτηρία δὲ ὑπάρχει ἐν πολλῇ βουλῇ

text_en: He shall be afflicted with evil , that is surety for a stranger: but he that is aware of snares, shall be secure.
text_la: Affligetur malo qui fidem facit pro extraneo; qui autem cavet laqueos securus erit.
text_pt: Decerto sofrerá severamente aquele que fica por fiador do estranho, mas o que evita a fiança estará seguro.
text_el: πονηρὸς κακοποιεῖ ὅταν συμμείξῃ δικαίῳ μισεῖ δὲ ἦχον ἀσφαλείας

text_en: A gracious woman shall find glory : and the strong shall have riches.
text_la: Mulier gratiosa inveniet gloriam, et robusti habebunt divitias.
text_pt: A mulher graciosa guarda a honra como os violentos guardam as riquezas.
text_el: γυνὴ εὐχάριστος ἐγείρει ἀνδρὶ δόξαν θρόνος δὲ ἀτιμίας γυνὴ μισοῦσα δίκαια πλούτου ὀκνηροὶ ἐνδεεῖς γίνονται οἱ δὲ ἀνδρεῖοι ἐρείδονται πλούτῳ

text_en: A merciful man does good to his own soul : but he that is cruel casts off even his own kindred.
text_la: Benefacit animæ suæ vir misericors; qui autem crudelis est, etiam propinquos abjicit.
text_pt: O homem bom cuida bem de si mesmo, mas o cruel prejudica o seu corpo.
text_el: τῇ ψυχῇ αὐτοῦ ἀγαθὸν ποιεῖ ἀνὴρ ἐλεήμων ἐξολλύει δὲ αὐτοῦ σῶμα ὁ ἀνελεήμων

text_en: The wicked makes an unsteady work: but to him that sows justice , there is a faithful reward.
text_la: Impius facit opus instabile, seminanti autem justitiam merces fidelis.
text_pt: O ímpio faz obra falsa, mas para o que semeia justiça haverá galardão fiel.
text_el: ἀσεβὴς ποιεῖ ἔργα ἄδικα σπέρμα δὲ δικαίων μισθὸς ἀληθείας

text_en: Clemency prepares life: and the pursuing of evil things, death.
text_la: Clementia præparat vitam, et sectatio malorum mortem.
text_pt: Como a justiça encaminha para a vida, assim o que segue o mal vai para a sua morte.
text_el: υἱὸς δίκαιος γεννᾶται εἰς ζωήν διωγμὸς δὲ ἀσεβοῦς εἰς θάνατον

text_en: A perverse heart is abominable to the Lord : and his will is in them that walk sincerely.
text_la: Abominabile Domino cor pravum, et voluntas ejus in iis qui simpliciter ambulant.
text_pt: Abominação ao Senhor são os perversos de coração, mas os de caminho sincero são o seu deleite.
text_el: βδέλυγμα κυρίῳ διεστραμμέναι ὁδοί προσδεκτοὶ δὲ αὐτῷ πάντες ἄμωμοι ἐν ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτῶν

text_en: Hand in hand the evil man shall not be innocent: but the seed of the just shall be saved.
text_la: Manus in manu non erit innocens malus; semen autem justorum salvabitur.
text_pt: Ainda que junte as mãos, o mau não ficará impune, mas a semente dos justos será liberada.
text_el: χειρὶ χεῖρας ἐμβαλὼν ἀδίκως οὐκ ἀτιμώρητος ἔσται ὁ δὲ σπείρων δικαιοσύνην λήμψεται μισθὸν πιστόν

text_en: A golden ring in a swine's snout, a woman fair and foolish.
text_la: Circulus aureus in naribus suis, mulier pulchra et fatua.
text_pt: Como jóia de ouro no focinho de uma porca, assim é a mulher formosa que não tem discrição.
text_el: ὥσπερ ἐνώτιον ἐν ῥινὶ ὑός οὕτως γυναικὶ κακόφρονι κάλλος

text_en: The desire of the just is all good , the expectation of the wicked is indignation.
text_la: Desiderium justorum omne bonum est; præstolatio impiorum furor.
text_pt: O desejo dos justos é tão somente para o bem, mas a esperança dos ímpios é criar contrariedades.
text_el: ἐπιθυμία δικαίων πᾶσα ἀγαθή ἐλπὶς δὲ ἀσεβῶν ἀπολεῖται

text_en: Some distribute their own goods, and grow richer: others take away what is not their own, and are always in want.
text_la: Alii dividunt propria, et ditiores fiunt; alii rapiunt non sua, et semper in egestate sunt.
text_pt: Ao que distribui mais se lhe acrescenta, e ao que retém mais do que é justo, é para a sua perda.
text_el: εἰσὶν οἳ τὰ ἴδια σπείροντες πλείονα ποιοῦσιν εἰσὶν καὶ οἳ συνάγοντες ἐλαττονοῦνται

text_en: The soul that blesses , shall be made fat: and he that inebriates, shall be inebriated also himself.
text_la: Anima quæ benedicit impinguabitur, et qui inebriat, ipse quoque inebriabitur.
text_pt: A alma generosa prosperará e aquele que atende também será atendido.
text_el: ψυχὴ εὐλογουμένη πᾶσα ἁπλῆ ἀνὴρ δὲ θυμώδης οὐκ εὐσχήμων

text_en: He that hides up corn, shall be cursed among the people: but a blessing upon the head of them that sell.
text_la: Qui abscondit frumenta maledicetur in populis; benedictio autem super caput vendentium.
text_pt: Ao que retém o trigo o povo amaldiçoa, mas bênção haverá sobre a cabeça do que o vende.
text_el: ὁ συνέχων σῖτον ὑπολίποιτο αὐτὸν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν εὐλογία δὲ εἰς κεφαλὴν τοῦ μεταδιδόντος

text_en: Well does he rise early who seeks good things; but he that seeks after evil things, shall be oppressed by them.
text_la: Bene consurgit diluculo qui quærit bona; qui autem investigator malorum est, opprimetur ab eis.
text_pt: O que cedo busca o bem, busca favor, mas o que procura o mal, esse lhe sobrevirá.
text_el: τεκταινόμενος ἀγαθὰ ζητεῖ χάριν ἀγαθήν ἐκζητοῦντα δὲ κακά καταλήμψεται αὐτόν

text_en: He that trusts in his riches shall fall: but the just shall spring up as a green leaf.
text_la: Qui confidit in divitiis suis corruet : justi autem quasi virens folium germinabunt.
text_pt: Aquele que confia nas suas riquezas cairá, mas os justos reverdecerão como a folhagem.
text_el: ὁ πεποιθὼς ἐπὶ πλούτῳ οὗτος πεσεῖται ὁ δὲ ἀντιλαμβανόμενος δικαίων οὗτος ἀνατελεῖ

text_en: He that troubles his own house, shall inherit the winds: and the fool shall serve the wise.
text_la: Qui conturbat domum suam possidebit ventos, et qui stultus est serviet sapienti.
text_pt: O que perturba a sua casa herdará o vento, e o tolo será servo do sábio de coração.
text_el: ὁ μὴ συμπεριφερόμενος τῷ ἑαυτοῦ οἴκῳ κληρονομήσει ἄνεμον δουλεύσει δὲ ἄφρων φρονίμῳ

text_en: The fruit of the just man is a tree of life: and he that gains souls is wise.
text_la: Fructus justi lignum vitæ, et qui suscipit animas sapiens est.
text_pt: O fruto do justo é árvore de vida, e o que ganha almas é sábio.
text_el: ἐκ καρποῦ δικαιοσύνης φύεται δένδρον ζωῆς ἀφαιροῦνται δὲ ἄωροι ψυχαὶ παρανόμων

text_en: If the just man receive in the earth, how much more the wicked and the sinner.
text_la: Si justus in terra recipit, quanto magis impius et peccator!
text_pt: Eis que o justo recebe na terra a retribuição; quanto mais o ímpio e o pecador!
text_el: εἰ ὁ μὲν δίκαιος μόλις σῴζεται ὁ ἀσεβὴς καὶ ἁμαρτωλὸς ποῦ φανεῖται

text_en: He that loves correction, loves knowledge : but he that hates reproof, is foolish.
text_la: Qui diligit disciplinam diligit scientiam; qui autem odit increpationes insipiens est.
text_pt: O que ama a instrução ama o conhecimento, mas o que odeia a repreensão é estúpido.
text_el: ὁ ἀγαπῶν παιδείαν ἀγαπᾷ αἴσθησιν ὁ δὲ μισῶν ἐλέγχους ἄφρων

text_en: He that is good , shall draw grace from the Lord : but he that trusts in his own devices, does wickedly .
text_la: Qui bonus est hauriet gratiam a Domino; qui autem confidit in cogitationibus suis impie agit.
text_pt: O homem de bem alcançará o favor do Senhor, mas ao homem de intenções perversas ele condenará.
text_el: κρείσσων ὁ εὑρὼν χάριν παρὰ κυρίῳ ἀνὴρ δὲ παράνομος παρασιωπηθήσεται

text_en: Man shall not be strengthened by wickedness : and the root of the just shall not be moved.
text_la: Non roborabitur homo ex impietate, et radix justorum non commovebitur.
text_pt: O homem não se estabelecerá pela impiedade, mas a raiz dos justos não será removida.
text_el: οὐ κατορθώσει ἄνθρωπος ἐξ ἀνόμου αἱ δὲ ῥίζαι τῶν δικαίων οὐκ ἐξαρθήσονται

text_en: A diligent woman is a crown to her husband: and she that does things worthy of confusion, is as rottenness in his bones.
text_la: Mulier diligens corona est viro suo; et putredo in ossibus ejus, quæ confusione res dignas gerit.
text_pt: A mulher virtuosa é a coroa do seu marido, mas a que o envergonha é como podridão nos seus ossos.
text_el: γυνὴ ἀνδρεία στέφανος τῷ ἀνδρὶ αὐτῆς ὥσπερ δὲ ἐν ξύλῳ σκώληξ οὕτως ἄνδρα ἀπόλλυσιν γυνὴ κακοποιός

text_en: The thoughts of the just are judgments: and the counsels of the wicked are deceitful.
text_la: Cogitationes justorum judicia, et consilia impiorum fraudulenta.
text_pt: Os pensamentos dos justos são retos, mas os conselhos dos ímpios, engano.
text_el: λογισμοὶ δικαίων κρίματα κυβερνῶσιν δὲ ἀσεβεῖς δόλους

text_en: The words of the wicked lie in wait for blood: the mouth of the just shall deliver them.
text_la: Verba impiorum insidiantur sanguini; os justorum liberabit eos.
text_pt: As palavras dos ímpios são ciladas para derramar sangue, mas a boca dos retos os livrará.
text_el: λόγοι ἀσεβῶν δόλιοι στόμα δὲ ὀρθῶν ῥύσεται αὐτούς

text_en: Turn the wicked , and they shall not be: but the house of the just shall stand firm.
text_la: Verte impios, et non erunt; domus autem justorum permanebit.
text_pt: Os ímpios serão transtornados e não subsistirão, mas a casa dos justos permanecerá.
text_el: οὗ ἐὰν στραφῇ ἀσεβὴς ἀφανίζεται οἶκοι δὲ δικαίων παραμένουσιν

text_en: A man shall be known by his learning: but he that is vain and foolish, shall be exposed to contempt .
text_la: Doctrina sua noscetur vir; qui autem vanus et excors est patebit contemptui.
text_pt: Cada qual será louvado segundo o seu entendimento, mas o perverso de coração estará em desprezo.
text_el: στόμα συνετοῦ ἐγκωμιάζεται ὑπὸ ἀνδρός νωθροκάρδιος δὲ μυκτηρίζεται

text_en: Better is the poor man that provides for himself, than he that is glorious and wants bread.
text_la: Melior est pauper et sufficiens sibi quam gloriosus et indigens pane.
text_pt: Melhor é o que se estima em pouco, e tem servos, do que o que se vangloria e tem falta de pão.
text_el: κρείσσων ἀνὴρ ἐν ἀτιμίᾳ δουλεύων ἑαυτῷ ἢ τιμὴν ἑαυτῷ περιτιθεὶς καὶ προσδεόμενος ἄρτου

text_en: The just regards the lives of his beasts: but the bowels of the wicked are cruel.
text_la: Novit justus jumentorum suorum animas; viscera autem impiorum crudelia.
text_pt: O justo tem consideração pela vida dos seus animais, mas as afeições dos ímpios são cruéis.
text_el: δίκαιος οἰκτίρει ψυχὰς κτηνῶν αὐτοῦ τὰ δὲ σπλάγχνα τῶν ἀσεβῶν ἀνελεήμονα

text_en: He that tills his land shall be satisfied with bread: but he that pursues idleness is very foolish. He that is delighted in passing his time over wine, leaves a reproach in his strong holds.
text_la: Qui operatur terram suam satiabitur panibus; qui autem sectatur otium stultissimus est. Qui suavis est in vini demorationibus, in suis munitionibus relinquit contumeliam.
text_pt: O que lavra a sua terra se fartará de pão; mas o que segue os ociosos é falto de juízo.
text_el: ὁ ἐργαζόμενος τὴν ἑαυτοῦ γῆν ἐμπλησθήσεται ἄρτων οἱ δὲ διώκοντες μάταια ἐνδεεῖς φρενῶν

text_en: The desire of the wicked is the fortification of evil men : but the root of the just shall prosper.
text_la: Desiderium impii munimentum est pessimorum; radix autem justorum proficiet.
text_pt: O ímpio deseja a rede dos maus, mas a raiz dos justos produz o seu fruto.
text_el: ἐπιθυμίαι ἀσεβῶν κακαί αἱ δὲ ῥίζαι τῶν εὐσεβῶν ἐν ὀχυρώμασιν

text_en: For the sins of the lips ruin draws near to the evil man : but the just shall escape out of distress.
text_la: Propter peccata labiorum ruina proximat malo; effugiet autem justus de angustia.
text_pt: O ímpio se enlaça na transgressão dos lábios, mas o justo sairá da angústia.
text_el: δι' ἁμαρτίαν χειλέων ἐμπίπτει εἰς παγίδας ἁμαρτωλός ἐκφεύγει δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν δίκαιος

text_en: By the fruit of his own mouth shall a man be filled with good things, and according to the works of his hands it shall be repaid him.
text_la: De fructu oris sui unusquisque replebitur bonis, et juxta opera manuum suarum retribuetur ei.
text_pt: Cada um se fartará do fruto da sua boca, e da obra das suas mãos o homem receberá a recompensa.
text_el: ἀπὸ καρπῶν στόματος ψυχὴ ἀνδρὸς πλησθήσεται ἀγαθῶν ἀνταπόδομα δὲ χειλέων αὐτοῦ δοθήσεται αὐτῷ

text_en: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes: but he that is wise hearkens unto counsels.
text_la: Via stulti recta in oculis ejus; qui autem sapiens est audit consilia.
text_pt: O caminho do insensato é reto aos seus próprios olhos, mas o que dá ouvidos ao conselho é sábio.
text_el: ὁδοὶ ἀφρόνων ὀρθαὶ ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν εἰσακούει δὲ συμβουλίας σοφός

text_en: A fool immediately shows his anger : but he that dissembles injuries is wise.
text_la: Fatuus statim indicat iram suam; qui autem dissimulat injuriam callidus est.
text_pt: A ira do insensato se conhece no mesmo dia, mas o prudente encobre a afronta.
text_el: ἄφρων αὐθημερὸν ἐξαγγέλλει ὀργὴν αὐτοῦ κρύπτει δὲ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἀτιμίαν πανοῦργος

text_en: He that speaks that which he knows , shows forth justice : but he that lies, is a deceitful witness.
text_la: Qui quod novit loquitur, index justitiæ est; qui autem mentitur, testis est fraudulentus.
text_pt: O que diz a verdade manifesta a justiça, mas a falsa testemunha diz engano.
text_el: ἐπιδεικνυμένην πίστιν ἀπαγγέλλει δίκαιος ὁ δὲ μάρτυς τῶν ἀδίκων δόλιος

text_en: There is that promises, and is pricked as it were with a sword of conscience : but the tongue of the wise is health.
text_la: Est qui promittit, et quasi gladio pungitur conscientiæ : lingua autem sapientium sanitas est.
text_pt: Há alguns que falam como que espada penetrante, mas a língua dos sábios é saúde.
text_el: εἰσὶν οἳ λέγοντες τιτρώσκουσιν μαχαίρᾳ γλῶσσαι δὲ σοφῶν ἰῶνται

text_en: The lip of truth shall be steadfast for ever: but he that is a hasty witness, frames a lying tongue.
text_la: Labium veritatis firmum erit in perpetuum; qui autem testis est repentinus, concinnat linguam mendacii.
text_pt: O lábio da verdade permanece para sempre, mas a língua da falsidade, dura por um só momento.
text_el: χείλη ἀληθινὰ κατορθοῖ μαρτυρίαν μάρτυς δὲ ταχὺς γλῶσσαν ἔχει ἄδικον

text_en: Deceit is in the heart of them that think evil things: but joy follows them that take counsels of peace.
text_la: Dolus in corde cogitantium mala; qui autem pacis ineunt consilia, sequitur eos gaudium.
text_pt: No coração dos que maquinam o mal há engano, mas os que aconselham a paz têm alegria.
text_el: δόλος ἐν καρδίᾳ τεκταινομένου κακά οἱ δὲ βουλόμενοι εἰρήνην εὐφρανθήσονται

text_en: Whatsoever shall befall the just man , shall not make him sad: but the wicked shall be filled with mischief.
text_la: Non contristabit justum quidquid ei acciderit : impii autem replebuntur malo.
text_pt: Nenhum agravo sobrevirá ao justo, mas os ímpios ficam cheios de mal.
text_el: οὐκ ἀρέσει τῷ δικαίῳ οὐδὲν ἄδικον οἱ δὲ ἀσεβεῖς πλησθήσονται κακῶν

text_en: Lying lips are an abomination to the Lord : but they that deal faithfully , please him.
text_la: Abominatio est Domino labia mendacia; qui autem fideliter agunt placent ei.
text_pt: Os lábios mentirosos são abomináveis ao Senhor, mas os que agem fielmente são o seu deleite.
text_el: βδέλυγμα κυρίῳ χείλη ψευδῆ ὁ δὲ ποιῶν πίστεις δεκτὸς παρ' αὐτῷ

text_en: A cautious man conceals knowledge : and the heart of fools publishes folly.
text_la: Homo versatus celat scientiam, et cor insipientium provocat stultitiam.
text_pt: O homem prudente encobre o conhecimento, mas o coração dos tolos proclama a estultícia.
text_el: ἀνὴρ συνετὸς θρόνος αἰσθήσεως καρδία δὲ ἀφρόνων συναντήσεται ἀραῖς

text_en: The hand of the valiant shall bear rule: but that which is slothful shall be under tribute.
text_la: Manus fortium dominabitur; quæ autem remissa est, tributis serviet.
text_pt: A mão dos diligentes dominará, mas os negligentes serão tributários.
text_el: χεὶρ ἐκλεκτῶν κρατήσει εὐχερῶς δόλιοι δὲ ἔσονται εἰς προνομήν

text_en: Grief in the heart of a man shall bring him low, but with a good word he shall be made glad.
text_la: Mœror in corde viri humiliabit illum, et sermone bono lætificabitur.
text_pt: A ansiedade no coração deixa o homem abatido, mas uma boa palavra o alegra.
text_el: φοβερὸς λόγος καρδίαν ταράσσει ἀνδρὸς δικαίου ἀγγελία δὲ ἀγαθὴ εὐφραίνει αὐτόν

text_en: He that neglects a loss for the sake of a friend, is just : but the way of the wicked shall deceive them.
text_la: Qui negligit damnum propter amicum, justus est; iter autem impiorum decipiet eos.
text_pt: O justo é mais excelente do que o seu próximo, mas o caminho dos ímpios faz errar.
text_el: ἐπιγνώμων δίκαιος ἑαυτοῦ φίλος ἔσται αἱ δὲ γνῶμαι τῶν ἀσεβῶν ἀνεπιεικεῖς ἁμαρτάνοντας καταδιώξεται κακά ἡ δὲ ὁδὸς τῶν ἀσεβῶν πλανήσει αὐτούς

text_en: The deceitful man shall not find gain: but the substance of a just man shall be precious gold.
text_la: Non inveniet fraudulentus lucrum, et substantia hominis erit auri pretium.
text_pt: O preguiçoso deixa de assar a sua caça, mas ser diligente é o precioso bem do homem.
text_el: οὐκ ἐπιτεύξεται δόλιος θήρας κτῆμα δὲ τίμιον ἀνὴρ καθαρός

text_en: In the path of justice is life: but the bye-way leads to death.
text_la: In semita justitiæ vita; iter autem devium ducit ad mortem.
text_pt: Na vereda da justiça está a vida, e no caminho da sua carreira não há morte.
text_el: ἐν ὁδοῖς δικαιοσύνης ζωή ὁδοὶ δὲ μνησικάκων εἰς θάνατον

text_en: A wise son hears the doctrine of his father: but he that is a scorner, hears not when he is reproved.
text_la: Filius sapiens doctrina patris; qui autem illusor est non audit cum arguitur.
text_pt: O filho sábio atende à instrução do pai; mas o escarnecedor não ouve a repreensão.
text_el: υἱὸς πανοῦργος ὑπήκοος πατρί υἱὸς δὲ ἀνήκοος ἐν ἀπωλείᾳ

text_en: Of the fruit of his own month shall a man be filled with good things: but the soul of transgressors is wicked .
text_la: De fructu oris sui homo satiabitur bonis : anima autem prævaricatorum iniqua.
text_pt: Do fruto da boca cada um comerá o bem, mas a alma dos prevaricadores comerá a violência.
text_el: ἀπὸ καρπῶν δικαιοσύνης φάγεται ἀγαθός ψυχαὶ δὲ παρανόμων ὀλοῦνται ἄωροι

text_en: He that keeps his mouth keeps his soul : but he that has no guard on his speech shall meet with evils .
text_la: Qui custodit os suum custodit animam suam; qui autem inconsideratus est ad loquendum, sentiet mala.
text_pt: O que guarda a sua boca conserva a sua alma, mas o que abre muito os seus lábios se destrói.
text_el: ὃς φυλάσσει τὸ ἑαυτοῦ στόμα τηρεῖ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχήν ὁ δὲ προπετὴς χείλεσιν πτοήσει ἑαυτόν

text_en: The sluggard wills, and wills not: but the soul of them that work, shall be made fat.
text_la: Vult et non vult piger; anima autem operantium impinguabitur.
text_pt: A alma do preguiçoso deseja, e coisa nenhuma alcança, mas a alma dos diligentes se farta.
text_el: ἐν ἐπιθυμίαις ἐστὶν πᾶς ἀεργός χεῖρες δὲ ἀνδρείων ἐν ἐπιμελείᾳ

text_en: The just shall hate a lying word: but the wicked confounds, and shall be confounded.
text_la: Verbum mendax justus detestabitur; impius autem confundit, et confundetur.
text_pt: O justo odeia a palavra de mentira, mas o ímpio faz vergonha e se confunde.
text_el: λόγον ἄδικον μισεῖ δίκαιος ἀσεβὴς δὲ αἰσχύνεται καὶ οὐχ ἕξει παρρησίαν

text_en: Justice keeps the way of the innocent: but wickedness overthrows the sinner.
text_la: Justitia custodit innocentis viam, impietas autem peccatorem supplantat.
text_pt: A justiça guarda ao que é de caminho certo, mas a impiedade transtornará o pecador.
text_el: δικαιοσύνη φυλάσσει ἀκάκους τοὺς δὲ ἀσεβεῖς φαύλους ποιεῖ ἁμαρτία

text_en: One is as it were rich, when he has nothing and another is as it were poor, when he has great riches.
text_la: Est quasi dives, cum nihil habeat, et est quasi pauper, cum in multis divitiis sit.
text_pt: Há alguns que se fazem de ricos, e não têm coisa nenhuma, e outros que se fazem de pobres e têm muitas riquezas.
text_el: εἰσὶν οἱ πλουτίζοντες ἑαυτοὺς μηδὲν ἔχοντες καὶ εἰσὶν οἱ ταπεινοῦντες ἑαυτοὺς ἐν πολλῷ πλούτῳ

text_en: The ransom of a man's life are his riches: but he that is poor, bears not reprehension.
text_la: Redemptio animæ viri divitiæ suæ; qui autem pauper est, increpationem non sustinet.
text_pt: O resgate da vida de cada um são as suas riquezas, mas o pobre não ouve ameaças.
text_el: λύτρον ἀνδρὸς ψυχῆς ὁ ἴδιος πλοῦτος πτωχὸς δὲ οὐχ ὑφίσταται ἀπειλήν

text_en: The light of the just gives joy : but the lamp of the wicked shall be put out.
text_la: Lux justorum lætificat : lucerna autem impiorum extinguetur.
text_pt: A luz dos justos alegra, mas a candeia dos ímpios se apagará.
text_el: φῶς δικαίοις διὰ παντός φῶς δὲ ἀσεβῶν σβέννυται

text_en: Among the proud there are always contentions: but they that do all things with counsel, are ruled by wisdom.
text_la: Inter superbos semper jurgia sunt; qui autem agunt omnia cum consilio, reguntur sapientia.
text_pt: Da soberba só provém a contenda, mas com os que se aconselham se acha a sabedoria.
text_el: κακὸς μεθ' ὕβρεως πράσσει κακά οἱ δὲ ἑαυτῶν ἐπιγνώμονες σοφοί

text_en: Substance got in haste shall be diminished: but that which by little and little is gathered with the hand, shall increase.
text_la: Substantia festinata minuetur; quæ autem paulatim colligitur manu, multiplicabitur.
text_pt: A riqueza de procedência vã diminuirá, mas quem a ajunta com o próprio trabalho a aumentará.
text_el: ὕπαρξις ἐπισπουδαζομένη μετὰ ἀνομίας ἐλάσσων γίνεται ὁ δὲ συνάγων ἑαυτῷ μετ' εὐσεβείας πληθυνθήσεται δίκαιος οἰκτίρει καὶ κιχρᾷ

text_en: Hope that is deferred afflicts the soul : desire when it comes, is a tree of life.
text_la: Spes quæ differtur affligit animam; lignum vitæ desiderium veniens.
text_pt: A esperança adiada desfalece o coração, mas o desejo atendido é árvore de vida.
text_el: κρείσσων ἐναρχόμενος βοηθῶν καρδίᾳ τοῦ ἐπαγγελλομένου καὶ εἰς ἐλπίδα ἄγοντος δένδρον γὰρ ζωῆς ἐπιθυμία ἀγαθή

text_en: Whosoever speaks ill of anything, binds himself for the time to come: but he that fears the commandment, shall dwell in peace. Deceitful souls go astray in sins : the just are merciful, and show mercy.
text_la: Qui detrahit alicui rei, ipse se in futurum obligat; qui autem timet præceptum, in pace versabitur. Animæ dolosæ errant in peccatis : justi autem misericordes sunt, et miserantur.
text_pt: O que despreza a palavra perecerá, mas o que teme o mandamento será galardoado.
text_el: ὃς καταφρονεῖ πράγματος καταφρονηθήσεται ὑπ' αὐτοῦ ὁ δὲ φοβούμενος ἐντολήν οὗτος ὑγιαίνει

text_en: The law of the wise is a fountain of life, that he may decline from the ruin of death.
text_la: Lex sapientis fons vitæ, ut declinet a ruina mortis.
text_pt: A doutrina do sábio é uma fonte de vida para se desviar dos laços da morte.
text_el: νόμος σοφοῦ πηγὴ ζωῆς ὁ δὲ ἄνους ὑπὸ παγίδος θανεῖται

text_en: Good instruction shall give grace : in the way of scorners is a deep pit.
text_la: Doctrina bona dabit gratiam; in itinere contemptorum vorago.
text_pt: O bom entendimento favorece, mas o caminho dos prevaricadores é áspero.
text_el: σύνεσις ἀγαθὴ δίδωσιν χάριν τὸ δὲ γνῶναι νόμον διανοίας ἐστὶν ἀγαθῆς ὁδοὶ δὲ καταφρονούντων ἐν ἀπωλείᾳ

text_en: The prudent man does all things with counsel: but he that is a fool, lays open his folly.
text_la: Astutus omnia agit cum consilio; qui autem fatuus est aperit stultitiam.
text_pt: Todo prudente procede com conhecimento, mas o insensato espraia a sua loucura.
text_el: πᾶς πανοῦργος πράσσει μετὰ γνώσεως ὁ δὲ ἄφρων ἐξεπέτασεν ἑαυτοῦ κακίαν

text_en: The messenger of the wicked shall fall into mischief: but a faithful ambassador is health.
text_la: Nuntius impii cadet in malum; legatus autem fidelis, sanitas.
text_pt: O que prega a maldade cai no mal, mas o embaixador fiel é saúde.
text_el: βασιλεὺς θρασὺς ἐμπεσεῖται εἰς κακά ἄγγελος δὲ πιστὸς ῥύσεται αὐτόν

text_en: Poverty and shame to him that refuses instruction: but he that yields to reproof shall be glorified .
text_la: Egestas et ignominia ei qui deserit disciplinam; qui autem acquiescit arguenti glorificabitur.
text_pt: Pobreza e afronta virão ao que rejeita a instrução, mas o que guarda a repreensão será honrado.
text_el: πενίαν καὶ ἀτιμίαν ἀφαιρεῖται παιδεία ὁ δὲ φυλάσσων ἐλέγχους δοξασθήσεται

text_en: The desire that is accomplished, delights the soul : fools hate them that flee from evil things.
text_la: Desiderium si compleatur delectat animam; detestantur stulti eos qui fugiunt mala.
text_pt: O desejo que se alcança deleita a alma, mas apartar-se do mal é abominável para os insensatos.
text_el: ἐπιθυμίαι εὐσεβῶν ἡδύνουσιν ψυχήν ἔργα δὲ ἀσεβῶν μακρὰν ἀπὸ γνώσεως

text_en: He that walks with the wise, shall be wise: a friend of fools shall become like to them.
text_la: Qui cum sapientibus graditur sapiens erit; amicus stultorum similis efficietur.
text_pt: O que anda com os sábios ficará sábio, mas o companheiro dos tolos será destruído.
text_el: ὁ συμπορευόμενος σοφοῖς σοφὸς ἔσται ὁ δὲ συμπορευόμενος ἄφροσι γνωσθήσεται

text_en: Evil pursues sinners: and to the just good shall be repaid.
text_la: Peccatores persequitur malum, et justis retribuentur bona.
text_pt: O mal perseguirá os pecadores, mas os justos serão galardoados com o bem.
text_el: ἁμαρτάνοντας καταδιώξεται κακά τοὺς δὲ δικαίους καταλήμψεται ἀγαθά

text_en: The good man leaves heirs, sons, and grandsons: and the substance of the sinner is kept for the just .
text_la: Bonus reliquit hæredes filios et nepotes, et custoditur justo substantia peccatoris.
text_pt: O homem de bem deixa uma herança aos filhos de seus filhos, mas a riqueza do pecador é depositada para o justo.
text_el: ἀγαθὸς ἀνὴρ κληρονομήσει υἱοὺς υἱῶν θησαυρίζεται δὲ δικαίοις πλοῦτος ἀσεβὼν

text_en: Much food is in the tillage of fathers: but for others it is gathered without judgment.
text_la: Multi cibi in novalibus patrum, et aliis congregantur absque judicio.
text_pt: O pobre, do sulco da terra, tira mantimento em abundância; mas há os que se consomem por falta de juízo.
text_el: δίκαιοι ποιήσουσιν ἐν πλούτῳ ἔτη πολλά ἄδικοι δὲ ἀπολοῦνται συντόμως

text_en: He that spares the rod, hates his son: but he that loves him, corrects him betimes.
text_la: Qui parcit virgæ odit filium suum; qui autem diligit illum instanter erudit.
text_pt: O que não faz uso da vara odeia seu filho, mas o que o ama, desde cedo o castiga.
text_el: ὃς φείδεται τῆς βακτηρίας μισεῖ τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ ὁ δὲ ἀγαπῶν ἐπιμελῶς παιδεύει

text_en: The just eats and fills his soul : but the belly of the wicked is never to be filled.
text_la: Justus comedit et replet animam suam; venter autem impiorum insaturabilis.
text_pt: O justo come até ficar satisfeito, mas o ventre dos ímpios passará necessidade.
text_el: δίκαιος ἔσθων ἐμπιπλᾷ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ψυχαὶ δὲ ἀσεβῶν ἐνδεεῖς

text_en: A wise woman builds her house: but the foolish will pull down with her hands that also which is built.
text_la: Sapiens mulier ædificat domum suam; insipiens exstructam quoque manibus destruet.
text_pt: Toda mulher sábia edifica a sua casa; mas a tola a derruba com as próprias mãos.
text_el: σοφαὶ γυναῖκες ᾠκοδόμησαν οἴκους ἡ δὲ ἄφρων κατέσκαψεν ταῖς χερσὶν αὐτῆς

text_en: He that walks in the right way, and fears God , is despised by him that goes by an infamous way.
text_la: Ambulans recto itinere, et timens Deum, despicitur ab eo qui infami graditur via.
text_pt: O que anda na retidão teme ao Senhor, mas o que se desvia de seus caminhos o despreza.
text_el: ὁ πορευόμενος ὀρθῶς φοβεῖται τὸν κύριον ὁ δὲ σκολιάζων ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτοῦ ἀτιμασθήσεται

text_en: In the mouth of a fool is the rod of pride : but the lips of the wise preserve them.
text_la: In ore stulti virga superbiæ; labia autem sapientium custodiunt eos.
text_pt: Na boca do tolo está a punição da soberba, mas os sábios se conservam pelos próprios lábios.
text_el: ἐκ στόματος ἀφρόνων βακτηρία ὕβρεως χείλη δὲ σοφῶν φυλάσσει αὐτούς

text_en: Where there are no oxen, the crib is empty: but where there is much corn, there the strength of the ox is manifest.
text_la: Ubi non sunt boves, præsepe vacuum est; ubi autem plurimæ segetes, ibi manifesta est fortitudo bovis.
text_pt: Não havendo bois o estábulo fica limpo, mas pela força do boi há abundância de colheita.
text_el: οὗ μή εἰσιν βόες φάτναι καθαραί οὗ δὲ πολλὰ γενήματα φανερὰ βοὸς ἰσχύς

text_en: A faithful witness will not lie: but a deceitful witness utters a lie.
text_la: Testis fidelis non mentitur; profert autem mendacium dolosus testis.
text_pt: A verdadeira testemunha não mentirá, mas a testemunha falsa se desboca em mentiras.
text_el: μάρτυς πιστὸς οὐ ψεύδεται ἐκκαίει δὲ ψεύδη μάρτυς ἄδικος

text_en: A scorner seeks wisdom, and finds it not: the learning of the wise is easy.
text_la: Quærit derisor sapientiam, et non invenit; doctrina prudentium facilis.
text_pt: O escarnecedor busca sabedoria e não acha nenhuma, para o prudente, porém, o conhecimento é fácil.
text_el: ζητήσεις σοφίαν παρὰ κακοῖς καὶ οὐχ εὑρήσεις αἴσθησις δὲ παρὰ φρονίμοις εὐχερής

text_en: Go against a foolish man , and he knows not the lips of prudence .
text_la: Vade contra virum stultum, et nescit labia prudentiæ.
text_pt: Desvia-te do homem insensato, porque nele não acharás lábios de conhecimento.
text_el: πάντα ἐναντία ἀνδρὶ ἄφρονι ὅπλα δὲ αἰσθήσεως χείλη σοφά

text_en: The wisdom of a discreet man is to understand his way: and the imprudence of fools errs.
text_la: Sapientia callidi est intelligere viam suam, et imprudentia stultorum errans.
text_pt: A sabedoria do prudente é entender o seu caminho, mas a estultícia dos insensatos é engano.
text_el: σοφία πανούργων ἐπιγνώσεται τὰς ὁδοὺς αὐτῶν ἄνοια δὲ ἀφρόνων ἐν πλάνῃ

text_en: A fool will laugh at sin , but among the just grace shall abide.
text_la: Stultus illudet peccatum, et inter justos morabitur gratia.
text_pt: Os insensatos zombam do pecado, mas entre os retos há benevolência.
text_el: οἰκίαι παρανόμων ὀφειλήσουσιν καθαρισμόν οἰκίαι δὲ δικαίων δεκταί

text_en: The heart that knows the bitterness of his own soul , in his joy the stranger shall not intermeddle.
text_la: Cor quod novit amaritudinem animæ suæ, in gaudio ejus non miscebitur extraneus.
text_pt: O coração conhece a sua própria amargura, e o estranho não participará no íntimo da sua alegria.
text_el: καρδία ἀνδρὸς αἰσθητική λυπηρὰ ψυχὴ αὐτοῦ ὅταν δὲ εὐφραίνηται οὐκ ἐπιμείγνυται ὕβρει

text_en: The house of the wicked shall be destroyed: but the tabernacles of the just shall flourish.
text_la: Domus impiorum delebitur : tabernacula vero justorum germinabunt.
text_pt: A casa dos ímpios se desfará, mas a tenda dos retos florescerá.
text_el: οἰκίαι ἀσεβῶν ἀφανισθήσονται σκηναὶ δὲ κατορθούντων στήσονται

text_en: There is a way which seems just to a man : but the ends thereof lead to death.
text_la: Est via quæ videtur homini justa, novissima autem ejus deducunt ad mortem.
text_pt: Há um caminho que ao homem parece direito, mas o fim dele são os caminhos da morte.
text_el: ἔστιν ὁδὸς ἣ δοκεῖ ὀρθὴ εἶναι παρὰ ἀνθρώποις τὰ δὲ τελευταῖα αὐτῆς ἔρχεται εἰς πυθμένα ᾅδου

text_en: Laughter shall be mingled with sorrow, and mourning takes hold of the ends of joy .
text_la: Risus dolore miscebitur, et extrema gaudii luctus occupat.
text_pt: Até no riso o coração sente dor e o fim da alegria é tristeza.
text_el: ἐν εὐφροσύναις οὐ προσμείγνυται λύπη τελευταία δὲ χαρὰ εἰς πένθος ἔρχεται

text_en: A fool shall be filled with his own ways, and the good man shall be above him.
text_la: Viis suis replebitur stultus, et super eum erit vir bonus.
text_pt: O que no seu coração comete deslize, se enfada dos seus caminhos, mas o homem bom fica satisfeito com o seu proceder.
text_el: τῶν ἑαυτοῦ ὁδῶν πλησθήσεται θρασυκάρδιος ἀπὸ δὲ τῶν διανοημάτων αὐτοῦ ἀνὴρ ἀγαθός

text_en: The innocent believes every word: the discreet man considers his steps. No good shall come to the deceitful son: but the wise servant shall prosper in his dealings, and his way shall be made straight.
text_la: Innocens credit omni verbo; astutus considerat gressus suos. Filio doloso nihil erit boni; servo autem sapienti prosperi erunt actus, et dirigetur via ejus.
text_pt: O simples dá crédito a cada palavra, mas o prudente atenta para os seus passos.
text_el: ἄκακος πιστεύει παντὶ λόγῳ πανοῦργος δὲ ἔρχεται εἰς μετάνοιαν

text_en: A wise man fears, and declines from evil : the fool leaps over, and is confident.
text_la: Sapiens timet, et declinat a malo; stultus transilit, et confidit.
text_pt: O sábio teme, e desvia-se do mal, mas o tolo se encoleriza, e dá-se por seguro.
text_el: σοφὸς φοβηθεὶς ἐξέκλινεν ἀπὸ κακοῦ ὁ δὲ ἄφρων ἑαυτῷ πεποιθὼς μείγνυται ἀνόμῳ

text_en: The impatient man shall work folly: and the crafty man is hateful .
text_la: Impatiens operabitur stultitiam, et vir versutus odiosus est.
text_pt: O que se indigna à toa fará doidices, e o homem de maus intentos será odiado.
text_el: ὀξύθυμος πράσσει μετὰ ἀβουλίας ἀνὴρ δὲ φρόνιμος πολλὰ ὑποφέρει

text_en: The childish shall possess folly, and the prudent shall look for knowledge .
text_la: Possidebunt parvuli stultitiam, et exspectabunt astuti scientiam.
text_pt: Os simples herdarão a estultícia, mas os prudentes serão coroados de conhecimento.
text_el: μεριοῦνται ἄφρονες κακίαν οἱ δὲ πανοῦργοι κρατήσουσιν αἰσθήσεως

text_en: The evil shall fall down before the good : and the wicked before the gates of the just .
text_la: Jacebunt mali ante bonos, et impii ante portas justorum.
text_pt: Os maus inclinam-se diante dos bons, e os ímpios diante das portas dos justos.
text_el: ὀλισθήσουσιν κακοὶ ἔναντι ἀγαθῶν καὶ ἀσεβεῖς θεραπεύσουσιν θύρας δικαίων

text_en: The poor man shall be hateful even to his own neighbour: but the friends of the rich are many.
text_la: Etiam proximo suo pauper odiosus erit : amici vero divitum multi.
text_pt: O pobre é odiado até pelo seu próximo, porém os amigos dos ricos são muitos.
text_el: φίλοι μισήσουσιν φίλους πτωχούς φίλοι δὲ πλουσίων πολλοί

text_en: He that despises his neighbour, sins : but he that shows mercy to the poor, shall be blessed . He that believes in the Lord , loves mercy.
text_la: Qui despicit proximum suum peccat; qui autem miseretur pauperis beatus erit. Qui credit in Domino misericordiam diligit.
text_pt: O que despreza ao seu próximo peca, mas o que se compadece dos humildes é bem-aventurado.
text_el: ὁ ἀτιμάζων πένητας ἁμαρτάνει ἐλεῶν δὲ πτωχοὺς μακαριστός

text_en: They err that work evil : but mercy and truth prepare good things.
text_la: Errant qui operantur malum; misericordia et veritas præparant bona.
text_pt: Porventura não erram os que praticam o mal? mas beneficência e fidelidade haverá para os que praticam o bem.
text_el: πλανώμενοι τεκταίνουσι κακά ἔλεον δὲ καὶ ἀλήθειαν τεκταίνουσιν ἀγαθοί οὐκ ἐπίστανται ἔλεον καὶ πίστιν τέκτονες κακῶν ἐλεημοσύναι δὲ καὶ πίστεις παρὰ τέκτοσιν ἀγαθοῖς

text_en: In much work there shall be abundance: but where there are many words, there is oftentimes want.
text_la: In omni opere erit abundantia; ubi autem verba sunt plurima, ibi frequenter egestas.
text_pt: Em todo trabalho há proveito, mas ficar só em palavras leva à pobreza.
text_el: ἐν παντὶ μεριμνῶντι ἔνεστιν περισσόν ὁ δὲ ἡδὺς καὶ ἀνάλγητος ἐν ἐνδείᾳ ἔσται

text_en: The crown of the wise, is their riches: the folly of fools, imprudence.
text_la: Corona sapientium divitiæ eorum; fatuitas stultorum imprudentia.
text_pt: A coroa dos sábios é a sua riqueza, a estultícia dos tolos é só estultícia.
text_el: στέφανος σοφῶν πανοῦργος ἡ δὲ διατριβὴ ἀφρόνων κακή

text_en: A faithful witness delivers souls : and the double dealer utters lies.
text_la: Liberat animas testis fidelis, et profert mendacia versipellis.
text_pt: A testemunha verdadeira livra as almas, mas o que se desboca em mentiras é enganador.
text_el: ῥύσεται ἐκ κακῶν ψυχὴν μάρτυς πιστός ἐκκαίει δὲ ψεύδη δόλιος

text_en: In the fear of the Lord is confidence of strength, and there shall be hope for his children.
text_la: In timore Domini fiducia fortitudinis, et filiis ejus erit spes.
text_pt: No temor do Senhor há firme confiança e ele será um refúgio para seus filhos.
text_el: ἐν φόβῳ κυρίου ἐλπὶς ἰσχύος τοῖς δὲ τέκνοις αὐτοῦ καταλείπει ἔρεισμα

text_en: The fear of the Lord is a fountain of life, to decline from the ruin of death.
text_la: Timor Domini fons vitæ, ut declinent a ruina mortis.
text_pt: O temor do Senhor é fonte de vida, para desviar dos laços da morte.
text_el: πρόσταγμα κυρίου πηγὴ ζωῆς ποιεῖ δὲ ἐκκλίνειν ἐκ παγίδος θανάτου

text_en: In the multitude of people is the dignity of the king: and in the small number of the people the dishonour of the prince.
text_la: In multitudine populi dignitas regis, et in paucitate plebis ignominia principis.
text_pt: Na multidão do povo está a glória do rei, mas na falta de povo a ruína do príncipe.
text_el: ἐν πολλῷ ἔθνει δόξα βασιλέως ἐν δὲ ἐκλείψει λαοῦ συντριβὴ δυνάστου

text_en: He that is patient, is governed with much wisdom: but he that is impatient, exalts his folly.
text_la: Qui patiens est multa gubernatur prudentia; qui autem impatiens est exaltat stultitiam suam.
text_pt: O longânimo é grande em entendimento, mas o que é de espírito impaciente mostra a sua loucura.
text_el: μακρόθυμος ἀνὴρ πολὺς ἐν φρονήσει ὁ δὲ ὀλιγόψυχος ἰσχυρῶς ἄφρων

text_en: Soundness of heart is the life of the flesh: but envy is the rottenness of the bones.
text_la: Vita carnium sanitas cordis; putredo ossium invidia.
text_pt: O sentimento sadio é vida para o corpo, mas a inveja é podridão para os ossos.
text_el: πραΰθυμος ἀνὴρ καρδίας ἰατρός σὴς δὲ ὀστέων καρδία αἰσθητική

text_en: He that oppresses the poor, upbraids his maker: but he that has pity on the poor, honours him.
text_la: Qui calumniatur egentem exprobrat factori ejus; honorat autem eum qui miseretur pauperis.
text_pt: O que oprime o pobre insulta àquele que o criou, mas o que se compadece do necessitado o honra.
text_el: ὁ συκοφαντῶν πένητα παροξύνει τὸν ποιήσαντα αὐτόν ὁ δὲ τιμῶν αὐτὸν ἐλεᾷ πτωχόν

text_en: The wicked man shall be driven out in his wickedness : but the just has hope in his death.
text_la: In malitia sua expelletur impius : sperat autem justus in morte sua.
text_pt: Pela sua própria malícia é lançado fora o perverso, mas o justo até na morte se mantém confiante.
text_el: ἐν κακίᾳ αὐτοῦ ἀπωσθήσεται ἀσεβής ὁ δὲ πεποιθὼς τῇ ἑαυτοῦ ὁσιότητι δίκαιος

text_en: In the heart of the prudent rests wisdom, and it shall instruct all the ignorant .
text_la: In corde prudentis requiescit sapientia, et indoctos quosque erudiet.
text_pt: No coração do prudente a sabedoria permanece, mas o que está no interior dos tolos se faz conhecido.
text_el: ἐν καρδίᾳ ἀγαθῇ ἀνδρὸς σοφία ἐν δὲ καρδίᾳ ἀφρόνων οὐ διαγινώσκεται

text_en: Justice exalts a nation: but sin makes nations miserable.
text_la: Justitia elevat gentem; miseros autem facit populos peccatum.
text_pt: A justiça exalta os povos, mas o pecado é a vergonha das nações.
text_el: δικαιοσύνη ὑψοῖ ἔθνος ἐλασσονοῦσι δὲ φυλὰς ἁμαρτίαι

text_en: A wise servant is acceptable to the king: he that is good for nothing shall feel his anger .
text_la: Acceptus est regi minister intelligens; iracundiam ejus inutilis sustinebit.
text_pt: O rei se alegra no servo prudente, mas sobre o que o envergonha cairá o seu furor.
text_el: δεκτὸς βασιλεῖ ὑπηρέτης νοήμων τῇ δὲ ἑαυτοῦ εὐστροφίᾳ ἀφαιρεῖται ἀτιμίαν

text_en: A mild answer breaks wrath : but a harsh word stirs up fury.
text_la: Responsio mollis frangit iram; sermo durus suscitat furorem.
text_pt: A resposta branda desvia o furor, mas a palavra dura suscita a ira.
text_el: ὀργὴ ἀπόλλυσιν καὶ φρονίμους ἀπόκρισις δὲ ὑποπίπτουσα ἀποστρέφει θυμόν λόγος δὲ λυπηρὸς ἐγείρει ὀργάς

text_en: The tongue of the wise adorns knowledge : but the mouth of fools bubbles out folly.
text_la: Lingua sapientium ornat scientiam; os fatuorum ebullit stultitiam.
text_pt: A língua dos sábios adorna a sabedoria, mas a boca dos tolos derrama a estultícia.
text_el: γλῶσσα σοφῶν καλὰ ἐπίσταται στόμα δὲ ἀφρόνων ἀναγγελεῖ κακά

text_en: The eyes of the Lord in every place behold the good and the evil .
text_la: In omni loco, oculi Domini contemplantur bonos et malos.
text_pt: Os olhos do Senhor estão em todo lugar, contemplando os maus e os bons.
text_el: ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ ὀφθαλμοὶ κυρίου σκοπεύουσιν κακούς τε καὶ ἀγαθούς

text_en: A peaceable tongue is a tree of life: but that which is immoderate, shall crush the spirit.
text_la: Lingua placabilis lignum vitæ; quæ autem immoderata est conteret spiritum.
text_pt: A língua benigna é árvore de vida, mas a perversidade nela deprime o espírito.
text_el: ἴασις γλώσσης δένδρον ζωῆς ὁ δὲ συντηρῶν αὐτὴν πλησθήσεται πνεύματος

text_en: A fool laughs at the instruction of his father: but he that regards reproofs shall become prudent . In abundant justice there is the greatest strength: but the devices of the wicked shall be rooted out.
text_la: Stultus irridet disciplinam patris sui; qui autem custodit increpationes astutior fiet. In abundanti justitia virtus maxima est : cogitationes autem impiorum eradicabuntur.
text_pt: O tolo despreza a instrução de seu pai, mas o que observa a repreensão se haverá prudentemente.
text_el: ἄφρων μυκτηρίζει παιδείαν πατρός ὁ δὲ φυλάσσων ἐντολὰς πανουργότερος

text_en: The house of the just is very much strength: and in the fruits of the wicked is trouble.
text_la: Domus justi plurima fortitudo, et in fructibus impii conturbatio.
text_pt: Na casa do justo há um grande tesouro, mas nos ganhos do ímpio há perturbação.
text_el: ἐν πλεοναζούσῃ δικαιοσύνῃ ἰσχὺς πολλή οἱ δὲ ἀσεβεῖς ὁλόρριζοι ἐκ γῆς ὀλοῦνται οἴκοις δικαίων ἰσχὺς πολλή καρποὶ δὲ ἀσεβῶν ἀπολοῦνται

text_en: The lips of the wise shall disperse knowledge : the heart of fools shall be unlike.
text_la: Labia sapientium disseminabunt scientiam; cor stultorum dissimile erit.
text_pt: Os lábios dos sábios derramam o conhecimento, mas o coração dos tolos não faz assim.
text_el: χείλη σοφῶν δέδεται αἰσθήσει καρδίαι δὲ ἀφρόνων οὐκ ἀσφαλεῖς

text_en: The victims of the wicked are abominable to the Lord : the vows of the just are acceptable.
text_la: Victimæ impiorum abominabiles Domino; vota justorum placabilia.
text_pt: O sacrifício dos ímpios é abominável ao Senhor, mas a oração dos retos é o seu contentamento.
text_el: θυσίαι ἀσεβῶν βδέλυγμα κυρίῳ εὐχαὶ δὲ κατευθυνόντων δεκταὶ παρ' αὐτῷ

text_en: The way of the wicked is an abomination to the Lord : he that follows justice is beloved by him.
text_la: Abominatio est Domino via impii; qui sequitur justitiam diligitur ab eo.
text_pt: O caminho do ímpio é abominável ao Senhor, mas ao que segue a justiça ele ama.
text_el: βδέλυγμα κυρίῳ ὁδοὶ ἀσεβοῦς διώκοντας δὲ δικαιοσύνην ἀγαπᾷ

text_en: Instruction is grievous to him that forsakes the way of life: he that hates reproof shall die.
text_la: Doctrina mala deserenti viam vitæ; qui increpationes odit, morietur.
text_pt: Correção severa há para o que deixa a vereda, e o que odeia a repreensão morrerá.
text_el: παιδεία ἀκάκου γνωρίζεται ὑπὸ τῶν παριόντων οἱ δὲ μισοῦντες ἐλέγχους τελευτῶσιν αἰσχρῶς

text_en: Hell and destruction are before the Lord : how much more the hearts of the children of men ?
text_la: Infernus et perditio coram Domino; quanto magis corda filiorum hominum!
text_pt: O inferno e a perdição estão perante o Senhor; quanto mais os corações dos filhos dos homens?
text_el: ᾅδης καὶ ἀπώλεια φανερὰ παρὰ τῷ κυρίῳ πῶς οὐχὶ καὶ αἱ καρδίαι τῶν ἀνθρώπων

text_en: A corrupt man loves not one that reproves him: nor will he go to the wise.
text_la: Non amat pestilens eum qui se corripit, nec ad sapientes graditur.
text_pt: O escarnecedor não ama aquele que o repreende, nem se chegará aos sábios.
text_el: οὐκ ἀγαπήσει ἀπαίδευτος τοὺς ἐλέγχοντας αὐτόν μετὰ δὲ σοφῶν οὐχ ὁμιλήσει

text_en: A glad heart makes a cheerful countenance: but by grief of mind the spirit is cast down.
text_la: Cor gaudens exhilarat faciem; in mœrore animi dejicitur spiritus.
text_pt: O coração alegre aformoseia o rosto, mas pela dor do coração o espírito se abate.
text_el: καρδίας εὐφραινομένης πρόσωπον θάλλει ἐν δὲ λύπαις οὔσης σκυθρωπάζει

text_en: The heart of the wise seeks instruction: and the mouth of fools feeds on foolishness.
text_la: Cor sapientis quærit doctrinam, et os stultorum pascitur imperitia.
text_pt: O coração entendido buscará o conhecimento, mas a boca dos tolos se apascentará de estultícia.
text_el: καρδία ὀρθὴ ζητεῖ αἴσθησιν στόμα δὲ ἀπαιδεύτων γνώσεται κακά

text_en: All the days of the poor are evil : a secure mind is like a continual feast.
text_la: Omnes dies pauperis, mali; secura mens quasi juge convivium.
text_pt: Todos os dias do oprimido são maus, mas o coração alegre é um banquete contínuo.
text_el: πάντα τὸν χρόνον οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ τῶν κακῶν προσδέχονται κακά οἱ δὲ ἀγαθοὶ ἡσυχάζουσιν διὰ παντός

text_en: Better is a little with the fear of the Lord , than great treasures without content.
text_la: Melius est parum cum timore Domini, quam thesauri magni et insatiabiles.
text_pt: Melhor é o pouco com o temor do Senhor, do que um grande tesouro onde há inquietação.
text_el: κρείσσων μικρὰ μερὶς μετὰ φόβου κυρίου ἢ θησαυροὶ μεγάλοι μετὰ ἀφοβίας

text_en: It is better to be invited to herbs with love , than to a fatted calf with hatred .
text_la: Melius est vocari ad olera cum caritate, quam ad vitulum saginatum cum odio.
text_pt: Melhor é a comida de hortaliça, onde há amor, do que o boi cevado, e com ele o ódio.
text_el: κρείσσων ξενισμὸς λαχάνων πρὸς φιλίαν καὶ χάριν ἢ παράθεσις μόσχων μετὰ ἔχθρας

text_en: A passionate man stirs up strifes: he that is patient appeases those that are stirred up.
text_la: Vir iracundus provocat rixas; qui patiens est mitigat suscitatas.
text_pt: O homem iracundo suscita contendas, mas o longânimo apaziguará a luta.
text_el: ἀνὴρ θυμώδης παρασκευάζει μάχας μακρόθυμος δὲ καὶ τὴν μέλλουσαν καταπραΰνει

text_en: The way of the slothful is as a hedge of thorns: the way of the just is without offence.
text_la: Iter pigrorum quasi sepes spinarum; via justorum absque offendiculo.
text_pt: O caminho do preguiçoso é cercado de espinhos, mas a vereda dos retos é bem aplanada.
text_el: ὁδοὶ ἀεργῶν ἐστρωμέναι ἀκάνθαις αἱ δὲ τῶν ἀνδρείων τετριμμέναι

text_en: A wise son makes a father joyful: but the foolish man despises his mother.
text_la: Filius sapiens lætificat patrem, et stultus homo despicit matrem suam.
text_pt: O filho sábio alegra seu pai, mas o homem insensato despreza a sua mãe.
text_el: υἱὸς σοφὸς εὐφραίνει πατέρα υἱὸς δὲ ἄφρων μυκτηρίζει μητέρα αὐτοῦ

text_en: Folly is joy to the fool: and the wise man makes straight his steps.
text_la: Stultitia gaudium stulto, et vir prudens dirigit gressus suos.
text_pt: A estultícia é alegria para o que carece de entendimento, mas o homem entendido anda retamente.
text_el: ἀνοήτου τρίβοι ἐνδεεῖς φρενῶν ἀνὴρ δὲ φρόνιμος κατευθύνων πορεύεται

text_en: Designs are brought to nothing where there is no counsel: but where there are many counsellors, they are established.
text_la: Dissipantur cogitationes ubi non est consilium; ubi vero sunt plures consiliarii, confirmantur.
text_pt: Quando não há conselhos os planos se dispersam, mas havendo muitos conselheiros eles se firmam.
text_el: ὑπερτίθενται λογισμοὺς οἱ μὴ τιμῶντες συνέδρια ἐν δὲ καρδίαις βουλευομένων μένει βουλή

text_en: A man rejoices in the sentence of his mouth: and a word in due time is best.
text_la: Lætatur homo in sententia oris sui, et sermo opportunus est optimus.
text_pt: O homem se alegra em responder bem, e quão boa é a palavra dita a seu tempo!
text_el: οὐ μὴ ὑπακούσῃ ὁ κακὸς αὐτῇ οὐδὲ μὴ εἴπῃ καίριόν τι καὶ καλὸν τῷ κοινῷ

text_en: The path of life is above for the wise, that he may decline from the lowest hell.
text_la: Semita vitæ super eruditum, ut declinet de inferno novissimo.
text_pt: Para o entendido, o caminho da vida leva para cima, para que se desvie do inferno em baixo.
text_el: ὁδοὶ ζωῆς διανοήματα συνετοῦ ἵνα ἐκκλίνας ἐκ τοῦ ᾅδου σωθῇ

text_en: The Lord will destroy the house of the proud : and will strengthen the borders of the widow .
text_la: Domum superborum demolietur Dominus, et firmos faciet terminos viduæ.
text_pt: O Senhor desarraiga a casa dos soberbos, mas estabelece o termo da viúva.
text_el: οἴκους ὑβριστῶν κατασπᾷ κύριος ἐστήρισεν δὲ ὅριον χήρας

text_en: Evil thoughts are an abomination to the Lord : and pure words most beautiful shall be confirmed by him.
text_la: Abominatio Domini cogitationes malæ, et purus sermo pulcherrimus firmabitur ab eo.
text_pt: Abomináveis são para o Senhor os pensamentos do mau, mas as palavras dos puros são aprazíveis.
text_el: βδέλυγμα κυρίῳ λογισμὸς ἄδικος ἁγνῶν δὲ ῥήσεις σεμναί

text_en: He that is greedy of gain troubles his own house: but he that hates bribes shall live. By mercy and faith sins are purged away: and by the fear of the Lord every one declines from evil .
text_la: Conturbat domum suam qui sectatur avaritiam; qui autem odit munera, vivet. Per misericordiam et fidem purgantur peccata : per timorem autem Domini declinat omnis a malo.
text_pt: O que agir com avareza perturba a sua casa, mas o que odeia presentes viverá.
text_el: ἐξόλλυσιν ἑαυτὸν ὁ δωρολήμπτης ὁ δὲ μισῶν δώρων λήμψεις σῴζεται

text_en: The mind of the just studies obedience : the mouth of the wicked overflows with evils .
text_la: Mens justi meditatur obedientiam; os impiorum redundat malis.
text_pt: O coração do justo medita no que há de responder, mas a boca dos ímpios jorra coisas más.
text_el: καρδίαι δικαίων μελετῶσιν πίστεις στόμα δὲ ἀσεβῶν ἀποκρίνεται κακά

text_en: The Lord is far from the wicked : and he will hear the prayers of the just .
text_la: Longe est Dominus ab impiis, et orationes justorum exaudiet.
text_pt: O Senhor está longe dos ímpios, mas a oração dos justos escutará.
text_el: μακρὰν ἀπέχει ὁ θεὸς ἀπὸ ἀσεβῶν εὐχαῖς δὲ δικαίων ἐπακούει

text_en: The light of the eyes rejoices the soul : a good name makes the bones fat.
text_la: Lux oculorum lætificat animam; fama bona impinguat ossa.
text_pt: A luz dos olhos alegra o coração, a boa notícia fortalece os ossos.
text_el: θεωρῶν ὀφθαλμὸς καλὰ εὐφραίνει καρδίαν φήμη δὲ ἀγαθὴ πιαίνει ὀστᾶ

text_en: The ear that hears the reproofs of life, shall abide in the midst of the wise.
text_la: Auris quæ audit increpationes vitæ in medio sapientium commorabitur.
text_pt: Os ouvidos que atendem à repreensão da vida farão a sua morada no meio dos sábios.

text_en: He that rejects instruction, despises his own soul : but he that yields to reproof, possesses understanding.
text_la: Qui abjicit disciplinam despicit animam suam; qui autem acquiescit increpationibus possessor est cordis.
text_pt: O que rejeita a instrução menospreza a própria alma, mas o que escuta a repreensão adquire entendimento.
text_el: ὃς ἀπωθεῖται παιδείαν μισεῖ ἑαυτόν ὁ δὲ τηρῶν ἐλέγχους ἀγαπᾷ ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ

text_en: The fear of the Lord is the lesson of wisdom: and humility goes before glory .
text_la: Timor Domini disciplina sapientiæ, et gloriam præcedit humilitas.
text_pt: O temor do Senhor é a instrução da sabedoria, e precedendo a honra vai a humildade.
text_el: φόβος θεοῦ παιδεία καὶ σοφία καὶ ἀρχὴ δόξης ἀποκριθήσεται αὐτῇ

text_en: It is the part of man to prepare the soul : and of the Lord to govern the tongue.
text_la: Hominis est animam præparare, et Domini gubernare linguam.
text_pt: Do homem são as preparações do coração, mas do SENHOR a resposta da língua.

text_en: All the ways of a man are open to his eyes: the Lord is the weigher of spirits.
text_la: Omnes viæ hominis patent oculis ejus; spirituum ponderator est Dominus.
text_pt: Todos os caminhos do homem são puros aos seus olhos, mas o Senhor pesa o espírito.
text_el: πάντα τὰ ἔργα τοῦ ταπεινοῦ φανερὰ παρὰ τῷ θεῷ οἱ δὲ ἀσεβεῖς ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κακῇ ὀλοῦνται

text_en: Lay open your works to the Lord : and your thoughts shall be directed.
text_la: Revela Domino opera tua, et dirigentur cogitationes tuæ.
text_pt: Confia ao Senhor as tuas obras, e teus pensamentos serão estabelecidos.

text_en: The Lord has made all things for himself: the wicked also for the evil day.
text_la: Universa propter semetipsum operatus est Dominus; impium quoque ad diem malum.
text_pt: O Senhor fez todas as coisas para atender aos seus próprios desígnios, até o ímpio para o dia do mal.

text_en: Every proud man is an abomination to the Lord : though hand should be joined to hand, he is not innocent. The beginning of a good way is to do justice : and this is more acceptable with God , than to offer sacrifices .
text_la: Abominatio Domini est omnis arrogans; etiamsi manus ad manum fuerit, non est innocens. Initium viæ bonæ facere justitiam; accepta est autem apud Deum magis quam immolare hostias.
text_pt: Abominação é ao Senhor todo o altivo de coração; não ficará impune mesmo de mãos postas.
text_el: ἀκάθαρτος παρὰ θεῷ πᾶς ὑψηλοκάρδιος χειρὶ δὲ χεῖρας ἐμβαλὼν ἀδίκως οὐκ ἀθῳωθήσεται

text_en: By mercy and truth iniquity is redeemed ; and by the fear of the Lord men depart from evil .
text_la: Misericordia et veritate redimitur iniquitas, et in timore Domini declinatur a malo.
text_pt: Pela misericórdia e verdade a iniqüidade é perdoada, e pelo temor do Senhor os homens se desviam do pecado.

text_en: When the ways of man shall please the Lord , he will convert even his enemies to peace.
text_la: Cum placuerint Domino viæ hominis, inimicos quoque ejus convertet ad pacem.
text_pt: Sendo os caminhos do homem agradáveis ao Senhor, até a seus inimigos faz que tenham paz com ele.
text_el: ἀρχὴ ὁδοῦ ἀγαθῆς τὸ ποιεῖν τὰ δίκαια δεκτὰ δὲ παρὰ θεῷ μᾶλλον ἢ θύειν θυσίας

text_en: Better is a little with justice , than great revenues with iniquity .
text_la: Melius est parum cum justitia quam multi fructus cum iniquitate.
text_pt: Melhor é o pouco com justiça, do que a abundância de bens com injustiça.
text_el: ὁ ζητῶν τὸν κύριον εὑρήσει γνῶσιν μετὰ δικαιοσύνης οἱ δὲ ὀρθῶς ζητοῦντες αὐτὸν εὑρήσουσιν εἰρήνην

text_en: The heart of man disposes his way: but the Lord must direct his steps.
text_la: Cor hominis disponit viam suam, sed Domini est dirigere gressus ejus.
text_pt: O coração do homem planeja o seu caminho, mas o Senhor lhe dirige os passos.
text_el: πάντα τὰ ἔργα τοῦ κυρίου μετὰ δικαιοσύνης φυλάσσεται δὲ ὁ ἀσεβὴς εἰς ἡμέραν κακήν

text_en: Divination is in the lips of the king, his mouth shall not err in judgment.
text_la: Divinatio in labiis regis; in judicio non errabit os ejus.
text_pt: Nos lábios do rei se acha a sentença divina; a sua boca não transgride quando julga.
text_el: μαντεῖον ἐπὶ χείλεσιν βασιλέως ἐν δὲ κρίσει οὐ μὴ πλανηθῇ τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ

text_en: Weight and balance are judgments of the Lord : and his work all the weights of the bag.
text_la: Pondus et statera judicia Domini sunt, et opera ejus omnes lapides sacculi.
text_pt: O peso e a balança justos são do Senhor; obra sua são os pesos da bolsa.
text_el: ῥοπὴ ζυγοῦ δικαιοσύνη παρὰ κυρίῳ τὰ δὲ ἔργα αὐτοῦ στάθμια δίκαια

text_en: They that act wickedly are abominable to the king: for the throne is established by justice .
text_la: Abominabiles regi qui agunt impie, quoniam justitia firmatur solium.
text_pt: Abominação é aos reis praticarem impiedade, porque com justiça é que se estabelece o trono.
text_el: βδέλυγμα βασιλεῖ ὁ ποιῶν κακά μετὰ γὰρ δικαιοσύνης ἑτοιμάζεται θρόνος ἀρχῆς

text_en: Just lips are the delight of kings: he that speaks right things shall be loved .
text_la: Voluntas regum labia justa; qui recta loquitur diligetur.
text_pt: Os lábios de justiça são o contentamento dos reis; eles amarão o que fala coisas retas.
text_el: δεκτὰ βασιλεῖ χείλη δίκαια λόγους δὲ ὀρθοὺς ἀγαπᾷ

text_en: The wrath of a king is as messengers of death: and the wise man will pacify it.
text_la: Indignatio regis nuntii mortis, et vir sapiens placabit eam.
text_pt: O furor do rei é mensageiro da morte, mas o homem sábio o apaziguará.
text_el: θυμὸς βασιλέως ἄγγελος θανάτου ἀνὴρ δὲ σοφὸς ἐξιλάσεται αὐτόν

text_en: In the cheerfulness of the king's countenance is life: and his clemency is like the latter rain.
text_la: In hilaritate vultus regis vita, et clementia ejus quasi imber serotinus.
