text_pt: No semblante iluminado do rei está a vida, e a sua benevolência é como a nuvem da chuva serôdia.
text_el: ἐν φωτὶ ζωῆς υἱὸς βασιλέως οἱ δὲ προσδεκτοὶ αὐτῷ ὥσπερ νέφος ὄψιμον

text_en: Get wisdom, because it is better than gold: and purchase prudence , for it is more precious than silver.
text_la: Posside sapientiam, quia auro melior est, et acquire prudentiam, quia pretiosior est argento.
text_pt: Quão melhor é adquirir a sabedoria do que o ouro! e quão mais excelente é adquirir a prudência do que a prata!
text_el: νοσσιαὶ σοφίας αἱρετώτεραι χρυσίου νοσσιαὶ δὲ φρονήσεως αἱρετώτεραι ὑπὲρ ἀργύριον

text_en: The path of the just departs from evils : he that keeps his soul keeps his way.
text_la: Semita justorum declinat mala; custos animæ suæ servat viam suam.
text_pt: Os retos fazem o seu caminho desviar-se do mal; o que guarda o seu caminho preserva a sua alma.
text_el: τρίβοι ζωῆς ἐκκλίνουσιν ἀπὸ κακῶν μῆκος δὲ βίου ὁδοὶ δικαιοσύνης ὁ δεχόμενος παιδείαν ἐν ἀγαθοῖς ἔσται ὁ δὲ φυλάσσων ἐλέγχους σοφισθήσεται ὃς φυλάσσει τὰς ἑαυτοῦ ὁδούς τηρεῖ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχήν ἀγαπῶν δὲ ζωὴν αὐτοῦ φείσεται στόματος αὐτοῦ

text_en: Pride goes before destruction: and the spirit is lifted up before a fall.
text_la: Contritionem præcedit superbia, et ante ruinam exaltatur spiritus.
text_pt: A soberba precede a ruína, e a altivez do espírito precede a queda.
text_el: πρὸ συντριβῆς ἡγεῖται ὕβρις πρὸ δὲ πτώματος κακοφροσύνη

text_en: It is better to be humbled with the meek, than to divide spoils with the proud .
text_la: Melius est humiliari cum mitibus quam dividere spolia cum superbis.
text_pt: Melhor é ser humilde de espírito com os mansos, do que repartir o despojo com os soberbos.
text_el: κρείσσων πραΰθυμος μετὰ ταπεινώσεως ἢ ὃς διαιρεῖται σκῦλα μετὰ ὑβριστῶν

text_en: The learned in word shall find good things: and he that trusts in the Lord is blessed .
text_la: Eruditus in verbo reperiet bona, et qui sperat in Domino beatus est.
text_pt: O que atenta prudentemente para o assunto achará o bem, e o que confia no Senhor será bem-aventurado.
text_el: συνετὸς ἐν πράγμασιν εὑρετὴς ἀγαθῶν πεποιθὼς δὲ ἐπὶ θεῷ μακαριστός

text_en: The wise in heart shall be called prudent : and he that is sweet in words, shall attain to greater things.
text_la: Qui sapiens est corde appellabitur prudens, et qui dulcis eloquio majora percipiet.
text_pt: O sábio de coração será chamado prudente, e a doçura dos lábios aumentará o ensino.
text_el: τοὺς σοφοὺς καὶ συνετοὺς φαύλους καλοῦσιν οἱ δὲ γλυκεῖς ἐν λόγῳ πλείονα ἀκούσονται

text_en: Knowledge is a fountain of life to him that possesses it: the instruction of fools is foolishness.
text_la: Fons vitæ eruditio possidentis; doctrina stultorum fatuitas.
text_pt: O entendimento para aqueles que o possuem, é uma fonte de vida, mas a instrução dos tolos é a sua estultícia.
text_el: πηγὴ ζωῆς ἔννοια τοῖς κεκτημένοις παιδεία δὲ ἀφρόνων κακή

text_en: The heart of the wise shall instruct his mouth: and shall add grace to his lips.
text_la: Cor sapientis erudiet os ejus, et labiis ejus addet gratiam.
text_pt: O coração do sábio instrui a sua boca, e aumenta o ensino dos seus lábios.
text_el: καρδία σοφοῦ νοήσει τὰ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἰδίου στόματος ἐπὶ δὲ χείλεσιν φορέσει ἐπιγνωμοσύνην

text_en: Well ordered words are as a honeycomb: sweet to the soul , and health to the bones.
text_la: Favus mellis composita verba; dulcedo animæ sanitas ossium.
text_pt: As palavras suaves são favos de mel, doces para a alma, e saúde para os ossos.
text_el: κηρία μέλιτος λόγοι καλοί γλύκασμα δὲ αὐτῶν ἴασις ψυχῆς

text_en: There is a way that seems to a man right: and the ends thereof lead to death.
text_la: Est via quæ videtur homini recta, et novissima ejus ducunt ad mortem.
text_pt: Há um caminho que parece direito ao homem, mas o seu fim são os caminhos da morte.
text_el: εἰσὶν ὁδοὶ δοκοῦσαι εἶναι ὀρθαὶ ἀνδρί τὰ μέντοι τελευταῖα αὐτῶν βλέπει εἰς πυθμένα ᾅδου

text_en: The soul of him that labours, labours for himself, because his mouth has obliged him to it.
text_la: Anima laborantis laborat sibi, quia compulit eum os suum.
text_pt: O trabalhador trabalha para si mesmo, porque a sua boca o incita.
text_el: ἀνὴρ ἐν πόνοις πονεῖ ἑαυτῷ καὶ ἐκβιάζεται ἑαυτοῦ τὴν ἀπώλειαν ὁ μέντοι σκολιὸς ἐπὶ τῷ ἑαυτοῦ στόματι φορεῖ τὴν ἀπώλειαν

text_en: The wicked man digs evil , and in his lips is a burning fire.
text_la: Vir impius fodit malum, et in labiis ejus ignis ardescit.
text_pt: O homem ímpio cava o mal, e nos seus lábios há como que uma fogueira.
text_el: ἀνὴρ ἄφρων ὀρύσσει ἑαυτῷ κακά ἐπὶ δὲ τῶν ἑαυτοῦ χειλέων θησαυρίζει πῦρ

text_en: A perverse man stirs up quarrels: and one full of words separates princes.
text_la: Homo perversus suscitat lites, et verbosus separat principes.
text_pt: O homem perverso instiga a contenda, e o intrigante separa os maiores amigos.
text_el: ἀνὴρ σκολιὸς διαπέμπεται κακὰ καὶ λαμπτῆρα δόλου πυρσεύει κακοῖς καὶ διαχωρίζει φίλους

text_en: An unjust man allures his friend: and leads him into a way that is not good .
text_la: Vir iniquus lactat amicum suum, et ducit eum per viam non bonam.
text_pt: O homem violento coage o seu próximo, e o faz deslizar por caminhos nada bons.
text_el: ἀνὴρ παράνομος ἀποπειρᾶται φίλων καὶ ἀπάγει αὐτοὺς ὁδοὺς οὐκ ἀγαθάς

text_en: He that with fixed eyes devises wicked things, biting his lips, brings evil to pass.
text_la: Qui attonitis oculis cogitat prava, mordens labia sua perficit malum.
text_pt: O que fecha os olhos para imaginar coisas ruins, ao cerrar os lábios pratica o mal.
text_el: στηρίζων ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ λογίζεται διεστραμμένα ὁρίζει δὲ τοῖς χείλεσιν αὐτοῦ πάντα τὰ κακά οὗτος κάμινός ἐστιν κακίας

text_en: Old age is a crown of dignity, when it is found in the ways of justice .
text_la: Corona dignitatis senectus, quæ in viis justitiæ reperietur.
text_pt: Coroa de honra são as cãs, quando elas estão no caminho da justiça.
text_el: στέφανος καυχήσεως γῆρας ἐν δὲ ὁδοῖς δικαιοσύνης εὑρίσκεται

text_en: The patient man is better than the valiant : and he that rules his spirit, than he that takes cities.
text_la: Melior est patiens viro forti, et qui dominatur animo suo expugnatore urbium.
text_pt: Melhor é o que tarda em irar-se do que o poderoso, e o que controla o seu ânimo do que aquele que toma uma cidade.
text_el: κρείσσων ἀνὴρ μακρόθυμος ἰσχυροῦ ὁ δὲ κρατῶν ὀργῆς κρείσσων καταλαμβανομένου πόλιν

text_en: Lots are cast into the lap, but they are disposed of by the Lord .
text_la: Sortes mittuntur in sinum, sed a Domino temperantur.
text_pt: A sorte se lança no regaço, mas do Senhor procede toda a determinação.
text_el: εἰς κόλπους ἐπέρχεται πάντα τοῖς ἀδίκοις παρὰ δὲ κυρίου πάντα τὰ δίκαια

text_en: Better is a dry morsel with joy , than a house full of victims with strife.
text_la: Melior est buccella sicca cum gaudio quam domus plena victimis cum jurgio.
text_pt: É melhor um bocado seco, e com ele a tranqüilidade, do que a casa cheia de iguarias e com desavença.
text_el: κρείσσων ψωμὸς μεθ' ἡδονῆς ἐν εἰρήνῃ ἢ οἶκος πλήρης πολλῶν ἀγαθῶν καὶ ἀδίκων θυμάτων μετὰ μάχης

text_en: A wise servant shall rule over foolish sons, and shall divide the inheritance among the brethren.
text_la: Servus sapiens dominabitur filiis stultis, et inter fratres hæreditatem dividet.
text_pt: O servo prudente dominará sobre o filho que faz envergonhar; e repartirá a herança entre os irmãos.
text_el: οἰκέτης νοήμων κρατήσει δεσποτῶν ἀφρόνων ἐν δὲ ἀδελφοῖς διελεῖται μέρη

text_en: As silver is tried by fire, and gold in the furnace: so the Lord tries the hearts.
text_la: Sicut igne probatur argentum et aurum camino, ita corda probat Dominus.
text_pt: O crisol é para a prata, e o forno para o ouro; mas o Senhor é quem prova os corações.
text_el: ὥσπερ δοκιμάζεται ἐν καμίνῳ ἄργυρος καὶ χρυσός οὕτως ἐκλεκταὶ καρδίαι παρὰ κυρίῳ

text_en: The evil man obeys an unjust tongue: and the deceitful hearkens to lying lips.
text_la: Malus obedit linguæ iniquæ, et fallax obtemperat labiis mendacibus.
text_pt: O ímpio atenta para o lábio iníquo, o mentiroso inclina os ouvidos à língua maligna.
text_el: κακὸς ὑπακούει γλώσσης παρανόμων δίκαιος δὲ οὐ προσέχει χείλεσιν ψευδέσιν

text_en: He that despises the poor, reproaches his maker: and he that rejoices at another man's ruin, shall not be unpunished.
text_la: Qui despicit pauperem exprobrat factori ejus, et qui ruina lætatur alterius non erit impunitus.
text_pt: O que escarnece do pobre insulta ao seu Criador, o que se alegra da calamidade não ficará impune.
text_el: ὁ καταγελῶν πτωχοῦ παροξύνει τὸν ποιήσαντα αὐτόν ὁ δὲ ἐπιχαίρων ἀπολλυμένῳ οὐκ ἀθῳωθήσεται ὁ δὲ ἐπισπλαγχνιζόμενος ἐλεηθήσεται

text_en: Children's children are the crown of old men : and the glory of children are their fathers.
text_la: Corona senum filii filiorum, et gloria filiorum patres eorum.
text_pt: A coroa dos velhos são os filhos dos filhos; e a glória dos filhos são seus pais.
text_el: στέφανος γερόντων τέκνα τέκνων καύχημα δὲ τέκνων πατέρες αὐτῶν

text_en: Eloquent words do not become a fool, nor lying lips a prince.
text_la: Non decent stultum verba composita, nec principem labium mentiens.
text_pt: Não convém ao tolo a fala excelente; quanto menos ao príncipe, o lábio mentiroso.
text_el: οὐχ ἁρμόσει ἄφρονι χείλη πιστὰ οὐδὲ δικαίῳ χείλη ψευδῆ

text_en: The expectation of him that expects is a most acceptable jewel: wherever he turns himself, he understands wisely.
text_la: Gemma gratissima exspectatio præstolantis; quocumque se vertit, prudenter intelligit.
text_pt: O presente é, aos olhos dos que o recebem, como pedra preciosa; para onde quer que se volte servirá de proveito.
text_el: μισθὸς χαρίτων ἡ παιδεία τοῖς χρωμένοις οὗ δ' ἂν ἐπιστρέψῃ εὐοδωθήσεται

text_en: He that conceals a transgression, seeks friendships: he that repeats it again, separates friends.
text_la: Qui celat delictum quærit amicitias; qui altero sermone repetit, separat fœderatos.
text_pt: Aquele que encobre a transgressão busca a amizade, mas o que revolve o assunto separa os maiores amigos.
text_el: ὃς κρύπτει ἀδικήματα ζητεῖ φιλίαν ὃς δὲ μισεῖ κρύπτειν διίστησιν φίλους καὶ οἰκείους

text_en: A reproof avails more with a wise man , than a hundred stripes with a fool.
text_la: Plus proficit correptio apud prudentem, quam centum plagæ apud stultum.
text_pt: A repreensão penetra mais profundamente no prudente do que cem açoites no tolo.
text_el: συντρίβει ἀπειλὴ καρδίαν φρονίμου ἄφρων δὲ μαστιγωθεὶς οὐκ αἰσθάνεται

text_en: An evil man always seeks quarrels: but a cruel angel shall be sent against him.
text_la: Semper jurgia quærit malus : angelus autem crudelis mittetur contra eum.
text_pt: Na verdade o rebelde não busca senão o mal; afinal, um mensageiro cruel será enviado contra ele.
text_el: ἀντιλογίας ἐγείρει πᾶς κακός ὁ δὲ κύριος ἄγγελον ἀνελεήμονα ἐκπέμψει αὐτῷ

text_en: It is better to meet a bear robbed of her whelps, than a fool trusting in his own folly.
text_la: Expedit magis ursæ occurrere raptis fœtibus, quam fatuo confidenti in stultitia sua.
text_pt: Encontre-se o homem com a ursa roubada dos filhos, mas não com o louco na sua estultícia.
text_el: ἐμπεσεῖται μέριμνα ἀνδρὶ νοήμονι οἱ δὲ ἄφρονες διαλογιοῦνται κακά

text_en: He that renders evil for good , evil shall not depart from his house.
text_la: Qui reddit mala pro bonis, non recedet malum de domo ejus.
text_pt: Quanto àquele que paga o bem com o mal, não se apartará o mal da sua casa.
text_el: ὃς ἀποδίδωσιν κακὰ ἀντὶ ἀγαθῶν οὐ κινηθήσεται κακὰ ἐκ τοῦ οἴκου αὐτοῦ

text_en: The beginning of quarrels is as when one lets out water: and before he suffers reproach, he forsakes judgment.
text_la: Qui dimittit aquam caput est jurgiorum, et antequam patiatur contumeliam judicium deserit.
text_pt: Como o soltar das águas é o início da contenda, assim, antes que sejas envolvido afasta-te da questão.
text_el: ἐξουσίαν δίδωσιν λόγοις ἀρχὴ δικαιοσύνης προηγεῖται δὲ τῆς ἐνδείας στάσις καὶ μάχη

text_en: He that justifies the wicked , and he that condemns the just , both are abominable before God .
text_la: Qui justificat impium, et qui condemnat justum, abominabilis est uterque apud Deum.
text_pt: O que justifica o ímpio, e o que condena o justo, tanto um como o outro são abomináveis ao Senhor.
text_el: ὃς δίκαιον κρίνει τὸν ἄδικον ἄδικον δὲ τὸν δίκαιον ἀκάθαρτος καὶ βδελυκτὸς παρὰ θεῷ

text_en: What does it avail a fool to have riches, seeing he cannot buy wisdom? He that makes his house high, seeks a downfall: and he that refuses to learn, shall fall into evils .
text_la: Quid prodest stulto habere divitias, cum sapientiam emere non possit? Qui altum facit domum suam quærit ruinam, et qui evitat discere incidet in mala.
text_pt: De que serviria o preço na mão do tolo para comprar sabedoria, visto que não tem entendimento?
text_el: ἵνα τί ὑπῆρξεν χρήματα ἄφρονι κτήσασθαι γὰρ σοφίαν ἀκάρδιος οὐ δυνήσεται

text_en: He that is a friend loves at all times: and a brother is proved in distress.
text_la: Omni tempore diligit qui amicus est, et frater in angustiis comprobatur.
text_pt: Em todo o tempo ama o amigo e para a hora da angústia nasce o irmão.
text_el: εἰς πάντα καιρὸν φίλος ὑπαρχέτω σοι ἀδελφοὶ δὲ ἐν ἀνάγκαις χρήσιμοι ἔστωσαν τούτου γὰρ χάριν γεννῶνται

text_en: A foolish man will clap hands, when he is surety for his friend.
text_la: Stultus homo plaudet manibus, cum spoponderit pro amico suo.
text_pt: O homem falto de entendimento compromete-se, ficando por fiador na presença do seu amigo.
text_el: ἀνὴρ ἄφρων ἐπικροτεῖ καὶ ἐπιχαίρει ἑαυτῷ ὡς καὶ ὁ ἐγγυώμενος ἐγγύῃ τὸν ἑαυτοῦ φίλον

text_en: He that studies discords, loves quarrels: and he that exalts his door, seeks ruin.
text_la: Qui meditatur discordias diligit rixas, et qui exaltat ostium quærit ruinam.
text_pt: O que ama a transgressão ama a contenda; o que exalta a sua porta busca a ruína.
text_el: φιλαμαρτήμων χαίρει μάχαις

text_en: He that is of a perverse heart, shall not find good : and he that perverts his tongue, shall fall into evil .
text_la: Qui perversi cordis est non inveniet bonum, et qui vertit linguam incidet in malum.
text_pt: O perverso de coração jamais achará o bem; e o que tem a língua dobre vem a cair no mal.
text_el: ὁ δὲ σκληροκάρδιος οὐ συναντᾷ ἀγαθοῖς ἀνὴρ εὐμετάβολος γλώσσῃ ἐμπεσεῖται εἰς κακά

text_en: A fool is born to his own disgrace: and even his father shall not rejoice in a fool.
text_la: Natus est stultus in ignominiam suam; sed nec pater in fatuo lætabitur.
text_pt: O que gera um tolo para a sua tristeza o faz; e o pai do insensato não tem alegria.
text_el: καρδία δὲ ἄφρονος ὀδύνη τῷ κεκτημένῳ αὐτήν οὐκ εὐφραίνεται πατὴρ ἐπὶ υἱῷ ἀπαιδεύτῳ υἱὸς δὲ φρόνιμος εὐφραίνει μητέρα αὐτοῦ

text_en: A joyful mind makes age flourishing: a sorrowful spirit dries up the bones.
text_la: Animus gaudens ætatem floridam facit; spiritus tristis exsiccat ossa.
text_pt: O coração alegre é como o bom remédio, mas o espírito abatido seca até os ossos.
text_el: καρδία εὐφραινομένη εὐεκτεῖν ποιεῖ ἀνδρὸς δὲ λυπηροῦ ξηραίνεται τὰ ὀστᾶ

text_en: The wicked man takes gifts out of the bosom, that he may pervert the paths of judgment.
text_la: Munera de sinu impius accipit, ut pervertat semitas judicii.
text_pt: O ímpio toma presentes em secreto para perverter as veredas da justiça.
text_el: λαμβάνοντος δῶρα ἐν κόλπῳ ἀδίκως οὐ κατευοδοῦνται ὁδοί ἀσεβὴς δὲ ἐκκλίνει ὁδοὺς δικαιοσύνης

text_en: Wisdom shines in the face of the wise: the eyes of fools are in the ends of the earth.
text_la: In facie prudentis lucet sapientia; oculi stultorum in finibus terræ.
text_pt: No rosto do entendido se vê a sabedoria, mas os olhos do tolo vagam pelas extremidades da terra.
text_el: πρόσωπον συνετὸν ἀνδρὸς σοφοῦ οἱ δὲ ὀφθαλμοὶ τοῦ ἄφρονος ἐπ' ἄκρα γῆς

text_en: A foolish son is the anger of the father: and the sorrow of the mother that bore him.
text_la: Ira patris filius stultus, et dolor matris quæ genuit eum.
text_pt: O filho insensato é tristeza para seu pai, e amargura para aquela que o deu à luz.
text_el: ὀργὴ πατρὶ υἱὸς ἄφρων καὶ ὀδύνη τῇ τεκούσῃ αὐτοῦ

text_en: It is no good thing to do hurt to the just : nor to strike the prince, who judges right.
text_la: Non est bonum damnum inferre justo, nec percutere principem qui recta judicat.
text_pt: Também não é bom punir o justo, nem tampouco ferir aos príncipes por eqüidade.
text_el: ζημιοῦν ἄνδρα δίκαιον οὐ καλόν οὐδὲ ὅσιον ἐπιβουλεύειν δυνάσταις δικαίοις

text_en: He that sets bounds to his words, is knowing and wise: and the man of understanding is of a precious spirit.
text_la: Qui moderatur sermones suos doctus et prudens est, et pretiosi spiritus vir eruditus.
text_pt: O que possui o conhecimento guarda as suas palavras, e o homem de entendimento é de precioso espírito.
text_el: ὃς φείδεται ῥῆμα προέσθαι σκληρόν ἐπιγνώμων μακρόθυμος δὲ ἀνὴρ φρόνιμος

text_en: Even a fool, if he will hold his peace, shall be counted wise: and if he close his lips, a man of understanding.
text_la: Stultus quoque, si tacuerit, sapiens reputabitur, et si compresserit labia sua, intelligens.
text_pt: Até o tolo, quando se cala, é reputado por sábio; e o que cerra os seus lábios é tido por entendido.
text_el: ἀνοήτῳ ἐπερωτήσαντι σοφίαν σοφία λογισθήσεται ἐνεὸν δέ τις ἑαυτὸν ποιήσας δόξει φρόνιμος εἶναι

text_en: He that has a mind to depart from a friend, seeks occasions: he shall ever be subject to reproach.
text_la: Occasiones quærit qui vult recedere ab amico : omni tempore erit exprobrabilis.
text_pt: Busca satisfazer seu próprio desejo aquele que se isola; ele se insurge contra toda sabedoria.
text_el: προφάσεις ζητεῖ ἀνὴρ βουλόμενος χωρίζεσθαι ἀπὸ φίλων ἐν παντὶ δὲ καιρῷ ἐπονείδιστος ἔσται

text_en: A fool receives not the words of prudence : unless you say those things which are in his heart.
text_la: Non recipit stultus verba prudentiæ, nisi ea dixeris quæ versantur in corde ejus.
text_pt: O tolo não tem prazer na sabedoria, mas só em que se manifeste aquilo que agrada o seu coração.
text_el: οὐ χρείαν ἔχει σοφίας ἐνδεὴς φρενῶν μᾶλλον γὰρ ἄγεται ἀφροσύνῃ

text_en: The wicked man , when he has come into the depths of sins , contemns: but ignominy and reproach follow him.
text_la: Impius, cum in profundum venerit peccatorum, contemnit; sed sequitur eum ignominia et opprobrium.
text_pt: Vindo o ímpio, vem também o desprezo, e com a ignomínia a vergonha.
text_el: ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἀσεβὴς εἰς βάθος κακῶν καταφρονεῖ ἐπέρχεται δὲ αὐτῷ ἀτιμία καὶ ὄνειδος

text_en: Words from the mouth of a man are as deep water: and the fountain of wisdom is an overflowing stream.
text_la: Aqua profunda verba ex ore viri, et torrens redundans fons sapientiæ.
text_pt: Águas profundas são as palavras da boca do homem, e ribeiro transbordante é a fonte da sabedoria.
text_el: ὕδωρ βαθὺ λόγος ἐν καρδίᾳ ἀνδρός ποταμὸς δὲ ἀναπηδύει καὶ πηγὴ ζωῆς

text_en: It is not good to accept the person of the wicked , to decline from the truth of judgment.
text_la: Accipere personam impii non est bonum, ut declines a veritate judicii.
text_pt: Não é bom favorecer o ímpio, e com isso, fazer o justo perder a questão.
text_el: θαυμάσαι πρόσωπον ἀσεβοῦς οὐ καλόν οὐδὲ ὅσιον ἐκκλίνειν τὸ δίκαιον ἐν κρίσει

text_en: The lips of a fool intermeddle with strife: and his mouth provokes quarrels.
text_la: Labia stulti miscent se rixis, et os ejus jurgia provocat.
text_pt: Os lábios do tolo entram na contenda, e a sua boca brada por açoites.
text_el: χείλη ἄφρονος ἄγουσιν αὐτὸν εἰς κακά τὸ δὲ στόμα αὐτοῦ τὸ θρασὺ θάνατον ἐπικαλεῖται

text_en: The mouth of a fool is his destruction: and his lips are the ruin of his soul .
text_la: Os stulti contritio ejus, et labia ipsius ruina animæ ejus.
text_pt: A boca do tolo é a sua própria destruição, e os seus lábios um laço para a sua alma.
text_el: στόμα ἄφρονος συντριβὴ αὐτῷ τὰ δὲ χείλη αὐτοῦ παγὶς τῇ ψυχῇ αὐτοῦ

text_en: The words of the double tongued are as if they were harmless: and they reach even to the inner parts of the bowels. Fear casts down the slothful: and the souls of the effeminate shall be hungry.
text_la: Verba bilinguis quasi simplicia, et ipsa perveniunt usque ad interiora ventris. Pigrum dejicit timor; animæ autem effeminatorum esurient.
text_pt: As palavras do mexeriqueiro são como doces bocados; elas descem ao íntimo do ventre.
text_el: ὀκνηροὺς καταβάλλει φόβος ψυχαὶ δὲ ἀνδρογύνων πεινάσουσιν

text_en: He that is loose and slack in his work, is the brother of him that wastes his own works.
text_la: Qui mollis et dissolutus est in opere suo frater est sua opera dissipantis.
text_pt: O que é negligente na sua obra é também irmão do desperdiçador.
text_el: ὁ μὴ ἰώμενος ἑαυτὸν ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις αὐτοῦ ἀδελφός ἐστιν τοῦ λυμαινομένου ἑαυτόν

text_en: The name of the Lord is a strong tower: the just runs to it, and shall be exalted.
text_la: Turris fortissima nomen Domini; ad ipsum currit justus, et exaltabitur.
text_pt: Torre forte é o nome do Senhor; a ela correrá o justo, e estará em alto refúgio.
text_el: ἐκ μεγαλωσύνης ἰσχύος ὄνομα κυρίου αὐτῷ δὲ προσδραμόντες δίκαιοι ὑψοῦνται

text_en: The substance of the rich man is the city of his strength, and as a strong wall compassing him about.
text_la: Substantia divitis urbs roboris ejus, et quasi murus validus circumdans eum.
text_pt: Os bens do rico são a sua cidade forte, e como uma muralha na sua imaginação.
text_el: ὕπαρξις πλουσίου ἀνδρὸς πόλις ὀχυρά ἡ δὲ δόξα αὐτῆς μέγα ἐπισκιάζει

text_en: Before destruction, the heart of a man is exalted: and before he be glorified , it is humbled .
text_la: Antequam conteratur, exaltatur cor hominis, et antequam glorificetur, humiliatur.
text_pt: O coração do homem se exalta antes de ser abatido e diante da honra vai a humildade.
text_el: πρὸ συντριβῆς ὑψοῦται καρδία ἀνδρός καὶ πρὸ δόξης ταπεινοῦται

text_en: He that answers before he hears, shows himself to be a fool, and worthy of confusion.
text_la: Qui prius respondet quam audiat, stultum se esse demonstrat, et confusione dignum.
text_pt: O que responde antes de ouvir comete estultícia que é para vergonha sua.
text_el: ὃς ἀποκρίνεται λόγον πρὶν ἀκοῦσαι ἀφροσύνη αὐτῷ ἐστιν καὶ ὄνειδος

text_en: The spirit of a man upholds his infirmity: but a spirit that is easily angered , who can bear?
text_la: Spiritus viri sustentat imbecillitatem suam; spiritum vero ad irascendum facilem quis poterit sustinere?
text_pt: O espírito do homem susterá a sua enfermidade, mas ao espírito abatido, quem o suportará?
text_el: θυμὸν ἀνδρὸς πραΰνει θεράπων φρόνιμος ὀλιγόψυχον δὲ ἄνδρα τίς ὑποίσει

text_en: A wise heart shall acquire knowledge : and the ear of the wise seeks instruction.
text_la: Cor prudens possidebit scientiam, et auris sapientium quærit doctrinam.
text_pt: O coração do entendido adquire o conhecimento, e o ouvido dos sábios busca a sabedoria.
text_el: καρδία φρονίμου κτᾶται αἴσθησιν ὦτα δὲ σοφῶν ζητεῖ ἔννοιαν

text_en: A man's gift enlarges his way, and makes him room before princes.
text_la: Donum hominis dilatat viam ejus, et ante principes spatium ei facit.
text_pt: Com presentes o homem alarga o seu caminho e o eleva diante dos grandes.
text_el: δόμα ἀνθρώπου ἐμπλατύνει αὐτὸν καὶ παρὰ δυνάσταις καθιζάνει αὐτόν

text_en: The just is first accuser of himself: his friend comes, and shall search him.
text_la: Justus prior est accusator sui : venit amicus ejus, et investigabit eum.
text_pt: O que pleiteia por algo, a princípio parece justo, porém vem o seu próximo e o examina.
text_el: δίκαιος ἑαυτοῦ κατήγορος ἐν πρωτολογίᾳ ὡς δ' ἂν ἐπιβάλῃ ὁ ἀντίδικος ἐλέγχεται

text_en: The lot suppresses contentions, and determines even between the mighty.
text_la: Contradictiones comprimit sors, et inter potentes quoque dijudicat.
text_pt: A sorte faz cessar os pleitos, e faz separação entre os poderosos.
text_el: ἀντιλογίας παύει κλῆρος ἐν δὲ δυνάσταις ὁρίζει

text_en: A brother that is helped by his brother, is like a strong city: and judgments are like the bars of cities.
text_la: Frater qui adjuvatur a fratre quasi civitas firma, et judicia quasi vectes urbium.
text_pt: O irmão ofendido é mais difícil de conquistar do que uma cidade forte; e as contendas são como os ferrolhos de um palácio.
text_el: ἀδελφὸς ὑπὸ ἀδελφοῦ βοηθούμενος ὡς πόλις ὀχυρὰ καὶ ὑψηλή ἰσχύει δὲ ὥσπερ τεθεμελιωμένον βασίλειον

text_en: Of the fruit of a man's mouth shall his belly be satisfied: and the offspring of his lips shall fill him.
text_la: De fructu oris viri replebitur venter ejus, et genimina labiorum ipsius saturabunt eum.
text_pt: Do fruto da boca de cada um se fartará o seu ventre; dos renovos dos seus lábios ficará satisfeito.
text_el: ἀπὸ καρπῶν στόματος ἀνὴρ πίμπλησιν κοιλίαν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ δὲ καρπῶν χειλέων αὐτοῦ ἐμπλησθήσεται

text_en: Death and life are in the power of the tongue: they that love it, shall eat the fruits thereof.
text_la: Mors et vita in manu linguæ; qui diligunt eam comedent fructus ejus.
text_pt: A morte e a vida estão no poder da língua; e aquele que a ama comerá do seu fruto.
text_el: θάνατος καὶ ζωὴ ἐν χειρὶ γλώσσης οἱ δὲ κρατοῦντες αὐτῆς ἔδονται τοὺς καρποὺς αὐτῆς

text_en: He that has found a good wife, has found a good thing, and shall receive a pleasure from the Lord . He that drives away a good wife, drives away a good thing: but he that keeps an adulteress, is foolish and wicked .
text_la: Qui invenit mulierem bonam invenit bonum, et hauriet jucunditatem a Domino. Qui expellit mulierem bonam expellit bonum; qui autem tenet adulteram stultus est et impius.
text_pt: Aquele que encontra uma esposa, acha o bem, e alcança a benevolência do Senhor.
text_el: ὃς εὗρεν γυναῖκα ἀγαθήν εὗρεν χάριτας ἔλαβεν δὲ παρὰ θεοῦ ἱλαρότητα

text_en: The poor will speak with supplications, and the rich will speak roughly.
text_la: Cum obsecrationibus loquetur pauper, et dives effabitur rigide.
text_pt: O pobre fala com rogos, mas o rico responde com dureza.

text_en: A man amiable in society, shall be more friendly than a brother.
text_la: Vir amabilis ad societatem magis amicus erit quam frater.
text_pt: O homem de muitos amigos deve mostrar-se amigável, mas há um amigo mais chegado do que um irmão.

text_en: Better is the poor man , that walks in his simplicity, than a rich man that is perverse in his lips and unwise.
text_la: Melior est pauper qui ambulat in simplicitate sua quam dives torquens labia sua, et insipiens.
text_pt: Melhor é o pobre que anda na sua integridade do que o perverso de lábios e tolo.

text_en: Where there is no knowledge of the soul , there is no good : and he that is hasty with his feet shall stumble.
text_la: Ubi non est scientia animæ, non est bonum, et qui festinus est pedibus offendet.
text_pt: Assim como não é bom ficar a alma sem conhecimento, peca aquele que se apressa com seus pés.

text_en: The folly of a man supplants his steps: and he frets in his mind against God .
text_la: Stultitia hominis supplantat gressus ejus, et contra Deum fervet animo suo.
text_pt: A estultícia do homem perverterá o seu caminho, e o seu coração se irará contra o Senhor.
text_el: ἀφροσύνη ἀνδρὸς λυμαίνεται τὰς ὁδοὺς αὐτοῦ τὸν δὲ θεὸν αἰτιᾶται τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ

text_en: Riches make many friends: but from the poor man , even they whom he had, depart.
text_la: Divitiæ addunt amicos plurimos; a paupere autem et hi quos habuit separantur.
text_pt: As riquezas granjeiam muitos amigos, mas ao pobre, o seu próprio amigo o deixa.
text_el: πλοῦτος προστίθησιν φίλους πολλούς ὁ δὲ πτωχὸς καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ ὑπάρχοντος φίλου λείπεται

text_en: A false witness shall not be unpunished: and he that speaks lies, shall not escape.
text_la: Testis falsus non erit impunitus, et qui mendacia loquitur non effugiet.
text_pt: A falsa testemunha não ficará impune e o que respira mentiras não escapará.
text_el: μάρτυς ψευδὴς οὐκ ἀτιμώρητος ἔσται ὁ δὲ ἐγκαλῶν ἀδίκως οὐ διαφεύξεται

text_en: Many honour the person of him that is mighty, and are friends of him that gives gifts.
text_la: Multi colunt personam potentis, et amici sunt dona tribuentis.
text_pt: Muitos se deixam acomodar pelos favores do príncipe, e cada um é amigo daquele que dá presentes.
text_el: πολλοὶ θεραπεύουσιν πρόσωπα βασιλέων πᾶς δὲ ὁ κακὸς γίνεται ὄνειδος ἀνδρί

text_en: The brethren of the poor man hate him: moreover also his friends have departed far from him. He that follows after words only, shall have nothing.
text_la: Fratres hominis pauperis oderunt eum; insuper et amici procul recesserunt ab eo. Qui tantum verba sectatur nihil habebit;
text_pt: Todos os irmãos do pobre o odeiam; quanto mais se afastarão dele os seus amigos! Corre após eles com palavras, que não servem de nada.
text_el: πᾶς ὃς ἀδελφὸν πτωχὸν μισεῖ καὶ φιλίας μακρὰν ἔσται ἔννοια ἀγαθὴ τοῖς εἰδόσιν αὐτὴν ἐγγιεῖ ἀνὴρ δὲ φρόνιμος εὑρήσει αὐτήν ὁ πολλὰ κακοποιῶν τελεσιουργεῖ κακίαν ὃς δὲ ἐρεθίζει λόγους οὐ σωθήσεται

text_en: But he that possesses a mind, loves his own soul , and he that keeps prudence , shall find good things.
text_la: qui autem possessor est mentis diligit animam suam, et custos prudentiæ inveniet bona.
text_pt: O que adquire entendimento ama a sua alma; o que cultiva a inteligência achará o bem.
text_el: ὁ κτώμενος φρόνησιν ἀγαπᾷ ἑαυτόν ὃς δὲ φυλάσσει φρόνησιν εὑρήσει ἀγαθά

text_en: A false witness shall not be unpunished: and he that speaks lies, shall perish.
text_la: Falsus testis non erit impunitus, et qui loquitur mendacia peribit.
text_pt: A falsa testemunha não ficará impune; e o que profere mentiras perecerá.
text_el: μάρτυς ψευδὴς οὐκ ἀτιμώρητος ἔσται ὃς δ' ἂν ἐκκαύσῃ κακίαν ἀπολεῖται ὑπ' αὐτῆς

text_en: Delicacies are not seemly for a fool: nor for a servant to have rule over princes.
text_la: Non decent stultum deliciæ, nec servum dominari principibus.
text_pt: Ao tolo não é certo gozar de deleites; quanto menos ao servo dominar sobre os príncipes!
text_el: οὐ συμφέρει ἄφρονι τρυφή καὶ ἐὰν οἰκέτης ἄρξηται μεθ' ὕβρεως δυναστεύειν

text_en: The learning of a man is known by patience: and his glory is to pass over wrongs.
text_la: Doctrina viri per patientiam noscitur, et gloria ejus est iniqua prætergredi.
text_pt: A prudência do homem faz reter a sua ira, e é glória sua o passar por cima da transgressão.
text_el: ἐλεήμων ἀνὴρ μακροθυμεῖ τὸ δὲ καύχημα αὐτοῦ ἐπέρχεται παρανόμοις

text_en: As the roaring of a lion, so also is the anger of a king: and his cheerfulness as the dew upon the grass.
text_la: Sicut fremitus leonis, ita et regis ira, et sicut ros super herbam, ita et hilaritas ejus.
text_pt: Como o rugido do leão jovem é a indignação do rei, mas como o orvalho sobre a relva é a sua benevolência.
text_el: βασιλέως ἀπειλὴ ὁμοία βρυγμῷ λέοντος ὥσπερ δὲ δρόσος ἐπὶ χόρτῳ οὕτως τὸ ἱλαρὸν αὐτοῦ

text_en: A foolish son is the grief of his father: and a wrangling wife is like a roof continually dropping through.
text_la: Dolor patris filius stultus, et tecta jugiter perstillantia litigiosa mulier.
text_pt: O filho insensato é uma desgraça para o pai, e um gotejar contínuo as contendas da mulher.
text_el: αἰσχύνη πατρὶ υἱὸς ἄφρων καὶ οὐχ ἁγναὶ εὐχαὶ ἀπὸ μισθώματος ἑταίρας

text_en: House and riches are given by parents : but a prudent wife is properly from the Lord .
text_la: Domus et divitiæ dantur a parentibus; a Domino autem proprie uxor prudens.
text_pt: A casa e os bens são herança dos pais; porém do Senhor vem a esposa prudente.
text_el: οἶκον καὶ ὕπαρξιν μερίζουσιν πατέρες παισίν παρὰ δὲ θεοῦ ἁρμόζεται γυνὴ ἀνδρί

text_en: Slothfulness casts into a deep sleep, and an idle soul shall suffer hunger.
text_la: Pigredo immittit soporem, et anima dissoluta esuriet.
text_pt: A preguiça faz cair em profundo sono, e a alma indolente padecerá fome.
text_el: δειλία κατέχει ἀνδρογύναιον ψυχὴ δὲ ἀεργοῦ πεινάσει

text_en: He that keeps the commandment, keeps his own soul : but he that neglects his own way, shall die.
text_la: Qui custodit mandatum custodit animam suam; qui autem negligit viam suam mortificabitur.
text_pt: O que guardar o mandamento guardará a sua alma; porém o que desprezar os seus caminhos morrerá.
text_el: ὃς φυλάσσει ἐντολήν τηρεῖ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχήν ὁ δὲ καταφρονῶν τῶν ἑαυτοῦ ὁδῶν ἀπολεῖται

text_en: He that has mercy on the poor, lends to the Lord : and he will repay him.
text_la: Fœneratur Domino qui miseretur pauperis, et vicissitudinem suam reddet ei.
text_pt: Ao Senhor empresta o que se compadece do pobre, ele lhe pagará o seu benefício.
text_el: δανίζει θεῷ ὁ ἐλεῶν πτωχόν κατὰ δὲ τὸ δόμα αὐτοῦ ἀνταποδώσει αὐτῷ

text_en: Chastise your son, despair not: but to the killing of him set not your soul .
text_la: Erudi filium tuum; ne desperes : ad interfectionem autem ejus ne ponas animam tuam.
text_pt: Castiga o teu filho enquanto há esperança, mas não deixes que o teu ânimo se exalte até o matar.
text_el: παίδευε υἱόν σου οὕτως γὰρ ἔσται εὔελπις εἰς δὲ ὕβριν μὴ ἐπαίρου τῇ ψυχῇ σου

text_en: He that is impatient, shall suffer damage: and when he shall take away, he shall add another thing.
text_la: Qui impatiens est sustinebit damnum, et cum rapuerit, aliud apponet.
text_pt: O homem de grande indignação deve sofrer o dano; porque se tu o livrares ainda terás de tornar a fazê-lo.
text_el: κακόφρων ἀνὴρ πολλὰ ζημιωθήσεται ἐὰν δὲ λοιμεύηται καὶ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ προσθήσει

text_en: Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that you may be wise in your latter end.
text_la: Audi consilium, et suscipe disciplinam, ut sis sapiens in novissimis tuis.
text_pt: Ouve o conselho, e recebe a correção, para que no fim sejas sábio.
text_el: ἄκουε υἱέ παιδείαν πατρός σου ἵνα σοφὸς γένῃ ἐπ' ἐσχάτων σου

text_en: There are many thoughts in the heart of a man : but the will of the Lord shall stand firm.
text_la: Multæ cogitationes in corde viri; voluntas autem Domini permanebit.
text_pt: Muitos propósitos há no coração do homem, porém o conselho do Senhor permanecerá.
text_el: πολλοὶ λογισμοὶ ἐν καρδίᾳ ἀνδρός ἡ δὲ βουλὴ τοῦ κυρίου εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα μένει

text_en: A needy man is merciful: and better is the poor than the lying man .
text_la: Homo indigens misericors est, et melior est pauper quam vir mendax.
text_pt: O que o homem mais deseja é o que lhe faz bem; porém é melhor ser pobre do que mentiroso.
text_el: καρπὸς ἀνδρὶ ἐλεημοσύνη κρείσσων δὲ πτωχὸς δίκαιος ἢ πλούσιος ψεύστης

text_en: The fear of the Lord is unto life: and he shall abide in the fullness without being visited with evil .
text_la: Timor Domini ad vitam, et in plenitudine commorabitur absque visitatione pessima.
text_pt: O temor do Senhor encaminha para a vida; aquele que o tem ficará satisfeito, e não o visitará mal nenhum.
text_el: φόβος κυρίου εἰς ζωὴν ἀνδρί ὁ δὲ ἄφοβος αὐλισθήσεται ἐν τόποις οὗ οὐκ ἐπισκοπεῖται γνῶσις

text_en: The slothful hides his hand under his armpit, and will not so much as bring it to his mouth.
text_la: Abscondit piger manum suam sub ascella, nec ad os suum applicat eam.
text_pt: O preguiçoso esconde a sua mão ao seio; e não tem disposição nem de torná-la à sua boca.
text_el: ὁ ἐγκρύπτων εἰς τὸν κόλπον αὐτοῦ χεῖρας ἀδίκως οὐδὲ τῷ στόματι οὐ μὴ προσαγάγῃ αὐτάς

text_en: The wicked man being scourged, the fool shall be wiser: but if you rebuke a wise man , he will understand discipline.
text_la: Pestilente flagellato stultus sapientior erit; si autem corripueris sapientem, intelliget disciplinam.
text_pt: Açoita o escarnecedor, e o simples tomará aviso; repreende ao entendido, e aprenderá conhecimento.
text_el: λοιμοῦ μαστιγουμένου ἄφρων πανουργότερος γίνεται ἐὰν δὲ ἐλέγχῃς ἄνδρα φρόνιμον νοήσει αἴσθησιν

text_en: He that afflicts his father, and chases away his mother, is infamous and unhappy.
text_la: Qui affligit patrem, et fugat matrem, ignominiosus est et infelix.
text_pt: O que aflige o seu pai, ou manda embora sua mãe, é filho que traz vergonha e desonra.
text_el: ὁ ἀτιμάζων πατέρα καὶ ἀπωθούμενος μητέρα αὐτοῦ καταισχυνθήσεται καὶ ἐπονείδιστος ἔσται

text_en: Cease not, O my son, to hear instruction, and be not ignorant of the words of knowledge .
text_la: Non cesses, fili, audire doctrinam, nec ignores sermones scientiæ.
text_pt: Filho meu, ouvindo a instrução, cessa de te desviares das palavras do conhecimento.
text_el: υἱὸς ἀπολειπόμενος φυλάξαι παιδείαν πατρὸς μελετήσει ῥήσεις κακάς

text_en: An unjust witness scorns judgment: and the mouth of the wicked devours iniquity .
text_la: Testis iniquus deridet judicium, et os impiorum devorat iniquitatem.
text_pt: O ímpio escarnece do juízo, e a boca dos perversos devora a iniqüidade.
text_el: ὁ ἐγγυώμενος παῖδα ἄφρονα καθυβρίζει δικαίωμα στόμα δὲ ἀσεβῶν καταπίεται κρίσεις

text_en: Judgments are prepared for scorners: and striking hammers for the bodies of fools.
text_la: Parata sunt derisoribus judicia, et mallei percutientes stultorum corporibus.
text_pt: Preparados estão os juízos para os escarnecedores, e os açoites para as costas dos tolos.
text_el: ἑτοιμάζονται ἀκολάστοις μάστιγες καὶ τιμωρίαι ὤμοις ἀφρόνων

text_en: Wine is a luxurious thing, and drunkenness riotous: whosoever is delighted therewith, shall not be wise.
text_la: Luxuriosa res vinum, et tumultuosa ebrietas : quicumque his delectatur non erit sapiens.
text_pt: O vinho é escarnecedor, a bebida forte alvoroçadora; e todo aquele que neles errar nunca será sábio.
text_el: ἀκόλαστον οἶνος καὶ ὑβριστικὸν μέθη πᾶς δὲ ὁ συμμειγνύμενος αὐτῇ οὐκ ἔσται σοφός

text_en: As the roaring of a lion, so also is the dread of a king: he that provokes him, sins against his own soul .
text_la: Sicut rugitus leonis, ita et terror regis : qui provocat eum peccat in animam suam.
text_pt: Como o rugido do leão é o terror do rei; o que o provoca à ira peca contra a sua própria alma.
text_el: οὐ διαφέρει ἀπειλὴ βασιλέως θυμοῦ λέοντος ὁ δὲ παροξύνων αὐτὸν ἁμαρτάνει εἰς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχήν

text_en: It is an honour for a man to separate himself from quarrels: but all fools are meddling with reproaches.
text_la: Honor est homini qui separat se a contentionibus; omnes autem stulti miscentur contumeliis.
text_pt: Honroso é para o homem desviar-se de questões, mas todo tolo é intrometido.
text_el: δόξα ἀνδρὶ ἀποστρέφεσθαι λοιδορίας πᾶς δὲ ἄφρων τοιούτοις συμπλέκεται

text_en: Because of the cold the sluggard would not plough: he shall beg therefore in the summer, and it shall not be given him.
text_la: Propter frigus piger arare noluit; mendicabit ergo æstate, et non dabitur illi.
text_pt: O preguiçoso não lavrará por causa do inverno, pelo que mendigará na sega, mas nada receberá.
text_el: ὀνειδιζόμενος ὀκνηρὸς οὐκ αἰσχύνεται ὡσαύτως καὶ ὁ δανιζόμενος σῖτον ἐν ἀμήτῳ

text_en: Counsel in the heart of a man is like deep water: but a wise man will draw it out.
text_la: Sicut aqua profunda, sic consilium in corde viri; sed homo sapiens exhauriet illud.
text_pt: Como as águas profundas é o conselho no coração do homem; mas o homem de inteligência o trará para fora.
text_el: ὕδωρ βαθὺ βουλὴ ἐν καρδίᾳ ἀνδρός ἀνὴρ δὲ φρόνιμος ἐξαντλήσει αὐτήν

text_en: Many men are called merciful: but who shall find a faithful man ?
text_la: Multi homines misericordes vocantur; virum autem fidelem quis inveniet?
text_pt: A multidão dos homens apregoa a sua própria bondade, porém o homem fidedigno quem o achará?
text_el: μέγα ἄνθρωπος καὶ τίμιον ἀνὴρ ἐλεήμων ἄνδρα δὲ πιστὸν ἔργον εὑρεῖν

text_en: The just that walks in his simplicity, shall leave behind him blessed children.
text_la: Justus qui ambulat in simplicitate sua beatos post se filios derelinquet.
text_pt: O justo anda na sua sinceridade; bem-aventurados serão os seus filhos depois dele.
text_el: ὃς ἀναστρέφεται ἄμωμος ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ μακαρίους τοὺς παῖδας αὐτοῦ καταλείψει

text_en: The king, that sits on the throne of judgment, scatters away all evil with his look.
text_la: Rex qui sedet in solio judicii dissipat omne malum intuitu suo.
text_pt: Assentando-se o rei no trono do juízo, com os seus olhos dissipa todo o mal.
text_el: ὅταν βασιλεὺς δίκαιος καθίσῃ ἐπὶ θρόνου οὐκ ἐναντιοῦται ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς αὐτοῦ πᾶν πονηρόν

text_en: Who can say: My heart is clean, I am pure from sin ?
text_la: Quis potest dicere : Mundum est cor meum; purus sum a peccato?
text_pt: Quem poderá dizer: Purifiquei o meu coração, limpo estou de meu pecado?
text_el: τίς καυχήσεται ἁγνὴν ἔχειν τὴν καρδίαν ἢ τίς παρρησιάσεται καθαρὸς εἶναι ἀπὸ ἁμαρτιῶν

text_en: Diverse weights and diverse measures, both are abominable before God .
text_la: Pondus et pondus, mensura et mensura : utrumque abominabile est apud Deum.
text_pt: Dois pesos diferentes e duas espécies de medida são abominação ao Senhor, tanto um como outro.
text_el: στάθμιον μέγα καὶ μικρὸν καὶ μέτρα δισσά ἀκάθαρτα ἐνώπιον κυρίου καὶ ἀμφότερα

text_en: By his inclinations a child is known , if his works be clean and right.
text_la: Ex studiis suis intelligitur puer, si munda et recta sint opera ejus.
text_pt: Até a criança se dará a conhecer pelas suas ações, se a sua obra é pura e reta.
text_el: καὶ ὁ ποιῶν αὐτὰ ἐν τοῖς ἐπιτηδεύμασιν αὐτοῦ συμποδισθήσεται νεανίσκος μετὰ ὁσίου καὶ εὐθεῖα ἡ ὁδὸς αὐτοῦ

text_en: The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, the Lord has made them both.
text_la: Aurem audientem, et oculum videntem : Dominus fecit utrumque.
text_pt: O ouvido que ouve, e o olho que vê, o Senhor os fez a ambos.
text_el: οὖς ἀκούει καὶ ὀφθαλμὸς ὁρᾷ κυρίου ἔργα καὶ ἀμφότερα

text_en: Love not sleep, lest poverty oppress you: open your eyes, and be filled with bread.
text_la: Noli diligere somnum, ne te egestas opprimat : aperi oculos tuos, et saturare panibus.
text_pt: Não ames o sono, para que não empobreças; abre os teus olhos, e te fartarás de pão.
text_el: μὴ ἀγάπα καταλαλεῖν ἵνα μὴ ἐξαρθῇς διάνοιξον τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς σου καὶ ἐμπλήσθητι ἄρτων

text_en: It is naught, it is naught, says every buyer: and when he has gone away, then he will boast.
text_la: Malum est, malum est, dicit omnis emptor; et cum recesserit, tunc gloriabitur.
text_pt: Nada vale, nada vale, dirá o comprador, mas, indo-se, então se gabará.

text_en: There is gold and a multitude of jewels : but the lips of knowledge are a precious vessel.
text_la: Est aurum et multitudo gemmarum, et vas pretiosum labia scientiæ.
text_pt: Há ouro e abundância de rubis, mas os lábios do conhecimento são jóia preciosa.

text_en: Take away the garment of him that is surety for a stranger, and take a pledge from him for strangers.
text_la: Tolle vestimentum ejus qui fidejussor extitit alieni, et pro extraneis aufer pignus ab eo.
text_pt: Ficando alguém por fiador de um estranho, tome-se-lhe a roupa; e por penhor àquele que se obriga pela mulher estranha.

text_en: The bread of lying is sweet to a man : but afterwards his mouth shall be filled with gravel.
text_la: Suavis est homini panis mendacii, et postea implebitur os ejus calculo.
text_pt: Suave é ao homem o pão da mentira, mas depois a sua boca se encherá de cascalho.

text_en: Designs are strengthened by counsels: and wars are to be managed by governments.
text_la: Cogitationes consiliis roborantur, et gubernaculis tractanda sunt bella.
text_pt: Cada pensamento se confirma com conselho e com bons conselhos se faz a guerra.

text_en: Meddle not with him that reveals secrets, and walks deceitfully, and opens wide his lips.
text_la: Ei qui revelat mysteria, et ambulat fraudulenter, et dilatat labia sua, ne commiscearis.
text_pt: O que anda tagarelando revela o segredo; não te intrometas com o que lisonjeia com os seus lábios.

text_en: He that curses his father, and mother, his lamp shall be put out in the midst of darkness.
text_la: Qui maledicit patri suo et matri, extinguetur lucerna ejus in mediis tenebris :
text_pt: O que amaldiçoa seu pai ou sua mãe, apagar-se-á a sua lâmpada em negras trevas.

text_en: The inheritance gotten hastily in the beginning, in the end shall be without a blessing .
text_la: hæreditas ad quam festinatur in principio, in novissimo benedictione carebit.
text_pt: A herança que no princípio é adquirida às pressas, no fim não será abençoada.

text_en: Say not: I will return evil : wait for the Lord , and he will deliver you.
text_la: Ne dicas : Reddam malum : exspecta Dominum, et liberabit te.
text_pt: Não digas: Vingar-me-ei do mal; espera pelo Senhor, e ele te livrará.

text_en: Diverse weights are an abomination before the Lord : a deceitful balance is not good .
text_la: Abominatio est apud Dominum pondus et pondus; statera dolosa non est bona.
text_pt: Pesos diferentes são abomináveis ao Senhor, e balança enganosa não é boa.
text_el: βδέλυγμα κυρίῳ δισσὸν στάθμιον καὶ ζυγὸς δόλιος οὐ καλὸν ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ

text_en: The steps of men are guided by the Lord : but who is the man that can understand his own way?
text_la: A Domino diriguntur gressus viri : quis autem hominum intelligere potest viam suam?
text_pt: Os passos do homem são dirigidos pelo Senhor; como, pois, entenderá o homem o seu caminho?
text_el: παρὰ κυρίου εὐθύνεται τὰ διαβήματα ἀνδρί θνητὸς δὲ πῶς ἂν νοήσαι τὰς ὁδοὺς αὐτοῦ

text_en: It is ruin to a man to devour holy ones, and after vows to retract.
text_la: Ruina est homini devorare sanctos, et post vota retractare.
text_pt: Laço é para o homem apropriar-se do que é santo, e só refletir depois de feitos os votos.
text_el: παγὶς ἀνδρὶ ταχύ τι τῶν ἰδίων ἁγιάσαι μετὰ γὰρ τὸ εὔξασθαι μετανοεῖν γίνεται

text_en: A wise king scatters the wicked , and brings over them the wheel.
text_la: Dissipat impios rex sapiens, et incurvat super eos fornicem.
text_pt: O rei sábio dispersa os ímpios e faz passar sobre eles a roda.
text_el: λικμήτωρ ἀσεβῶν βασιλεὺς σοφὸς καὶ ἐπιβαλεῖ αὐτοῖς τροχόν

text_en: The spirit of a man is the lamp of the Lord , which searches all the hidden things of the bowels.
text_la: Lucerna Domini spiraculum hominis, quæ investigat omnia secreta ventris.
text_pt: O espírito do homem é a lâmpada do Senhor, que esquadrinha todo o interior até o mais íntimo do ventre.
text_el: φῶς κυρίου πνοὴ ἀνθρώπων ὃς ἐρευνᾷ ταμίεια κοιλίας

text_en: Mercy and truth preserve the king, and his throne is strengthened by clemency.
text_la: Misericordia et veritas custodiunt regem, et roboratur clementia thronus ejus.
text_pt: Benignidade e verdade guardam ao rei, e com benignidade sustém ele o seu trono.
text_el: ἐλεημοσύνη καὶ ἀλήθεια φυλακὴ βασιλεῖ καὶ περικυκλώσουσιν ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ τὸν θρόνον αὐτοῦ

text_en: The joy of young men is their strength: and the dignity of old men , their grey hairs.
text_la: Exsultatio juvenum fortitudo eorum, et dignitas senum canities.
text_pt: A glória do jovem é a sua força; e a beleza dos velhos são as cãs.
text_el: κόσμος νεανίαις σοφία δόξα δὲ πρεσβυτέρων πολιαί

text_en: The blueness of a wound shall wipe away evils : and stripes in the more inward parts of the belly.
text_la: Livor vulneris absterget mala, et plagæ in secretioribus ventris.
text_pt: Os vergões das feridas são a purificação dos maus, como também as pancadas que penetram até o mais íntimo do ventre.
text_el: ὑπώπια καὶ συντρίμματα συναντᾷ κακοῖς πληγαὶ δὲ εἰς ταμίεια κοιλίας

text_en: As the divisions of waters, so the heart of the king is in the hand of the Lord: wherever he will, he shall turn it.
text_la: Sicut divisiones aquarum, ita cor regis in manu Domini : quocumque voluerit, inclinabit illud.
text_pt: Como ribeiros de águas assim é o coração do rei na mão do SENHOR, que o inclina a todo o seu querer.
text_el: ὥσπερ ὁρμὴ ὕδατος οὕτως καρδία βασιλέως ἐν χειρὶ θεοῦ οὗ ἐὰν θέλων νεύσῃ ἐκεῖ ἔκλινεν αὐτήν

text_en: Every way of a man seems right to himself: but the Lord weighs the hearts.
text_la: Omnis via viri recta sibi videtur : appendit autem corda Dominus.
text_pt: Todo caminho do homem é reto aos seus olhos, mas o Senhor sonda os corações.
text_el: πᾶς ἀνὴρ φαίνεται ἑαυτῷ δίκαιος κατευθύνει δὲ καρδίας κύριος

text_en: To do mercy and judgment, pleases the Lord more than victims.
text_la: Facere misericordiam et judicium magis placet Domino quam victimæ.
text_pt: Fazer justiça e juízo é mais aceitável ao Senhor do que sacrifício.
text_el: ποιεῖν δίκαια καὶ ἀληθεύειν ἀρεστὰ παρὰ θεῷ μᾶλλον ἢ θυσιῶν αἷμα

text_en: Haughtiness of the eyes is the enlarging of the heart: the lamp of the wicked is sin .
text_la: Exaltatio oculorum est dilatatio cordis; lucerna impiorum peccatum.
text_pt: Os olhos altivos, o coração orgulhoso e a lavoura dos ímpios é pecado.
text_el: μεγαλόφρων ἐφ' ὕβρει θρασυκάρδιος λαμπτὴρ δὲ ἀσεβῶν ἁμαρτία

text_en: The thoughts of the industrious always bring forth abundance: but every sluggard is always in want.
text_la: Cogitationes robusti semper in abundantia; omnis autem piger semper in egestate est.
text_pt: Os pensamentos do diligente tendem só para a abundância, porém os de todo apressado, tão-somente para a pobreza.

text_en: He that gathers treasures by a lying tongue, is vain and foolish, and shall stumble upon the snares of death.
text_la: Qui congregat thesauros lingua mendacii vanus et excors est, et impingetur ad laqueos mortis.
text_pt: Trabalhar com língua falsa para ajuntar tesouros é vaidade que conduz aqueles que buscam a morte.
text_el: ὁ ἐνεργῶν θησαυρίσματα γλώσσῃ ψευδεῖ μάταια διώκει ἐπὶ παγίδας θανάτου

text_en: The robberies of the wicked shall be their downfall, because they would not do judgment.
text_la: Rapinæ impiorum detrahent eos, quia noluerunt facere judicium.
text_pt: As rapinas dos ímpios os destruirão, porquanto se recusam a fazer justiça.
text_el: ὄλεθρος ἀσεβέσιν ἐπιξενωθήσεται οὐ γὰρ βούλονται πράσσειν τὰ δίκαια

text_en: The perverse way of a man is strange: but as for him that is pure, his work is right.
text_la: Perversa via viri aliena est; qui autem mundus est, rectum opus ejus.
text_pt: O caminho do homem é todo perverso e estranho, porém a obra do homem puro é reta.
text_el: πρὸς τοὺς σκολιοὺς σκολιὰς ὁδοὺς ἀποστέλλει ὁ θεός ἁγνὰ γὰρ καὶ ὀρθὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ

text_en: It is better to sit in a corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman , and in a common house.
text_la: Melius est sedere in angulo domatis, quam cum muliere litigiosa, et in domo communi.
text_pt: É melhor morar num canto de telhado do que ter como companheira em casa ampla uma mulher briguenta.
text_el: κρεῖσσον οἰκεῖν ἐπὶ γωνίας ὑπαίθρου ἢ ἐν κεκονιαμένοις μετὰ ἀδικίας καὶ ἐν οἴκῳ κοινῷ

text_en: The soul of the wicked desires evil , he will not have pity on his neighbour.
text_la: Anima impii desiderat malum : non miserebitur proximo suo.
text_pt: A alma do ímpio deseja o mal; o seu próximo não agrada aos seus olhos.
text_el: ψυχὴ ἀσεβοῦς οὐκ ἐλεηθήσεται ὑπ' οὐδενὸς τῶν ἀνθρώπων

text_en: When a pestilent man is punished, the little one will be wiser: and if he follow the wise, he will receive knowledge .
text_la: Mulctato pestilente, sapientior erit parvulus, et si sectetur sapientem, sumet scientiam.
text_pt: Quando o escarnecedor é castigado, o simples torna-se sábio; e o sábio quando é instruído recebe o conhecimento.
text_el: ζημιουμένου ἀκολάστου πανουργότερος γίνεται ὁ ἄκακος συνίων δὲ σοφὸς δέξεται γνῶσιν

text_en: The just considers seriously the house of the wicked , that he may withdraw the wicked from evil .
text_la: Excogitat justus de domo impii, ut detrahat impios a malo.
text_pt: O justo considera com prudência a casa do ímpio; mas Deus destrói os ímpios por causa dos seus males.
text_el: συνίει δίκαιος καρδίας ἀσεβῶν καὶ φαυλίζει ἀσεβεῖς ἐν κακοῖς

text_en: He that stops his ear against the cry of the poor, shall also cry himself, and shall not be heard.
text_la: Qui obturat aurem suam ad clamorem pauperis, et ipse clamabit, et non exaudietur.
text_pt: O que tapa o seu ouvido ao clamor do pobre, ele mesmo também clamará e não será ouvido.
text_el: ὃς φράσσει τὰ ὦτα τοῦ μὴ ἐπακοῦσαι ἀσθενοῦς καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπικαλέσεται καὶ οὐκ ἔσται ὁ εἰσακούων

text_en: A secret present quenches anger : and a gift in the bosom, the greatest wrath .
text_la: Munus absconditum extinguit iras, et donum in sinu indignationem maximam.
text_pt: O presente dado em segredo aplaca a ira, e a dádiva no regaço põe fim à maior indignação.
text_el: δόσις λάθριος ἀνατρέπει ὀργάς δώρων δὲ ὁ φειδόμενος θυμὸν ἐγείρει ἰσχυρόν

text_en: It is joy to the just to do judgment: and dread to them that work iniquity .
text_la: Gaudium justo est facere judicium, et pavor operantibus iniquitatem.
text_pt: O fazer justiça é alegria para o justo, mas destruição para os que praticam a iniqüidade.
text_el: εὐφροσύνη δικαίων ποιεῖν κρίμα ὅσιος δὲ ἀκάθαρτος παρὰ κακούργοις

text_en: A man that shall wander out of the way of doctrine, shall abide in the company of the giants.
text_la: Vir qui erraverit a via doctrinæ in cœtu gigantum commorabitur.
text_pt: O homem que anda desviado do caminho do entendimento, na congregação dos mortos repousará.
text_el: ἀνὴρ πλανώμενος ἐξ ὁδοῦ δικαιοσύνης ἐν συναγωγῇ γιγάντων ἀναπαύσεται

text_en: He that loves good cheer, shall be in want: he that loves wine, and fat things, shall not be rich.
text_la: Qui diligit epulas in egestate erit; qui amat vinum et pinguia non ditabitur.
text_pt: O que ama os prazeres padecerá necessidade; o que ama o vinho e o azeite nunca enriquecerá.
text_el: ἀνὴρ ἐνδεὴς ἀγαπᾷ εὐφροσύνην φιλῶν οἶνον καὶ ἔλαιον εἰς πλοῦτον

text_en: The wicked is delivered up for the just : and the unjust for the righteous.
text_la: Pro justo datur impius, et pro rectis iniquus.
text_pt: O resgate do justo é o ímpio; o do honrado é o perverso.
text_el: περικάθαρμα δὲ δικαίου ἄνομος

text_en: It is better to dwell in a wilderness , than with a quarrelsome and passionate woman .
text_la: Melius est habitare in terra deserta quam cum muliere rixosa et iracunda.
text_pt: É melhor morar numa terra deserta do que com a mulher rixosa e irritadiça.
text_el: κρεῖσσον οἰκεῖν ἐν γῇ ἐρήμῳ ἢ μετὰ γυναικὸς μαχίμου καὶ γλωσσώδους καὶ ὀργίλου

text_en: There is a treasure to be desired, and oil in the dwelling of the just : and the foolish man shall spend it.
text_la: Thesaurus desiderabilis, et oleum in habitaculo justi : et imprudens homo dissipabit illud.
text_pt: Tesouro desejável e azeite há na casa do sábio, mas o homem insensato os esgota.
text_el: θησαυρὸς ἐπιθυμητὸς ἀναπαύσεται ἐπὶ στόματος σοφοῦ ἄφρονες δὲ ἄνδρες καταπίονται αὐτόν

text_en: He that follows justice and mercy, shall find life, justice , and glory .
text_la: Qui sequitur justitiam et misericordiam inveniet vitam, justitiam, et gloriam.
text_pt: O que segue a justiça e a beneficência achará a vida, a justiça e a honra.
text_el: ὁδὸς δικαιοσύνης καὶ ἐλεημοσύνης εὑρήσει ζωὴν καὶ δόξαν

text_en: The wise man has scaled the city of the strong, and has cast down the strength of the confidence thereof.
text_la: Civitatem fortium ascendit sapiens, et destruxit robur fiduciæ ejus.
text_pt: O sábio escala a cidade do poderoso e derruba a força da sua confiança.
text_el: πόλεις ὀχυρὰς ἐπέβη σοφὸς καὶ καθεῖλεν τὸ ὀχύρωμα ἐφ' ᾧ ἐπεποίθεισαν οἱ ἀσεβεῖς

text_en: He that keeps his mouth and his tongue, keeps his soul from distress.
text_la: Qui custodit os suum et linguam suam custodit ab angustiis animam suam.
text_pt: O que guarda a sua boca e a sua língua guarda a sua alma das angústias.
text_el: ὃς φυλάσσει τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν γλῶσσαν διατηρεῖ ἐκ θλίψεως τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ

text_en: The proud and the arrogant is called ignorant , who in anger works pride .
text_la: Superbus et arrogans vocatur indoctus, qui in ira operatur superbiam.
text_pt: O soberbo e presumido, zombador é o seu nome, trata com indignação e soberba.
text_el: θρασὺς καὶ αὐθάδης καὶ ἀλαζὼν λοιμὸς καλεῖται ὃς δὲ μνησικακεῖ παράνομος

text_en: Desires kill the slothful: for his hands have refused to work at all.
text_la: Desideria occidunt pigrum : noluerunt enim quidquam manus ejus operari.
text_pt: O desejo do preguiçoso o mata, porque as suas mãos recusam trabalhar.
text_el: ἐπιθυμίαι ὀκνηρὸν ἀποκτείνουσιν οὐ γὰρ προαιροῦνται αἱ χεῖρες αὐτοῦ ποιεῖν τι

text_en: He longs and desires all the day: but he that is just , will give, and will not cease.
text_la: Tota die concupiscit et desiderat; qui autem justus est, tribuet, et non cessabit.
text_pt: O cobiçoso cobiça o dia todo, mas o justo dá, e nada retém.
text_el: ἀσεβὴς ἐπιθυμεῖ ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν ἐπιθυμίας κακάς ὁ δὲ δίκαιος ἐλεᾷ καὶ οἰκτίρει ἀφειδῶς

text_en: The sacrifices of the wicked are abominable, because they are offered of wickedness .
text_la: Hostiæ impiorum abominabiles, quia offeruntur ex scelere.
text_pt: O sacrifício dos ímpios já é abominação; quanto mais oferecendo-o com má intenção!
text_el: θυσίαι ἀσεβῶν βδέλυγμα κυρίῳ καὶ γὰρ παρανόμως προσφέρουσιν αὐτάς

text_en: A lying witness shall perish: an obedient man shall speak of victory.
text_la: Testis mendax peribit; vir obediens loquetur victoriam.
text_pt: A falsa testemunha perecerá, porém o homem que dá ouvidos falará sempre.
text_el: μάρτυς ψευδὴς ἀπολεῖται ἀνὴρ δὲ ὑπήκοος φυλασσόμενος λαλήσει

text_en: The wicked man impudently hardens his face: but he that is righteous, corrects his way.
text_la: Vir impius procaciter obfirmat vultum suum; qui autem rectus est corrigit viam suam.
text_pt: O homem ímpio endurece o seu rosto; mas o reto considera o seu caminho.
text_el: ἀσεβὴς ἀνὴρ ἀναιδῶς ὑφίσταται προσώπῳ ὁ δὲ εὐθὴς αὐτὸς συνίει τὰς ὁδοὺς αὐτοῦ

text_en: There is no wisdom, there is no prudence , there is no counsel against the Lord .
text_la: Non est sapientia, non est prudentia, non est consilium contra Dominum.
text_pt: Não há sabedoria, nem inteligência, nem conselho contra o Senhor.
text_el: οὐκ ἔστιν σοφία οὐκ ἔστιν ἀνδρεία οὐκ ἔστιν βουλὴ πρὸς τὸν ἀσεβῆ

text_en: The horse is prepared for the day of battle: but the Lord gives safety.
text_la: Equus paratur ad diem belli; Dominus autem salutem tribuit.
text_pt: Prepara-se o cavalo para o dia da batalha, porém do Senhor vem a vitória.
text_el: ἵππος ἑτοιμάζεται εἰς ἡμέραν πολέμου παρὰ δὲ κυρίου ἡ βοήθεια

text_en: A good name is better than great riches: and good favour is above silver and gold.
text_la: Melius est nomen bonum quam divitiæ multæ; super argentum et aurum gratia bona.
text_pt: Vale mais ter um bom nome do que muitas riquezas; e o ser estimado é melhor do que a riqueza e o ouro.
text_el: αἱρετώτερον ὄνομα καλὸν ἢ πλοῦτος πολύς ὑπὲρ δὲ ἀργύριον καὶ χρυσίον χάρις ἀγαθή

text_en: The rich and poor have met one another: the Lord is the maker of them both.
text_la: Dives et pauper obviaverunt sibi : utriusque operator est Dominus.
text_pt: O rico e o pobre se encontram; a todos o Senhor os fez.
text_el: πλούσιος καὶ πτωχὸς συνήντησαν ἀλλήλοις ἀμφοτέρους δὲ ὁ κύριος ἐποίησεν

text_en: The prudent man saw the evil , and hid himself: the simple passed on, and suffered loss.
text_la: Callidus vidit malum, et abscondit se; innocens pertransiit, et afflictus est damno.
text_pt: O prudente prevê o mal, e esconde-se; mas os simples passam e acabam pagando.
text_el: πανοῦργος ἰδὼν πονηρὸν τιμωρούμενον κραταιῶς αὐτὸς παιδεύεται οἱ δὲ ἄφρονες παρελθόντες ἐζημιώθησαν

text_en: The fruit of humility is the fear of the Lord , riches and glory and life.
text_la: Finis modestiæ timor Domini, divitiæ, et gloria, et vita.
text_pt: O galardão da humildade e o temor do Senhor são riquezas, honra e vida.
text_el: γενεὰ σοφίας φόβος κυρίου καὶ πλοῦτος καὶ δόξα καὶ ζωή

text_en: Arms and swords are in the way of the perverse: but he that keeps his own soul , departs far from them.
text_la: Arma et gladii in via perversi; custos autem animæ suæ longe recedit ab eis.
text_pt: Espinhos e laços há no caminho do perverso; o que guarda a sua alma retira-se para longe dele.
text_el: τρίβολοι καὶ παγίδες ἐν ὁδοῖς σκολιαῖς ὁ δὲ φυλάσσων τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχὴν ἀφέξεται αὐτῶν

text_en: It is a proverb: A young man according to his way, even when he is old, he will not depart from it.
text_la: Proverbium est : adolescens juxta viam suam; etiam cum senuerit, non recedet ab ea.
text_pt: Educa a criança no caminho em que deve andar; e até quando envelhecer não se desviará dele.

text_en: The rich rules over the poor: and the borrower is servant to him that lends.
text_la: Dives pauperibus imperat, et qui accipit mutuum servus est fœnerantis.
text_pt: O rico domina sobre os pobres e o que toma emprestado é servo do que empresta.
text_el: πλούσιοι πτωχῶν ἄρξουσιν καὶ οἰκέται ἰδίοις δεσπόταις δανιοῦσιν

text_en: He that sows iniquity , shall reap evils , and with the rod of his anger he shall be consumed.
text_la: Qui seminat iniquitatem metet mala, et virga iræ suæ consummabitur.
text_pt: O que semear a perversidade segará males; e com a vara da sua própria indignação será extinto.
text_el: ὁ σπείρων φαῦλα θερίσει κακά πληγὴν δὲ ἔργων αὐτοῦ συντελέσει

text_en: He that is inclined to mercy, shall be blessed : for of his bread he has given to the poor. He that makes presents, shall purchase victory and honour : but he carries away the souls of the receivers.
text_la: Qui pronus est ad misericordiam benedicetur : de panibus enim suis dedit pauperi. Victoriam et honorem acquiret qui dat munera; animam autem aufert accipientium.
text_pt: O que vê com bons olhos será abençoado, porque dá do seu pão ao pobre.
text_el: ὁ ἐλεῶν πτωχὸν αὐτὸς διατραφήσεται τῶν γὰρ ἑαυτοῦ ἄρτων ἔδωκεν τῷ πτωχῷ

text_en: Cast out the scoffer, and contention shall go out with him, and quarrels and reproaches shall cease.
text_la: Ejice derisorem, et exibit cum eo jurgium, cessabuntque causæ et contumeliæ.
text_pt: Lança fora o escarnecedor, e se irá a contenda; e acabará a questão e a vergonha.
text_el: ἔκβαλε ἐκ συνεδρίου λοιμόν καὶ συνεξελεύσεται αὐτῷ νεῖκος ὅταν γὰρ καθίσῃ ἐν συνεδρίῳ πάντας ἀτιμάζει

text_en: He that loves cleanness of heart, for the grace of his lips shall have the king for his friend.
text_la: Qui diligit cordis munditiam, propter gratiam labiorum suorum habebit amicum regem.
text_pt: O que ama a pureza de coração, e é amável de lábios, será amigo do rei.
text_el: ἀγαπᾷ κύριος ὁσίας καρδίας δεκτοὶ δὲ αὐτῷ πάντες ἄμωμοι χείλεσιν ποιμαίνει βασιλεύς

text_en: The eyes of the Lord preserve knowledge : and the words of the unjust are overthrown.
text_la: Oculi Domini custodiunt scientiam, et supplantantur verba iniqui.
text_pt: Os olhos do Senhor conservam o conhecimento, mas as palavras do iníquo ele transtornará.
text_el: οἱ δὲ ὀφθαλμοὶ κυρίου διατηροῦσιν αἴσθησιν φαυλίζει δὲ λόγους παράνομος

text_en: The slothful man says: There is a lion without, I shall be slain in the midst of the streets.
text_la: Dicit piger : Leo est foris; in medio platearum occidendus sum.
text_pt: Diz o preguiçoso: Um leão está lá fora; serei morto no meio das ruas.
text_el: προφασίζεται καὶ λέγει ὀκνηρός λέων ἐν ταῖς ὁδοῖς ἐν δὲ ταῖς πλατείαις φονευταί

text_en: The mouth of a strange woman is a deep pit: he whom the Lord is angry with, shall fall into it.
text_la: Fovea profunda os alienæ : cui iratus est Dominus, incidet in eam.
text_pt: Cova profunda é a boca das mulheres estranhas; aquele contra quem o Senhor se irar, cairá nela.
text_el: βόθρος βαθὺς στόμα παρανόμου ὁ δὲ μισηθεὶς ὑπὸ κυρίου ἐμπεσεῖται εἰς αὐτόν

text_en: Folly is bound up in the heart of a child, and the rod of correction shall drive it away.
text_la: Stultitia colligata est in corde pueri, et virga disciplinæ fugabit eam.
text_pt: A estultícia está ligada ao coração da criança, mas a vara da correção a afugentará dela.
text_el: ἄνοια ἐξῆπται καρδίας νέου ῥάβδος δὲ καὶ παιδεία μακρὰν ἀπ' αὐτοῦ

text_en: He that oppresses the poor, to increase his own riches, shall himself give to one that is richer, and shall be in need.
text_la: Qui calumniatur pauperem ut augeat divitias suas, dabit ipse ditiori, et egebit.
text_pt: O que oprime ao pobre para se engrandecer a si mesmo, ou o que dá ao rico, certamente empobrecerá.
text_el: ὁ συκοφαντῶν πένητα πολλὰ ποιεῖ τὰ ἑαυτοῦ δίδωσιν δὲ πλουσίῳ ἐπ' ἐλάσσονι

text_en: Incline your ear, and hear the words of the wise: and apply your heart to my doctrine:
text_la: Inclina aurem tuam, et audi verba sapientium : appone autem cor ad doctrinam meam,
text_pt: Inclina o teu ouvido e ouve as palavras dos sábios, e aplica o teu coração ao meu conhecimento.
text_el: λόγοις σοφῶν παράβαλλε σὸν οὖς καὶ ἄκουε ἐμὸν λόγον τὴν δὲ σὴν καρδίαν ἐπίστησον ἵνα γνῷς ὅτι καλοί εἰσιν

text_en: Which shall be beautiful for you, if you keep it in your bowels, and it shall flow in your lips:
text_la: quæ pulchra erit tibi cum servaveris eam in ventre tuo, et redundabit in labiis tuis :
text_pt: Porque te será agradável se as guardares no teu íntimo, se aplicares todas elas aos teus lábios.
text_el: καὶ ἐὰν ἐμβάλῃς αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν καρδίαν σου εὐφρανοῦσίν σε ἅμα ἐπὶ σοῖς χείλεσιν

text_en: That your trust may be in the Lord , wherefore I have also shown it to you this day.
text_la: ut sit in Domino fiducia tua, unde et ostendi eam tibi hodie.
text_pt: Para que a tua confiança esteja no Senhor, faço-te sabê-las hoje, a ti mesmo.
text_el: ἵνα σου γένηται ἐπὶ κύριον ἡ ἐλπὶς καὶ γνωρίσῃ σοι τὴν ὁδὸν αὐτοῦ

text_en: Behold I have described it to you three manner of ways, in thoughts and knowledge :
text_la: Ecce descripsi eam tibi tripliciter, in cogitationibus et scientia :
text_pt: Porventura não te escrevi excelentes coisas, acerca de todo conselho e conhecimento,
text_el: καὶ σὺ δὲ ἀπόγραψαι αὐτὰ σεαυτῷ τρισσῶς εἰς βουλὴν καὶ γνῶσιν ἐπὶ τὸ πλάτος τῆς καρδίας σου

text_en: That I might show you the certainty , and the words of truth , to answer out of these to them that sent you.
text_la: ut ostenderem tibi firmitatem et eloquia veritatis, respondere ex his illis qui miserunt te.
text_pt: Para fazer-te saber a certeza das palavras da verdade, e assim possas responder palavras de verdade aos que te consultarem?
text_el: διδάσκω οὖν σε ἀληθῆ λόγον καὶ γνῶσιν ἀγαθὴν ὑπακούειν τοῦ ἀποκρίνεσθαι λόγους ἀληθείας τοῖς προβαλλομένοις σοι

text_en: Do no violence to the poor, because he is poor: and do not oppress the needy in the gate:
text_la: Non facias violentiam pauperi quia pauper est, neque conteras egenum in porta :
text_pt: Não roubes ao pobre, porque é pobre, nem atropeles na porta o aflito;
text_el: μὴ ἀποβιάζου πένητα πτωχὸς γάρ ἐστιν καὶ μὴ ἀτιμάσῃς ἀσθενῆ ἐν πύλαις

text_en: Because the Lord will judge his cause: and will afflict them that have afflicted his soul .
text_la: quia judicabit Dominus causam ejus, et configet eos qui confixerunt animam ejus.
text_pt: Porque o Senhor defenderá a sua causa em juízo, e aos que os roubam ele lhes tirará a vida.
text_el: ὁ γὰρ κύριος κρινεῖ αὐτοῦ τὴν κρίσιν καὶ ῥύσῃ σὴν ἄσυλον ψυχήν

text_en: Be not a friend to an angry man , and do not walk with a furious man :
text_la: Noli esse amicus homini iracundo, neque ambules cum viro furioso :
text_pt: Não sejas companheiro do homem briguento nem andes com o colérico,
text_el: μὴ ἴσθι ἑταῖρος ἀνδρὶ θυμώδει φίλῳ δὲ ὀργίλῳ μὴ συναυλίζου

text_en: Lest perhaps you learn his ways, and take scandal to your soul .
text_la: ne forte discas semitas ejus, et sumas scandalum animæ tuæ.
text_pt: Para que não aprendas as suas veredas, e tomes um laço para a tua alma.
text_el: μήποτε μάθῃς τῶν ὁδῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ λάβῃς βρόχους τῇ σῇ ψυχῇ

text_en: Be not with them that fasten down their hands, and that offer themselves sureties for debts:
text_la: Noli esse cum his qui defigunt manus suas, et qui vades se offerunt pro debitis :
text_pt: Não estejas entre os que se comprometem, e entre os que ficam por fiadores de dívidas,
text_el: μὴ δίδου σεαυτὸν εἰς ἐγγύην αἰσχυνόμενος πρόσωπον

text_en: For if you have not wherewith to restore, what cause is there that he should take the covering from your bed?
text_la: si enim non habes unde restituas, quid causæ est ut tollat operimentum de cubili tuo?
text_pt: Pois se não tens com que pagar, deixarias que te tirassem até a tua cama de debaixo de ti?
text_el: ἐὰν γὰρ μὴ ἔχῃς πόθεν ἀποτείσῃς λήμψονται τὸ στρῶμα τὸ ὑπὸ τὰς πλευράς σου

text_en: Pass not beyond the ancient bounds which your fathers have set.
text_la: Ne transgrediaris terminos antiquos, quos posuerunt patres tui.
text_pt: Não removas os antigos limites que teus pais fizeram.
text_el: μὴ μέταιρε ὅρια αἰώνια ἃ ἔθεντο οἱ πατέρες σου

text_en: Have you seen a man swift in his work? He shall stand before kings, and shall not be before those that are obscure.
text_la: Vidisti virum velocem in opere suo? coram regibus stabit, nec erit ante ignobiles.
text_pt: Viste o homem diligente na sua obra? Perante reis será posto; não permanecerá entre os de posição inferior.
text_el: ὁρατικὸν ἄνδρα καὶ ὀξὺν ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις αὐτοῦ βασιλεῦσι δεῖ παρεστάναι καὶ μὴ παρεστάναι ἀνδράσι νωθροῖς

text_en: When you shall sit to eat with a prince, consider diligently what is set before your face:
text_la: Quando sederis ut comedas cum principe, diligenter attende quæ apposita sunt ante faciem tuam.
text_pt: Quando te assentares a comer com um governador, atenta bem para o que é posto diante de ti,
text_el: ἐὰν καθίσῃς δειπνεῖν ἐπὶ τραπέζης δυναστῶν νοητῶς νόει τὰ παρατιθέμενά σοι

text_en: And put a knife to your throat, if it be so that you have your soul in your own power.
text_la: Et statue cultrum in gutture tuo : si tamen habes in potestate animam tuam.
text_pt: E se és homem de grande apetite, põe uma faca à tua garganta.
text_el: καὶ ἐπίβαλλε τὴν χεῖρά σου εἰδὼς ὅτι τοιαῦτά σε δεῖ παρασκευάσαι

text_en: Be not desirous of his meats, in which is the bread of deceit .
text_la: Ne desideres de cibis ejus, in quo est panis mendacii.
text_pt: Não cobices as suas iguarias porque são comidas enganosas.
text_el: εἰ δὲ ἀπληστότερος εἶ μὴ ἐπιθύμει τῶν ἐδεσμάτων αὐτοῦ ταῦτα γὰρ ἔχεται ζωῆς ψευδοῦς

text_en: Labour not to be rich: but set bounds to your prudence .
text_la: Noli laborare ut diteris, sed prudentiæ tuæ pone modum.
text_pt: Não te fatigues para enriqueceres; e não apliques nisso a tua sabedoria.
text_el: μὴ παρεκτείνου πένης ὢν πλουσίῳ τῇ δὲ σῇ ἐννοίᾳ ἀπόσχου

text_en: Lift not up your eyes to riches which you can not have: because they shall make themselves wings like those of an eagle, and shall fly towards heaven .
text_la: Ne erigas oculos tuos ad opes quas non potes habere, quia facient sibi pennas quasi aquilæ, et volabunt in cælum.
text_pt: Porventura fixarás os teus olhos naquilo que não é nada? porque certamente criará asas e voará ao céu como a águia.
text_el: ἐὰν ἐπιστήσῃς τὸ σὸν ὄμμα πρὸς αὐτόν οὐδαμοῦ φανεῖται κατεσκεύασται γὰρ αὐτῷ πτέρυγες ὥσπερ ἀετοῦ καὶ ὑποστρέφει εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ προεστηκότος αὐτοῦ

text_en: Eat not with an envious man , and desire not his meats:
text_la: Ne comedas cum homine invido, et ne desideres cibos ejus :
text_pt: Não comas o pão daquele que tem o olhar maligno, nem cobices as suas iguarias gostosas.
text_el: μὴ συνδείπνει ἀνδρὶ βασκάνῳ μηδὲ ἐπιθύμει τῶν βρωμάτων αὐτοῦ

text_en: Because, like a soothsayer, and diviner, he thinks that which he knows not. Eat and drink, will he say to you: and his mind is not with you.
text_la: quoniam in similitudinem arioli et conjectoris æstimat quod ignorat. Comede et bibe, dicet tibi; et mens ejus non est tecum.
text_pt: Porque, como imaginou no seu coração, assim é ele. Come e bebe, te disse ele; porém o seu coração não está contigo.
text_el: ὃν τρόπον γὰρ εἴ τις καταπίοι τρίχα οὕτως ἐσθίει καὶ πίνει

text_en: The meats which you had eaten, you shall vomit up: and shall lose your beautiful words.
text_la: Cibos quos comederas evomes, et perdes pulchros sermones tuos.
text_pt: Vomitarás o bocado que comeste, e perderás as tuas suaves palavras.
text_el: μηδὲ πρὸς σὲ εἰσαγάγῃς αὐτὸν καὶ φάγῃς τὸν ψωμόν σου μετ' αὐτοῦ ἐξεμέσει γὰρ αὐτὸν καὶ λυμανεῖται τοὺς λόγους σου τοὺς καλούς

text_en: Speak not in the ears of fools: because they will despise the instruction of your speech.
text_la: In auribus insipientium ne loquaris, qui despicient doctrinam eloquii tui.
text_pt: Não fales ao ouvido do tolo, porque desprezará a sabedoria das tuas palavras.
text_el: εἰς ὦτα ἄφρονος μηδὲν λέγε μήποτε μυκτηρίσῃ τοὺς συνετοὺς λόγους σου

text_en: Touch not the bounds of little ones: and enter not into the field of the fatherless :
text_la: Ne attingas parvulorum terminos, et agrum pupillorum ne introëas :
text_pt: Não removas os limites antigos nem entres nos campos dos órfãos,
text_el: μὴ μεταθῇς ὅρια αἰώνια εἰς δὲ κτῆμα ὀρφανῶν μὴ εἰσέλθῃς

text_en: For their near kinsman is strong: and he will judge their cause against you.
text_la: propinquus enim illorum fortis est, et ipse judicabit contra te causam illorum.
text_pt: Porque o seu redentor é poderoso; e pleiteará a causa deles contra ti.
text_el: ὁ γὰρ λυτρούμενος αὐτοὺς κύριος κραταιός ἐστιν καὶ κρινεῖ τὴν κρίσιν αὐτῶν μετὰ σοῦ

text_en: Let your heart apply itself to instruction and your ears to words of knowledge .
text_la: Ingrediatur ad doctrinam cor tuum, et aures tuæ ad verba scientiæ.
text_pt: Aplica o teu coração à instrução e os teus ouvidos às palavras do conhecimento.
text_el: δὸς εἰς παιδείαν τὴν καρδίαν σου τὰ δὲ ὦτά σου ἑτοίμασον λόγοις αἰσθήσεως

text_en: Withhold not correction from a child: for if you strike him with the rod, he shall not die.
text_la: Noli subtrahere a puero disciplinam : si enim percusseris eum virga, non morietur.
text_pt: Não retires a disciplina da criança; pois se a fustigares com a vara, nem por isso morrerá.
text_el: μὴ ἀπόσχῃ νήπιον παιδεύειν ὅτι ἐὰν πατάξῃς αὐτὸν ῥάβδῳ οὐ μὴ ἀποθάνῃ

text_en: You shall beat him with the rod, and deliver his soul from hell.
text_la: Tu virga percuties eum, et animam ejus de inferno liberabis.
text_pt: Tu a fustigarás com a vara, e livrarás a sua alma do inferno.
text_el: σὺ μὲν γὰρ πατάξεις αὐτὸν ῥάβδῳ τὴν δὲ ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἐκ θανάτου ῥύσῃ

text_en: My son, if your mind be wise, my heart shall rejoice with you:
text_la: Fili mi, si sapiens fuerit animus tuus, gaudebit tecum cor meum :
text_pt: Filho meu, se o teu coração for sábio, alegrar-se-á o meu coração, sim, o meu próprio.
text_el: υἱέ ἐὰν σοφὴ γένηταί σου ἡ καρδία εὐφρανεῖς καὶ τὴν ἐμὴν καρδίαν

text_en: And my reins shall rejoice, when your lips shall speak what is right.
text_la: et exsultabunt renes mei, cum locuta fuerint rectum labia tua.
text_pt: E exultarão os meus rins, quando os teus lábios falarem coisas retas.
text_el: καὶ ἐνδιατρίψει λόγοις τὰ σὰ χείλη πρὸς τὰ ἐμὰ χείλη ἐὰν ὀρθὰ ὦσιν

text_en: Let not your heart envy sinners: but be in the fear of the Lord all the day long:
text_la: Non æmuletur cor tuum peccatores, sed in timore Domini esto tota die :
text_pt: O teu coração não inveje os pecadores; antes permanece no temor do Senhor todo dia.
text_el: μὴ ζηλούτω ἡ καρδία σου ἁμαρτωλούς ἀλλὰ ἐν φόβῳ κυρίου ἴσθι ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν

text_en: Because you shall have hope in the latter end, and your expectation shall not be taken away.
text_la: quia habebis spem in novissimo, et præstolatio tua non auferetur.
text_pt: Porque certamente acabará bem; não será malograda a tua esperança.
text_el: ἐὰν γὰρ τηρήσῃς αὐτά ἔσται σοι ἔκγονα ἡ δὲ ἐλπίς σου οὐκ ἀποστήσεται

text_en: Hear, my son, and be wise: and guide your mind in the way.
text_la: Audi, fili mi, et esto sapiens, et dirige in via animum tuum.
text_pt: Ouve tu, filho meu, e sê sábio, e dirige no caminho o teu coração.
text_el: ἄκουε υἱέ καὶ σοφὸς γίνου καὶ κατεύθυνε ἐννοίας σῆς καρδίας

text_en: Be not in the feasts of great drinkers, nor in their revellings, who contribute flesh to eat:
text_la: Noli esse in conviviis potatorum, nec in comessationibus eorum qui carnes ad vescendum conferunt :
text_pt: Não estejas entre os beberrões de vinho, nem entre os comilões de carne.
text_el: μὴ ἴσθι οἰνοπότης μηδὲ ἐκτείνου συμβολαῖς κρεῶν τε ἀγορασμοῖς

text_en: Because they that give themselves to drinking, and that club together, shall be consumed: and drowsiness shall be clothed with rags.
text_la: quia vacantes potibus et dantes symbola consumentur, et vestietur pannis dormitatio.
text_pt: Porque o beberrão e o comilão acabarão na pobreza; e a sonolência os faz vestir-se de trapos.
text_el: πᾶς γὰρ μέθυσος καὶ πορνοκόπος πτωχεύσει καὶ ἐνδύσεται διερρηγμένα καὶ ῥακώδη πᾶς ὑπνώδης

text_en: Hearken to your father, that begot you: and despise not your mother when she is old.
text_la: Audi patrem tuum, qui genuit te, et ne contemnas cum senuerit mater tua.
text_pt: Ouve teu pai, que te gerou, e não desprezes tua mãe, quando vier a envelhecer.
text_el: ἄκουε υἱέ πατρὸς τοῦ γεννήσαντός σε καὶ μὴ καταφρόνει ὅτι γεγήρακέν σου ἡ μήτηρ

text_en: Buy truth , and do not sell wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.
text_la: Veritatem eme, et noli vendere sapientiam, et doctrinam, et intelligentiam.
text_pt: Compra a verdade, e não a vendas; e também a sabedoria, a instrução e o entendimento.

text_en: The father of the just rejoices greatly: he that has begotten a wise son, shall have joy in him.
text_la: Exsultat gaudio pater justi; qui sapientem genuit, lætabitur in eo.
text_pt: Grandemente se regozijará o pai do justo, e o que gerar um sábio, se alegrará nele.
text_el: καλῶς ἐκτρέφει πατὴρ δίκαιος ἐπὶ δὲ υἱῷ σοφῷ εὐφραίνεται ἡ ψυχὴ αὐτοῦ

text_en: Let your father and your mother be joyful, and let her rejoice that bore you.
text_la: Gaudeat pater tuus et mater tua, et exsultet quæ genuit te.
text_pt: Alegrem-se teu pai e tua mãe, e regozije-se a que te gerou.
text_el: εὐφραινέσθω ὁ πατὴρ καὶ ἡ μήτηρ ἐπὶ σοί καὶ χαιρέτω ἡ τεκοῦσά σε

text_en: My son, give me your heart: and let your eyes keep my ways.
text_la: Præbe, fili mi, cor tuum mihi, et oculi tui vias meas custodiant.
text_pt: Dá-me, filho meu, o teu coração, e os teus olhos observem os meus caminhos.
text_el: δός μοι υἱέ σὴν καρδίαν οἱ δὲ σοὶ ὀφθαλμοὶ ἐμὰς ὁδοὺς τηρείτωσαν

text_en: For a harlot is a deep ditch: and a strange woman is a narrow pit.
text_la: Fovea enim profunda est meretrix, et puteus angustus aliena.
text_pt: Porque cova profunda é a prostituta, e poço estreito a estranha.
text_el: πίθος γὰρ τετρημένος ἐστὶν ἀλλότριος οἶκος καὶ φρέαρ στενὸν ἀλλότριον

text_en: She lies in wait in the way as a robber, and him whom she shall see unwary, she will kill.
text_la: Insidiatur in via quasi latro, et quos incautos viderit, interficiet.
text_pt: Pois ela, como um salteador, se põe à espreita, e multiplica entre os homens os iníquos.
text_el: οὗτος γὰρ συντόμως ἀπολεῖται καὶ πᾶς παράνομος ἀναλωθήσεται

text_en: Who has woe? Whose father has woe? Who has contentions? Who falls into pits? Who has wounds without cause? Who has redness of eyes?
text_la: Cui væ? cujus patri væ? cui rixæ? cui foveæ? cui sine causa vulnera? cui suffusio oculorum?
text_pt: Para quem são os ais? Para quem os pesares? Para quem as pelejas? Para quem as queixas? Para quem as feridas sem causa? E para quem os olhos vermelhos?
text_el: τίνι οὐαί τίνι θόρυβος τίνι κρίσις τίνι ἀηδίαι καὶ λέσχαι τίνι συντρίμματα διὰ κενῆς τίνος πέλειοι οἱ ὀφθαλμοί

text_en: Surely they that pass their time in wine, and study to drink off their cups.
text_la: nonne his qui commorantur in vino, et student calicibus epotandis?
text_pt: Para os que se demoram perto do vinho, para os que andam buscando vinho misturado.
text_el: οὐ τῶν ἐγχρονιζόντων ἐν οἴνοις οὐ τῶν ἰχνευόντων ποῦ πότοι γίνονται

text_en: Look not upon the wine when it is yellow, when the colour thereof shines in the glass: it goes in pleasantly,
text_la: Ne intuearis vinum quando flavescit, cum splenduerit in vitro color ejus : ingreditur blande,
text_pt: Não olhes para o vinho quando se mostra vermelho, quando resplandece no copo e se escoa suavemente.
text_el: μὴ μεθύσκεσθε οἴνῳ ἀλλὰ ὁμιλεῖτε ἀνθρώποις δικαίοις καὶ ὁμιλεῖτε ἐν περιπάτοις ἐὰν γὰρ εἰς τὰς φιάλας καὶ τὰ ποτήρια δῷς τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς σου ὕστερον περιπατήσεις γυμνότερος ὑπέρου

text_en: but in the end, it will bite like a snake, and will spread abroad poison like a basilisk.
text_la: sed in novissimo mordebit ut coluber, et sicut regulus venena diffundet.
text_pt: No fim, picará como a cobra, e como o basilisco morderá.
text_el: τὸ δὲ ἔσχατον ὥσπερ ὑπὸ ὄφεως πεπληγὼς ἐκτείνεται καὶ ὥσπερ ὑπὸ κεράστου διαχεῖται αὐτῷ ὁ ἰός

text_en: Your eyes shall behold strange women , and your heart shall utter perverse things.
text_la: Oculi tui videbunt extraneas, et cor tuum loquetur perversa.
text_pt: Os teus olhos olharão para as mulheres estranhas, e o teu coração falará perversidades.
text_el: οἱ ὀφθαλμοί σου ὅταν ἴδωσιν ἀλλοτρίαν τὸ στόμα σου τότε λαλήσει σκολιά

text_en: And you shall be as one sleeping in the midst of the sea, and as a pilot fast asleep when the stern is lost.
