text_la: Et eris sicut dormiens in medio mari, et quasi sopitus gubernator, amisso clavo.
text_pt: E serás como o que se deita no meio do mar, e como o que jaz no topo do mastro.
text_el: καὶ κατακείσῃ ὥσπερ ἐν καρδίᾳ θαλάσσης καὶ ὥσπερ κυβερνήτης ἐν πολλῷ κλύδωνι

text_en: And you shall say: They have beaten me, but I was not sensible of pain: they drew me, and I felt not: when shall I awake and find wine again?
text_la: Et dices : Verberaverunt me, sed non dolui; traxerunt me, et ego non sensi. Quando evigilabo, et rursus vina reperiam?
text_pt: E dirás: Espancaram-me e não me doeu; bateram-me e nem senti; quando despertarei? aí então beberei outra vez.
text_el: ἐρεῖς δέ τύπτουσίν με καὶ οὐκ ἐπόνεσα καὶ ἐνέπαιξάν μοι ἐγὼ δὲ οὐκ ᾔδειν πότε ὄρθρος ἔσται ἵνα ἐλθὼν ζητήσω μεθ' ὧν συνελεύσομαι

text_en: Seek not to be like evil men , neither desire to be with them:
text_la: Ne æmuleris viros malos, nec desideres esse cum eis :
text_pt: Não tenhas inveja dos homens malignos, nem desejes estar com eles.
text_el: υἱέ μὴ ζηλώσῃς κακοὺς ἄνδρας μηδὲ ἐπιθυμήσῃς εἶναι μετ' αὐτῶν

text_en: Because their mind studies robberies, and their lips speak deceits.
text_la: quia rapinas meditatur mens eorum, et fraudes labia eorum loquuntur.
text_pt: Porque o seu coração medita a rapina, e os seus lábios falam a malícia.
text_el: ψεύδη γὰρ μελετᾷ ἡ καρδία αὐτῶν καὶ πόνους τὰ χείλη αὐτῶν λαλεῖ

text_en: By wisdom the house shall be built, and by prudence it shall be strengthened.
text_la: Sapientia ædificabitur domus, et prudentia roborabitur.
text_pt: Com a sabedoria se edifica a casa, e com o entendimento ela se estabelece;
text_el: μετὰ σοφίας οἰκοδομεῖται οἶκος καὶ μετὰ συνέσεως ἀνορθοῦται

text_en: By instruction the storerooms shall be filled with all precious and most beautiful wealth.
text_la: In doctrina replebuntur cellaria, universa substantia pretiosa et pulcherrima.
text_pt: E pelo conhecimento se encherão as câmaras com todos os bens preciosos e agradáveis.
text_el: μετὰ αἰσθήσεως ἐμπίμπλαται ταμίεια ἐκ παντὸς πλούτου τιμίου καὶ καλοῦ

text_en: A wise man is strong: and a knowing man , stout and valiant .
text_la: Vir sapiens fortis est, et vir doctus robustus et validus :
text_pt: O homem sábio é forte, e o homem de conhecimento consolida a força.
text_el: κρείσσων σοφὸς ἰσχυροῦ καὶ ἀνὴρ φρόνησιν ἔχων γεωργίου μεγάλου

text_en: Because war is managed by due ordering: and there shall be safety where there are many counsels.
text_la: quia cum dispositione initur bellum, et erit salus ubi multa consilia sunt.
text_pt: Com conselhos prudentes tu farás a guerra; e há vitória na multidão dos conselheiros.
text_el: μετὰ κυβερνήσεως γίνεται πόλεμος βοήθεια δὲ μετὰ καρδίας βουλευτικῆς

text_en: Wisdom is too high for a fool; in the gate he shall not open his mouth.
text_la: Excelsa stulto sapientia; in porta non aperiet os suum.
text_pt: A sabedoria é demasiadamente alta para o tolo, na porta não abrirá a sua boca.
text_el: σοφία καὶ ἔννοια ἀγαθὴ ἐν πύλαις σοφῶν σοφοὶ οὐκ ἐκκλίνουσιν ἐκ στόματος κυρίου

text_en: He that devises to do evils , shall be called a fool.
text_la: Qui cogitat mala facere stultus vocabitur:
text_pt: Àquele que cuida em fazer mal, chamá-lo-ão de pessoa danosa.
text_el: ἀλλὰ λογίζονται ἐν συνεδρίοις ἀπαιδεύτοις συναντᾷ θάνατος

text_en: The thought of a fool is sin : and the detractor is the abomination of men .
text_la: cogitatio stulti peccatum est, et abominatio hominum detractor.
text_pt: O pensamento do tolo é pecado, e abominável aos homens é o escarnecedor.
text_el: ἀποθνῄσκει δὲ ἄφρων ἐν ἁμαρτίαις ἀκαθαρσία δὲ ἀνδρὶ λοιμῷ ἐμμολυνθήσεται

text_en: If you lose hope , being weary in the day of distress, your strength shall be diminished.
text_la: Si desperaveris lassus in die angustiæ, imminuetur fortitudo tua.
text_pt: Se te mostrares fraco no dia da angústia, é que a tua força é pequena.
text_el: ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κακῇ καὶ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ θλίψεως ἕως ἂν ἐκλίπῃ

text_en: Deliver them that are led to death: and those that are drawn to death, forbear not to deliver.
text_la: Erue eos qui ducuntur ad mortem, et qui trahuntur ad interitum, liberare ne cesses.
text_pt: Se tu deixares de livrar os que estão sendo levados para a morte, e aos que estão sendo levados para a matança;
text_el: ῥῦσαι ἀγομένους εἰς θάνατον καὶ ἐκπρίου κτεινομένους μὴ φείσῃ

text_en: If you say: I have not strength enough: he that sees into the heart, he understands, and nothing deceives the keeper of your soul , and he shall render to a man according to his works.
text_la: Si dixeris : Vires non suppetunt; qui inspector est cordis ipse intelligit : et servatorem animæ tuæ nihil fallit, reddetque homini juxta opera sua.
text_pt: Se disseres: Eis que não o sabemos; porventura não o considerará aquele que pondera os corações? Não o saberá aquele que atenta para a tua alma? Não dará ele ao homem conforme a sua obra?
text_el: ἐὰν δὲ εἴπῃς οὐκ οἶδα τοῦτον γίνωσκε ὅτι κύριος καρδίας πάντων γινώσκει καὶ ὁ πλάσας πνοὴν πᾶσιν αὐτὸς οἶδεν πάντα ὃς ἀποδίδωσιν ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ

text_en: Eat honey, my son, because it is good , and the honeycomb most sweet to your throat.
text_la: Comede, fili mi, mel, quia bonum est, et favum dulcissimum gutturi tuo.
text_pt: Come mel, meu filho, porque é bom; o favo de mel é doce ao teu paladar.
text_el: φάγε μέλι υἱέ ἀγαθὸν γὰρ κηρίον ἵνα γλυκανθῇ σου ὁ φάρυγξ

text_en: So also is the doctrine of wisdom to your soul : which when you have found, you shall have hope in the end, and your hope shall not perish.
text_la: Sic et doctrina sapientiæ animæ tuæ : quam cum inveneris, habebis in novissimis spem, et spes tua non peribit.
text_pt: Assim será para a tua alma o conhecimento da sabedoria; se a achares, haverá galardão para ti e não será cortada a tua esperança.
text_el: οὕτως αἰσθήσῃ σοφίαν τῇ σῇ ψυχῇ ἐὰν γὰρ εὕρῃς ἔσται καλὴ ἡ τελευτή σου καὶ ἐλπίς σε οὐκ ἐγκαταλείψει

text_en: Lie not in wait, nor seek after wickedness in the house of the just , nor spoil his rest.
text_la: Ne insidieris, et quæras impietatem in domo justi, neque vastes requiem ejus.
text_pt: Não armes ciladas contra a habitação do justo, ó ímpio, nem assoles o seu lugar de repouso,
text_el: μὴ προσαγάγῃς ἀσεβῆ νομῇ δικαίων μηδὲ ἀπατηθῇς χορτασίᾳ κοιλίας

text_en: For a just man shall fall seven times, and shall rise again: but the wicked shall fall down into evil .
text_la: Septies enim cadet justus, et resurget : impii autem corruent in malum.
text_pt: Porque sete vezes cairá o justo, e se levantará; mas os ímpios tropeçarão no mal.
text_el: ἑπτάκι γὰρ πεσεῖται ὁ δίκαιος καὶ ἀναστήσεται οἱ δὲ ἀσεβεῖς ἀσθενήσουσιν ἐν κακοῖς

text_en: When your enemy shall fall, be not glad, and in his ruin let not your heart rejoice:
text_la: Cum ceciderit inimicus tuus ne gaudeas, et in ruina ejus ne exsultet cor tuum :
text_pt: Quando cair o teu inimigo, não te alegres, nem se regozije o teu coração quando ele tropeçar;
text_el: ἐὰν πέσῃ ὁ ἐχθρός σου μὴ ἐπιχαρῇς αὐτῷ ἐν δὲ τῷ ὑποσκελίσματι αὐτοῦ μὴ ἐπαίρου

text_en: Lest the Lord see, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.
text_la: ne forte videat Dominus, et displiceat ei, et auferat ab eo iram suam.
text_pt: Para que, vendo-o o Senhor, seja isso mau aos seus olhos, e desvie dele a sua ira.
text_el: ὅτι ὄψεται κύριος καὶ οὐκ ἀρέσει αὐτῷ καὶ ἀποστρέψει τὸν θυμὸν αὐτοῦ ἀπ' αὐτοῦ

text_en: Contend not with the wicked , nor seek to be like the ungodly.
text_la: Ne contendas cum pessimis, nec æmuleris impios :
text_pt: Não te indignes por causa dos malfeitores, nem tenhas inveja dos ímpios,
text_el: μὴ χαῖρε ἐπὶ κακοποιοῖς μηδὲ ζήλου ἁμαρτωλούς

text_en: For evil men have no hope of things to come, and the lamp of the wicked shall be put out.
text_la: quoniam non habent futurorum spem mali, et lucerna impiorum extinguetur.
text_pt: Porque o homem maligno não terá galardão, e a lâmpada dos ímpios se apagará.
text_el: οὐ γὰρ μὴ γένηται ἔκγονα πονηρῶν λαμπτὴρ δὲ ἀσεβῶν σβεσθήσεται

text_en: My son, fear the Lord , and the king: and have nothing to do with detractors.
text_la: Time Dominum, fili mi, et regem, et cum detractoribus non commiscearis :
text_pt: Teme ao Senhor, filho meu, e ao rei, e não te ponhas com os que buscam mudanças,
text_el: φοβοῦ τὸν θεόν υἱέ καὶ βασιλέα καὶ μηθετέρῳ αὐτῶν ἀπειθήσῃς

text_en: For their destruction shall rise suddenly: and who knows the ruin of both?
text_la: quoniam repente consurget perditio eorum, et ruinam utriusque quis novit?
text_pt: Porque de repente se levantará a sua destruição, e a ruína de ambos, quem o sabe?
text_el: ἐξαίφνης γὰρ τείσονται τοὺς ἀσεβεῖς τὰς δὲ τιμωρίας ἀμφοτέρων τίς γνώσεται

text_en: These things also to the wise: It is not good to have respect to persons in judgment.
text_la: Hæc quoque sapientibus. Cognoscere personam in judicio non est bonum.
text_pt: Também estes são provérbios dos sábios: Ter respeito a pessoas no julgamento não é bom.
text_el: ταῦτα δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν τοῖς σοφοῖς ἐπιγινώσκειν αἰδεῖσθαι πρόσωπον ἐν κρίσει οὐ καλόν

text_en: They that say to the wicked man : You are just : shall be cursed by the people, and the tribes shall abhor them.
text_la: Qui dicunt impio : Justus es : maledicent eis populi, et detestabuntur eos tribus.
text_pt: O que disser ao ímpio: Justo és, os povos o amaldiçoarão, as nações o detestarão.
text_el: ὁ εἰπὼν τὸν ἀσεβῆ δίκαιός ἐστιν ἐπικατάρατος λαοῖς ἔσται καὶ μισητὸς εἰς ἔθνη

text_en: They that rebuke him shall be praised: and a blessing shall come upon them.
text_la: Qui arguunt eum laudabuntur, et super ipsos veniet benedictio.
text_pt: Mas para os que o repreenderem haverá delícias, e sobre eles virá a bênção do bem.
text_el: οἱ δὲ ἐλέγχοντες βελτίους φανοῦνται ἐπ' αὐτοὺς δὲ ἥξει εὐλογία ἀγαθή

text_en: He shall kiss the lips, who answers right words.
text_la: Labia deosculabitur qui recta verba respondet.
text_pt: Beijados serão os lábios do que responde com palavras retas.
text_el: χείλη δὲ φιλήσουσιν ἀποκρινόμενα λόγους ἀγαθούς

text_en: Prepare your work without, and diligently till your ground: that afterward you may build your house.
text_la: Præpara foris opus tuum, et diligenter exerce agrum tuum, ut postea ædifices domum tuam.
text_pt: Prepara de fora a tua obra, e aparelha-a no campo, e então edifica a tua casa.
text_el: ἑτοίμαζε εἰς τὴν ἔξοδον τὰ ἔργα σου καὶ παρασκευάζου εἰς τὸν ἀγρὸν καὶ πορεύου κατόπισθέν μου καὶ ἀνοικοδομήσεις τὸν οἶκόν σου

text_en: Be not witness without cause against your neighbour: and deceive not any man with your lips.
text_la: Ne sis testis frustra contra proximum tuum, nec lactes quemquam labiis tuis.
text_pt: Não sejas testemunha sem causa contra o teu próximo; e não enganes com os teus lábios.
text_el: μὴ ἴσθι ψευδὴς μάρτυς ἐπὶ σὸν πολίτην μηδὲ πλατύνου σοῖς χείλεσιν

text_en: Say not: I will do to him as he has done to me: I will render to every one according to his work.
text_la: Ne dicas : Quomodo fecit mihi, sic faciam ei; reddam unicuique secundum opus suum.
text_pt: Não digas: Como ele me fez a mim, assim o farei eu a ele; pagarei a cada um segundo a sua obra.
text_el: μὴ εἴπῃς ὃν τρόπον ἐχρήσατό μοι χρήσομαι αὐτῷ τείσομαι δὲ αὐτὸν ἅ με ἠδίκησεν

text_en: I passed by the field of the slothful man , and by the vineyard of the foolish man :
text_la: Per agrum hominis pigri transivi, et per vineam viri stulti :
text_pt: Passei pelo campo do preguiçoso, e junto à vinha do homem falto de entendimento,
text_el: ὥσπερ γεώργιον ἀνὴρ ἄφρων καὶ ὥσπερ ἀμπελὼν ἄνθρωπος ἐνδεὴς φρενῶν

text_en: And behold it was all filled with nettles, and thorns had covered the face thereof, and the stone wall was broken down.
text_la: et ecce totum repleverant urticæ, et operuerant superficiem ejus spinæ, et maceria lapidum destructa erat.
text_pt: Eis que estava toda cheia de cardos, e a sua superfície coberta de urtiga, e o seu muro de pedras estava derrubado.
text_el: ἐὰν ἀφῇς αὐτόν χερσωθήσεται καὶ χορτομανήσει ὅλος καὶ γίνεται ἐκλελειμμένος οἱ δὲ φραγμοὶ τῶν λίθων αὐτοῦ κατασκάπτονται

text_en: Which when I had seen, I laid it up in my heart, and by the example I received instruction.
text_la: Quod cum vidissem, posui in corde meo, et exemplo didici disciplinam.
text_pt: O que eu tenho visto, o guardarei no coração, e vendo-o recebi instrução.
text_el: ὕστερον ἐγὼ μετενόησα ἐπέβλεψα τοῦ ἐκλέξασθαι παιδείαν

text_en: You will sleep a little, said I, you will slumber a little, you will fold your hands a little to rest.
text_la: Parum, inquam, dormies, modicum dormitabis; pauxillum manus conseres ut quiescas :
text_pt: Um pouco a dormir, um pouco a cochilar; outro pouco deitado de mãos cruzadas, para dormir,
text_el: ὀλίγον νυστάζω ὀλίγον δὲ καθυπνῶ ὀλίγον δὲ ἐναγκαλίζομαι χερσὶν στήθη

text_en: And poverty shall come to you as a runner, and beggary as an armed man .
text_la: et veniet tibi quasi cursor egestas, et mendicitas quasi vir armatus.
text_pt: Assim te sobrevirá a tua pobreza como um vagabundo, e a tua necessidade como um homem armado.
text_el: ἐὰν δὲ τοῦτο ποιῇς ἥξει προπορευομένη ἡ πενία σου καὶ ἡ ἔνδειά σου ὥσπερ ἀγαθὸς δρομεύς

text_en: These are also parables of Solomon , which the men of Ezechias , king of Juda , copied out.
text_la: Hæ quoque parabolæ Salomonis, quas transtulerunt viri Ezechiæ regis Juda.
text_pt: Também estes são provérbios de Salomão, os quais transcreveram os homens de Ezequias, rei de Judá.
text_el: αὗται αἱ παιδεῖαι σαλωμῶντος αἱ ἀδιάκριτοι ἃς ἐξεγράψαντο οἱ φίλοι Εζεκιου τοῦ βασιλέως τῆς Ιουδαίας

text_en: It is the glory of God to conceal the word, and the glory of kings to search out the speech.
text_la: Gloria Dei est celare verbum, et gloria regum investigare sermonem.
text_pt: A glória de Deus está nas coisas encobertas; mas a honra dos reis, está em descobri-las.
text_el: δόξα θεοῦ κρύπτει λόγον δόξα δὲ βασιλέως τιμᾷ πράγματα

text_en: The heaven above and the earth beneath, and the heart of kings is unsearchable.
text_la: Cælum sursum, et terra deorsum, et cor regum inscrutabile.
text_pt: Os céus, pela altura, e a terra, pela profundidade, assim o coração dos reis é insondável.
text_el: οὐρανὸς ὑψηλός γῆ δὲ βαθεῖα καρδία δὲ βασιλέως ἀνεξέλεγκτος

text_en: Take away the rust from silver, and there shall come forth a most pure vessel:
text_la: Aufer rubiginem de argento, et egredietur vas purissimum.
text_pt: Tira da prata as escórias, e sairá vaso para o fundidor;
text_el: τύπτε ἀδόκιμον ἀργύριον καὶ καθαρισθήσεται καθαρὸν ἅπαν

text_en: Take away wickedness from the face of the king, and his throne shall be established with justice .
text_la: Aufer impietatem de vultu regis, et firmabitur justitia thronus ejus.
text_pt: Tira o ímpio da presença do rei, e o seu trono se firmará na justiça.
text_el: κτεῖνε ἀσεβεῖς ἐκ προσώπου βασιλέως καὶ κατορθώσει ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ ὁ θρόνος αὐτοῦ

text_en: Appear not glorious before the king, and stand not in the place of great men .
text_la: Ne gloriosus appareas coram rege, et in loco magnorum ne steteris.
text_pt: Não te glories na presença do rei, nem te ponhas no lugar dos grandes;
text_el: μὴ ἀλαζονεύου ἐνώπιον βασιλέως μηδὲ ἐν τόποις δυναστῶν ὑφίστασο

text_en: For it is better that it should be said to you: Come up hither; than that you should be humbled before the prince.
text_la: Melius est enim ut dicatur tibi : Ascende huc, quam ut humilieris coram principe.
text_pt: Porque melhor é que te digam: Sobe aqui; do que seres humilhado diante do príncipe que os teus olhos já viram.
text_el: κρεῖσσον γάρ σοι τὸ ῥηθῆναι ἀνάβαινε πρός με ἢ ταπεινῶσαί σε ἐν προσώπῳ δυνάστου ἃ εἶδον οἱ ὀφθαλμοί σου λέγε

text_en: The things which your eyes have seen, utter not hastily in a quarrel: lest afterward you may not be able to make amends, when you have dishonoured your friend.
text_la: Quæ viderunt oculi tui ne proferas in jurgio cito, ne postea emendare non possis, cum dehonestaveris amicum tuum.
text_pt: Não te precipites em litigar, para que depois, ao fim, fiques sem ação, quando teu próximo te puser em apuros.
text_el: μὴ πρόσπιπτε εἰς μάχην ταχέως ἵνα μὴ μεταμεληθῇς ἐπ' ἐσχάτων ἡνίκα ἄν σε ὀνειδίσῃ ὁ σὸς φίλος

text_en: Treat your cause with your friend, and discover not the secret to a stranger:
text_la: Causam tuam tracta cum amico tuo, et secretum extraneo ne reveles :
text_pt: Pleiteia a tua causa com o teu próximo, e não reveles o segredo a outrem,
text_el: ἀναχώρει εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω μὴ καταφρόνει

text_en: Lest he insult over you, when he has heard it, and cease not to upbraid you. Grace and friendship deliver a man : keep these for yourself, lest you fall under reproach.
text_la: ne forte insultet tibi cum audierit, et exprobrare non cesset. Gratia et amicitia liberant : quas tibi serva, ne exprobrabilis fias.
text_pt: Para que não te desonre o que o ouvir, e a tua infâmia não se aparte de ti.
text_el: μή σε ὀνειδίσῃ μὲν ὁ φίλος ἡ δὲ μάχη σου καὶ ἡ ἔχθρα οὐκ ἀπέσται ἀλλ' ἔσται σοι ἴση θανάτῳ

text_en: To speak a word in due time, is like apples of gold on beds of silver.
text_la: Mala aurea in lectis argenteis, qui loquitur verbum in tempore suo.
text_pt: Como maçãs de ouro em salvas de prata, assim é a palavra dita a seu tempo.
text_el: μῆλον χρυσοῦν ἐν ὁρμίσκῳ σαρδίου οὕτως εἰπεῖν λόγον

text_en: As an earring of gold and a bright pearl, so is he that reproves the wise, and the obedient ear.
text_la: Inauris aurea, et margaritum fulgens, qui arguit sapientem et aurem obedientem.
text_pt: Como pendentes de ouro e gargantilhas de ouro fino, assim é o sábio repreensor para o ouvido atento.
text_el: εἰς ἐνώτιον χρυσοῦν σάρδιον πολυτελὲς δέδεται λόγος σοφὸς εἰς εὐήκοον οὖς

text_en: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to him that sent him, for he refreshes his soul .
text_la: Sicut frigus nivis in die messis, ita legatus fidelis ei qui misit eum : animam ipsius requiescere facit.
text_pt: Como o frio da neve no tempo da sega, assim é o mensageiro fiel para com os que o enviam; porque refresca a alma dos seus senhores.
text_el: ὥσπερ ἔξοδος χιόνος ἐν ἀμήτῳ κατὰ καῦμα ὠφελεῖ οὕτως ἄγγελος πιστὸς τοὺς ἀποστείλαντας αὐτόν ψυχὰς γὰρ τῶν αὐτῷ χρωμένων ὠφελεῖ

text_en: As clouds, and wind, when no rain follows, so is the man that boasts, and does not fulfil his promises.
text_la: Nubes, et ventus, et pluviæ non sequentes, vir gloriosus et promissa non complens.
text_pt: Como nuvens e ventos que não trazem chuva, assim é o homem que se gaba falsamente de dádivas.
text_el: ὥσπερ ἄνεμοι καὶ νέφη καὶ ὑετοὶ ἐπιφανέστατοι οὕτως οἱ καυχώμενοι ἐπὶ δόσει ψευδεῖ

text_en: By patience a prince shall be appeased, and a soft tongue shall break hardness.
text_la: Patientia lenietur princeps, et lingua mollis confringet duritiam.
text_pt: Pela longanimidade se persuade o príncipe, e a língua branda amolece até os ossos.
text_el: ἐν μακροθυμίᾳ εὐοδία βασιλεῦσιν γλῶσσα δὲ μαλακὴ συντρίβει ὀστᾶ

text_en: You have found honey, eat what is sufficient for you, lest being glutted therewith you vomit it up.
text_la: Mel invenisti : comede quod sufficit tibi, ne forte satiatus evomas illud.
text_pt: Achaste mel? come só o que te basta; para que porventura não te fartes dele, e o venhas a vomitar.
text_el: μέλι εὑρὼν φάγε τὸ ἱκανόν μήποτε πλησθεὶς ἐξεμέσῃς

text_en: Withdraw your foot from the house of your neighbour, lest having his fill he hate you.
text_la: Subtrahe pedem tuum de domo proximi tui, nequando satiatus oderit te.
text_pt: Não ponhas muito os pés na casa do teu próximo; para que se não enfade de ti, e passe a te odiar.
text_el: σπάνιον εἴσαγε σὸν πόδα πρὸς τὸν σεαυτοῦ φίλον μήποτε πλησθείς σου μισήσῃ σε

text_en: A man that bears false witness against his neighbour, is like a dart and a sword and a sharp arrow.
text_la: Jaculum, et gladius, et sagitta acuta, homo qui loquitur contra proximum suum falsum testimonium.
text_pt: Martelo, espada e flecha aguda é o homem que profere falso testemunho contra o seu próximo.
text_el: ῥόπαλον καὶ μάχαιρα καὶ τόξευμα ἀκιδωτόν οὕτως καὶ ἀνὴρ ὁ καταμαρτυρῶν τοῦ φίλου αὐτοῦ μαρτυρίαν ψευδῆ

text_en: To trust in an unfaithful man in the time of trouble, is like a rotten tooth, and weary foot,
text_la: Dens putridus, et pes lassus, qui sperat super infideli in die angustiæ,
text_pt: Como dente quebrado, e pé desconjuntado, é a confiança no desleal, no tempo da angústia.
text_el: ὀδοὺς κακοῦ καὶ ποὺς παρανόμου ὀλεῖται ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κακῇ

text_en: and one that loosens his garment in cold weather. As vinegar upon nitre, so is he that sings songs to a very evil heart. As a moth does by a garment, and a worm by the wood: so the sadness of a man consumes the heart.
text_la: et amittit pallium in die frigoris. Acetum in nitro, qui cantat carmina cordi pessimo. Sicut tinea vestimento, et vermis ligno, ita tristitia viri nocet cordi.
text_pt: O que canta canções para o coração aflito é como aquele que despe a roupa num dia de frio, ou como o vinagre sobre salitre.
text_el: ὥσπερ ὄξος ἕλκει ἀσύμφορον οὕτως προσπεσὸν πάθος ἐν σώματι καρδίαν λυπεῖ

text_en: If your enemy be hungry, give him to eat: if he thirst, give him water to drink:
text_la: Si esurierit inimicus tuus, ciba illum; si sitierit, da ei aquam bibere :
text_pt: Se o teu inimigo tiver fome, dá-lhe pão para comer; e se tiver sede, dá-lhe água para beber;
text_el: ἐὰν πεινᾷ ὁ ἐχθρός σου τρέφε αὐτόν ἐὰν διψᾷ πότιζε αὐτόν

text_en: For you shall heap hot coals upon his head, and the Lord will reward you.
text_la: prunas enim congregabis super caput ejus, et Dominus reddet tibi.
text_pt: Porque assim lhe amontoarás brasas sobre a cabeça; e o Senhor to retribuirá.
text_el: τοῦτο γὰρ ποιῶν ἄνθρακας πυρὸς σωρεύσεις ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ ὁ δὲ κύριος ἀνταποδώσει σοι ἀγαθά

text_en: The north wind drives away rain, as does a sad countenance a backbiting tongue.
text_la: Ventus aquilo dissipat pluvias, et facies tristis linguam detrahentem.
text_pt: O vento norte afugenta a chuva, e a face irada, a língua fingida.
text_el: ἄνεμος βορέας ἐξεγείρει νέφη πρόσωπον δὲ ἀναιδὲς γλῶσσαν ἐρεθίζει

text_en: It is better to sit in a corner of the housetop: than with a brawling woman , and in a common house.
text_la: Melius est sedere in angulo domatis quam cum muliere litigiosa et in domo communi.
text_pt: Melhor é morar só num canto de telhado do que com a mulher briguenta numa casa ampla.
text_el: κρεῖττον οἰκεῖν ἐπὶ γωνίας δώματος ἢ μετὰ γυναικὸς λοιδόρου ἐν οἰκίᾳ κοινῇ

text_en: As cold water to a thirsty soul , so are good tidings from a far country.
text_la: Aqua frigida animæ sitienti, et nuntius bonus de terra longinqua.
text_pt: Como água fresca para a alma cansada, tais são as boas novas vindas da terra distante.
text_el: ὥσπερ ὕδωρ ψυχρὸν ψυχῇ διψώσῃ προσηνές οὕτως ἀγγελία ἀγαθὴ ἐκ γῆς μακρόθεν

text_en: A just man falling down before the wicked , is as a fountain troubled with the foot and a corrupted spring.
text_la: Fons turbatus pede et vena corrupta, justus cadens coram impio.
text_pt: Como fonte turvada, e manancial poluído, assim é o justo que cede diante do ímpio.
text_el: ὥσπερ εἴ τις πηγὴν φράσσοι καὶ ὕδατος ἔξοδον λυμαίνοιτο οὕτως ἄκοσμον δίκαιον πεπτωκέναι ἐνώπιον ἀσεβοῦς

text_en: As it is not good for a man to eat much honey, so he that is a searcher of majesty shall be overwhelmed by glory .
text_la: Sicut qui mel multum comedit non est ei bonum, sic qui scrutator est majestatis opprimetur a gloria.
text_pt: Comer mel demais não é bom; assim, a busca da própria glória não é glória.
text_el: ἐσθίειν μέλι πολὺ οὐ καλόν τιμᾶν δὲ χρὴ λόγους ἐνδόξους

text_en: As a city that lies open and is not compassed with walls, so is a man that cannot refrain his own spirit in speaking.
text_la: Sicut urbs patens et absque murorum ambitu, ita vir qui non potest in loquendo cohibere spiritum suum.
text_pt: Como a cidade derrubada, sem muro, assim é o homem que não pode conter o seu espírito.
text_el: ὥσπερ πόλις τὰ τείχη καταβεβλημένη καὶ ἀτείχιστος οὕτως ἀνὴρ ὃς οὐ μετὰ βουλῆς τι πράσσει

text_en: As snow in summer, and rain in harvest, so glory is not seemly for a fool.
text_la: Quomodo nix in æstate, et pluviæ in messe, sic indecens est stulto gloria.
text_pt: Como a neve no verão, e como a chuva na sega, assim não fica bem para o tolo a honra.
text_el: ὥσπερ δρόσος ἐν ἀμήτῳ καὶ ὥσπερ ὑετὸς ἐν θέρει οὕτως οὐκ ἔστιν ἄφρονι τιμή

text_en: As a bird flying to other places, and a sparrow going here or there: so a curse uttered without cause shall come upon a man .
text_la: Sicut avis ad alia transvolans, et passer quolibet vadens, sic maledictum frustra prolatum in quempiam superveniet.
text_pt: Como ao pássaro o vaguear, como à andorinha o voar, assim a maldição sem causa não virá.
text_el: ὥσπερ ὄρνεα πέταται καὶ στρουθοί οὕτως ἀρὰ ματαία οὐκ ἐπελεύσεται οὐδενί

text_en: A whip for a horse, and a snaffle for an ass, and a rod for the back of fools.
text_la: Flagellum equo, et camus asino, et virga in dorso imprudentium.
text_pt: O açoite é para o cavalo, o freio é para o jumento, e a vara é para as costas dos tolos.
text_el: ὥσπερ μάστιξ ἵππῳ καὶ κέντρον ὄνῳ οὕτως ῥάβδος ἔθνει παρανόμῳ

text_en: Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest you be made like him.
text_la: Ne respondeas stulto juxta stultitiam suam, ne efficiaris ei similis.
text_pt: Não respondas ao tolo segundo a sua estultícia; para que também não te faças semelhante a ele.
text_el: μὴ ἀποκρίνου ἄφρονι πρὸς τὴν ἐκείνου ἀφροσύνην ἵνα μὴ ὅμοιος γένῃ αὐτῷ

text_en: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he imagine himself to be wise.
text_la: Responde stulto juxta stultitiam suam, ne sibi sapiens esse videatur.
text_pt: Responde ao tolo segundo a sua estultícia, para que não seja sábio aos seus próprios olhos.
text_el: ἀλλὰ ἀποκρίνου ἄφρονι κατὰ τὴν ἀφροσύνην αὐτοῦ ἵνα μὴ φαίνηται σοφὸς παρ' ἑαυτῷ

text_en: He that sends words by a foolish messenger, is lame of feet and drinks iniquity .
text_la: Claudus pedibus, et iniquitatem bibens, qui mittit verba per nuntium stultum.
text_pt: Os pés corta, e o dano sorve, aquele que manda mensagem pela mão dum tolo.
text_el: ἐκ τῶν ἑαυτοῦ ποδῶν ὄνειδος πίεται ὁ ἀποστείλας δι' ἀγγέλου ἄφρονος λόγον

text_en: As a lame man has fair legs in vain: so a parable is unseemly in the mouth of fools.
text_la: Quomodo pulchras frustra habet claudus tibias, sic indecens est in ore stultorum parabola.
text_pt: Como as pernas do coxo, que pendem flácidas, assim é o provérbio na boca dos tolos.
text_el: ἀφελοῦ πορείαν σκελῶν καὶ παροιμίαν ἐκ στόματος ἀφρόνων

text_en: As he that casts a stone into the heap of Mercury: so is he that gives honour to a fool.
text_la: Sicut qui mittit lapidem in acervum Mercurii, ita qui tribuit insipienti honorem.
text_pt: Como o que arma a funda com pedra preciosa, assim é aquele que concede honra ao tolo.
text_el: ὃς ἀποδεσμεύει λίθον ἐν σφενδόνῃ ὅμοιός ἐστιν τῷ διδόντι ἄφρονι δόξαν

text_en: As if a thorn should grow in the hand of a drunkard: so is a parable in the mouth of fools.
text_la: Quomodo si spina nascatur in manu temulenti, sic parabola in ore stultorum.
text_pt: Como o espinho que entra na mão do bêbado, assim é o provérbio na boca dos tolos.
text_el: ἄκανθαι φύονται ἐν χειρὶ τοῦ μεθύσου δουλεία δὲ ἐν χειρὶ τῶν ἀφρόνων

text_en: Judgment determines causes: and he that puts a fool to silence, appeases anger .
text_la: Judicium determinat causas, et qui imponit stulto silentium iras mitigat.
text_pt: O Poderoso, que formou todas as coisas, paga ao tolo, e recompensa ao transgressor.
text_el: πολλὰ χειμάζεται πᾶσα σὰρξ ἀφρόνων συντρίβεται γὰρ ἡ ἔκστασις αὐτῶν

text_en: As a dog that returns to his vomit, so is the fool that repeats his folly.
text_la: Sicut canis qui revertitur ad vomitum suum, sic imprudens qui iterat stultitiam suam.
text_pt: Como o cão torna ao seu vômito, assim o tolo repete a sua estultícia.
text_el: ὥσπερ κύων ὅταν ἐπέλθῃ ἐπὶ τὸν ἑαυτοῦ ἔμετον καὶ μισητὸς γένηται οὕτως ἄφρων τῇ ἑαυτοῦ κακίᾳ ἀναστρέψας ἐπὶ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἁμαρτίαν

text_en: Have you seen a man wise in his own conceit? There shall be more hope of a fool than of him.
text_la: Vidisti hominem sapientem sibi videri? magis illo spem habebit insipiens.
text_pt: Tens visto o homem que é sábio a seus próprios olhos? Pode-se esperar mais do tolo do que dele.
text_el: εἶδον ἄνδρα δόξαντα παρ' ἑαυτῷ σοφὸν εἶναι ἐλπίδα μέντοι ἔσχεν μᾶλλον ἄφρων αὐτοῦ

text_en: The slothful man says: There is a lion in the way, and a lioness in the roads.
text_la: Dicit piger : Leo est in via, et leæna in itineribus.
text_pt: Diz o preguiçoso: Um leão está no caminho; um leão está nas ruas.
text_el: λέγει ὀκνηρὸς ἀποστελλόμενος εἰς ὁδόν λέων ἐν ταῖς ὁδοῖς

text_en: As the door turns upon its hinges, so does the slothful upon his bed.
text_la: Sicut ostium vertitur in cardine suo, ita piger in lectulo suo.
text_pt: Como a porta gira nos seus gonzos, assim o preguiçoso na sua cama.
text_el: ὥσπερ θύρα στρέφεται ἐπὶ τοῦ στρόφιγγος οὕτως ὀκνηρὸς ἐπὶ τῆς κλίνης αὐτοῦ

text_en: The slothful hides his hand under his armpit, and it grieves him to turn it to his mouth.
text_la: Abscondit piger manum sub ascella sua, et laborat si ad os suum eam converterit.
text_pt: O preguiçoso esconde a sua mão ao seio; e cansa-se até de torná-la à sua boca.
text_el: κρύψας ὀκνηρὸς τὴν χεῖρα ἐν τῷ κόλπῳ αὐτοῦ οὐ δυνήσεται ἐπενεγκεῖν ἐπὶ τὸ στόμα

text_en: The sluggard is wiser in his own conceit, than seven men that speak sentences.
text_la: Sapientior sibi piger videtur septem viris loquentibus sententias.
text_pt: Mais sábio é o preguiçoso a seus próprios olhos do que sete homens que respondem bem.
text_el: σοφώτερος ἑαυτῷ ὀκνηρὸς φαίνεται τοῦ ἐν πλησμονῇ ἀποκομίζοντος ἀγγελίαν

text_en: As he that takes a dog by the ears, so is he that passes by in anger , and meddles with another man's quarrel.
text_la: Sicut qui apprehendit auribus canem, sic qui transit impatiens et commiscetur rixæ alterius.
text_pt: O que, passando, se põe em questão alheia, é como aquele que pega um cão pelas orelhas.
text_el: ὥσπερ ὁ κρατῶν κέρκου κυνός οὕτως ὁ προεστὼς ἀλλοτρίας κρίσεως

text_en: As he is guilty that shoots arrows, and lances unto death.
text_la: Sicut noxius est qui mittit sagittas et lanceas in mortem,
text_pt: Como o louco que solta faíscas, flechas, e mortandades,
text_el: ὥσπερ οἱ ἰώμενοι προβάλλουσιν λόγους εἰς ἀνθρώπους ὁ δὲ ἀπαντήσας τῷ λόγῳ πρῶτος ὑποσκελισθήσεται

text_en: So is the man that hurts his friend deceitfully: and when he is taken, says: I did it in jest.
text_la: ita vir fraudulenter nocet amico suo, et cum fuerit deprehensus dicit : Ludens feci.
text_pt: Assim é o homem que engana o seu próximo, e diz: Fiz isso por brincadeira.
text_el: οὕτως πάντες οἱ ἐνεδρεύοντες τοὺς ἑαυτῶν φίλους ὅταν δὲ φωραθῶσιν λέγουσιν ὅτι παίζων ἔπραξα

text_en: When the wood fails, the fire shall go out: and when the talebearer is taken away, contentions shall cease.
text_la: Cum defecerint ligna extinguetur ignis, et susurrone subtracto, jurgia conquiescent.
text_pt: Sem lenha, o fogo se apagará; e não havendo intrigante, cessará a contenda.
text_el: ἐν πολλοῖς ξύλοις θάλλει πῦρ ὅπου δὲ οὐκ ἔστιν δίθυμος ἡσυχάζει μάχη

text_en: As coals are to burning coals, and wood to fire, so an angry man stirs up strife.
text_la: Sicut carbones ad prunas, et ligna ad ignem, sic homo iracundus suscitat rixas.
text_pt: Como o carvão para as brasas, e a lenha para o fogo, assim é o homem contencioso para acender rixas.
text_el: ἐσχάρα ἄνθραξιν καὶ ξύλα πυρί ἀνὴρ δὲ λοίδορος εἰς ταραχὴν μάχης

text_en: The words of a talebearer are as it were simple, but they reach to the innermost parts of the belly.
text_la: Verba susurronis quasi simplicia, et ipsa perveniunt ad intima ventris.
text_pt: As palavras do intrigante são como doces bocados; elas descem ao mais íntimo do ventre.
text_el: λόγοι κερκώπων μαλακοί οὗτοι δὲ τύπτουσιν εἰς ταμίεια σπλάγχνων

text_en: Swelling lips joined with a corrupt heart, are like an earthen vessel adorned with silver dross.
text_la: Quomodo si argento sordido ornare velis vas fictile, sic labia tumentia cum pessimo corde sociata.
text_pt: Como o caco de vaso coberto de escórias de prata, assim são os lábios ardentes com o coração maligno.
text_el: ἀργύριον διδόμενον μετὰ δόλου ὥσπερ ὄστρακον ἡγητέον χείλη λεῖα καρδίαν καλύπτει λυπηράν

text_en: An enemy is known by his lips, when in his heart he entertains deceit .
text_la: Labiis suis intelligitur inimicus, cum in corde tractaverit dolos.
text_pt: Aquele que odeia dissimula com seus lábios, mas no seu íntimo encobre o engano;
text_el: χείλεσιν πάντα ἐπινεύει ἀποκλαιόμενος ἐχθρός ἐν δὲ τῇ καρδίᾳ τεκταίνεται δόλους

text_en: When he shall speak low, trust him not: because there are seven mischiefs in his heart.
text_la: Quando submiserit vocem suam, ne credideris ei, quoniam septem nequitiæ sunt in corde illius.
text_pt: Quando te suplicar com voz suave não te fies nele, porque abriga sete abominações no seu coração,
text_el: ἐάν σου δέηται ὁ ἐχθρὸς μεγάλῃ τῇ φωνῇ μὴ πεισθῇς ἑπτὰ γάρ εἰσιν πονηρίαι ἐν τῇ ψυχῇ αὐτοῦ

text_en: He that covers hatred deceitfully, his malice shall be laid open in the public assembly.
text_la: Qui operit odium fraudulenter, revelabitur malitia ejus in consilio.
text_pt: Cujo ódio se encobre com engano, a sua maldade será exposta perante a congregação.
text_el: ὁ κρύπτων ἔχθραν συνίστησιν δόλον ἐκκαλύπτει δὲ τὰς ἑαυτοῦ ἁμαρτίας εὔγνωστος ἐν συνεδρίοις

text_en: He that digs a pit, shall fall into it: and he that rolls a stone, it shall return to him.
text_la: Qui fodit foveam incidet in eam, et qui volvit lapidem revertetur ad eum.
text_pt: O que cava uma cova cairá nela; e o que revolve a pedra, esta voltará sobre ele.
text_el: ὁ ὀρύσσων βόθρον τῷ πλησίον ἐμπεσεῖται εἰς αὐτόν ὁ δὲ κυλίων λίθον ἐφ' ἑαυτὸν κυλίει

text_en: A deceitful tongue loves not truth : and a slippery mouth works ruin.
text_la: Lingua fallax non amat veritatem, et os lubricum operatur ruinas.
text_pt: A língua falsa odeia aos que ela fere, e a boca lisonjeira provoca a ruína.
text_el: γλῶσσα ψευδὴς μισεῖ ἀλήθειαν στόμα δὲ ἄστεγον ποιεῖ ἀκαταστασίας

text_en: Boast not for tomorrow, for you know not what the day to come may bring forth.
text_la: Ne glorieris in crastinum, ignorans quid superventura pariat dies.
text_pt: Não presumas do dia de amanhã, porque não sabes o que ele trará.
text_el: μὴ καυχῶ τὰ εἰς αὔριον οὐ γὰρ γινώσκεις τί τέξεται ἡ ἐπιοῦσα

text_en: Let another praise you, and not your own mouth: a stranger, and not your own lips.
text_la: Laudet te alienus, et non os tuum; extraneus, et non labia tua.
text_pt: Que um outro te louve, e não a tua própria boca; o estranho, e não os teus lábios.
text_el: ἐγκωμιαζέτω σε ὁ πέλας καὶ μὴ τὸ σὸν στόμα ἀλλότριος καὶ μὴ τὰ σὰ χείλη

text_en: A stone is heavy, and sand weighty: but the anger of a fool is heavier than them both.
text_la: Grave est saxum, et onerosa arena, sed ira stulti utroque gravior.
text_pt: A pedra é pesada, e a areia é espessa; porém a ira do insensato é mais pesada que ambas.
text_el: βαρὺ λίθος καὶ δυσβάστακτον ἄμμος ὀργὴ δὲ ἄφρονος βαρυτέρα ἀμφοτέρων

text_en: Anger has no mercy: nor fury, when it breaks forth: and who can bear the violence of one provoked?
text_la: Ira non habet misericordiam nec erumpens furor, et impetum concitati ferre quis poterit?
text_pt: O furor é cruel e a ira impetuosa, mas quem poderá enfrentar a inveja?
text_el: ἀνελεήμων θυμὸς καὶ ὀξεῖα ὀργή ἀλλ' οὐδένα ὑφίσταται ζῆλος

text_en: Open rebuke is better than hidden love .
text_la: Melior est manifesta correptio quam amor absconditus.
text_pt: Melhor é a repreensão franca do que o amor encoberto.
text_el: κρείσσους ἔλεγχοι ἀποκεκαλυμμένοι κρυπτομένης φιλίας

text_en: Better are the wounds of a friend, than the deceitful kisses of an enemy.
text_la: Meliora sunt vulnera diligentis quam fraudulenta oscula odientis.
text_pt: Leais são as feridas feitas pelo amigo, mas os beijos do inimigo são enganosos.
text_el: ἀξιοπιστότερά ἐστιν τραύματα φίλου ἢ ἑκούσια φιλήματα ἐχθροῦ

text_en: A soul that is full shall tread upon the honeycomb: and a soul that is hungry shall take even bitter for sweet.
text_la: Anima saturata calcabit favum, et anima esuriens etiam amarum pro dulci sumet.
text_pt: A alma farta pisa o favo de mel, mas para a alma faminta todo amargo é doce.
text_el: ψυχὴ ἐν πλησμονῇ οὖσα κηρίοις ἐμπαίζει ψυχῇ δὲ ἐνδεεῖ καὶ τὰ πικρὰ γλυκεῖα φαίνεται

text_en: As a bird that wanders from her nest, so is a man that leaves his place.
text_la: Sicut avis transmigrans de nido suo, sic vir qui derelinquit locum suum.
text_pt: Qual a ave que vagueia longe do seu ninho, tal é o homem que anda vagueando longe da sua morada.
text_el: ὥσπερ ὅταν ὄρνεον καταπετασθῇ ἐκ τῆς ἰδίας νοσσιᾶς οὕτως ἄνθρωπος δουλοῦται ὅταν ἀποξενωθῇ ἐκ τῶν ἰδίων τόπων

text_en: Ointment and perfumes rejoice the heart: and the good counsels of a friend are sweet to the soul .
text_la: Unguento et variis odoribus delectatur cor, et bonis amici consiliis anima dulcoratur.
text_pt: O óleo e o perfume alegram o coração; assim o faz a doçura do amigo pelo conselho cordial.
text_el: μύροις καὶ οἴνοις καὶ θυμιάμασιν τέρπεται καρδία καταρρήγνυται δὲ ὑπὸ συμπτωμάτων ψυχή

text_en: Your own friend, and your father's friend, forsake not: and go not into your brother's house in the day of your affliction. Better is a neighbour that is near than a brother afar off.
text_la: Amicum tuum et amicum patris tui ne dimiseris, et domum fratris tui ne ingrediaris in die afflictionis tuæ. Melior est vicinus juxta quam frater procul.
text_pt: Não deixes o teu amigo, nem o amigo de teu pai; nem entres na casa de teu irmão no dia da tua adversidade; melhor é o vizinho perto do que o irmão longe.
text_el: φίλον σὸν ἢ φίλον πατρῷον μὴ ἐγκαταλίπῃς εἰς δὲ τὸν οἶκον τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου μὴ εἰσέλθῃς ἀτυχῶν κρείσσων φίλος ἐγγὺς ἢ ἀδελφὸς μακρὰν οἰκῶν

text_en: Study wisdom, my son, and make my heart joyful, that you may give an answer to him that reproaches.
text_la: Stude sapientiæ, fili mi, et lætifica cor meum, ut possis exprobranti respondere sermonem.
text_pt: Sê sábio, filho meu, e alegra o meu coração, para que tenha alguma coisa que responder àquele que me desprezar.
text_el: σοφὸς γίνου υἱέ ἵνα εὐφραίνηταί μου ἡ καρδία καὶ ἀπόστρεψον ἀπὸ σοῦ ἐπονειδίστους λόγους

text_en: The prudent man seeing evil hides himself: little ones passing on have suffered losses.
text_la: Astutus videns malum, absconditus est : parvuli transeuntes sustinuerunt dispendia.
text_pt: O avisado vê o mal e esconde-se; mas os simples passam e sofrem a pena.
text_el: πανοῦργος κακῶν ἐπερχομένων ἀπεκρύβη ἄφρονες δὲ ἐπελθόντες ζημίαν τείσουσιν

text_en: Take away his garment that has been surety for a stranger: and take from him a pledge for strangers.
text_la: Tolle vestimentum ejus qui spopondit pro extraneo, et pro alienis aufer ei pignus.
text_pt: Quando alguém fica por fiador do estranho, toma-lhe até a sua roupa, e por penhor àquele que se obriga pela mulher estranha.
text_el: ἀφελοῦ τὸ ἱμάτιον αὐτοῦ παρῆλθεν γάρ ὑβριστὴς ὅστις τὰ ἀλλότρια λυμαίνεται

text_en: He that blesses his neighbour with a loud voice, rising in the night, shall be like to him that curses .
text_la: Qui benedicit proximo suo voce grandi, de nocte consurgens maledicenti similis erit.
text_pt: O que, pela manhã de madrugada, abençoa o seu amigo em alta voz, lho será imputado por maldição.
text_el: ὃς ἂν εὐλογῇ φίλον τὸ πρωὶ μεγάλῃ τῇ φωνῇ καταρωμένου οὐδὲν διαφέρειν δόξει

text_en: Roofs dropping through in a cold day, and a contentious woman are alike.
text_la: Tecta perstillantia in die frigoris et litigiosa mulier comparantur.
text_pt: O gotejar contínuo em dia de grande chuva, e a mulher contenciosa, uma e outra são semelhantes;
text_el: σταγόνες ἐκβάλλουσιν ἄνθρωπον ἐν ἡμέρᾳ χειμερινῇ ἐκ τοῦ οἴκου αὐτοῦ ὡσαύτως καὶ γυνὴ λοίδορος ἐκ τοῦ ἰδίου οἴκου

text_en: He that retains her, is as he that would hold the wind, and shall call the oil of his right hand.
text_la: Qui retinet eam quasi qui ventum teneat, et oleum dexteræ suæ vocabit.
text_pt: Tentar moderá-la será como deter o vento, ou como conter o óleo dentro da sua mão direita.
text_el: βορέας σκληρὸς ἄνεμος ὀνόματι δὲ ἐπιδέξιος καλεῖται

text_en: Iron sharpens iron, so a man sharpens the countenance of his friend.
text_la: Ferrum ferro exacuitur, et homo exacuit faciem amici sui.
text_pt: Como o ferro com ferro se aguça, assim o homem afia o rosto do seu amigo.
text_el: σίδηρος σίδηρον ὀξύνει ἀνὴρ δὲ παροξύνει πρόσωπον ἑταίρου

text_en: He that keeps the fig tree, shall eat the fruit thereof: and he that is the keeper of his master, shall be glorified .
text_la: Qui servat ficum comedet fructus ejus, et qui custos est domini sui glorificabitur.
text_pt: O que cuida da figueira comerá do seu fruto; e o que atenta para o seu senhor será honrado.
text_el: ὃς φυτεύει συκῆν φάγεται τοὺς καρποὺς αὐτῆς ὃς δὲ φυλάσσει τὸν ἑαυτοῦ κύριον τιμηθήσεται

text_en: As the faces of them that look therein, shine in the water, so the hearts of men are laid open to the wise.
text_la: Quomodo in aquis resplendent vultus prospicientium, sic corda hominum manifesta sunt prudentibus.
text_pt: Como na água o rosto corresponde ao rosto, assim o coração do homem ao homem.
text_el: ὥσπερ οὐχ ὅμοια πρόσωπα προσώποις οὕτως οὐδὲ αἱ καρδίαι τῶν ἀνθρώπων

text_en: Hell and destruction are never filled: so the eyes of men are never satisfied.
text_la: Infernus et perditio numquam implentur : similiter et oculi hominum insatiabiles.
text_pt: Como o inferno e a perdição nunca se fartam, assim os olhos do homem nunca se satisfazem.
text_el: ᾅδης καὶ ἀπώλεια οὐκ ἐμπίμπλανται ὡσαύτως καὶ οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἄπληστοι

text_en: As silver is tried in the fining-pot, and gold in the furnace: so a man is tried by the mouth of him that praises. The heart of the wicked seeks after evils , but the righteous heart seeks after knowledge .
text_la: Quomodo probatur in conflatorio argentum et in fornace aurum, sic probatur homo ore laudantis. Cor iniqui inquirit mala, cor autem rectum inquirit scientiam.
text_pt: Como o crisol é para a prata, e o forno para o ouro, assim o homem é provado pelos louvores.
text_el: δοκίμιον ἀργύρῳ καὶ χρυσῷ πύρωσις ἀνὴρ δὲ δοκιμάζεται διὰ στόματος ἐγκωμιαζόντων αὐτόν

text_en: Though you should bray a fool in the mortar, as when a pestle strikes upon sodden barley, his folly would not be taken from him.
text_la: Si contuderis stultum in pila quasi ptisanas feriente desuper pilo, non auferetur ab eo stultitia ejus.
text_pt: Ainda que repreendas o tolo como quem bate o trigo com a mão de gral entre grãos pilados, não se apartará dele a sua estultícia.
text_el: ἐὰν μαστιγοῖς ἄφρονα ἐν μέσῳ συνεδρίου ἀτιμάζων οὐ μὴ περιέλῃς τὴν ἀφροσύνην αὐτοῦ

text_en: Be diligent to know the countenance of your cattle, and consider your own flocks:
text_la: Diligenter agnosce vultum pecoris tui, tuosque greges considera :
text_pt: Procura conhecer o estado das tuas ovelhas; põe o teu coração sobre os teus rebanhos,
text_el: γνωστῶς ἐπιγνώσῃ ψυχὰς ποιμνίου σου καὶ ἐπιστήσεις καρδίαν σου σαῖς ἀγέλαις

text_en: For you shall not always have power: but a crown shall be given to generation and generation .
text_la: non enim habebis jugiter potestatem, sed corona tribuetur in generationem et generationem.
text_pt: Porque o tesouro não dura para sempre; e durará a coroa de geração em geração?
text_el: ὅτι οὐ τὸν αἰῶνα ἀνδρὶ κράτος καὶ ἰσχύς οὐδὲ παραδίδωσιν ἐκ γενεᾶς εἰς γενεάν

text_en: The meadows are open, and the green herbs have appeared, and the hay is gathered out of the mountains.
text_la: Aperta sunt prata, et apparuerunt herbæ virentes, et collecta sunt fœna de montibus.
text_pt: Quando brotar a erva, e aparecerem os renovos, e se juntarem as ervas dos montes,
text_el: ἐπιμελοῦ τῶν ἐν τῷ πεδίῳ χλωρῶν καὶ κερεῖς πόαν καὶ σύναγε χόρτον ὀρεινόν

text_en: Lambs are for your clothing: and kids for the price of the field.
text_la: Agni ad vestimentum tuum, et hædi ad agri pretium.
text_pt: Então os cordeiros serão para te vestires, e os bodes para o preço do campo;
text_el: ἵνα ἔχῃς πρόβατα εἰς ἱματισμόν τίμα πεδίον ἵνα ὦσίν σοι ἄρνες

text_en: Let the milk of the goats be enough for your food, and for the necessities of your house, and for maintenance for your handmaids.
text_la: Sufficiat tibi lac caprarum in cibos tuos, et in necessaria domus tuæ, et ad victum ancillis tuis.
text_pt: E a abastança do leite das cabras para o teu sustento, para sustento da tua casa e para sustento das tuas servas.
text_el: υἱέ παρ' ἐμοῦ ἔχεις ῥήσεις ἰσχυρὰς εἰς τὴν ζωήν σου καὶ εἰς τὴν ζωὴν σῶν θεραπόντων

text_en: The wicked man flees, when no man pursues: but the just , bold as a lion, shall be without dread.
text_la: Fugit impius nemine persequente; justus autem, quasi leo confidens, absque terrore erit.
text_pt: Os ímpios fogem sem que haja ninguém a persegui-los; mas os justos são ousados como um leão.
text_el: φεύγει ἀσεβὴς μηδενὸς διώκοντος δίκαιος δὲ ὥσπερ λέων πέποιθεν

text_en: For the sins of the land many are the princes thereof: and for the wisdom of a man , and the knowledge of those things that are said, the life of the prince shall be prolonged.
text_la: Propter peccata terræ multi principes ejus; et propter hominis sapientiam, et horum scientiam quæ dicuntur, vita ducis longior erit.
text_pt: Pela transgressão da terra muitos são os seus príncipes, mas por homem prudente e entendido a sua continuidade será prolongada.
text_el: δι' ἁμαρτίας ἀσεβῶν κρίσεις ἐγείρονται ἀνὴρ δὲ πανοῦργος κατασβέσει αὐτάς

text_en: A poor man that oppresses the poor, is like a violent shower, which brings a famine.
text_la: Vir pauper calumnians pauperes similis est imbri vehementi in quo paratur fames.
text_pt: O homem pobre que oprime os pobres é como a chuva impetuosa, que causa a falta de alimento.
text_el: ἀνδρεῖος ἐν ἀσεβείαις συκοφαντεῖ πτωχούς ὥσπερ ὑετὸς λάβρος καὶ ἀνωφελής

text_en: They that forsake the law, praise the wicked man : they that keep it, are incensed against him.
text_la: Qui derelinquunt legem laudant impium; qui custodiunt, succenduntur contra eum.
text_pt: Os que deixam a lei louvam o ímpio; porém os que guardam a lei contendem com eles.
text_el: οὕτως οἱ ἐγκαταλείποντες τὸν νόμον ἐγκωμιάζουσιν ἀσέβειαν οἱ δὲ ἀγαπῶντες τὸν νόμον περιβάλλουσιν ἑαυτοῖς τεῖχος

text_en: Evil men think not on judgment: but they that seek after the Lord , take notice of all things.
text_la: Viri mali non cogitant judicium; qui autem inquirunt Dominum animadvertunt omnia.
text_pt: Os homens maus não entendem o juízo, mas os que buscam ao Senhor entendem tudo.
text_el: ἄνδρες κακοὶ οὐ νοήσουσιν κρίμα οἱ δὲ ζητοῦντες τὸν κύριον συνήσουσιν ἐν παντί

text_en: Better is the poor man walking in his simplicity, than the rich in crooked ways.
text_la: Melior est pauper ambulans in simplicitate sua quam dives in pravis itineribus.
text_pt: Melhor é o pobre que anda na sua integridade do que o de caminhos perversos ainda que seja rico.
text_el: κρείσσων πτωχὸς πορευόμενος ἐν ἀληθείᾳ πλουσίου ψευδοῦς

text_en: He that keeps the law, is a wise son: but he that feeds gluttons, shames his father.
text_la: Qui custodit legem filius sapiens est; qui autem comessatores pascit confundit patrem suum.
text_pt: O que guarda a lei é filho sábio, mas o companheiro dos desregrados envergonha a seu pai.
text_el: φυλάσσει νόμον υἱὸς συνετός ὃς δὲ ποιμαίνει ἀσωτίαν ἀτιμάζει πατέρα

text_en: He that heaps together riches by usury and loan, gathers them for him that will be bountiful to the poor.
text_la: Qui coacervat divitias usuris et fœnore, liberali in pauperes congregat eas.
text_pt: O que aumenta os seus bens com usura e ganância ajunta-os para o que se compadece do pobre.
text_el: ὁ πληθύνων τὸν πλοῦτον αὐτοῦ μετὰ τόκων καὶ πλεονασμῶν τῷ ἐλεῶντι πτωχοὺς συνάγει αὐτόν

text_en: He that turns away his ears from hearing the law, his prayer shall be an abomination.
text_la: Qui declinat aures suas ne audiat legem, oratio ejus erit execrabilis.
text_pt: O que desvia os seus ouvidos de ouvir a lei, até a sua oração será abominável.
text_el: ὁ ἐκκλίνων τὸ οὖς αὐτοῦ τοῦ μὴ εἰσακοῦσαι νόμου καὶ αὐτὸς τὴν προσευχὴν αὐτοῦ ἐβδέλυκται

text_en: He that deceives the just in a wicked way, shall fall in his own destruction: and the upright shall possess his goods.
text_la: Qui decipit justos in via mala, in interitu suo corruet, et simplices possidebunt bona ejus.
text_pt: O que faz com que os retos errem por mau caminho, ele mesmo cairá na sua cova; mas os bons herdarão o bem.
text_el: ὃς πλανᾷ εὐθεῖς ἐν ὁδῷ κακῇ εἰς διαφθορὰν αὐτὸς ἐμπεσεῖται οἱ δὲ ἄνομοι διελεύσονται ἀγαθὰ καὶ οὐκ εἰσελεύσονται εἰς αὐτά

text_en: The rich man seems to himself wise: but the poor man that is prudent shall search him out.
text_la: Sapiens sibi videtur vir dives; pauper autem prudens scrutabitur eum.
text_pt: O homem rico é sábio aos seus próprios olhos, mas o pobre que é entendido, o examina.
text_el: σοφὸς παρ' ἑαυτῷ ἀνὴρ πλούσιος πένης δὲ νοήμων καταγνώσεται αὐτοῦ

text_en: In the joy of the just there is great glory : when the wicked reign, men are ruined.
text_la: In exsultatione justorum multa gloria est; regnantibus impiis, ruinæ hominum.
text_pt: Quando os justos exultam, grande é a glória; mas quando os ímpios sobem, os homens se escondem.
text_el: διὰ βοήθειαν δικαίων πολλὴ γίνεται δόξα ἐν δὲ τόποις ἀσεβῶν ἁλίσκονται ἄνθρωποι

text_en: He that hides his sins , shall not prosper: but he that shall confess, and forsake them, shall obtain mercy.
text_la: Qui abscondit scelera sua non dirigetur; qui autem confessus fuerit et reliquerit ea, misericordiam consequetur.
text_pt: O que encobre as suas transgressões nunca prosperará, mas o que as confessa e deixa, alcançará misericórdia.
text_el: ὁ ἐπικαλύπτων ἀσέβειαν ἑαυτοῦ οὐκ εὐοδωθήσεται ὁ δὲ ἐξηγούμενος ἐλέγχους ἀγαπηθήσεται

text_en: Blessed is the man that is always fearful: but he that is hardened in mind shall fall into evil .
text_la: Beatus homo qui semper est pavidus; qui vero mentis est duræ corruet in malum.
text_pt: Bem-aventurado o homem que continuamente teme; mas o que endurece o seu coração cairá no mal.
text_el: μακάριος ἀνήρ ὃς καταπτήσσει πάντα δι' εὐλάβειαν ὁ δὲ σκληρὸς τὴν καρδίαν ἐμπεσεῖται κακοῖς

text_en: As a roaring lion, and a hungry bear, so is a wicked prince over the poor people.
text_la: Leo rugiens et ursus esuriens, princeps impius super populum pauperem.
text_pt: Como leão rugidor, e urso faminto, assim é o ímpio que domina sobre um povo pobre.
text_el: λέων πεινῶν καὶ λύκος διψῶν ὃς τυραννεῖ πτωχὸς ὢν ἔθνους πενιχροῦ

text_en: A prince void of prudence shall oppress many by calumny : but he that hates covetousness , shall prolong his days.
text_la: Dux indigens prudentia multos opprimet per calumniam; qui autem odit avaritiam, longi fient dies ejus.
text_pt: O príncipe falto de entendimento é também um grande opressor, mas o que odeia a avareza prolongará seus dias.
text_el: βασιλεὺς ἐνδεὴς προσόδων μέγας συκοφάντης ὁ δὲ μισῶν ἀδικίαν μακρὸν χρόνον ζήσεται

text_en: A man that does violence to the blood of a person, if he flee even to the pit, no man will stay him.
text_la: Hominem qui calumniatur animæ sanguinem, si usque ad lacum fugerit, nemo sustinet.
text_pt: O homem carregado do sangue de qualquer pessoa fugirá até à cova; ninguém o detenha.
text_el: ἄνδρα τὸν ἐν αἰτίᾳ φόνου ὁ ἐγγυώμενος φυγὰς ἔσται καὶ οὐκ ἐν ἀσφαλείᾳ

text_en: He that walks uprightly, shall be saved: he that is perverse in his ways, shall fall at once.
text_la: Qui ambulat simpliciter salvus erit; qui perversis graditur viis concidet semel.
text_pt: O que anda sinceramente salvar-se-á, mas o perverso em seus caminhos cairá logo.
text_el: ὁ πορευόμενος δικαίως βεβοήθηται ὁ δὲ σκολιαῖς ὁδοῖς πορευόμενος ἐμπλακήσεται

text_en: He that tills his ground, shall be filled with bread: but he that follows idleness , shall be filled with poverty.
text_la: Qui operatur terram suam satiabitur panibus; qui autem sectatur otium replebitur egestate.
text_pt: O que lavrar a sua terra virá a fartar-se de pão, mas o que segue a ociosos se fartará de pobreza.
text_el: ὁ ἐργαζόμενος τὴν ἑαυτοῦ γῆν πλησθήσεται ἄρτων ὁ δὲ διώκων σχολὴν πλησθήσεται πενίας

text_en: A faithful man shall be much praised: but he that makes haste to be rich, shall not be innocent.
text_la: Vir fidelis multum laudabitur; qui autem festinat ditari non erit innocens.
text_pt: O homem fiel será coberto de bênçãos, mas o que se apressa a enriquecer não ficará impune.
text_el: ἀνὴρ ἀξιόπιστος πολλὰ εὐλογηθήσεται ὁ δὲ κακὸς οὐκ ἀτιμώρητος ἔσται

text_en: He that has respect to a person in judgment, does not well: such a man even for a morsel of bread forsakes the truth .
text_la: Qui cognoscit in judicio faciem non bene facit; iste et pro buccella panis deserit veritatem.
text_pt: Dar importância à aparência das pessoas não é bom, porque até por um bocado de pão um homem prevaricará.
text_el: ὃς οὐκ αἰσχύνεται πρόσωπα δικαίων οὐκ ἀγαθός ὁ τοιοῦτος ψωμοῦ ἄρτου ἀποδώσεται ἄνδρα

text_en: A man that makes haste to be rich, and envies others, is ignorant that poverty shall come upon him.
text_la: Vir qui festinat ditari, et aliis invidet, ignorat quod egestas superveniet ei.
text_pt: O que quer enriquecer depressa é homem de olho maligno, porém não sabe que a pobreza há de vir sobre ele.
text_el: σπεύδει πλουτεῖν ἀνὴρ βάσκανος καὶ οὐκ οἶδεν ὅτι ἐλεήμων κρατήσει αὐτοῦ

text_en: He that rebukes a man , shall afterward find favour with him, more than he that by a flattering tongue deceives him.
text_la: Qui corripit hominem gratiam postea inveniet apud eum, magis quam ille qui per linguæ blandimenta decipit.
text_pt: O que repreende o homem gozará depois mais amizade do que aquele que lisonjeia com a língua.
text_el: ὁ ἐλέγχων ἀνθρώπου ὁδοὺς χάριτας ἕξει μᾶλλον τοῦ γλωσσοχαριτοῦντος

text_en: He that steals anything from his father, or from his mother: and says, This is no sin , is the partner of a murderer .
text_la: Qui subtrahit aliquid a patre suo et a matre, et dicit hoc non esse peccatum, particeps homicidæ est.
text_pt: O que rouba a seu próprio pai, ou a sua mãe, e diz: Não é transgressão, companheiro é do homem destruidor.
text_el: ὃς ἀποβάλλεται πατέρα ἢ μητέρα καὶ δοκεῖ μὴ ἁμαρτάνειν οὗτος κοινωνός ἐστιν ἀνδρὸς ἀσεβοῦς

text_en: He that boasts and puffs up himself, stirs up quarrels: but he that trusts in the Lord , shall be healed.
text_la: Qui se jactat et dilatat, jurgia concitat; qui vero sperat in Domino sanabitur.
text_pt: O orgulhoso de coração levanta contendas, mas o que confia no Senhor prosperará.
text_el: ἄπληστος ἀνὴρ κρίνει εἰκῇ ὃς δὲ πέποιθεν ἐπὶ κύριον ἐν ἐπιμελείᾳ ἔσται

text_en: He that trusts in his own heart, is a fool: but he that walks wisely, he shall be saved.
text_la: Qui confidit in corde suo stultus est; qui autem graditur sapienter, ipse salvabitur.
text_pt: O que confia no seu próprio coração é insensato, mas o que anda em sabedoria, será salvo.
text_el: ὃς πέποιθεν θρασείᾳ καρδίᾳ ὁ τοιοῦτος ἄφρων ὃς δὲ πορεύεται σοφίᾳ σωθήσεται

text_en: He that gives to the poor shall not want: he that despises his intreaty, shall suffer indigence.
text_la: Qui dat pauperi non indigebit; qui despicit deprecantem sustinebit penuriam.
text_pt: O que dá ao pobre não terá necessidade, mas o que esconde os seus olhos terá muitas maldições.
text_el: ὃς δίδωσιν πτωχοῖς οὐκ ἐνδεηθήσεται ὃς δὲ ἀποστρέφει τὸν ὀφθαλμὸν αὐτοῦ ἐν πολλῇ ἀπορίᾳ ἔσται

text_en: When the wicked rise up, men shall hide themselves: when they perish, the just shall be multiplied.
text_la: Cum surrexerint impii, abscondentur homines; cum illi perierint, multiplicabuntur justi.
text_pt: Quando os ímpios se elevam, os homens andam se escondendo, mas quando perecem, os justos se multiplicam.
text_el: ἐν τόποις ἀσεβῶν στένουσι δίκαιοι ἐν δὲ τῇ ἐκείνων ἀπωλείᾳ πληθυνθήσονται δίκαιοι

text_en: The man that with a stiff neck despises him that reproves him, shall suddenly be destroyed: and health shall not follow him.
text_la: Viro qui corripientem dura cervice contemnit, repentinus ei superveniet interitus, et eum sanitas non sequetur.
text_pt: O Homem que muitas vezes repreendido endurece a cerviz, de repente será destruído sem que haja remédio.
text_el: κρείσσων ἀνὴρ ἐλέγχων ἀνδρὸς σκληροτραχήλου ἐξαπίνης γὰρ φλεγομένου αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἔστιν ἴασις

text_en: When just men increase, the people shall rejoice: when the wicked shall bear rule, the people shall mourn.
text_la: In multiplicatione justorum lætabitur vulgus; cum impii sumpserint principatum, gemet populus.
text_pt: Quando os justos se engrandecem, o povo se alegra, mas quando o ímpio domina, o povo geme.
text_el: ἐγκωμιαζομένων δικαίων εὐφρανθήσονται λαοί ἀρχόντων δὲ ἀσεβῶν στένουσιν ἄνδρες

text_en: A man that loves wisdom, rejoices his father: but he that maintains harlots, shall squander away his substance.
text_la: Vir qui amat sapientiam lætificat patrem suum; qui autem nutrit scorta perdet substantiam.
text_pt: O homem que ama a sabedoria alegra a seu pai, mas o companheiro de prostitutas desperdiça os bens.
text_el: ἀνδρὸς φιλοῦντος σοφίαν εὐφραίνεται πατὴρ αὐτοῦ ὃς δὲ ποιμαίνει πόρνας ἀπολεῖ πλοῦτον

text_en: A just king sets up the land: a covetous man shall destroy it.
text_la: Rex justus erigit terram; vir avarus destruet eam.
text_pt: O rei com juízo sustém a terra, mas o amigo de peitas a transtorna.
text_el: βασιλεὺς δίκαιος ἀνίστησιν χώραν ἀνὴρ δὲ παράνομος κατασκάπτει

text_en: A man that speaks to his friend with flattering and dissembling words, spreads a net for his feet.
text_la: Homo qui blandis fictisque sermonibus loquitur amico suo rete expandit gressibus ejus.
text_pt: O homem que lisonjeia o seu próximo arma uma rede aos seus passos.
text_el: ὃς παρασκευάζεται ἐπὶ πρόσωπον τοῦ ἑαυτοῦ φίλου δίκτυον περιβάλλει αὐτὸ τοῖς ἑαυτοῦ ποσίν

text_en: A snare shall entangle the wicked man when he sins : and the just shall praise and rejoice.
text_la: Peccantem virum iniquum involvet laqueus, et justus laudabit atque gaudebit.
text_pt: Na transgressão do homem mau há laço, mas o justo jubila e se alegra.
text_el: ἁμαρτάνοντι ἀνδρὶ μεγάλη παγίς δίκαιος δὲ ἐν χαρᾷ καὶ ἐν εὐφροσύνῃ ἔσται

text_en: The just takes notice of the cause of the poor: the wicked is void of knowledge .
text_la: Novit justus causam pauperum; impius ignorat scientiam.
text_pt: O justo se informa da causa dos pobres, mas o ímpio nem sequer toma conhecimento.
text_el: ἐπίσταται δίκαιος κρίνειν πενιχροῖς ὁ δὲ ἀσεβὴς οὐ συνήσει γνῶσιν καὶ πτωχῷ οὐχ ὑπάρχει νοῦς ἐπιγνώμων

text_en: Corrupt men bring a city to ruin: but wise men turn away wrath .
text_la: Homines pestilentes dissipant civitatem; sapientes vero avertunt furorem.
text_pt: Os homens escarnecedores alvoroçam a cidade, mas os sábios desviam a ira.
text_el: ἄνδρες λοιμοὶ ἐξέκαυσαν πόλιν σοφοὶ δὲ ἀπέστρεψαν ὀργήν

text_en: If a wise man contend with a fool, whether he be angry , or laugh, he shall find no rest.
text_la: Vir sapiens si cum stulto contenderit, sive irascatur, sive rideat, non inveniet requiem.
text_pt: O homem sábio que pleiteia com o tolo, quer se zangue, quer se ria, não terá descanso.
text_el: ἀνὴρ σοφὸς κρίνει ἔθνη ἀνὴρ δὲ φαῦλος ὀργιζόμενος καταγελᾶται καὶ οὐ καταπτήσσει

text_en: Bloodthirsty men hate the upright: but just men seek his soul .
text_la: Viri sanguinum oderunt simplicem; justi autem quærunt animam ejus.
text_pt: Os homens sanguinários odeiam ao sincero, mas os justos procuram o seu bem.
text_el: ἄνδρες αἱμάτων μέτοχοι μισήσουσιν ὅσιον οἱ δὲ εὐθεῖς ἐκζητήσουσιν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ

text_en: A fool utters all his mind: a wise man defers, and keeps it till afterwards.
text_la: Totum spiritum suum profert stultus; sapiens differt, et reservat in posterum.
text_pt: O tolo revela todo o seu pensamento, mas o sábio o guarda até o fim.
text_el: ὅλον τὸν θυμὸν αὐτοῦ ἐκφέρει ἄφρων σοφὸς δὲ ταμιεύεται κατὰ μέρος

text_en: A prince that gladly hears lying words, has all his servants wicked .
text_la: Princeps qui libenter audit verba mendacii, omnes ministros habet impios.
text_pt: O governador que dá atenção às palavras mentirosas, achará que todos os seus servos são ímpios.
text_el: βασιλέως ὑπακούοντος λόγον ἄδικον πάντες οἱ ὑπ' αὐτὸν παράνομοι

text_en: The poor man and the creditor have met one another: the Lord is the enlightener of them both.
text_la: Pauper et creditor obviaverunt sibi : utriusque illuminator est Dominus.
text_pt: O pobre e o usurário se encontram; o Senhor ilumina os olhos de ambos.
text_el: δανιστοῦ καὶ χρεοφειλέτου ἀλλήλοις συνελθόντων ἐπισκοπὴν ποιεῖται ἀμφοτέρων ὁ κύριος

text_en: The king that judges the poor in truth , his throne shall be established for ever.
text_la: Rex qui judicat in veritate pauperes, thronus ejus in æternum firmabitur.
text_pt: O rei que julga os pobres conforme a verdade firmará o seu trono para sempre.
text_el: βασιλέως ἐν ἀληθείᾳ κρίνοντος πτωχοὺς ὁ θρόνος αὐτοῦ εἰς μαρτύριον κατασταθήσεται

text_en: The rod and reproof give wisdom: but the child that is left to his own will, brings his mother to shame.
text_la: Virga atque correptio tribuit sapientiam; puer autem qui dimittitur voluntati suæ confundit matrem suam.
text_pt: A vara e a repreensão dão sabedoria, mas a criança entregue a si mesma, envergonha a sua mãe.
text_el: πληγαὶ καὶ ἔλεγχοι διδόασιν σοφίαν παῖς δὲ πλανώμενος αἰσχύνει γονεῖς αὐτοῦ

text_en: When the wicked are multiplied, crimes shall be multiplied: but the just shall see their downfall.
text_la: In multiplicatione impiorum multiplicabuntur scelera, et justi ruinas eorum videbunt.
text_pt: Quando os ímpios se multiplicam, multiplicam-se as transgressões, mas os justos verão a sua queda.
text_el: πολλῶν ὄντων ἀσεβῶν πολλαὶ γίνονται ἁμαρτίαι οἱ δὲ δίκαιοι ἐκείνων πιπτόντων κατάφοβοι γίνονται

text_en: Instruct your son and he shall refresh you, and shall give delight to your soul .
text_la: Erudi filium tuum, et refrigerabit te, et dabit delicias animæ tuæ.
text_pt: Castiga o teu filho, e te dará descanso; e dará delícias à tua alma.
text_el: παίδευε υἱόν σου καὶ ἀναπαύσει σε καὶ δώσει κόσμον τῇ ψυχῇ σου

text_en: When prophecy shall fail, the people shall be scattered abroad : but he that keeps the law, is blessed .
text_la: Cum prophetia defecerit, dissipabitur populus; qui vero custodit legem beatus est.
text_pt: Não havendo profecia, o povo perece; porém o que guarda a lei, esse é bem-aventurado.
text_el: οὐ μὴ ὑπάρξῃ ἐξηγητὴς ἔθνει παρανόμῳ ὁ δὲ φυλάσσων τὸν νόμον μακαριστός

text_en: A slave will not be corrected by words: because he understands what you say, and will not answer.
text_la: Servus verbis non potest erudiri, quia quod dicis intelligit, et respondere contemnit.
text_pt: O servo não se emendará com palavras, porque, ainda que entenda, todavia não atenderá.
text_el: λόγοις οὐ παιδευθήσεται οἰκέτης σκληρός ἐὰν γὰρ καὶ νοήσῃ ἀλλ' οὐχ ὑπακούσεται

text_en: Have you seen a man hasty to speak? Folly is rather to be looked for, than his amendment.
text_la: Vidisti hominem velocem ad loquendum? stultitia magis speranda est quam illius correptio.
text_pt: Tens visto um homem precipitado no falar? Maior esperança há para um tolo do que para ele.
text_el: ἐὰν ἴδῃς ἄνδρα ταχὺν ἐν λόγοις γίνωσκε ὅτι ἐλπίδα ἔχει μᾶλλον ἄφρων αὐτοῦ

text_en: He that nourishes his servant delicately from his childhood, afterwards shall find him stubborn.
text_la: Qui delicate a pueritia nutrit servum suum postea sentiet eum contumacem.
text_pt: Quando alguém cria o seu servo com mimos desde a meninice, por fim ele tornar-se-á seu filho.
text_el: ὃς κατασπαταλᾷ ἐκ παιδός οἰκέτης ἔσται ἔσχατον δὲ ὀδυνηθήσεται ἐφ' ἑαυτῷ

text_en: A passionate man provokes quarrels: and he that is easily stirred up to wrath , shall be more prone to sin .
text_la: Vir iracundus provocat rixas, et qui ad indignandum facilis est erit ad peccandum proclivior.
text_pt: O homem irascível levanta contendas; e o furioso multiplica as transgressões.
text_el: ἀνὴρ θυμώδης ὀρύσσει νεῖκος ἀνὴρ δὲ ὀργίλος ἐξώρυξεν ἁμαρτίας

text_en: Humiliation follows the proud : and glory shall uphold the humble of spirit .
text_la: Superbum sequitur humilitas, et humilem spiritu suscipiet gloria.
text_pt: A soberba do homem o abaterá, mas a honra sustentará o humilde de espírito.
text_el: ὕβρις ἄνδρα ταπεινοῖ τοὺς δὲ ταπεινόφρονας ἐρείδει δόξῃ κύριος

text_en: He that is partaker with a thief , hates his own soul : he hears one putting him to his oath , and discovers not.
text_la: Qui cum fure participat odit animam suam; adjurantem audit, et non indicat.
text_pt: O que tem parte com o ladrão odeia a sua própria alma; ouve maldições, e não o denuncia.
text_el: ὃς μερίζεται κλέπτῃ μισεῖ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχήν ἐὰν δὲ ὅρκου προτεθέντος ἀκούσαντες μὴ ἀναγγείλωσιν

text_en: He that fears man shall quickly fall: he that trusts in the Lord , shall be set on high.
text_la: Qui timet hominem cito corruet; qui sperat in Domino sublevabitur.
text_pt: O temor do homem armará laços, mas o que confia no Senhor será posto em alto retiro.
text_el: φοβηθέντες καὶ αἰσχυνθέντες ἀνθρώπους ὑπεσκελίσθησαν ὁ δὲ πεποιθὼς ἐπὶ κύριον εὐφρανθήσεται ἀσέβεια ἀνδρὶ δίδωσιν σφάλμα ὃς δὲ πέποιθεν ἐπὶ τῷ δεσπότῃ σωθήσεται

text_en: Many seek the face of the prince: but the judgment of every one comes forth from the Lord .
text_la: Multi requirunt faciem principis, et judicium a Domino egreditur singulorum.
text_pt: Muitos buscam o favor do poderoso, mas o juízo de cada um vem do Senhor.
text_el: πολλοὶ θεραπεύουσιν πρόσωπα ἡγουμένων παρὰ δὲ κυρίου γίνεται τὸ δίκαιον ἀνδρί

text_en: The just abhor a wicked man : and the wicked loathe them that are in the right way. The son that keeps the word, shall be free from destruction.
text_la: Abominantur justi virum impium, et abominantur impii eos qui in recta sunt via. Verbum custodiens filius extra perditionem erit.
text_pt: Abominação é, para os justos, o homem iníquo; mas abominação é, para o iníquo, o de retos caminhos.
text_el: βδέλυγμα δικαίοις ἀνὴρ ἄδικος βδέλυγμα δὲ ἀνόμῳ κατευθύνουσα ὁδός

text_en: The words of Gatherer the son of Vomiter. The vision which the man spoke, with whom God is, and who being strengthened by God , abiding with him, said:
text_la: Verba Congregantis, filii Vomentis. Visio quam locutus est vir cum quo est Deus, et qui Deo secum morante confortatus, ait:
text_pt: Palavras de Agur, filho de Jaque, o masaíta, que proferiu este homem a Itiel, a Itiel e a Ucal:
text_el: τοὺς ἐμοὺς λόγους υἱέ φοβήθητι καὶ δεξάμενος αὐτοὺς μετανόει τάδε λέγει ὁ ἀνὴρ τοῖς πιστεύουσιν θεῷ καὶ παύομαι

text_en: I am the most foolish of men , and the wisdom of men is not with me.
text_la: Stultissimus sum virorum, et sapientia hominum non est mecum.
text_pt: Na verdade eu sou o mais bruto dos homens, nem mesmo tenho o conhecimento de homem.
text_el: ἀφρονέστατος γάρ εἰμι πάντων ἀνθρώπων καὶ φρόνησις ἀνθρώπων οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν ἐμοί

text_en: I have not learned wisdom, and have not known the science of saints .
text_la: Non didici sapientiam, et non novi scientiam sanctorum.
text_pt: Nem aprendi a sabedoria, nem tenho o conhecimento do santo.
text_el: θεὸς δεδίδαχέν με σοφίαν καὶ γνῶσιν ἁγίων ἔγνωκα

text_en: Who has ascended up into heaven , and descended? Who has held the wind in his hands? Who has bound up the waters together as in a garment? Who has raised up all the borders of the earth? What is his name , and what is the name of his son, if you know ?
text_la: Quis ascendit in cælum, atque descendit? quis continuit spiritum in manibus suis? quis colligavit aquas quasi in vestimento? quis suscitavit omnes terminos terræ? quod nomen est ejus, et quod nomen filii ejus, si nosti?
text_pt: Quem subiu ao céu e desceu? Quem encerrou os ventos nos seus punhos? Quem amarrou as águas numa roupa? Quem estabeleceu todas as extremidades da terra? Qual é o seu nome? E qual é o nome de seu filho, se é que o sabes?
text_el: τίς ἀνέβη εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ κατέβη τίς συνήγαγεν ἀνέμους ἐν κόλπῳ τίς συνέστρεψεν ὕδωρ ἐν ἱματίῳ τίς ἐκράτησεν πάντων τῶν ἄκρων τῆς γῆς τί ὄνομα αὐτῷ ἢ τί ὄνομα τοῖς τέκνοις αὐτοῦ ἵνα γνῷς

text_en: Every word of God is fire tried: he is a buckler to them that hope in him.
text_la: Omnis sermo Dei ignitus : clypeus est sperantibus in se.
text_pt: Toda a Palavra de Deus é pura; escudo é para os que confiam nele.
text_el: πάντες λόγοι θεοῦ πεπυρωμένοι ὑπερασπίζει δὲ αὐτὸς τῶν εὐλαβουμένων αὐτόν

text_en: Add not anything to his words, lest you be reproved and found a liar :
text_la: Ne addas quidquam verbis illius, et arguaris, inveniarisque mendax.
text_pt: Nada acrescentes às suas palavras, para que não te repreenda e sejas achado mentiroso.
text_el: μὴ προσθῇς τοῖς λόγοις αὐτοῦ ἵνα μὴ ἐλέγξῃ σε καὶ ψευδὴς γένῃ

text_en: Two things I have asked of you, deny them not to me before I die.
text_la: Duo rogavi te : ne deneges mihi antequam moriar :
text_pt: Duas coisas te pedi; não mas negues, antes que morra:
text_el: δύο αἰτοῦμαι παρὰ σοῦ μὴ ἀφέλῃς μου χάριν πρὸ τοῦ ἀποθανεῖν με

text_en: Remove far from me vanity, and lying words. Give me neither beggary, nor riches: give me only the necessaries of life:
text_la: vanitatem et verba mendacia longe fac a me; mendicitatem et divitias ne dederis mihi : tribue tantum victui meo necessaria,
text_pt: Afasta de mim a vaidade e a palavra mentirosa; não me dês nem a pobreza nem a riqueza; mantém-me do pão da minha porção de costume;
text_el: μάταιον λόγον καὶ ψευδῆ μακράν μου ποίησον πλοῦτον δὲ καὶ πενίαν μή μοι δῷς σύνταξον δέ μοι τὰ δέοντα καὶ τὰ αὐτάρκη

text_en: Lest perhaps being filled, I should be tempted to deny, and say: Who is the Lord ? Or being compelled by poverty, I should steal, and forswear the name of my God .
text_la: ne forte satiatus illiciar ad negandum, et dicam : Quis est Dominus? aut egestate compulsus, furer, et perjurem nomen Dei mei.
text_pt: Para que, porventura, estando farto não te negue, e venha a dizer: Quem é o Senhor? ou que, empobrecendo, não venha a furtar, e tome o nome de Deus em vão.
text_el: ἵνα μὴ πλησθεὶς ψευδὴς γένωμαι καὶ εἴπω τίς με ὁρᾷ ἢ πενηθεὶς κλέψω καὶ ὀμόσω τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ θεοῦ

text_en: Accuse not a servant to his master, lest he curse you, and you fall.
text_la: Ne accuses servum ad dominum suum, ne forte maledicat tibi, et corruas.
text_pt: Não acuses o servo diante de seu senhor, para que não te amaldiçoe e tu fiques o culpado.
text_el: μὴ παραδῷς οἰκέτην εἰς χεῖρας δεσπότου μήποτε καταράσηταί σε καὶ ἀφανισθῇς

text_en: There is a generation that curses their father, and does not bless their mother.
text_la: Generatio quæ patri suo maledicit, et quæ matri suæ non benedicit;
text_pt: Há uma geração que amaldiçoa a seu pai, e que não bendiz a sua mãe.
text_el: ἔκγονον κακὸν πατέρα καταρᾶται τὴν δὲ μητέρα οὐκ εὐλογεῖ

text_en: A generation that are pure in their own eyes, and yet are not washed from their filthiness.
text_la: generatio quæ sibi munda videtur, et tamen non est lota a sordibus suis;
text_pt: Há uma geração que é pura aos seus próprios olhos, mas que nunca foi lavada da sua imundícia.
text_el: ἔκγονον κακὸν δίκαιον ἑαυτὸν κρίνει τὴν δὲ ἔξοδον αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἀπένιψεν

text_en: A generation , whose eyes are lofty, and their eyelids lifted up on high.
text_la: generatio cujus excelsi sunt oculi, et palpebræ ejus in alta surrectæ;
text_pt: Há uma geração cujos olhos são altivos, e as suas pálpebras são sempre levantadas.
text_el: ἔκγονον κακὸν ὑψηλοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχει τοῖς δὲ βλεφάροις αὐτοῦ ἐπαίρεται

text_en: A generation that for teeth has swords, and grinds with their jaw teeth, to devour the needy from off the earth, and the poor from among men .
text_la: generatio quæ pro dentibus gladios habet, et commandit molaribus suis, ut comedat inopes de terra, et pauperes ex hominibus.
text_pt: Há uma geração cujos dentes são espadas, e cujas queixadas são facas, para consumirem da terra os aflitos, e os necessitados dentre os homens.
text_el: ἔκγονον κακὸν μαχαίρας τοὺς ὀδόντας ἔχει καὶ τὰς μύλας τομίδας ὥστε ἀναλίσκειν καὶ κατεσθίειν τοὺς ταπεινοὺς ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς καὶ τοὺς πένητας αὐτῶν ἐξ ἀνθρώπων

text_en: The horseleech has two daughters that say: Bring, bring. There are three things that never are satisfied, and the fourth never says: It is enough.
text_la: Sanguisugæ duæ sunt filiæ, dicentes : Affer, affer. Tria sunt insaturabilia, et quartum quod numquam dicit : Sufficit.
text_pt: A sanguessuga tem duas filhas: Dá e Dá. Estas três coisas nunca se fartam; e com a quarta, nunca dizem: Basta!
text_el: τῇ βδέλλῃ τρεῖς θυγατέρες ἦσαν ἀγαπήσει ἀγαπώμεναι καὶ αἱ τρεῖς αὗται οὐκ ἐνεπίμπλασαν αὐτήν καὶ ἡ τετάρτη οὐκ ἠρκέσθη εἰπεῖν ἱκανόν

text_en: Hell and the mouth of the womb, and the earth which is not satisfied with water: and the fire never says: It is enough.
text_la: Infernus, et os vulvæ, et terra quæ non satiatur aqua : ignis vero numquam dicit : Sufficit.
text_pt: A sepultura; a madre estéril; a terra que não se farta de água; e o fogo; nunca dizem: Basta!
text_el: ᾅδης καὶ ἔρως γυναικὸς καὶ τάρταρος καὶ γῆ οὐκ ἐμπιπλαμένη ὕδατος καὶ ὕδωρ καὶ πῦρ οὐ μὴ εἴπωσιν ἀρκεῖ

text_en: The eye that mocks at his father, and that despises the labour of his mother in bearing him, let the ravens of the brooks pick it out, and the young eagles eat it.
text_la: Oculum qui subsannat patrem, et qui despicit partum matris suæ, effodiant eum corvi de torrentibus, et comedant eum filii aquilæ!
text_pt: Os olhos que zombam do pai, ou desprezam a obediência à mãe, corvos do ribeiro os arrancarão e os filhotes da águia os comerão.
text_el: ὀφθαλμὸν καταγελῶντα πατρὸς καὶ ἀτιμάζοντα γῆρας μητρός ἐκκόψαισαν αὐτὸν κόρακες ἐκ τῶν φαράγγων καὶ καταφάγοισαν αὐτὸν νεοσσοὶ ἀετῶν

text_en: Three things are hard to me, and the fourth I am utterly ignorant of.
text_la: Tria sunt difficilia mihi, et quartum penitus ignoro :
text_pt: Estas três coisas me maravilham; e quatro há que não conheço:
text_el: τρία δέ ἐστιν ἀδύνατά μοι νοῆσαι καὶ τὸ τέταρτον οὐκ ἐπιγινώσκω

text_en: The way of an eagle in the air, the way of a serpent upon a rock, the way of a ship in the midst of the sea, and the way of a man in youth.
text_la: viam aquilæ in cælo, viam colubri super petram, viam navis in medio mari, et viam viri in adolescentia.
text_pt: O caminho da águia no ar; o caminho da cobra na penha; o caminho do navio no meio do mar; e o caminho do homem com uma virgem.
text_el: ἴχνη ἀετοῦ πετομένου καὶ ὁδοὺς ὄφεως ἐπὶ πέτρας καὶ τρίβους νηὸς ποντοπορούσης καὶ ὁδοὺς ἀνδρὸς ἐν νεότητι

text_en: Such also is the way of an adulterous woman , who eats and wipes her mouth, and says: I have done no evil .
text_la: Talis est et via mulieris adulteræ, quæ comedit, et tergens os suum dicit : Non sum operata malum.
text_pt: O caminho da mulher adúltera é assim: ela come, depois limpa a sua boca e diz: Não fiz nada de mal!
text_el: τοιαύτη ὁδὸς γυναικὸς μοιχαλίδος ἥ ὅταν πράξῃ ἀπονιψαμένη οὐδέν φησιν πεπραχέναι ἄτοπον

text_en: By three things the earth is disturbed, and the fourth it cannot bear.
text_la: Per tria movetur terra, et quartum non potest sustinere :
text_pt: Por três coisas se alvoroça a terra; e por quatro que não pode suportar:
text_el: διὰ τριῶν σείεται ἡ γῆ τὸ δὲ τέταρτον οὐ δύναται φέρειν

text_en: By a slave when he reigns: by a fool when he is filled with meat:
text_la: per servum, cum regnaverit; per stultum, cum saturatus fuerit cibo;
text_pt: Pelo servo, quando reina; e pelo tolo, quando vive na fartura;
text_el: ἐὰν οἰκέτης βασιλεύσῃ καὶ ἄφρων πλησθῇ σιτίων

text_en: By an odious woman when she is married : and by a bondwoman when she is heir to her mistress.
text_la: per odiosam mulierem, cum in matrimonio fuerit assumpta; et per ancillam, cum fuerit hæres dominæ suæ.
text_pt: Pela mulher odiosa, quando é casada; e pela serva, quando fica herdeira da sua senhora.
text_el: καὶ οἰκέτις ἐὰν ἐκβάλῃ τὴν ἑαυτῆς κυρίαν καὶ μισητὴ γυνὴ ἐὰν τύχῃ ἀνδρὸς ἀγαθοῦ

text_en: There are four very little things of the earth, and they are wiser than the wise.
text_la: Quatuor sunt minima terræ, et ipsa sunt sapientiora sapientibus :
text_pt: Estas quatro coisas são das menores da terra, porém bem providas de sabedoria:
text_el: τέσσαρα δέ ἐστιν ἐλάχιστα ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ταῦτα δέ ἐστιν σοφώτερα τῶν σοφῶν

text_en: The ants, a feeble people, which provide themselves food in the harvest:
text_la: formicæ, populus infirmus, qui præparat in messe cibum sibi;
text_pt: As formigas não são um povo forte; todavia no verão preparam a sua comida;
text_el: οἱ μύρμηκες οἷς μὴ ἔστιν ἰσχὺς καὶ ἑτοιμάζονται θέρους τὴν τροφήν

text_en: The rabbit, a weak people, which makes its bed in the rock:
text_la: lepusculus, plebs invalida, qui collocat in petra cubile suum;
text_pt: Os coelhos são um povo débil; e contudo, põem a sua casa na rocha;
text_el: καὶ οἱ χοιρογρύλλιοι ἔθνος οὐκ ἰσχυρόν οἳ ἐποιήσαντο ἐν πέτραις τοὺς ἑαυτῶν οἴκους

text_en: The locust has no king, yet they all go out by their bands:
text_la: regem locusta non habet, et egreditur universa per turmas suas;
text_pt: Os gafanhotos não têm rei; e contudo todos saem, e em bandos se repartem;
text_el: ἀβασίλευτόν ἐστιν ἡ ἀκρὶς καὶ ἐκστρατεύει ἀφ' ἑνὸς κελεύσματος εὐτάκτως

text_en: The stellio supports itself on hands, and dwells in kings' houses.
text_la: stellio manibus nititur, et moratur in ædibus regis.
text_pt: A aranha se pendura com as mãos, e está nos palácios dos reis.
text_el: καὶ καλαβώτης χερσὶν ἐρειδόμενος καὶ εὐάλωτος ὢν κατοικεῖ ἐν ὀχυρώμασιν βασιλέως

text_en: There are three things, which go well, and the fourth that walks happily:
text_la: Tria sunt quæ bene gradiuntur, et quartum quod incedit feliciter :
text_pt: Estes três têm um bom andar, e quatro passeiam airosamente;
text_el: τρία δέ ἐστιν ἃ εὐόδως πορεύεται καὶ τὸ τέταρτον ὃ καλῶς διαβαίνει

text_en: A lion, the strongest of beasts, who has no fear of anything he meets:
text_la: leo, fortissimus bestiarum, ad nullius pavebit occursum;
text_pt: O leão, o mais forte entre os animais, que não foge de nada;
text_el: σκύμνος λέοντος ἰσχυρότερος κτηνῶν ὃς οὐκ ἀποστρέφεται οὐδὲ καταπτήσσει κτῆνος

text_en: A cock girded about the loins: and a ram: and a king, whom none can resist.
text_la: gallus succinctus lumbos; et aries; nec est rex, qui resistat ei.
text_pt: O galgo; o bode também; e o rei a quem não se pode resistir.
text_el: καὶ ἀλέκτωρ ἐμπεριπατῶν θηλείαις εὔψυχος καὶ τράγος ἡγούμενος αἰπολίου καὶ βασιλεὺς δημηγορῶν ἐν ἔθνει

text_en: There is that has appeared a fool after he was lifted up on high: for if he had understood, he would have laid his hand upon his mouth.
text_la: Est qui stultus apparuit postquam elevatus est in sublime; si enim intellexisset, ori suo imposuisset manum.
text_pt: Se procedeste loucamente, exaltando-te, e se planejaste o mal, leva a mão à boca;
text_el: ἐὰν πρόῃ σεαυτὸν εἰς εὐφροσύνην καὶ ἐκτείνῃς τὴν χεῖρά σου μετὰ μάχης ἀτιμασθήσῃ

text_en: And he that strongly squeezes the paps to bring out milk, strains out butter: and he that violently blows his nose, brings out blood: and he that provokes wrath , brings forth strife.
text_la: Qui autem fortiter premit ubera ad eliciendum lac exprimit butyrum; et qui vehementer emungit elicit sanguinem; et qui provocat iras producit discordias.
text_pt: Porque o mexer do leite produz manteiga, o espremer do nariz produz sangue; assim o forçar da ira produz contenda.
text_el: ἄμελγε γάλα καὶ ἔσται βούτυρον ἐὰν δὲ ἐκπιέζῃς μυκτῆρας ἐξελεύσεται αἷμα ἐὰν δὲ ἐξέλκῃς λόγους ἐξελεύσονται κρίσεις καὶ μάχαι

text_en: The words of King Lamuel . The vision wherewith his mother instructed him.
text_la: Verba Lamuelis regis. Visio qua erudivit eum mater sua.
text_pt: Palavras do rei Lemuel, a profecia que lhe ensinou a sua mãe.
text_el: οἱ ἐμοὶ λόγοι εἴρηνται ὑπὸ θεοῦ βασιλέως χρηματισμός ὃν ἐπαίδευσεν ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ

text_en: What, O my beloved, what, O the beloved of my womb, what, O the beloved of my vows ?
text_la: Quid, dilecte mi? quid, dilecte uteri mei? quid, dilecte votorum meorum?
text_pt: Como, filho meu? e como, filho do meu ventre? e como, filho dos meus votos?
text_el: τί τέκνον τηρήσεις τί ῥήσεις θεοῦ πρωτογενές σοὶ λέγω υἱέ τί τέκνον ἐμῆς κοιλίας τί τέκνον ἐμῶν εὐχῶν

text_en: Give not your substance to women , and your riches to destroy kings.
