text_la: Ne dederis mulieribus substantiam tuam, et divitias tuas ad delendos reges.
text_pt: Não dês às mulheres a tua força, nem os teus caminhos ao que destrói os reis.
text_el: μὴ δῷς γυναιξὶ σὸν πλοῦτον καὶ τὸν σὸν νοῦν καὶ βίον εἰς ὑστεροβουλίαν

text_en: Give not to kings, O Lamuel , give not wine to kings: because there is no secret where drunkenness reigns:
text_la: Noli regibus, o Lamuel, noli regibus dare vinum, quia nullum secretum est ubi regnat ebrietas;
text_pt: Não é próprio dos reis, ó Lemuel, não é próprio dos reis beber vinho, nem dos príncipes o desejar bebida forte;
text_el: μετὰ βουλῆς πάντα ποίει μετὰ βουλῆς οἰνοπότει οἱ δυνάσται θυμώδεις εἰσίν οἶνον δὲ μὴ πινέτωσαν

text_en: And lest they drink and forget judgments, and pervert the cause of the children of the poor.
text_la: et ne forte bibant, et obliviscantur judiciorum, et mutent causam filiorum pauperis.
text_pt: Para que bebendo, se esqueçam da lei, e pervertam o direito de todos os aflitos.
text_el: ἵνα μὴ πιόντες ἐπιλάθωνται τῆς σοφίας καὶ ὀρθὰ κρῖναι οὐ μὴ δύνωνται τοὺς ἀσθενεῖς

text_en: Give strong drink to them that are sad; and wine to them that are grieved in mind:
text_la: Date siceram mœrentibus, et vinum his qui amaro sunt animo.
text_pt: Dai bebida forte ao que está prestes a perecer, e o vinho aos amargurados de espírito.
text_el: δίδοτε μέθην τοῖς ἐν λύπαις καὶ οἶνον πίνειν τοῖς ἐν ὀδύναις

text_en: Let them drink, and forget their want, and remember their sorrow no more.
text_la: Bibant, et obliviscantur egestatis suæ, et doloris sui non recordentur amplius.
text_pt: Que beba, e esqueça da sua pobreza, e da sua miséria não se lembre mais.
text_el: ἵνα ἐπιλάθωνται τῆς πενίας καὶ τῶν πόνων μὴ μνησθῶσιν ἔτι

text_en: Open your mouth for the dumb, and for the causes of all the children that pass.
text_la: Aperi os tuum muto, et causis omnium filiorum qui pertranseunt.
text_pt: Abre a tua boca a favor do mudo, pela causa de todos que são designados à destruição.
text_el: ἄνοιγε σὸν στόμα λόγῳ θεοῦ καὶ κρῖνε πάντας ὑγιῶς

text_en: Open your mouth, decree that which is just , and do justice to the needy and poor.
text_la: Aperi os tuum, decerne quod justum est, et judica inopem et pauperem.
text_pt: Abre a tua boca; julga retamente; e faze justiça aos pobres e aos necessitados.
text_el: ἄνοιγε σὸν στόμα καὶ κρῖνε δικαίως διάκρινε δὲ πένητα καὶ ἀσθενῆ

text_en: Who shall find a valiant woman ? Far, and from the uttermost coasts is the price of her.
text_la: Mulierem fortem quis inveniet? procul et de ultimis finibus pretium ejus.
text_pt: Mulher virtuosa quem a achará? O seu valor muito excede ao de rubis.
text_el: γυναῖκα ἀνδρείαν τίς εὑρήσει τιμιωτέρα δέ ἐστιν λίθων πολυτελῶν ἡ τοιαύτη

text_en: The heart of her husband trusts in her, and he shall have no need of spoils.
text_la: Confidit in ea cor viri sui, et spoliis non indigebit.
text_pt: O coração do seu marido está nela confiado; assim ele não necessitará de despojo.
text_el: θαρσεῖ ἐπ' αὐτῇ ἡ καρδία τοῦ ἀνδρὸς αὐτῆς ἡ τοιαύτη καλῶν σκύλων οὐκ ἀπορήσει

text_en: She will render him good , and not evil all the days of her life.
text_la: Reddet ei bonum, et non malum, omnibus diebus vitæ suæ.
text_pt: Ela só lhe faz bem, e não mal, todos os dias da sua vida.
text_el: ἐνεργεῖ γὰρ τῷ ἀνδρὶ ἀγαθὰ πάντα τὸν βίον

text_en: She has sought wool and flax, and has wrought by the counsel of her hands.
text_la: Quæsivit lanam et linum, et operata est consilia manuum suarum.
text_pt: Busca lã e linho, e trabalha de boa vontade com suas mãos.
text_el: μηρυομένη ἔρια καὶ λίνον ἐποίησεν εὔχρηστον ταῖς χερσὶν αὐτῆς

text_en: She is like the merchant's ship, she brings her bread from afar.
text_la: Facta est quasi navis institoris, de longe portans panem suum.
text_pt: Como o navio mercante, ela traz de longe o seu pão.
text_el: ἐγένετο ὡσεὶ ναῦς ἐμπορευομένη μακρόθεν συνάγει δὲ αὕτη τὸν βίον

text_en: And she has risen in the night, and given a prey to her household, and victuals to her maidens.
text_la: Et de nocte surrexit, deditque prædam domesticis suis, et cibaria ancillis suis.
text_pt: Levanta-se, mesmo à noite, para dar de comer aos da casa, e distribuir a tarefa das servas.
text_el: καὶ ἀνίσταται ἐκ νυκτῶν καὶ ἔδωκεν βρώματα τῷ οἴκῳ καὶ ἔργα ταῖς θεραπαίναις

text_en: She has considered a field, and bought it: with the fruit of her hands she has planted a vineyard.
text_la: Consideravit agrum, et emit eum; de fructu manuum suarum plantavit vineam.
text_pt: Examina uma propriedade e adquire-a; planta uma vinha com o fruto de suas mãos.
text_el: θεωρήσασα γεώργιον ἐπρίατο ἀπὸ δὲ καρπῶν χειρῶν αὐτῆς κατεφύτευσεν κτῆμα

text_en: She has girded her loins with strength, and has strengthened her arm.
text_la: Accinxit fortitudine lumbos suos, et roboravit brachium suum.
text_pt: Cinge os seus lombos de força, e fortalece os seus braços.
text_el: ἀναζωσαμένη ἰσχυρῶς τὴν ὀσφὺν αὐτῆς ἤρεισεν τοὺς βραχίονας αὐτῆς εἰς ἔργον

text_en: She has tasted, and seen that her traffic is good : her lamp shall not be put out in the night.
text_la: Gustavit, et vidit quia bona est negotiatio ejus; non extinguetur in nocte lucerna ejus.
text_pt: Vê que é boa a sua mercadoria; e a sua lâmpada não se apaga de noite.
text_el: ἐγεύσατο ὅτι καλόν ἐστιν τὸ ἐργάζεσθαι καὶ οὐκ ἀποσβέννυται ὅλην τὴν νύκτα ὁ λύχνος αὐτῆς

text_en: She has put out her hand to strong things, and her fingers have taken hold of the spindle.
text_la: Manum suam misit ad fortia, et digiti ejus apprehenderunt fusum.
text_pt: Estende as suas mãos ao fuso, e suas mãos pegam na roca.
text_el: τοὺς πήχεις αὐτῆς ἐκτείνει ἐπὶ τὰ συμφέροντα τὰς δὲ χεῖρας αὐτῆς ἐρείδει εἰς ἄτρακτον

text_en: She has opened her hand to the needy, and stretched out her hands to the poor.
text_la: Manum suam aperuit inopi, et palmas suas extendit ad pauperem.
text_pt: Abre a sua mão ao pobre, e estende as suas mãos ao necessitado.
text_el: χεῖρας δὲ αὐτῆς διήνοιξεν πένητι καρπὸν δὲ ἐξέτεινεν πτωχῷ

text_en: She shall not fear for her house in the cold of snow: for all her domestics are clothed with double garments.
text_la: Non timebit domui suæ a frigoribus nivis; omnes enim domestici ejus vestiti sunt duplicibus.
text_pt: Não teme a neve na sua casa, porque toda a sua família está vestida de escarlata.
text_el: οὐ φροντίζει τῶν ἐν οἴκῳ ὁ ἀνὴρ αὐτῆς ὅταν που χρονίζῃ πάντες γὰρ οἱ παρ' αὐτῆς ἐνδιδύσκονται

text_en: She has made for herself clothing of tapestry : fine linen, and purple, is her covering.
text_la: Stragulatam vestem fecit sibi; byssus et purpura indumentum ejus.
text_pt: Faz para si cobertas de tapeçaria; seu vestido é de seda e de púrpura.
text_el: δισσὰς χλαίνας ἐποίησεν τῷ ἀνδρὶ αὐτῆς ἐκ δὲ βύσσου καὶ πορφύρας ἑαυτῇ ἐνδύματα

text_en: Her husband is honourable in the gates, when he sits among the senators of the land.
text_la: Nobilis in portis vir ejus, quando sederit cum senatoribus terræ.
text_pt: Seu marido é conhecido nas portas, e assenta-se entre os anciãos da terra.
text_el: περίβλεπτος δὲ γίνεται ἐν πύλαις ὁ ἀνὴρ αὐτῆς ἡνίκα ἂν καθίσῃ ἐν συνεδρίῳ μετὰ τῶν γερόντων κατοίκων τῆς γῆς

text_en: She made fine linen, and sold it, and delivered a girdle to the Chanaanite .
text_la: Sindonem fecit, et vendidit, et cingulum tradidit Chananæo.
text_pt: Faz panos de linho fino e vende-os, e entrega cintos aos mercadores.
text_el: σινδόνας ἐποίησεν καὶ ἀπέδοτο περιζώματα δὲ τοῖς Χαναναίοις

text_en: Strength and beauty are her clothing, and she shall laugh in the latter day.
text_la: Fortitudo et decor indumentum ejus, et ridebit in die novissimo.
text_pt: A força e a honra são seu vestido, e se alegrará com o dia futuro.
text_el: στόμα αὐτῆς διήνοιξεν προσεχόντως καὶ ἐννόμως καὶ τάξιν ἐστείλατο τῇ γλώσσῃ αὐτῆς

text_en: She has opened her mouth to wisdom, and the law of clemency is on her tongue.
text_la: Os suum aperuit sapientiæ, et lex clementiæ in lingua ejus.
text_pt: Abre a sua boca com sabedoria, e a lei da beneficência está na sua língua.
text_el: ἰσχὺν καὶ εὐπρέπειαν ἐνεδύσατο καὶ εὐφράνθη ἐν ἡμέραις ἐσχάταις

text_en: She has looked well on the paths of her house, and has not eaten her bread idle.
text_la: Consideravit semitas domus suæ, et panem otiosa non comedit.
text_pt: Está atenta ao andamento da casa, e não come o pão da preguiça.
text_el: στεγναὶ διατριβαὶ οἴκων αὐτῆς σῖτα δὲ ὀκνηρὰ οὐκ ἔφαγεν

text_en: Her children rose up, and called her blessed : her husband, and he praised her.
text_la: Surrexerunt filii ejus, et beatissimam prædicaverunt; vir ejus, et laudavit eam.
text_pt: Levantam-se seus filhos e chamam-na bem-aventurada; seu marido também, e ele a louva.
text_el: τὸ στόμα δὲ ἀνοίγει σοφῶς καὶ νομοθέσμως ἡ δὲ ἐλεημοσύνη αὐτῆς ἀνέστησεν τὰ τέκνα αὐτῆς καὶ ἐπλούτησαν καὶ ὁ ἀνὴρ αὐτῆς ᾔνεσεν αὐτήν

text_en: Many daughters have gathered together riches: you have surpassed them all.
text_la: Multæ filiæ congregaverunt divitias; tu supergressa es universas.
text_pt: Muitas filhas têm procedido virtuosamente, mas tu és, de todas, a mais excelente!
text_el: πολλαὶ θυγατέρες ἐκτήσαντο πλοῦτον πολλαὶ ἐποίησαν δυνατά σὺ δὲ ὑπέρκεισαι καὶ ὑπερῆρας πάσας

text_en: Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: the woman that fears the Lord , she shall be praised.
text_la: Fallax gratia, et vana est pulchritudo : mulier timens Dominum, ipsa laudabitur.
text_pt: Enganosa é a beleza e vã a formosura, mas a mulher que teme ao Senhor, essa sim será louvada.
text_el: ψευδεῖς ἀρέσκειαι καὶ μάταιον κάλλος γυναικός γυνὴ γὰρ συνετὴ εὐλογεῖται φόβον δὲ κυρίου αὕτη αἰνείτω

text_en: Give her of the fruit of her hands: and let her works praise her in the gates.
text_la: Date ei de fructu manuum suarum, et laudent eam in portis opera ejus.
text_pt: Dai-lhe do fruto das suas mãos, e deixe o seu próprio trabalho louvá-la nas portas.
text_el: δότε αὐτῇ ἀπὸ καρπῶν χειρῶν αὐτῆς καὶ αἰνείσθω ἐν πύλαις ὁ ἀνὴρ αὐτῆς
